En az üç numune şişesi doldurulur: biri: At least three sample bottles are filled: one for the ship, one for the barge/supplier and one for independent laboratory analysis. Each bottle is labelled and sealed.
En büyük online jeneratör veya grup kayb: The spinning reserve, which assesses the frequency and the remaining capacity after the loss of the largest online generator or group, is followed. The standby generator is started and synchronised before the load trend reaches the limit, and the bridge is informed.
En etkili hazırlık, denetimden günler ön: The most effective preparation is not panic cleaning in the days before an inspection but a continuous "audit-ready" working culture. The Chief Officer makes real-time record keeping, well-maintained equipment and crew knowledge of procedures part of the daily routine. What an inspector looks at most is "the consistency between the records and the actual condition".
En iyi atık, hiç oluşmayan atıktır. Aşçı: The best waste is waste that is never created. The cook reduces food waste at source through portion control, correct ordering/stock management and FIFO rotation; this has a positive effect on both the MARPOL burden and the budget. By observing consumption data, the cook calibrates the quantity produced; constant leftovers are a sign of overproduction and waste.
En kısa mesafe (great circle) her zaman: The shortest distance (great circle) is not always the most economical route. Strong winds, waves and currents cause loss of speed and increased fuel consumption.
En sık LOP konuları: ship/shore figure f: The most frequent LOP subjects: ship/shore figure differences (especially ullage/quantity discrepancies on tankers), slow rate, terminal equipment breakdown, weather delays, cargo condition and late berthing. The Chief Officer issues a separate, dated and clear LOP for each. The other party may also issue LOPs to the ship; these are also recorded and answered.
En sık deficiency'ler: expired pyrotechn: The most frequent deficiencies are: expired pyrotechnics, overdue liferaft service, expired/missing HRUs, painted lashings, lifeboat engines that do not work, incomplete lifeboat inventory and inconsistencies between "records and physical condition". By tracking these items proactively, the Safety Officer comes through inspections without findings.
En sık deficiency'ler: güncel olmayan mu: The most common deficiencies: an out-of-date muster list (crew who have left the ship still on the list), conflicting or missing duty assignments, instructions not in the working language, crew without a station card, and inconsistencies between the drill records and the muster list. The Safety Officer checks these points proactively.
En sık deficiency'ler: imzasız/eksik fam: The most common deficiencies: unsigned or incomplete familiarization checklists, late familiarization, inconsistency with the drill records, and new crew members without basic safety knowledge. While making the record, the Safety Officer also ensures that real learning takes place on board.
En sık görülen hatalar: yalnızca lokal s: The most common errors are: relying only on the local stop without isolating the breaker, not releasing stored energy, not doing a try-out, and the oncoming team not verifying the isolation at the watch change. The Third/Fourth Engineer does not skip these steps; pressure because "we're in a hurry" can never justify relaxing the isolation.
En sık görülen sorunlar: water seal kayb: The most frequent problems are: loss of the water seal (wrong gravity disc, low feed/sealing water), oil loss (broken seal, excessive flow rate), vibration (sludge build-up in the bowl, incorrect assembly, bearing wear), incomplete desludge (operating water pressure/clogging problem) and water/dirt reaching the engine (general drop in efficiency). The root cause of each symptom is looked for systematically.
En sık hata, TRB'yi sefer sonuna kadar b: The most common mistake is leaving the TRB blank until the end of the voyage and trying to fill it in all at once. This produces entries that are both poor in quality and difficult for the trainer to approve. The second mistake is writing tasks in a vague and general way ("I looked at the engine"); the third is recording only easily accessible tasks without regard to the balance of competences.
En sık hatalar: scupper plug'ın takılı u: The most common errors: forgetting a scupper plug in place (water accumulation), lashing or blocking a freeing port, blocking an escape route with temporary materials, and leaving spills to be "cleaned later". This neglect leads both to routine accidents and to a serious stability/flooding risk in bad weather.
En sık problem, eksik veya geç alınan Se: The most frequent problem is a missing or late Sea Service certificate; the certificate is not obtained when leaving the ship and cannot be obtained afterwards. The second problem is missing fields on the certificate (engine power not stated, no stamp, incorrect date). The third is inconsistency between the Sea Service dates and the seafarer's book/TRB dates.
En sık saha hatası, taşlama öncesi bilge: The most common mistake in the field is not cleaning away oily rags and dirt in the bilges and under the floor plates before grinding. Falling sparks can cause delayed ignition and turn into a fire that goes unnoticed at a change of watch.
En sık separatör sorunu, yağ/yakıtın su: The most frequent separator problem is oil/fuel escaping through the water outlet (overboard); this may be caused by loss of the water seal, the wrong gravity disc or excessive throughput, and creates a risk of both fuel loss and pollution. Other problems are vibration (bowl imbalance), insufficient desludging and leaks.
En tehlikeli hata, tatbikatı \"göstermel: The most dangerous mistake is to hold drills "for show": writing "done" on paper without raising the alarm, and not actually using the equipment. Crew who meet the equipment for the first time in a real emergency panic and are late. The AB must take drills seriously and actually carry out every duty.
En tehlikeli yanı, tehlikenin görünmez v: The most dangerous aspect is that the hazard can be invisible and odorless: in a tank where the oxygen level has dropped, a person loses consciousness and collapses within a few breaths and cannot even give a warning. Rust (oxidation), decaying organic cargo, inert gas, welding gases and bilge gases consume oxygen or create a toxic atmosphere. This is why even a space where the air "looks clean" can be fatal.
En yaygın EEXI uyum yöntemi, Engine Powe: The most common EEXI compliance method is limiting the maximum available power with Engine Power Limitation (EPL) or Shaft Power Limitation (ShaPoLi). This lowers the attained EEXI by restricting the engine's MCR by software or mechanical means.
En yaygın eksiklikler; familiarizasyonun: The most common deficiencies are reducing familiarization to a "checklist signed" formality, confusing type-specific ECDIS training with generic training, COLREG remaining a memorized pattern that is not applied to real scenarios, and drills being carried out without realism. Another deficiency is failing to develop the junior team's courage to challenge.
En yaygın hata, changeover sırasında yen: The most common mistake is putting the new side into service during a changeover without venting it; an air pocket lowers the oil/fuel pressure and puts the engine at risk. The second common mistake is closing the cover without renewing the O-ring/gasket; this creates a risk of hot oil leakage and fire. The third is using oil of the wrong grade or a filter with the wrong mesh.
En yaygın hatalar: SWL aşımı (yükü hafif: The most common mistakes are: exceeding the SWL (underestimating the load), a wrong sling angle (excessive leg loads at a wide angle), using unlabeled/uncertified equipment, slings without protection at sharp edges, side-loaded shackles/eye bolts and using a chain block without testing its brake. Another is using damaged equipment with an "it's a short job, it'll do" mentality.
En yaygın hatalar: scupper'ı tıkamayı un: The most common mistakes are: forgetting to plug the scuppers, reducing the rate too late when topping off, setting up the valve line-up wrongly (wrong tank/overflow), emptying the drip tray too late and bypassing the OWS alarm in the belief that it is a "fault". Another is not reporting a small spill and trying to conceal it — this turns a small incident into a serious offense.
En yaygın hatalar; eski/tek hava verisin: The most common errors are relying on old or single-source weather data, failing to allow for swell-roll resonance, heading towards a storm under ETA pressure, starting preparations late, and mistaking significant wave height for the maximum wave height.
En yaygın hatalar; gyro error'un düzenli: The most common errors are not checking the gyro error regularly, an out-of-date deviation card, an incorrectly set echo sounder offset, skipping the radar performance monitor and never comparing the log with GNSS.
En yaygın hatalar; hafta atlayarak veya: The most common errors are making corrections with weeks skipped or in the wrong order, entering T&Ps in ink (indelible), loading ENC updates incompletely or in the wrong order, leaving the AIO layer switched off and navigating on an over-scaled ENC.
En yaygın hatalar; saat değişiminin yanl: The most common errors are making the clock change in the wrong direction (such as retarding the clocks when steaming east), loading the change onto one person so that rest hours are violated, not entering it in the logbook, and mistakenly converting the GMDSS log to zone time. Another error is to confuse the date line crossing with a clock change and skip the date correction.
En yaygın hatalar; tarihi geçmiş harita/: The most common errors are using out-of-date charts/publications, setting the ECDIS safety settings incorrectly, incomplete UKC/squat calculation, not determining an abort point, and a plan that stays on paper and is not owned by the team.
En yaygın yöntemler; transit (iki sabit: The most common methods are a transit (two fixed objects in line), azimuth/amplitude (comparing the calculated true azimuth of a celestial body with its gyro azimuth) and a known transit bearing. The error must be checked at least once a day in the open sea, and always before entering restricted waters.
En ölümcül hatalar: oksijen sınırı doğru: The most fatal errors: starting washing without verifying the oxygen limit, continuing operations after an IGS failure, using equipment without earthing it, and water washing in a tank that is not inert. The major tanker explosions in history (including several VLCCs) resulted from a combination of these errors and led to the introduction of the IG/COW rules.
Enclosed Space Entry Permit, girişin tüm: The Enclosed Space Entry Permit is a formal control tool that documents that all safety conditions for entry have been met and authorizes entry. A.1203(33) and the company SMS require this permit to be signed by an authorized person (usually the Chief Officer). The permit defines which space is to be entered, for how long, by whom and under what conditions.
Enclosed space (kapalı alan), sınırlı gi: An enclosed space is a space that has limited openings for entry/exit, is not continuously ventilated and is not designed for continuous occupancy. On board, these include cargo holds, ballast/fuel/oil tanks, void spaces, cofferdams, duct keels, pump rooms, chain lockers, sewage tanks and similar spaces. The atmosphere of these spaces cannot be judged by eye; it may be oxygen-deficient or toxic.
Enclosed-space entry requires risk asses: Enclosed-space entry requires risk assessment, isolation, ventilation, representative atmospheric testing and an authorised permit to work (PTW). A safe oxygen reading alone does not exclude toxic or flammable gases. Use suitable calibrated instruments and the approved acceptance limits, maintain communications and an attendant, and have a practised rescue plan. Never enter impulsively to rescue a casualty. SOLAS III/19.3.3 requires crew with entry or rescue duties to participate in entry and rescue drills at least every two months.
Endüstriyel 5S yaklaşımı (Seiri-ayıkla,: The industrial 5S approach (Seiri – sort, Seiton – set in order, Seiso – clean, Seiketsu – standardize, Shitsuke – sustain) applies directly to the ship's store. The Bosun sorts out unused/expired material, places the rest on labeled shelves, keeps the floor and ventilation clean, sets a labeling standard and keeps it going through watch changes.
Endüstriyel 5S yöntemi (Seiri-ayıkla, Se: The industrial 5S method (Seiri – sort, Seiton – set in order, Seiso – clean, Seiketsu – standardize, Shitsuke – sustain) can be applied directly on deck. The Bosun fixes "what belongs where" for each storage area; the places of hand tools are marked with shadow boards, so a missing tool is noticed at once.
Endüstriyel bulaşık makinesi hem hijyen: The industrial dishwasher is critical for both hygiene and efficiency; its strainers are cleaned in every working period, the spray arms are checked for blockage and the rinse water temperature (typically a final rinse of ≥82°C for sanitizing) is verified. Limescale build-up (especially with hard water) reduces performance; descaler is applied periodically.
Energy Efficiency Design Index: Yeni gem: Energy Efficiency Design Index: calculated at the design stage of new ships. A reference line has been set for each ship type and size range.
Energy management, emisyon takibi (EEXI/: Energy management, emissions monitoring (EEXI/CII), critical equipment reliability and continuous improvement are the basic expectations of these elements and must be documented.
Enerji sadece elektrik değildir: hidroli: Energy is not only electrical: hydraulic/pneumatic pressure, steam, spring tension, heat and gravity (a suspended load) are also "stored energy". Before dismantling a pump, the Oiler both isolates/locks out its electrical supply and closes the suction/discharge valves and drains the line; otherwise back pressure or an inadvertent start can cause serious injury.
Enerji tasarrufu sağlar (özellikle pompa: It saves energy (especially on pumps and fans). With a cubic load characteristic, a 20% reduction in speed saves about 50% of the power.
Enerji tüketimi evaporatöre göre daha yü: Its energy consumption is higher than that of an evaporator, but it has been reduced in modern systems with energy recovery.
Engine Log Book, makine dairesinin yasal: The Engine Log Book is the legal memory of the engine room. Hourly parameters (RPM, exhaust gas temp, scavenge air pressure, jacket cooling temp, LO pressure, FO temp/viscosity), tank levels and significant events are recorded. The cadet first takes readings under supervision, then starts keeping the log personally under the EOOW's control.
Engine room logbook (veya elektronik eşd: The engine room logbook (or its electronic equivalent) records the condition of the machinery every watch: main engine speed/load, auxiliary engine loads, temperatures and pressures, tank levels, water production, fuel/oil consumption and any abnormalities observed. The Third/Fourth Engineer enters the data for their own watch completely and legibly.
Engine room logbook, Oil Record Book Par: The engine room logbook must be consistent with the Oil Record Book Part I. Bilge transfers, OWS (Oily Water Separator) operation, oil transfers and sludge operations are also entered in the ORB; the raw data in the logbook supports this statutory record.
Enjeksiyon kalitesini belirleyen büyüklü: The quantity that determines injection quality is viscosity, not temperature. The viscometer controls the final heater according to the value it measures; the target viscosity range is taken from the engine maker's instructions and kept the same from one fuel to another.
Enjeksiyon öncesi yakıt viskozitesi 10-1: Before injection the fuel viscosity must be set to 10–15 cSt. The heating temperature is 130–150 °C for HFO and 80–100 °C for VLSFO.
Enjektör (injector): Nozzle iğnesi basın: Injector: the nozzle needle lifts under pressure and the fuel is atomised.
Enjektör açma basıncı periyodik olarak t: The injector opening pressure must be tested periodically. Low opening pressure causes poor atomisation; high pressure causes injection delay.
Entegre haşere yönetimi (Integrated Pest: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) leaves chemical intervention to the last step and is based first on environmental control. The basic principle is to cut off three kinds of access: access to food (closed containers, cleaning up spilled food immediately, keeping garbage covered), access to water (eliminating leaks/pools) and access to harborage/breeding sites (sealing cracks and holes, removing accumulated cardboard). Pests settle when they find one of these three resources; cutting off all three is the strongest control.
Entegre sistemde tüm cihazların aynı zam: In an integrated system, it is critical for alarm log analysis and event sequencing that all devices use the same timestamp. The ETO checks the NTP/time synchronization source, and also verifies that the data bridges (gateways) between different subsystems work correctly and that there are no scaling errors.
Erişim ekipmanı altında safety net ve ya: A safety net is rigged under the access equipment, and a lifebuoy + light + heaving line is kept nearby. These preparations are essential for a quick response if someone falls into the water. The Bosun ensures that these safety arrangements are always in place.
Erişim ekipmanı, güvenli açıyla, sağlam: Access equipment must be rigged at a safe angle, securely fastened, with non-slip steps and adequate lighting. After rigging and before use, the AB and the officer check the equipment; if there are loose fastenings, cracked steps, missing guardrails or insufficient light, it is not used. Access safety is not something to "fix later".
Erişim noktasında, ışıklı/dumanlı işaret: At the access point, a lifebuoy with a self-igniting light/smoke signal and a heaving line attached to it are kept ready. If the pilot or anyone else falls into the sea, the AB immediately throws the lifebuoy, keeps the person in sight and raises the alarm. The rescue boat/MOB boat must be ready; for night transfers, a searchlight is ready to illuminate the water.
Error sürekli artıyor veya sıçramalar gö: If the error keeps increasing or shows jumps, this is a sign of a fault; the Second Officer reports the situation to the Master and the technical department. It is also checked regularly that the repeaters are synchronized with the master gyro.
Escape trunk kapıları, korkuluklar ve me: The condition of the escape trunk doors, handrails and ladder steps is checked. In a fire or flooding emergency, seconds matter; a blocked escape route can have fatal consequences.
Esneme, dikkat dağınıklığı, gecikmiş tep: Yawning, distraction, delayed reactions, irritability and an increase in errors are signs of fatigue. The Master builds a culture in which the crew can report fatigue without hesitation; saying "I am tired" is not punished but taken seriously.
Et odası -18 °C, balık -25 °C, sebze +4: Typical temperatures: meat room −18 °C, fish −25 °C, vegetables +4 °C, dairy products +2 °C, dry provisions +10 °C.
Etkili ayrıştırma, kaynağında doğru topl: Effective segregation starts with correct collection at source. The Chief Officer places labeled, color-coded garbage bins at suitable points on deck and in the accommodation: separate bins for plastics, food, paper/cardboard, glass, metal and hazardous waste/e-waste. Labels must be clear and multilingual (because of the diversity of the crew). Wrongly segregated waste makes later sorting difficult and creates a risk of improper discharge.
Etkili bir D&A politikası yalnızca test: An effective D&A policy is not only testing and punishment; it also covers prevention and training. At periodic safety meetings the Master explains the D&A risks, the scope of the policy and how testing works. When the crew see the policy not as a "trap to catch people" but as a framework that protects everyone's safety, voluntary acceptance of the programme increases.
Etkili ekip yönetimi, hatanın kaçınılmaz: Effective team management accepts that error is inevitable and concentrates on catching it early. A "just culture" separates deliberate violations from human error: human error that is reported is not punished but learned from; reckless risk-taking or deliberate breaking of rules, however, has consequences. By striking this balance, the Master ensures that near misses and errors are reported rather than hidden.
Etkili eğitim, düzenli geri bildirimle o: Effective training depends on regular feedback. The cadet accepts feedback from the OOW and the Master without becoming defensive and applies it on the next watch. Mistakes (a wrong fix, a late maneuver proposal, an incomplete record) are learning opportunities; what matters is not repeating the same mistake.
Etkili gece talimatı, otoriteyle birlikt: Effective night orders encourage open communication alongside authority. The engineer officer of the watch must be able to pass on observations and concerns without hesitation. A culture is established in which the Chief Engineer is bothered not by late news but by late intervention.
Etkili lookout, ufku sistematik tarar: b: An effective lookout scans the horizon systematically: starting from the bow, they check both sides and the stern at regular intervals. 360° awareness, not just looking ahead, is essential; overtaking ships in particular approach from astern. Scanning is done both with the naked eye and with binoculars.
Etkinlik alanlarında kapasite ve çıkış y: In event areas, the capacity and clear escape routes are managed; the staff are trained in crowd management. In an emergency the guidance procedure is applied.
Evaporatör buzlanması, genleşme valfi ay: Icing of the evaporator, a maladjusted expansion valve and refrigerant leaks reduce the refrigerating capacity. For trend monitoring, the suction and discharge pressures, superheat and subcooling values should be recorded together.
Evaporatör kabuğu içinde vakum oluşturul: A vacuum is created in the evaporator shell, lowering the boiling temperature of the water to 40–60 °C. The main engine HT cooling water (70–85 °C) is used as the heat source.
Evaporatör yüzeyinde nem yoğuşur ve düşü: Moisture condenses on the evaporator surface and frost forms at low temperature; this reduces heat transfer. The ETO checks that the defrost system (electric heater, hot gas or off-cycle) works correctly, that the defrost timer/thermostat is set and the insulation of the defrost heater circuits. A faulty defrost turns the evaporator into a block of ice and stops refrigeration.
Evaporatör üzerinde biriken buz (frost): Ice (frost) building up on the evaporator reduces heat transfer; periodic defrosting (hot gas or electric) melts this ice. Too much humidity in the vegetable room causes rotting, too little causes drying out; ventilation and the balance of humidity preserve the quality of the food.
Evaporatör: Düşük basınçlı akışkan, soğu: Evaporator: the low-pressure refrigerant evaporates by drawing heat from the space to be cooled. This component provides the refrigerating effect.
Evaporatör: Korunacak hacimden ısı çekil: Evaporator: the refrigerating effect is produced by drawing heat from the space to be kept cool.
Evaporatörde periyodik kireç sökme (acid: On the evaporator, periodic descaling (acid cleaning), plate cleaning, ejector performance and vacuum tightness are checked. On the RO plant, the pre-filters are changed, the membranes are flushed (CIP) and the HP pump is maintained.
Even keel veya hafif by-stern trim genel: Even keel or a slight trim by the stern is generally preferred hydrodynamically. On modern ships, trim optimization software finds the trim giving the lowest resistance for a given speed and draft and saves 2-5% fuel.
Ex-proof ekipman bakımı yalnızca yetkili: Maintenance of Ex-proof equipment must be carried out only by authorised personnel. All screws, seals and cable entries on the equipment must be kept in their original condition. Damaged Ex-proof equipment must be taken out of use at once.
Execution, planın gerçek seyir koşulları: Execution is carrying out the plan under actual navigation conditions. Small revisions to the plan may be needed because of changes in the weather, the traffic situation or VTS instructions. These revisions must be entered in the log book and on the passage plan; without the Master's initiative, the officer of the watch cannot change the basic logic of the plan.
Execution, planın kaptan brifingi sonras: Execution means carrying out the plan after the Master's briefing; monitoring means cross-checking the position against the plan on every watch and detecting any deviation. The Second Officer ensures that the plan remains a "living document" and is updated for changes in weather, traffic or draft.
Exhaust gas economiser'da soot fire risk: The risk of a soot fire in the exhaust gas economizer is monitored; soot deposits can ignite during standby/low-load periods. Soot blowing is carried out regularly and the outlet gas temperature is monitored.
Exhaust gas economizer, ana makine egzoz: The exhaust gas economiser turns the main engine's exhaust heat into steam; at low load, accumulated soot and oil can ignite (soot fire / iron fire). Regular soot blowing, water washing and low-load warnings reduce this risk. A high exhaust outlet temperature can be an early sign.
Existing Energy Efficiency Index: Mevcut: Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index: applies to existing ships from 2023. The calculation is similar to the EEDI.
Eye bolt (mapa), ekipmana vidalanan kald: An eye bolt is a lifting point screwed into a piece of equipment (e.g. a pump casing, a motor). A plain eye bolt is suitable only for axial (vertical) loads; if it is loaded at an angle, it breaks — collar/swivel eye bolts are used for angled loads. The eye bolt must be screwed fully home (shoulder in contact) and its threads must be in good condition.
Eğer A cismi C cismiyle termal dengede i: If body A is in thermal equilibrium with body C, and body B is also in thermal equilibrium with body C, then bodies A and B are in thermal equilibrium with each other. This statement is the zeroth law of thermodynamics.
Eğer gündüzden devam eden bir sorun (örn: If there is a problem carried over from the day (e.g. a bearing temperature being monitored, a temporary repair, a rising trend), the night order specifically flags it and gives monitoring instructions.
Eğer varış limanı zone time'dan farklı y: If the arrival port uses a half-hour legal time that differs from zone time (e.g. UTC+5:30), the last change is made with a half-hour correction. The pilot station ETA, VTS reporting and cargo readiness times are always reported in the port's legal time; they must not be confused with the shipboard zone time.
Eğitim faaliyeti onboard training record: Training activity is documented with an onboard training record / familiarization checklist. Undocumented training counts as "not done" in Port State Control (PSC) inspections and internal company audits; in investigations after an accident, the absence of these records also increases the liability of the ship and the company.
Eğitim, \"anlatıldı\" ile değil, \"yetki: Training is complete not when "it has been explained" but when "competence has been gained". The Second Officer measures competence through observation, practical tasks and scenario tests. An officer's ability to use ECDIS safely is considered verified only when the officer can independently enter the correct safety contour and interpret the route check output.
Eğitimde \"son dakika manevrası\" tuzağı: Training also covers the "last-minute maneuver" trap: if the give-way ship does not take action, under Rule 17 the stand-on ship first gains the right to maneuver on her own (17(a)(ii)), and then the obligation to do so (17(b)). Judging the timing of this transition correctly comes only through experience and repeated scenarios.
Eğitmen mühendis, stajyerin gözlem keski: The training engineer regularly assesses the cadet's sharpness of observation, compliance with procedures and safety awareness. The cadet should actively ask for feedback: "What did I miss on this round?", "Did I respond correctly to this alarm?". This feedback loop is the basis of the progression from supervised participation to independent competence.
Eşanjörün ısı transfer kapasitesi LMTD k: The heat transfer capacity of the heat exchanger is calculated using the LMTD.
Eşitleme şarjı (equalizing charge), tüm: An equalising charge is a controlled overcharge applied periodically to bring all cells to the same voltage.
FCC (Yüz Merkezli Kübik): γ-demir (östen: FCC (face-centred cubic): γ-iron (austenite), stable at high temperature. Ductile and formable.
FCC ünitesinden gelen katalizör parçacık: Catalyst particles from the FCC unit (cat fines) are 1–20 μm in size and have a hardness of 6–7 on the Mohs scale (harder than steel). These particles cause rapid abrasive wear of fuel injector nozzles, pump plunger surfaces, cylinder liners and piston rings.
FFE, PSC'de en sık deficiency çıkan alan: FFE is one of the areas with the most frequent PSC deficiencies: expired/discharged extinguishers, an emergency fire pump that does not work, missing SCBA cylinders, broken EEBD seals, blocked fire stations and inconsistencies between "records and physical condition" are typical findings. By tracking these items proactively and keeping the records without gaps, the Safety Officer goes into inspections prepared.
FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) analizi, ti: FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) analysis breaks the vibration signal down into its frequency components, making it possible to identify the type of fault.
FFT (Hızlı Fourier Dönüşümü) analizi, ti: FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) analysis breaks the vibration signal down into its frequency components and identifies the source of a fault.
FIFO, \"önce giren önce çıkar\" prensibi: FIFO is the "first in, first out" principle: newly arrived stock is placed at the back/bottom and existing stock at the front/top, so that older products are used first. This prevents products passing their expiry date and prevents waste. After each provisioning, the cook rearranges the shelves according to FIFO; putting a new box in front of the old one is a typical mistake.
FM200 (HFC-227ea), kimyasal zincir reaks: FM200 (HFC-227ea) extinguishes by breaking the chemical chain reaction. It is effective at a lower concentration than CO₂ (7–9%). Its toxic effect on people is low.
FO separatörü ağır/kirli yakıtı işler; y: The FO separator processes heavy/dirty fuel; it focuses on high temperature, frequent desludging and the removal of cat fines/water. The LO separator, on the other hand, cleans the system oil continuously (bypass purification); it works with a cleaner feed and removes water and wear metals. The feed temperature, flow rate and desludge frequency of the two are different and must not be confused.
FO settling/service tank seviyeleri, vis: FO settling/service tank levels, the viscosity control unit (heater outlet viscosity), FO booster pressure and filter ΔP are monitored. On entering an ECA, the timing of the changeover to low-sulfur fuel and the rate of temperature change are controlled; a sudden temperature change causes the fuel pumps to stick.
FO ısıtma, viskozite ve pompalanabilirli: FO heating is necessary for viscosity and pumpability; however, overheating (close to the flash point) is dangerous. The service tank is always supplied with clean, separated fuel.
FO/DO iç transfer, LO yenileme ve fresh: Internal FO/DO transfers, LO replenishment and fresh water transfers are operations in which the cadet takes part under supervision. Before the transfer, the valve alignment is verified and the overflow tank level is checked; throughout the transfer, the level is monitored continuously. An incorrect valve line-up or an uncontrolled transfer creates a risk of overflow and pollution.
FPP (Fixed Pitch Propeller) sabit hatvel: An FPP (fixed pitch propeller) has a fixed pitch; for manoeuvring and going astern the engine reverses. A CPP (controllable pitch propeller) adjusts thrust and direction at constant speed by changing the blade angle; it gives high manoeuvrability and suits a shaft generator, but it is mechanically complex and expensive.
FRB genelde sertgövde-şişme (RIB) yapıda: A fast rescue boat (FRB) is usually a rigid-inflatable (RIB), driven by an outboard motor or a waterjet. A waterjet reduces the risk of propeller injuries in shallow water and when recovering people. The FRB must be fast (to manoeuvre in bad weather) and self-righting.
FSO/FPSO hareketi ve geminin coğrafi mev: The movement of the FSO/FPSO and the ship's geographic position are monitored together; the divergence alarm limits are verified. Alarms for drive-off/drift-off, hawser overload or loss of the relative PRS are matched with the ASOG actions.
FWG ve RO birlikte çalıştırılarak yüksek: The FWG and the RO plant are run together to meet the high demand; salinity and conductivity are monitored, and production is stopped near the coast and in port. The water is disinfected (chlorine/UV) and mineralised.
Faaliyeti güvenle durdurma süresi (termi: The time needed to stop the activity safely (terminate time), the least risky escape direction and the thrust and power that must remain after the Worst Case Failure (WCF) are calculated. These three values directly determine the DP class and redundancy required.
Failed/slow start bulgusu ASOG statüsüne: A failed or slow start finding is reflected in the ASOG status and the standby order is updated. After the test, all selectors, breakers and alarm bypasses are returned to their operational positions.
Failure mode FMEA ve IMCA M247 component: The failure mode is matched with the FMEA and the IMCA M247 component list, and the possibility of a common cause is investigated. Instead of a temporary reset, a safe configuration, the ASOG status and a permanent corrective action are decided.
Fairlead (panama chock): Halatı yönlendi: Fairlead (Panama chock): a guide used to lead the line. It may be of the roller or closed type.
Fairlead ve roller'lar serbest dönmeli;: Fairleads and rollers must turn freely; a seized roller chafes and cuts the line. Stoppers (chain/rope stoppers), bollard welds and Panama leads are checked for cracks and wear. The winch brake is tested periodically, and greasing is carried out according to the greasing schedule. This maintenance is closely linked with the deck maintenance covered under duty no. 3.
Familiarisation kaydı, planlama paketi v: The familiarisation record, the planning package and the task risk assessment are kept on file; these three are reviewed again whenever the task changes.
Familiarizasyon ile eğitim (training) fa: Familiarization and training are different concepts: familiarization means "getting to know this equipment on this ship", while training is the process of "developing and maintaining competence". The Second Officer manages both together; a newly joined officer is given basic familiarization within the first 24 hours, and skills are reinforced with regular drills throughout the voyage.
Familiarizasyon tamamlandığında, kayıt z: When the familiarization is complete, the record is signed by the officer and the Second Officer and placed in the ship's training file. Additional sessions are planned for items found insufficient; an incomplete item is not considered passed.
Familiarizasyon; safety settings (safety: The familiarization covers the safety settings (safety contour, safety depth, shallow/deep contour), setting the display modes (base/standard/all), alarm management, route planning and the route check function, the manual update layer, S-52 symbology and the S-57/S-63 ENC loading and updating processes. Each make presents these functions with a different menu logic; what must be taught is the logic of each function, not blind memorizing of menus.
Familiarization checklist imzalanmadan p: Personnel are not put on an independent watch until the familiarization checklist has been signed. This process is especially critical in multinational crews with a language barrier and is supported by visual/hands-on instruction.
Familiarization katmanlıdır: (1) safety/: Familiarization is layered: (1) safety/emergency familiarization (emergencies, LSA, escape), (2) company/SMS familiarization (procedures, reporting), (3) job/role familiarization (the person's own duties). The Safety Officer is primarily responsible for the safety part; the other parts are carried out by the Chief Officer, the Chief Engineer or the relevant supervisor.
Familiarization sırasında dilden kaynakl: Misunderstandings caused by language are identified early during familiarization. It is not enough for a crew member to "appear to read" the instructions; real understanding is verified by the crew member physically showing their station.
Familiarization, geminin temel emniyet k: Familiarization also covers the ship's basic safety rules: enclosed space entry permit, hot work permit, working aloft/overside, lockout-tagout (LOTO) and PPE requirements. New crew members learn that starting such work without these permits is prohibited.
Familiarization, kapıların neden önemli: Familiarization makes clear why the doors matter: a closed fire door delays the spread of a fire for minutes, and a closed watertight door can limit flooding to one compartment. When new crew members understand that these barriers protect the ship and themselves, they internalize compliance with the rules.
Fan stop ve damper kapatma sistemi makin: The fan stop and damper closing system cuts off the engine room ventilation and reduces the oxygen.
Fanlar belirlenen hava değişim oranını s: The fans run at a capacity that gives the required rate of air changes: full capacity during vehicle handling and the required rate at sea. A fan failure is signalled by an alarm.
Fark değeri limiti aşıyorsa yatak aşınma: If the difference exceeds the limit, bearing wear, deformation of the bedplate or shaft misalignment must be considered. The engine should not be run and the classification society should be informed.
Farklı bunker partileri (özellikle farkl: When different bunker batches (especially from different suppliers/of different types) are mixed, incompatibility can cause sludge precipitation and clogging of purifiers/filters. Where possible, batches are kept in separate tanks; if mixing is unavoidable, a compatibility test is carried out. Low-sulfur fuel for ECA areas is kept ready in a separate service tank.
Farklı kaynaklı yakıtların karışımı çökm: Mixing fuels from different sources can cause sedimentation/sludging (asphaltene precipitation). Where possible, the Second Engineer keeps new fuel in a separate tank; if mixing is unavoidable, a compatibility test is carried out. Fuel whose stability has broken down clogs filters/purifiers and leads to loss of fuel supply.
Farklı limanlardaki yakıt fiyatları önem: Fuel prices can vary considerably between ports. Bunker planning software suggests the optimum bunkering strategy using route, speed and price data.
Fast Rescue Boat (FRB): ro-ro passenger: Fast rescue boat (FRB): at least one is required on ro-ro passenger ships; on other ships it depends on the approved arrangement. The speed and endurance criteria may differ with the full complement on board.
Faz 0 (2013): Referans çizgisi. Faz 1 (2: Phase 0 (2013): reference line. Phase 1 (2015): 10% reduction. Phase 2 (2020): 20% reduction. Phase 3 (2025): 30% or more reduction.
Feed water pompası: hot well'den kazana: Feed water pump: pumps water from the hot well into the boiler.
Fener izleme paneli (navigation light pa: The navigation light panel shows the status of each light on the bridge. A light failure gives an audible and visual alarm.
Fener tanıma lookout'un en kritik beceri: Recognizing lights is the lookout's most critical skill: green (starboard) and red (port) sidelights, white masthead/stern lights, the all-round white light of a ship at anchor, and the special light combinations for fishing, towing and restricted in ability to maneuver are defined in COLREG Part C. Although the AB does not have to know the meaning of every light by heart, they must describe what they see correctly and clearly (color, number, arrangement) and pass it on to the OOW.
Ferritik (430): Manyetik, orta korozyon: Ferritic (430): magnetic, moderate corrosion resistance. Decorative applications.
Fiber optik jiroskop (FOG) ve ring laser: The fibre optic gyroscope (FOG) and the ring laser gyroscope (RLG) are modern solid-state types. They have no moving parts and are more reliable.
Filika indirme kazaları (free-fall erken: Lifeboat launching accidents (premature free-fall release, davit brake failure, parting of falls) account for a significant share of fatal accidents at sea; most are caused by the wrong sequence or poorly maintained equipment. The AB must follow the lifeboat procedure step by step, paying attention to the safety pins and brakes.
Filika kancası (release hook); off-load: The lifeboat release hook may be off-load (opens only without load, when the boat is waterborne) or on-load (can open under load, before the boat is waterborne). On-load release allows quick release but, if misused, can make the lifeboat fall from height. Interlocks and a hydrostatic interlock (which prevents opening before the boat is waterborne) are therefore important.
Filika launching appliance ve on-load re: Lifeboat launching appliances and on-load release gear are subject to an annual thorough examination and operational test; every 5 years, a dynamic load test (testing the winch brake with 1.1x load, overload test of the release gear) is carried out by an authorized service provider. Davit falls are turned end-for-end at intervals of not more than 30 months and renewed when necessary due to deterioration or at intervals of not more than 5 years, whichever is earlier.
Filika motoru haftalık olarak toplam en: The lifeboat engine is run weekly for a total of at least 3 minutes (SOLAS III/20.6); water-cooled engines are not run without cooling from the sea or an auxiliary water supply for longer than the period specified by the manufacturer. During running, oil pressure, charging, exhaust color and ease of starting are observed; the battery charge condition is verified.
Filika/sallarda kullanılmak üzere taşına: Portable GMDSS VHF radios (generally yellow or orange and waterproof) are carried for use in lifeboats and liferafts; they provide communication with SAR units and the ship during a rescue. They have separate (spare) batteries and are tested regularly.
Filika; SOLAS donanımı (kürek, işaret fi: The lifeboat is fitted with SOLAS equipment (oars, pyrotechnics, first aid, water and food, compass, SART/VHF, painter). It is checked regularly that these items are complete and within their expiry dates.
Filikalar; haftalık görsel/fonksiyonel k: Lifeboats are subject to weekly visual/functional checks, monthly operation (engine start, davit movement), launching and floating out during drills every 3 months, and an annual full function test. On-load release gear requires an overhaul and a dynamic load test every 5 years; this mechanism needs particular attention because it has caused many fatal accidents in the past.
Filtrasyon + UV: Ön filtre + UV kombinas: Filtration + UV: a combination of a pre-filter and UV.
Filtrasyon: Son aşama olarak otomatik ge: Filtration: automatic back-flushing filters (10–25 μm) are used as the final stage.
Filtre + Elektroklorinasyon (EC) sisteml: Filter + electrochlorination (EC) systems: produce active chlorine from seawater by electrolysis; disinfection takes place in the tank with chlorine. Neutralisation (sodium thiosulphate) is needed when deballasting.
Filtre + UV (ultraviyole) sistemleri: 40: Filter + UV (ultraviolet) systems: a 40 µm disc or screen filter holds back large organisms; the UV reactor removes the ability to reproduce by damaging the DNA. No distinction between fresh and salt water is needed.
Filtre elemanı üzerinde basınç farkı (ΔP: When the pressure difference (ΔP) across the filter element exceeds a set threshold, the system automatically back-flushes or starts its self-cleaning mechanism (brush/scraper), and the accumulated sediment is drained. Usually a fine automatic filter and a protective coarse filter work together. A high ΔP alarm signals blockage.
Filtre temizliği, purifier desludging, d: Waste from filter cleaning, purifier desludging, emptying of drip trays and oil changes is collected in the sludge/waste oil tank. Under MARPOL Annex I, these fluids are classified as "oily residue (sludge)" and must not be discharged into the sea; they are disposed of by delivery to a shore facility (shore disposal) or by burning in the ship's incinerator (incineration).
Filtre tıkanıklığı, gevşek bağlantı, küç: Problems such as a clogged filter, a loose connection, a small gasket leak, bleeding air (priming) or a simple electrical connection are within the authority and competence of a junior engineer. Before intervening, the LOTO and permit rules are followed; the solution and the outcome are recorded.
Filtre ve yağ işleri tekrarlayan ama asl: Filter and oil jobs are repetitive, but they must never be treated as mere routine. Disciplined changeovers, correct sampling, careful examination of filter contents and meticulous waste management protect both the engine and the environment. A good Oiler is not someone who simply changes a filter, but someone who reads what comes out of it and diagnoses the health of the engine.
Filtre üzerindeki metalik partiküller (ö: Metallic particles on a filter (especially an LO filter) can be an early sign of bearing/surface wear; the finding is assessed together with oil analysis and reported to the Chief Engineer.
Filtreler dönüş ve basınç hatlarında bul: Filters are fitted in the return and pressure lines; a differential pressure indicator signals contamination. If the filter bypass stays open, the system runs unfiltered and wear accelerates.
Filtreler genelde pompa basma tarafında: Filters are generally installed in two stages: on the pump discharge side (fine filter) and on the suction side (suction strainer / coarse filter). The Oiler must know by heart the location of each filter, its mesh size, the direction of the changeover lever and the drain/vent valves.
Fin stabilizer açılma/kapanma ve hidroli: The extending and retracting of the fin stabilisers and their hydraulic system are maintained; on anti-roll tank systems, water transfer and control are verified. The fins are housed in port.
Final cargo plan Birinci Zabit tarafında: The final cargo plan is signed by the Chief Officer, approved by the Master and handed to the chief stevedore, the terminal and the duty officer. For last-minute changes (contaminated cargo, a damaged trailer, a reefer failure), the software is run again and the plan updated. Approved printouts are kept; PSC and vetting inspections may ask for them.
Final cargo plan, Birinci Zabit tarafınd: The final cargo plan is signed by the Chief Officer and submitted to the Master for approval. The approved plan is handed to the chief stevedore, the terminal and the duty officer. If there are last-minute changes to the plan (e.g. a trailer with ramp damage on a ro-ro, contaminated cargo on a tanker), the stability software is run again.
Final kondisyon yalnız intact değil, MAR: The final condition must meet not only the intact stability criteria but also the damage stability criteria of MARPOL Annex I Reg. 28. Side and bottom damage scenarios are checked with the damage case module of the loading computer. The printouts are kept; they may be asked for in PSC and SIRE inspections.
Final mevkide relative ve absolute refer: In the final position, relative and absolute references are compared; the environmental limits and the thrust margin are monitored in accordance with the ASOG. While a hose or crane load is connected, or personnel are on deck, no setpoint or heading change is made without permission.
Fire blanket galley'de erişilebilir, hız: The fire blanket is kept in an accessible position in the galley where it can be pulled out quickly (usually on a wall near the door). The cook must know where the blanket is and which way to pull it, and must replace it with a new one after use (for single-use types).
Fire detection panel, sistemin merkezi b: The fire detection panel is the central brain of the system: it shows alarm, fault, disablement and test states by LEDs/LCD and provides outputs for alarm sounders, fire flaps and ventilation shutdown relays. The ETO must interpret the panel's alarm (red), fault (yellow) and power (green) indications correctly and identify recurring faults by regularly reviewing the panel event log.
Fire detection sistemi, ana güç kaybında: On loss of main power, the fire detection system must continue to be supplied from an emergency source (the emergency switchboard or a battery inside the panel); the FSS Code typically requires the system to be able to operate for a specified period after loss of the main source (e.g. detector + alarm operation). The ETO monitors the terminal voltage, internal resistance and replacement date of the panel backup batteries; aging batteries give a short duration in the annual test and are replaced.
Fire door ve watertight door kullanımı g: The use of fire doors and watertight doors is demonstrated: why they are kept closed, how they are opened and closed, and how the automatic closing system works in an emergency. It is stressed that holding a fire door open with a chock/wedge is prohibited and dangerous.
Fire door ve watertight door'ların kapan: Closing and locking of the fire doors and watertight doors is tested; the drencher/sprinkler system (vehicle deck) must be ready. Their status is monitored on the indicator panel.
Fire drill'de fire party SCBA donar, hos: In a fire drill, the fire party dons SCBA and runs out hoses, boundary cooling is set up, and the machinery stop/ventilation shut-down procedure is applied. In an abandon ship drill, the lifeboat/liferaft station is prepared, embarkation is explained and the engine is started. In an enclosed space drill, the permit to work, atmosphere testing, rescue and casualty handling are demonstrated.
Fire main hattı, ana ve emergency fire p: The fire main is pressurized by the main and emergency fire pumps; at least two jets of water, not from the same hydrant, must be able to reach any normally accessible part of the ship. The Safety Officer periodically checks the tightness of the hydrant valve glands, the condition of the hoses (couplings, lining, cracks), the function of the nozzles (dual-purpose jet/spray) and the accessibility of the hose boxes.
Fire main, makine dairesindeki yangın po: The fire main is supplied by the fire pumps in the engine room and distributed along the deck to the fire hydrants. There are isolating valves on the main; when a damaged section is isolated, the rest of the main stays pressurised. The main is kept under pressure continuously or ready to be pressurised quickly.
Fire senaryosunda muster list; fire part: In a fire scenario, the muster list defines the fire party leader (usually the Chief Officer or the Safety Officer), the nozzle man, the hose handler, the boundary cooling team, the BA (breathing apparatus) team and the engine room boundary cooling coordinator. The bridge control team manages the ventilation, the fuel valves (quick-closing) and the emergency shut-offs.
Fire, man-overboard (MOB) and abandon-sh: Fire, man-overboard (MOB) and abandon-ship exercises practise assigned duties, muster, communications and correct use of survival equipment. Operate equipment and conduct launches under the applicable safe procedures. Record the debrief and follow up deficiencies.
Fire-tube (alev borulu) kazanda sıcak ga: In a fire-tube boiler the hot gases pass through the tubes and the water is in the shell; it is simple and works at low pressure. In a water-tube boiler the water passes through the tubes and the gases are outside; it gives high pressure and fast steam raising. On many motor ships a composite boiler is heated both by fuel and by the exhaust gas.
Fireman's outfit (koruyucu giysi, eldive: Fireman's outfits (protective clothing, gloves, boots, helmet, lifeline, lamp, axe) and SCBA sets are kept complete and ready; SCBA cylinder pressure and mask seals are checked regularly. EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) locations and expiry dates are tracked. The breathing air compressor is checked for proper operation.
Fireman's outfit; alev geçirmez koruyucu: The fireman's outfit consists of flame-resistant protective clothing, boots/gloves, a helmet, a safety lamp (at least 3 hours), a fire axe and an SCBA. Depending on the type of ship, at least two sets are carried. The Safety Officer checks each set for completeness, the condition of the lamp battery and the soundness of the clothing.
First-stage audible başladıktan 15 saniy: If there is still no reset 15 seconds after the first-stage audible alarm starts, the second-stage remote audible alarm starts at the location of the designated back-up officer and/or the Master.
Fitter'ın ustalığı; ölçü disiplini, doğr: The Fitter's craftsmanship comes down to measurement discipline, choosing the right materials, uncompromising compliance with safety rules and clean workmanship. A well-made gasket change or valve overhaul goes unnoticed; a badly made one shows itself through leaks, breakdowns and even fire. That is why, for the Fitter, "correct and safe" always comes before "fast".
Fitter, atölye düzeyinde elektrik ark ka: At workshop level, the Fitter uses electric arc welding (MMA/stick) for tack welding, joining parts and simple repairs. The right electrode (according to material and position), the right current setting (according to electrode diameter) and a clean surface (free of rust/oil/paint) are the conditions for a good-quality weld. A damp electrode causes porosity; electrodes are kept dry.
Fitter, kullandığı yedek parça ve sarf m: The Fitter updates the stock records of the spare parts and consumables used; the engineer is informed when items such as gasket sheet, O-ring sets, packing, bolts/studs, electrodes and grinding discs are running low. It is important that critical spares (the minimum spare parts required by class) never run out.
Fixed CO2 sistemi MSC.1/Circ.1318'e göre: Under MSC.1/Circ.1318, the fixed CO2 system is subject to annual, two-yearly and ten-yearly maintenance: annual visual and alarm test, two-yearly hose/manifold check, ten-yearly cylinder hydro-test. These services are carried out and certified by an authorized company.
Fixed foam (boiler/oil-fired alanlar) ve: Layered protection is provided by fixed foam (boiler/oil-fired areas) and portable extinguishers (CO2, foam, dry powder). Fire main + emergency fire pump water must always be available at the hydrants and nozzles.
Fixed gas freeing fan ve hat purje düzen: Fixed gas-freeing fans and a line purging arrangement make the tank gas-free after washing.
Fixed smothering system (CO2 veya benzer: Before the fixed smothering system (CO2 or similar) is activated, the ventilation flaps must be closed and the fans stopped; otherwise the extinguishing gas is expelled and the fire cannot be extinguished. The cadet learns the order of these remote controls in the firefighting chain: shut off fuel → stop equipment → close ventilation → count personnel → release the fixed system.
Flag state ve PSC denetiminde kirli kama: In flag State and PSC inspections, a dirty cabin, a moldy shower, a blocked drain, poor ventilation or signs of pests are recorded directly as a deficiency and, in serious cases, can lead to the ship's detention. The steward's work is therefore not "cosmetic"; it is the front line of regulatory compliance.
Flanş montajında cıvatalar çapraz (star: When a flange is assembled, the bolts are tightened in a cross (star pattern) sequence and in torque stages; uneven tightening leads to crushing of the gasket and leaks. The cadet learns why the correct torque value and tightening sequence are important.

When flanges are fitted, the bolts are tightened crosswise (star pattern) in stages of torque; on lines that run hot, the bolts are re-torqued after the line has been in service. The use of asbestos gaskets is prohibited (SOLAS II-1/3-5); when old gaskets containing asbestos are removed, respiratory protection and special disposal are required.
Flanş yüzeyleri eski conta kalıntısından: Flange faces are cleaned completely of old gasket residue, burrs and dirt. The new gasket is fitted dry or with the lubrication recommended by the manufacturer. Bolts are always tightened in a crosswise (star) sequence with the torque applied in stages; applying full torque in one go crushes the gasket and causes leakage. A torque wrench is mandatory on high-pressure/high-temperature joints.
Flanş yüzeyleri paralel ve hizalı olmalı: Flange faces must be parallel and aligned; a flange joined out of alignment strains the bolts and leaks. After the gasket has been fitted, the bolts are torqued in a crosswise sequence. Before being put back into service, a repaired pressure line is hydrostatically tested above its working pressure and its tightness is verified.
Flanşlı kaplin: Şaft segmentlerini birbi: Flanged coupling: connects the shaft sections to each other.
Flap (Becker) dümen: Arka kenarda hareke: Flap (Becker) rudder: has a movable flap on the trailing edge; it improves manoeuvrability at low speed.
Float gauge: şamandıralı mekanik sistem;: Float gauge: a mechanical system with a float; easy to service but of low accuracy.
Flooding/collision senaryosunda watertig: In a flooding/collision scenario, duties are assigned for closing watertight doors, monitoring draft and list, ballast/bilge pumping and preparing damage control materials (cement box, wooden plugs, shoring). The Safety Officer verifies that these duties are rehearsed in drills and that the related equipment is accessible.
Flowmetre kalibrasyonu: Periyodik kalibr: Flow meter calibration: the periodic calibration certificates are checked.
Flue gas scrubber, kazan baca gazını den: The flue gas scrubber cleans SO₂ and soot from the boiler flue gas by washing it with seawater.
Flue gas; scrubber'da soğutulur ve SOx/p: The flue gas is cooled in the scrubber and cleaned of SOx and particulates. The deck water seal is the critical barrier that prevents gas from flowing back from the cargo tanks to the engine room; its water level is monitored continuously. If the deck seal runs dry, there is a risk of backflow and explosion.
Folding (katlanır) kapaklar, panelleri m: Folding covers have panels hinged to each other that fold like an accordion with hydraulic cylinders; they are common on container and general cargo ships. Side-rolling covers are preferred on bulk carriers; the panels roll sideways on wheels and open the hatch completely.
Folding (katlanır) tip: hidrolik silindi: Folding type: the cover panels are opened with hydraulic cylinders and folded at the end of the hatch.
Folding (katlanır), side-rolling (yana k: Folding, side-rolling, piggy-back and pontoon type hatch covers each require a different operating discipline. Before opening/closing, the Bosun confirms that the cleats have been released, the drainage channels are clean, there are no obstructions on the rails and the hydraulic system is ready.
Folio yönetimi, harita \"yeterliliği\" (: Folio management is directly linked to chart "adequacy": in critical areas, the largest-scale (most detailed) up-to-date chart must be used, not the smallest-scale chart. The Second Officer ensures that the chart of the correct scale is available and corrected for each leg of the passage plan.
Folio, geminin ticaret sahasına göre düz: A folio is a group of charts arranged according to the ship's trading area. The Second Officer selects from the folio the charts required for the planned voyage (passage chart, approach chart, harbor chart and suitable scales); if a scale or coverage is missing, a folio renewal request is raised.
Following ve quartering denizlerde dalga: In following and quartering seas, the righting arm temporarily decreases while a wave crest is amidships; there is a risk of broaching and loss of stability. MSC.1/Circ.1228 gives the Master practical guidance on choosing speed/course. The Chief Officer supports the management of these risks operationally through cargo distribution and the choice of GM.
Footprint plot ile gerçek pozisyon-baş d: The footprint plot records the actual spread of position and heading, the thrust used and the environmental trend. If the field performance does not match the model, the limits are reduced, the cause is investigated and action is taken in accordance with the ASOG.
For-cause (reasonable suspicion / for-ca: A for-cause (reasonable suspicion) test is applied when a person's behaviour, speech, smell or performance gives rise to reasonable suspicion. Where possible, the observations giving rise to the suspicion are recorded by two people (the Master and an officer); not a subjective "I don't like it" but concrete signs (unsteady walk, slurred speech, smell of alcohol, bloodshot eyes) are written down. Refusing a for-cause test has the same disciplinary consequence as a positive result under most SMSs.
Forming (oluşum): Tanışma, keşif. Stormi: Forming: Getting acquainted, exploration. Storming: Role clashes. Norming: Agreement, rules. Performing: Productive work.
Forward and aft stations maintain clear: Forward and aft stations maintain clear radio communication with the bridge. Commands such as Send the head line ashore, Heave on the spring, Slack away the breast, Make fast and Let go must identify the intended line and action. Repeat back, act only when understood and report completion. A breast line is not the anchoring report up and down.
Forward, midship ve aft draft'lar her ik: Forward, midship and aft drafts are read on both sides (six readings); in a seaway the wave effect is removed by averaging. The hog/sag correction (quarter mean / mean of means) is applied.
Fosfin hem öldürücü hem patlayıcıdır; at: Phosphine is both lethal and explosive; it is kept away from ignition sources and no one enters the hold without a gas measurement. Entry before ventilation and gas-freeing is prohibited.
Fouling aynı zamanda gemi hızını düşürür: Fouling also reduces the ship's speed and the propeller efficiency.
Fouling direnci (Rf) toplam ısıl dirence: The fouling resistance (Rf) is added to the total thermal resistance.
Fourier yasasına göre birim zamanda ilet: According to Fourier's law, the amount of heat conducted per unit time is directly proportional to the temperature gradient and the area of conduction, and depends on the thermal conductivity of the material.
Frame, silindir bloğu ve bedplate arasın: The frames, the cylinder block and the bedplate form a structure held together under tension by bolts (the tie rod system).
Free surface effect (FSC), kısmen dolu t: The free surface effect (corrected by the free surface correction, FSC) reduces the effective GM in partly filled tanks and holds. On tankers and in ballast operations the number of slack tanks is kept to a minimum. The Master checks that the FSC is entered correctly into the software.
Free-fall filikalarda haftalık kontrol,: For free-fall lifeboats, the weekly inspection includes the visual condition of the simulated launching equipment and of the free-fall system; the interval for an actual free-fall test is different. For a davit-launched liferaft, the davit and release system are also checked.
Free-fall lifeboat: tankers ve bulk için: Free-fall lifeboat: common on tankers and bulk carriers; drops into the water from an inclined ramp.
Freeing port'lar kesinlikle bağlanmaz, t: Freeing ports must never be lashed, blocked or permanently closed; otherwise water shipped on deck cannot drain away and the ship is endangered. The AB greases jammed hinges, reports rusted ones and does not block them with materials. These small flaps are the ship's stability safeguard in bad weather.
Freeing port'lar, gemi bordasındaki ment: Freeing ports are hinged flaps at the ship's side; they allow sea water shipped on deck (green water) to be cleared quickly. Water collecting on the well deck adds weight to the ship and endangers stability through free surface effect; freeing ports prevent this. The AB checks that the freeing port flaps move freely, are not rusted or jammed, and have not been lashed or closed.
Frekans dönüştürücü (VFD), motor hızını: A variable frequency drive (VFD) controls the motor speed by changing the supply frequency. The motor's magnetic flux is maintained by keeping the V/f ratio constant.
Frekans dönüştürücü, motorun gerilim ve: A frequency converter controls the voltage and frequency of the motor, giving smooth acceleration with low current from zero to rated speed. It offers energy savings, precise speed control and soft starting.
Fren %60 MBL'de kaymaya ayarlanır ki aşı: The brake is set to slip at 60% of the MBL, so that under an overload it renders (slips in a controlled way) before the line parts. This protects both the line and the crew: the snap-back of a parting line is lethal.
Fren testi kritiktir: yük kaldırıldığınd: The brake test is critical: when the load has been lifted and the hand chain is released, the load must stay where it is and must not slip. A slipping brake is lethal. A chain block is pulled straight; pulling it at a side angle jams the chain and damages the device.
Fritöz, galley'nin en yüksek yangın ve y: The deep fryer is the item of galley equipment with the highest fire and burn risk. The oil is filtered regularly and changed when it deteriorates (darker color, foaming, lower smoke point); the old oil is put into a separate waste container (disposal is covered in a separate task). The oil level is kept between min and max; an overfilled fryer creates a risk of overflow and fire.
Fumigasyon lisanslı fumigator tarafından: Fumigation is planned by a licensed fumigator; gas levels are monitored in the accommodation and adjacent spaces. Leak checks are made and warning signs are posted.
Fumigasyon sonrası alan, güvenli gaz kon: After fumigation, the area is kept closed until a safe gas concentration has been verified (by measurement) and an authorized "gas-free / safe for entry" approval has been given. The cook follows the fumigation plan on the food/galley side: protects or removes the products, cleans the surfaces afterwards and destroys any uncovered food at risk of contamination.
Fırtına sürerken Birinci Zabit, güvenli: While the storm continues, the Chief Officer monitors the cargo/lashing condition, water ingress and the ship's behavior from safe points (bridge, internal spaces). If slackening lashings, hatch cover leakage or container movement is detected, action is taken only when it is safe and with the Master's approval; any intervention that puts life at risk is avoided.
Fırtınada heave to (rüzgara karşı minimu: In a storm, the decision to heave to (holding head to wind at minimum speed), run before the sea (taking the sea from astern) or alter course is made according to the ship type and the direction of the sea. The Second Officer assesses the minimum steerage way needed to keep steering/propulsion capability, and the risks of slamming/racing.
Fırtınanın ilerleme yönüne göre bir tara: Relative to the storm's direction of travel, one side is the "dangerous semicircle" and the other the "navigable semicircle". In the dangerous semicircle the wind pushes the ship towards the storm track, whereas in the navigable semicircle it pushes the ship away from it. In the Northern Hemisphere, the right-hand side relative to the direction of travel is the dangerous semicircle.
GA ilan edildiğinde, kargo sahiplerinden: When GA is declared, documents securing their contributions are required from the cargo owners: an Average Bond (an undertaking signed by the cargo owner) and an Average Guarantee (a guarantee given by the cargo's insurer), or a cash deposit. Cargo is not delivered until this security is complete, because once the cargo has been delivered it becomes very difficult to collect the contribution. This process often delays delivery and requires careful coordination.
GA'yı ilan etme kararı genelde gemi sahi: The decision to declare GA is generally taken by the shipowner or the company, which appoints an average adjuster; however, the Master is responsible for documenting completely all the details of the event giving rise to GA (jettison, firefighting, salvage). The Master's records (which cargo was sacrificed, when and on what grounds) are the basis of the GA adjustment.
GM değerinin yükleme süresince intact st: The basic principle is that GM must not fall below the intact stability criteria during loading. The IMO 2008 IS Code sets minimum GM values according to ship type (≥0.15 m for general cargo, ≥0.15 m + correction for container ships, and for tankers calculated including the free surface of liquid cargo). Excessive GM, on the other hand, makes a "stiff" ship; short-period, violent rolling overloads the lashing forces and increases the risk of parametric rolling in container stacks.
GM, GZ veya strength değerleri limitlere: When GM, GZ or strength values approach their limits, the Chief Officer has the authority and the responsibility to stop the operation. "Charterer pressure" cannot override stability safety. Every decision to stop and its justification are recorded.
GM, IS Code minimumunun üzerinde ama par: GM is kept above the IS Code minimum but within the optimum range that does not trigger parametric rolling. A very high GM strains the lashings through violent, short-period rolling.
GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safe: The cadet is introduced to the GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) equipment — VHF DSC, MF/HF, EPIRB, SART, NAVTEX. The cadet learns that sending a distress alert by accident (false alert) has serious consequences and does not touch this equipment without authorization, but grasps the logic of GMDSS by observing the flow of alerts and messages.

GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) is regulated by SOLAS Chapter IV and recognises three levels of priority: Distress (MAYDAY — a ship or a person is in grave and imminent danger and needs immediate assistance), Urgency (PAN-PAN — an urgent but not life-threatening situation concerning the safety of a ship or a person, e.g. a serious medical case) and Safety (SECURITE — a navigational or meteorological warning). The Master chooses the level that matches the real seriousness of the situation; a distress alert sent too late is as dangerous as an unnecessary one.
GMDSS Radio Log (Radio Record), zorunlu: The GMDSS Radio Log (Radio Record) is a mandatory ship's document. A summary of distress, urgency and safety communications, the daily/weekly/monthly test results, the reserve battery status, equipment failures and repairs, and the operator signatures (designated operator and Master's approval) are entered in it.
GMDSS dokuz işlevi garanti eder; en krit: The GMDSS guarantees nine functions; the most critical are distress alerting (ship-to-shore, shore-to-ship, ship-to-ship), SAR coordination, on-scene communications, locating (SART), maritime safety information (MSI) and general communications. The aim is that no distress call goes unnoticed.
GMDSS ekipmanı, geminin seyrettiği deniz: The GMDSS equipment is determined by the sea area in which the ship operates. A1: within range of a VHF coast station (about 20–30 miles). A2: within range of an MF coast station (about 100–150 miles). A3: within Inmarsat (GEO satellite) coverage (about 70°N to 70°S). A4: the polar regions (outside Inmarsat coverage; HF required).
GMDSS ekipmanını yetkili operatör (GOC/R: The GMDSS equipment is operated by an authorised operator (holding a GOC/ROC certificate). Periodic tests (daily/weekly/monthly) according to the maintenance method are carried out and a radio log is kept. If a false distress alert is sent, it is cancelled at once.
GMDSS ekipmanının bakım stratejisi deniz: The GMDSS maintenance strategy depends on the sea area: in A3/A4, at least two of the methods "duplication of equipment", "shore-based maintenance" and "at-sea electronic maintenance" are chosen. If at-sea maintenance is chosen, a person holding a GMDSS Radio Electronic/Maintainer certificate (usually the ETO) must be on board.
GMDSS kapsamında EPIRB self-test, SART s: Under GMDSS, the EPIRB self-test, SART self-test, battery and charging checks, DSC test call and radio battery reserve tests are carried out. Depending on the ship's organization, the Safety Officer coordinates these tests with the radio officer or carries them out, and records them in the radio log.
GMDSS radyo kaydı (radio log), distress/: The GMDSS radio log, distress/urgency/safety communications and test records are always kept in UTC and are not affected by clock changes. This is critical so that, in investigations after an accident, the timeline can be built correctly on a single reference axis. The Second Officer or the person responsible for GMDSS ensures that the UTC axis of the radio log runs without interruption, however many times the ship's zone time changes.
GMDSS radyo kayıtları, distress/urgency/: GMDSS radio records, distress/urgency/safety messages, EGC messages and navigational warnings are always time-stamped in UTC. In this way, whatever time zone the ship is in, records can be compared worldwide on a single time axis. Although events in the deck logbook are entered in zone time, it is good seamanship practice to also note the UTC equivalent for critical events.
GMDSS reserve batarya, ana ve acil güç k: As required by SOLAS, the GMDSS reserve battery must supply the GMDSS equipment on loss of main and emergency power (1 hour if there is an emergency generator, otherwise 6 hours). The transitional emergency battery bridges the mandatory loads until the emergency generator comes on line (generally 30 min). The ETO makes sure that these durations are verified by an actual capacity test.
GMDSS reserve source of energy (batarya): Under SOLAS, the GMDSS reserve source of energy (batteries) must supply the GMDSS equipment on loss of main and emergency power for at least 1 hour (if an emergency generator is fitted) or 6 hours (if not). The ETO checks the specific gravity of the GMDSS batteries (vented type), their terminal voltage and the charger output daily/weekly, and carries out the annual discharge test.
GMDSS teçhizatı; ana güç (ship's main),: GMDSS equipment is supplied from three independent sources: main power (ship's main), emergency power (emergency generator) and the reserve source of energy (battery). The reserve battery must have the capacity to run the GMDSS for a set period (1 hour if the emergency source of electrical power fully complies with SOLAS II-1/42 or 43, including the supply to the radio installations; otherwise 6 hours) when the generator has also stopped.
GMDSS teçhizatını işletmek için geçerli: Operating GMDSS equipment requires a valid GMDSS operator certificate (GOC — General Operator's Certificate, or ROC depending on the sea area). The Second Officer must hold this certificate and be fully familiar with the distress traffic procedures (alert, acknowledge, relay).
GMDSS, ana güç kaybında bile çalışmalıdı: The GMDSS must work even when main power is lost; a separate battery (reserve source of energy) therefore supplies the GMDSS equipment for a set time (typically 1–6 hours, depending on the configuration). Availability of the equipment is ensured by duplication or shore-based maintenance.
GMDSS, deniz alanlarına (A1-A4) göre bel: The GMDSS requires specified communication redundancy according to the sea area (A1–A4). The ETO carries out the technical maintenance of VHF DSC (channel 70), MF/HF DSC (2187.5 kHz, etc.) and Inmarsat-C/FleetBroadband terminals. The DSC self-test, transmitter/receiver power output, antenna SWR (standing wave ratio) and the supply battery are checked.
GMDSS, gemi battığı an \"çalışmazsa hiç: GMDSS is a system that "is meaningless if it does not work" at the moment the ship sinks; this is why its value stays invisible as long as it is never used. The Second Officer's task is not only to test the equipment but to make sure that every test proves the real transmission chain, that the power supplies will hold up in a blackout and that the records will be complete at an inspection. Disciplined GMDSS routines are the only guarantee that, at the worst moment, the distress signal actually reaches the other side.
GMDSS, gemiyi tek bir cihaza değil dokuz: GMDSS equips the ship not around a single device but according to nine basic communication functions: ship-to-shore distress alerting, shore-to-ship distress alerting, ship-to-ship distress alerting, SAR coordinating communications, on-scene communications, locating signals (SART/RADAR transponder), broadcast of Maritime Safety Information (MSI), general communications and bridge-to-bridge communications. The Second Officer verifies that the equipment on board provides all of these functions.
GNSS sinyali çok zayıf olduğundan karışt: Because the GNSS signal is very weak, it is open to jamming (drowning the signal) and spoofing (a false signal giving a wrong position). In certain areas, loss of GPS or a sudden jump in position may be a sign of spoofing; independent positioning (radar fix, terrestrial methods, dual GNSS) is then used.
GNSS'li beacon encoded position gönderir: A beacon with GNSS sends an encoded position; the actual accuracy and update rate depend on the beacon's type approval, the antenna's view of the sky and the GNSS fix status. Without GNSS, the independent Cospas-Sarsat location solution may be slower and less accurate.
GNSS, heading, speed, depth, AIS, rudder: GNSS, heading, speed, depth, AIS, rudder, engine/propulsion orders and responses, alarms and other required sources; the scope depends on the installation date and performance standard.
GOV, ortalama sıcaklık ve density ile AS: Using the average temperature and density and the ASTM/API tables (e.g. 54B/6B), the GOV is converted to gross standard volume (GSV) and to weight (in vacuum/in air). This value is the basis of the B/L and the cargo measurement report.
GPS alıcısı, en az dört uydudan gelen si: A GPS receiver measures the travel time of signals from at least four satellites. Trilateration is done with the known position of each satellite and the range calculated from the signal time (pseudorange); three satellites give the position and the fourth resolves the receiver clock error. As the signal travels at the speed of light, timing at the nanosecond level is needed.
GPS, en az 4 uydudan gelen sinyal ile al: GPS calculates the receiver's position and time from the signals of at least 4 satellites. Each satellite broadcasts its own position and the time the signal was sent. The receiver calculates the range from the time the signal takes to arrive.
GPS, gyro, log, echo sounder ve anemomet: Sensors such as the GPS, gyro, log, echo sounder and anemometer supply data to consumers such as the radar, ECDIS and AIS via NMEA 0183 (serial) or NMEA 2000 / IEC 61162-450 (Ethernet). The ETO must know the topology of this data network, its distribution units and which devices each sensor feeds; a single sensor failure can affect many devices.
