GPS/GNSS alıcısı, konum ve zaman kaynağı: The GPS/GNSS receiver is the source of position and time; the ETO checks the antenna connector, cable losses and receiver health. Because of the risk of GNSS jamming/spoofing, a backup position source (second receiver, eLoran where available) and dead reckoning backup using gyro + log have become important. The antenna must be sited so that it is not shadowed and not affected by other antennas.
GRB en az iki yıl gemide saklanır. PSC,: The GRB is kept on board for at least two years. PSC looks for consistency between the GRB, the actual generation of garbage and the delivery receipts; any inconsistency raises suspicion of a deliberate violation.
Gain, boş alanda hafif speckle görülecek: The gain is checked manually by turning it back slightly from the level at which a light speckle appears in an empty area. Sea clutter suppresses wave echoes close to the ship; rain clutter suppresses precipitation cells. The controls are kept at the lowest level necessary and re-checked on different ranges to make sure small targets have not disappeared.
Galley ekipmanı bakımının temeli, arızay: The basis of galley equipment maintenance is preventing failures, not waiting for them. The cook puts the periodic maintenance steps specified in each item's manufacturer's manual (cleaning, seal checks, filter replacement, lubrication, calibration) on a schedule. Regular preventive maintenance reduces the likelihood of sudden breakdowns, pressure on spare parts and food safety risks all together.
Galley havalandırması yangını besleyen o: Galley ventilation is critically important in a fire because it carries the oxygen that feeds the fire as well as the grease in the duct. Fire dampers are fitted in the galley exhaust duct and in the supply air; in a fire, these are closed to stop flames/smoke spreading along the duct and to cut off the oxygen supply. The cook must know the manual closing points for the dampers and how to stop the hood fan.
Galley iş kazaları açısından geminin en: The galley is one of the riskiest areas of the ship for occupational accidents: hot surfaces, boiling liquids, hot oil and sharp tools all come together. Hot pans are carried with gloves, boiling water is poured off carefully, and water is never poured onto hot oil. The floor is not left wet/greasy; non-slip shoes are worn.
Galley nemli ve ıslak bir ortamdır; su i: The galley is a humid, wet environment; water and electricity together are one of the most lethal risks. Damage to cables, plugs and sockets (wear, water ingress) is reported immediately and damaged equipment is not used. Equipment is not operated with wet hands; earthing and residual current protection (RCD) are the basis of equipment safety, and these are under the supervision of the engine/electrical team.
Galley temizliği bir programa bağlanır:: Galley cleaning follows a schedule: daily (worktops, range top, floor, garbage, sinks), weekly (oven interior, fryer oil, hood filter, chiller interior) and periodic (deep cleaning, degreasing the hood duct, emptying and cleaning the stores completely). The "clean as you go" principle minimizes the build-up of dirt and the attraction of pests.
Galley ve depolar, MLC 2006 müfettişi, l: The galley and stores are inspected by the MLC 2006 inspector, Port State Control (PSC) and the port health authority. Cleaning records, temperature logs, pest control records and the Ship Sanitation Control Exemption Certificate are presented during the inspection. A well-organized, documented system reduces an inspection to a routine verification.
Galley yangınında müdahale sırası nettir: In a galley fire, the response sequence is clear: 1) cut off the heat source (switch off the range/fryer/gas), 2) if the fire is small and controllable, tackle it immediately with a suitable extinguisher/fire blanket, 3) raise the alarm (fire alarm button/bridge), 4) if it grows or gets out of control, trigger the suppression system, stop the fan, close the dampers and evacuate the galley. Life always comes before equipment; with a fire that cannot be controlled, the rule is not to fight it but to get out and leave it to an organized team response.
Galley'de aşçı pişirmeden, kamarot ise t: In the galley, the cook is responsible for cooking, and the steward for cleaning, dishwashing and preparation support; this division of work determines the flow of service. On the cook's instructions, the steward draws ingredients from the stores, does simple preparation (washing/chopping vegetables, weighing ingredients) and takes on all the dishwashing and cleaning after service. Good coordination allows two people to work efficiently in a small galley.
Galley'de pişirme yağı yangını için Clas: A Class F (K) wet chemical portable extinguisher is kept in the galley for cooking oil fires, and the cook knows where it is. In addition, a CO2 extinguisher for electrical fires is kept at a suitable position (on an oil fire, CO2 may be insufficient or may scatter the burning oil). The cook knows which fire each extinguisher is suitable for and the PASS technique (Pull-Aim-Squeeze-Sweep).
Galley'de yağ/fritöz yangınına asla su i: In the galley, water is never used on a cooking oil/deep-fryer fire; water makes the hot oil erupt, spreading the fire and causing serious burns. In a cooking oil fire, the heat source is cut off, a fire blanket or an extinguisher of the appropriate class is used (a special extinguisher is usually provided in the galley) and the alarm is raised immediately.
Galley, SOLAS II-2 kapsamında yangın alg: Under SOLAS II-2, the galley is connected to the fire detection system; heat/smoke detectors raise an alarm on the bridge. The cook ensures proper ventilation so that these detectors do not give false alarms from cooking fumes, but never switches off or covers the detectors. Early detection is the key to extinguishing a small fire before it grows.
Galley, geminin en yüksek gıda riski taş: The galley is the area of the ship with the highest food risk; hot surfaces, sharp tools, boiling liquids and the risk of pathogens all come together there. In this environment, the steward constantly maintains both hygiene and occupational safety discipline.
Galley, kabin, public space ve makine da: Fire scenarios in the galley, cabins, public spaces and engine room are practised; fire team response, closing of fire doors, sprinklers and passenger guidance are drilled.
Gangway altına ve yanına düşmeyi önleyen: A safety net is rigged under and beside the gangway to prevent falls; the net must be wide enough to cover the gap between the quay and the ship and must be securely fastened. It must not be forgotten that the angle will change with the tide; the gangway is checked and adjusted periodically. An excessively steep or flat angle increases the risk of falling.
Gangway ve shell door hidroliği, fren ve: The gangway and shell door hydraulics, brakes and locking systems are maintained; the SWL and the safety nets and railings are checked. A safe condition for passenger use is verified.
Gangway, ladder ve pilot transfer noktas: The gangway, ladder and pilot transfer point must be adequately lit at night; however, the lights are positioned so that they do not dazzle the pilot or other persons. When the pilot ladder area is illuminated, the ladder and the water surface must be visible, with no shadows. Backup lighting (portable lamp) is kept ready.
Gangway, vinç/davit ile kaldırılıp rıhtı: The gangway is lifted with a crane/davit and landed on the quay/pier at a suitable angle. The AB checks that the lower end of the gangway sits firmly on the quay and will not slip, that the wheels/support leg work properly and that the gangway can move freely (without jamming) as the tide and draft change. The guardrail ropes/chains on both sides must be taut.
Gangway, yolcu yaralanmalarının sık yaşa: The gangway is a frequent point of passenger injuries; maintenance and safety are important.
Gantry (portal) vinçler: Konteyner gemil: Gantry cranes: travel on rails fitted on container ships. SWL 30–50 tonnes.
Gantry crane (portal vinç): Konteyner ge: Gantry crane: a crane that travels over the hatch covers on container ships. It gives high speed and precise positioning.
Gantry crane: konteyner gemilerinde rays: Gantry crane: travels on rails on container ships.
Garanti edilen mesai dışındaki çalışma (: Work outside the guaranteed hours (overtime) is recorded and paid according to the contract/CBA. The Second Engineer makes sure that overtime is distributed fairly and does not breach the rest-hour rule. Excessive overtime is both a fatigue problem and a morale problem; if it has a structural cause (insufficient manning), it is escalated to the company through the Chief Engineer.
Garbage Management Plan 100 GT ve üzeri: A Garbage Management Plan is required on ships of 100 GT and above and on ships certified to carry 15 or more persons; a Garbage Record Book on ships of 400 GT and above and on ships certified to carry 15 or more persons. The Master checks that the GRB entries reflect every discharge, incineration and delivery ashore (with the reception facility receipt) completely.
Garbage Record Book (GRB) Part I (gemi a: Garbage Record Book (GRB) Part I (ship-generated garbage) and Part II (cargo residues) record every discharge/incineration/delivery operation with the date, position, quantity (m³) and category. The Chief Officer is responsible for keeping the records accurate and complete. The receipt obtained on delivery to a shore reception facility (garbage disposal receipt) is kept and cross-checked against the GRB.
Garbage Record Book (GRB), her atık işle: The Garbage Record Book (GRB) is the official document in which every garbage operation (discharge to sea, incineration, delivery to a reception facility) is recorded with its category, quantity, date, time and the ship's position. The record is usually kept by the responsible officer; the cook supports it by providing accurate information on the quantities and deliveries of galley-generated food waste and oil. An incorrect or incomplete GRB entry is a serious nonconformity that can lead to heavy penalties (especially in the USA).
Garbage Record Book, MARPOL Annex V kaps: The Garbage Record Book keeps records of discharges, incineration and delivery to port reception facilities by garbage category (A–K) under MARPOL Annex V. The Ballast Water Record Book records ballast uptake and discharge, treatment and exchange operations under the BWM Convention. Both books are open to inspection, and gaps in them are a reason for a deficiency.
Garbage Record Book, her atık işlemini k: The Garbage Record Book records every garbage operation: Part I records ship-generated garbage (discharge, incineration, delivery ashore) and Part II records cargo residues. Each entry includes the date, time, ship's position, garbage category, estimated amount (m³) and type of operation (discharge into the sea/incineration/delivery). The responsible officer signs each entry; the Master approves the pages. The Chief Officer is responsible for the accuracy of the records.
Gas free certificate alınmadan tanka gir: No one enters a tank without a gas-free certificate. The enclosed space entry permit includes continuous gas monitoring, a standby person, communications, a rescue plan and continued ventilation. Enclosed space entry and rescue drills are held regularly under SOLAS III/19.
Gasket (conta), flanşlar arasındaki sızd: The gasket provides the seal between flanges. The correct material (suitable for the fluid and temperature), the correct thickness and correct cutting are critical. The cadet learns to cut a gasket from gasket sheet using the flange as a template, to position the bolt holes correctly and to cut the inner diameter so that it does not obstruct the flow.
Gasket malzemesi akışkan, sıcaklık ve ba: Gasket material is selected according to the fluid, temperature and pressure: CNAF (fiber) for water/oil, spiral-wound or graphite for steam/high temperature, and an oil-resistant type for fuel. The wrong gasket material creates a risk of leakage, fire (fuel/oil) or steam burns.
Gate, globe, butterfly, check (non-retur: Gate, globe, butterfly, check (non-return) and ball valves have different functions: gate valves for fully open/closed isolation, globe valves for flow control, check valves for one-way flow and butterfly valves for quick isolation. The cadet learns which valve is used where and why their maintenance differs.
Gaz dedektörleri düzenli kalibrasyon ve: Gas detectors require regular calibration and a daily bump test (a quick response check with a known gas); otherwise a false "safe" reading can be fatal. Before use, the AB checks the instrument's charge, calibration date and function. SOLAS XI-1/7 requires ships to carry an appropriate atmosphere testing instrument.
Gece gözcülüğünde köprüüstü aydınlatması: For the lookout at night, the bridge lighting is dimmed (red night lighting) and the eyes adapt to the darkness; this adaptation takes about 20-30 minutes. Exposure to white light spoils the adaptation, so controlling bright screens and lighting on the night watch is a direct part of keeping a lookout.
Gece lookout'ta karanlığa adaptasyon (da: On a night lookout, dark adaptation takes 20-30 minutes; this is why bridge lighting is dimmed, white light is not used and red lighting is preferred. Even a phone/tablet screen or the glow of a cigarette spoils night vision. The AB picks out faint lights better by looking slightly to one side (off-center vision) rather than directly at the horizon, because the peripheral part of the eye is more sensitive in low light.
Gece talimatları imzalı bir defterde vey: Night orders are kept in a signed book or in a digital system; the engineer officer of the watch signs to confirm having read them. This record both documents the communication and is evidence of departmental discipline during inspections (vetting/PSC).
Gece talimatları, Engine Resource Manage: Night orders are part of the Engine Resource Management philosophy: effective use of resources (people, equipment, information) and clear communication. While using his or her authority, the Chief Engineer involves the team in decision-making and supports a "speak up" culture.
Gece talimatı, rounds sıklığını ve özell: The night order specifies the frequency of rounds and the points requiring particular attention. The Chief Engineer stresses that UMS means not "nobody there" but "monitored remotely, with a response ready".
Gece talimatı, vardiya zabitinin hangi k: The night order clarifies which decisions the engineer officer of the watch may take alone: routinely starting a standby pump, minor adjustments, normal transfers. The Chief Engineer calibrates this authority to the officer's level of experience.
Gece talimatının en kritik bölümü, Baş M: The most critical part of the night order is a clear definition of the situations in which the Chief Engineer is to be woken. These criteria must leave no room for hesitation: safety/pollution risk, a critical alarm, an unexpected parameter, any doubt.
Gece vardiyasında purifier diferansiyel: On the night watch a purifier differential pressure alarm was considered "temporary" and deferred, and the settling tank water drain check was skipped on the same watch. The next day the fuel viscosity fell below the target range, and irregular injection and an imbalance in the exhaust temperature distribution were seen.
Gece vardiyasında tank sounding, yakıt/y: During the night watch, tasks such as tank sounding, fuel/oil transfers, separator cleaning, monitoring FW production and generator changeover are planned. The Chief Engineer specifies in the orders in what order and with what care these are to be done.
Gece veya kötü görüş koşulunda istasyon: At night or in poor visibility, station lighting must be adequate but directed so that it does not spoil the view from the bridge. The AB keeps their radio and whistle at hand; hand signals can also be used in a noisy environment.
Gece, makine dairesinin en kırılgan zama: Night is the most vulnerable time in the engine room: the team is smaller, fatigue increases and an error may be noticed late. Through night orders, the Chief Engineer clearly tells the engineer officer of the watch what to pay attention to that night, which risks to expect and what his or her limits are.
Geleneksel düzende makine dairesi 7/24 v: In the conventional arrangement, the engine room is manned 24/7 on watches: typically a watchkeeping engineer and an oiler are on duty in 4-on/8-off periods. On ships approved for UMS (Unattended Machinery Space), the engine room may be left unmanned at night; in that case a comprehensive alarm system, the dead-man alarm and the duty engineer call system come into operation. The Second Engineer decides which arrangement is to be applied according to the voyage profile and class approval.
Geleneksel kronometre, UTC'ye göre bir h: A traditional chronometer has an error relative to UTC (chronometer error), and this error changes regularly from day to day (daily rate). The Second Officer measures the error by comparison with a time signal (radio time signal/GPS UTC), records it in the chronometer journal and monitors that the daily rate is stable. A sudden change in rate is a sign of a problem with the chronometer.
Geleneksel kural; tehlikeli yarımdaysanı: The traditional rule is: if you are in the dangerous semicircle, keep the wind on the starboard bow (in the Northern Hemisphere) and move away from the center; if you are in the navigable semicircle, bring the wind on the quarter and pass through quickly. The aim is always to stay as far as possible from the center and from the forecast track.
Geleneksel motorlarda yakıt pompası ve e: In conventional engines the fuel pumps and exhaust valves are driven by the camshaft. In modern electronically controlled engines (MAN ME, WinGD RT-flex), a high-pressure common rail fuel system and hydraulic servo optimise injection timing and valve movement for each load and speed; the camshaft is eliminated.
Geleneksel radarlarda magnetron, mikroda: In conventional radars, the magnetron is the tube that generates the microwave power, and it weakens over time; the ETO monitors transmitter/receiver performance and magnetron health with the performance monitor (echo box). Typical magnetron life is 3000–8000 hours; weakening reduces the detection of distant targets. Modern solid-state (SSPA) radars have no magnetron, but the power module and cooling are monitored.
Geleneksel tankerlerde pompa dairesinde: Conventional tankers have centrifugal cargo pumps in a pump room, driven by a shaft from the engine room or by a steam turbine. On modern product and chemical tankers each tank has its own deepwell or hydraulically driven (e.g. Framo) pump in the tank bottom; segregation and efficiency are better and the pump room is eliminated.
Geleneksel ticari gemilerde ana üretim 4: On conventional merchant ships, main generation is a 440 V or 690 V, 60 Hz three-phase system; 380 V / 50 Hz is found on some ships of European origin. Distribution is staged: 440 V goes from the main switchboard to large consumers (pumps, fans, cranes) and is stepped down through transformers to 230 V / 220 V for lighting and socket circuits. On modern large ships, 6.6 kV or 11 kV HV generation and electric propulsion (diesel-electric) are common.
Gelişmiş ülkeler 2036'ya kadar %85, geli: Developed countries are targeting an 85% reduction by 2036, and developing countries, depending on their group, an 80% reduction by 2045 or an 85% reduction by 2047.
Gemi PMS veritabanı ile şirket (office): The ship's PMS database and the company (office) database are synchronized regularly (replication). The Chief Engineer checks that synchronization has succeeded and that no jobs are missing; a break in synchronization leads to the superintendent in the office seeing incomplete data and making wrong decisions. In the job completion record, actual hours, spare parts consumption (ROB update) and the "remarks" field are filled in completely.
Gemi Planlı Bakım Sistemi (PMS) yazılımı: The ship's Planned Maintenance System (PMS) software (AMOS, TM Master, ShipManager, etc.) manages the spare parts linked to each item of equipment, the stock levels and the order status. The ETO updates the stock when a part is used; when the reorder point is reached, the system creates a requisition. Correct, up-to-date records ensure that the stock on record agrees with the physical count.
Gemi XTD limitini aşarsa veya UKC marjı: If the ship exceeds the XTD limit or the UKC margin is threatened, the officer immediately makes a corrective maneuver and, if necessary, calls the Master. If changes in weather, traffic or draft make the plan invalid, the plan is formally updated and approved again.
Gemi aşçısının başarısı, fark edilmediği: The success of a ship's cook comes from a system that works best when it goes unnoticed: meals that are on time, balanced, safe and suited to the crew's taste. A well-planned menu cycle, disciplined preparation and the ability to adapt flexibly are the quiet but decisive foundation of crew health and morale on long voyages.
Gemi batıya doğru seyrederken boylam aza: When the ship is steaming west, longitude decreases (towards W), and zone time must be put back by one hour for every 15° crossed (retard / put clocks back). In this case the ship "gains time": the day has 25 hours instead of 24. Westbound voyages are easier in terms of rest hours, because an extra hour is created.
Gemi doğuya doğru seyrederken boylam art: When the ship is steaming east, longitude increases (towards E), and zone time must be advanced by one hour for every 15° crossed (advance / put clocks forward). In this case the ship "loses time": the day has 23 hours instead of 24, and the time available to the crew that day is one hour shorter. For this reason, rest-hour planning is more delicate on eastbound voyages.
Gemi elektriği, dört zamanlı orta devirl: The ship's electrical power is supplied by four-stroke, medium-speed diesel generators. The cadet learns the logic of parallel operation of generators, load sharing, synchronization and preferential trip (disconnecting low-priority consumers on overload).
Gemi hareketinin (roll/pitch) yükü dinam: It is often forgotten that the ship's motion (roll/pitch) increases the load dynamically; a static SWL calculation may be inadequate when the ship is rolling. The Oiler leaves a safety margin, allowing for the sea state.
Gemi içinde kullanılan tüm pestisit/biyo: All pesticides/biocides used on board are applied in accordance with the label and the safety data sheet (SDS), away from food areas and with suitable PPE. Food preparation surfaces, stores and water systems are protected from the chemicals. The cook makes sure there is no cross-contact between food and pesticides; a product suspected of having been in contact is not consumed. The chemical and the method used are recorded.
Gemi jeneratörleri genellikle 440V veya: Ships' generators usually produce 440 V or 6600 V at 60 Hz (or 50 Hz). Four-pole generators run at 1800 rpm (60 Hz) or 1500 rpm (50 Hz).
Gemi kabloları IEC 60092 serisine göre ü: Ship cables are made to the IEC 60092 series. Flame retardance (IEC 60332), low smoke emission (IEC 61034) and freedom from halogens (IEC 60754) are the basic requirements.
Gemi kumanyası dört ana kategoride yönet: Ship's provisions are managed in four main categories: dry stores (flour, rice, pasta, canned food, spices), chilled food (milk, cheese, fresh meat, vegetables/fruit), frozen food (meat, fish, frozen vegetables) and beverages/basic supplies. Each category is kept in a different store, at a different temperature, and has a different shelf life. The cook keeps a separate stock record for each category.
Gemi makine dairesinde duplex (çift koll: The engine room has duplex (twin, allowing uninterrupted changeover), simplex (single), automatic backwash (auto-backwash), self-cleaning and magnetic filters. Duplex filters are standard on the main fuel/oil lines; while one side is being cleaned, the other remains in service and the engine does not stop.
Gemi makine dairesinde karşılaşılan başl: The main sources of irreversibility met in a ship's engine room are friction (bearings, piston and cylinder), heat transfer across a finite temperature difference (heat exchangers), mixing (fuel and air), throttling (valves) and electrical resistance.
Gemi makine dairesinde kullanılan temasl: Contact temperature sensors used in a ship's engine room (thermocouples, RTDs) work on the basis of this principle.
Gemi makine dairesinde tamamen correctiv: A system relying entirely on corrective maintenance is not acceptable in a ship's engine room. However, corrective maintenance is a component of every maintenance plan, together with the other strategies.
Gemi motorlarında çalışma gazı genellikl: Because the working gas in ship engines is generally at high temperature, the ideal gas assumption gives sufficient accuracy for engineering calculations.
Gemi mutfağı karadaki mutfaktan farklı o: Unlike a kitchen ashore, a ship's galley is constantly moving; when the ship rolls and pitches, heavy pots, hot oil and knives become hazards. The cook uses fiddles/rails (edging) on the range top, pot clamps and non-slip mats; lips (raised edges) on shelves and latched cupboard doors are mandatory. In heavy weather, use of the deep fryer and boiling large quantities of water are restricted.
Gemi mutfağında başlıca CCP'ler; soğuk z: The main CCPs in a ship's galley are the cold chain (storage temperature), core cooking temperature, hot/cold holding and reheating. The cook applies measurable limits at these points (e.g. chicken core temperature ≥75°C) and keeps daily records. The records are evidence both for verification and for inspections (PSC, flag, charterer inspection).
Gemi mutfağında yazılı bir temizlik prog: The ship's galley has a written cleaning schedule defining which area is to be cleaned, how often, with which chemical and by whom. Daily tasks (worktops, floor), weekly tasks (oven interior, hood filter, cupboard interiors) and periodic tasks (deep cleaning) are listed separately. Completed tasks are verified by a signed record; this record is presented during inspections.
Gemi ofisi (ship's office) ve kaptan/zab: When the ship's office and the Master's/officers' working areas are cleaned, documents and equipment are not touched; only surfaces and the floor are cleaned. Alleyways and stairways are critical for both hygiene and safety: a wet-mopped floor creates a slipping hazard, so a "wet floor" sign is put out and, where possible, half the width is left dry to allow passage.
Gemi otomasyon sistemlerinde kapalı döng: Closed-loop control is standard in ship automation systems.
Gemi provizyon soğutma sisteminde kompre: In a ship's provision refrigeration system, monitoring the compressor power is the basic indicator for catching a deterioration in the COP trend early.
Gemi revin ile ilk müdahale yapılır; ger: First aid is given in the ship's hospital; if necessary, TMAS (telemedical advice) is obtained and a medevac (by helicopter or tender) is planned. The transfer of the patient is coordinated safely.
Gemi router'ı; operasyonel trafiği (köpr: The ship's router separates operational traffic (bridge, engine, company) from crew internet and prioritizes the limited satellite bandwidth with QoS (Quality of Service). The ETO ensures that critical operational traffic (reporting, navigation data, e-mail) is given priority over crew traffic and that bandwidth quotas are applied.
Gemi rıhtımdan ayrılmadan rampa/bow door: Before the ship leaves the berth, it is verified both physically and on the indicators that the ramp and bow door are closed and locked; going to sea with a door open or partly closed creates a risk of water ingress and rapid capsizing.
Gemi sağlık prosedürleri, mürettebatı ve: Ship health procedures are an invisible shield that protects the crew and the communities visited from communicable diseases. The Master's up-to-date documents, transparent declarations and sound sanitation discipline ensure both legal compliance and real public health safety.
Gemi soğutma sistemlerinde özellikle bal: It is becoming common in ship refrigeration systems, especially on fishing vessels and in the reefer systems of container ships. It is neither toxic nor flammable.
Gemi tank ölçümleri ile BDN miktarı aras: If the difference between the ship's tank measurements and the BDN quantity exceeds 0.5%, a dispute is raised. A note of protest is added to the BDN ("received under protest").
Gemi tarafında bakım; soket/kablo bütünl: Maintenance on the ship's side covers the integrity of sockets and cables, testing of circuit breakers and earthing, the monitoring system and the power distribution boards. Maintenance of the refrigeration inside the unit is usually done by a shore service; on board, faults are diagnosed and recorded.
Gemi tehlikedeyse (oturmuş, yangın, maki: If the ship is in danger (aground, on fire, drifting with an engine failure) and outside salvage assistance is needed, the most common contract is Lloyd's Open Form (LOF). LOF is based on the "no cure – no pay" principle: if the salvor succeeds, it receives an award; if it fails, nothing is paid. The great advantage of LOF is that it can be signed quickly at a moment of danger without lengthy price negotiations; the amount of the award is determined afterwards by Lloyd's arbitration.
Gemi terk edilirken SART filikaya/sala a: When abandoning ship, the SART is taken into the lifeboat or liferaft and activated; it is held as high as possible. An activated SART helps SAR units find the survival craft by radar and AIS. The SART is kept on the bridge in an easily accessible, portable position.
Gemi test kiti temel parametreleri verir: The ship's test kit gives the basic parameters; for a comprehensive analysis, samples are periodically sent to a shore-side laboratory. The lab report verifies the shipboard tests and reveals more subtle problems (e.g. microbiological ones).
Gemi uygulamaları: Jeneratör statik uyar: Ship applications: generator static excitation systems, DC motor speed control, controlled rectifier circuits.
Gemi uygulamaları: kazan doğal sirkülasy: Ship applications: natural circulation in boilers, accommodation radiators, tank heating coils.
Gemi uygulamaları: merkezi soğutma suyu: Ship applications: the central cooling water system, air-conditioning fan-coil units, oil and fuel heaters.
Gemi yalpa/baş-kıç vururken kayma riski: When the ship is rolling/pitching, the risk of slipping multiplies; in bad weather the Wiper gives cleaning priority to the walkways and works on the principle of "one hand always on a handhold". A wet/oily floor may be marked with a warning sign, but the real solution is to dry the floor quickly.
Gemi yaşamı boyunca çok katmanlı denetim: Throughout its life, a ship is subject to several layers of inspection: flag State and class certification surveys, PSC (port State control), vetting (SIRE 2.0 for tankers, RightShip for bulk carriers), ISM internal and external audits, and charterer inspections. The Chief Officer prepares for all of these as regards deck equipment, safety systems and documentation.
Gemi çalışanı, vardiya temposu ve fiziks: Because of the watchkeeping routine and the energy demand of physical work, seafarers need a balanced macronutrient intake. The general target is to distribute daily energy so that about 50-55% comes from carbohydrates, 15-20% from protein and 25-30% from lipids. The cook builds this balance in practice by adding to each meal one quality protein (meat, fish, eggs, pulses), one complex carbohydrate (rice, pasta, potatoes, wholegrain bread) and colorful vegetables.

Because of the watchkeeping routine and the energy demand of physical work, seafarers need regular, balanced and timely meals. Stable blood sugar and sufficient energy mean alertness on the bridge, quick reflexes in the engine room and strength on deck. A crew member who works hungry, on an unbalanced diet or after a heavy meal loses concentration; at sea this is a direct safety risk.
Gemi çalışanının enerji ihtiyacı, vardiy: Seafarers' energy needs are high because of the watchkeeping routine and physical work. The general target is to distribute daily energy so that about 50-55% comes from carbohydrates, 15-20% from protein and 25-30% from lipids. The cook builds this balance in practice by adding to each main meal one quality protein (meat, fish, eggs, pulses), one complex carbohydrate (rice, pasta, potatoes, whole grains) and colorful vegetables.
Gemi çamaşırhanesi (ship's laundry) tipi: The ship's laundry typically contains industrial or semi-industrial washing machines, a tumble dryer, an iron/ironing board, laundry trolleys and a bag system that keeps dirty and clean laundry apart. The steward sets up a one-way workflow: "dirty in → sorting → washing → drying → folding/ironing → clean out". The paths of dirty and clean laundry never cross; this is the basic principle for preventing cross-contamination.
Gemi şebekeleri genelde izole (IT) siste: Ship networks are generally insulated (IT) systems; the first earth fault does not stop operation, but a second fault turns into a short circuit. The ETO takes insulation monitoring device (IMD) alarms seriously and isolates the faulty circuit by branch-by-branch testing. Regular megger measurements catch gradual insulation deterioration early.
Gemi şebekeleri genellikle izole (IT) to: Ship networks are usually insulated (IT) systems: the neutral is not connected to earth. This allows operation to continue after a first earth fault (continuity advantage), but a second fault becomes a phase-to-phase short circuit. The ETO detects the first fault with the insulation monitoring device (IMD) and clears it before a second fault occurs.
Gemi, kalabalık ve kapalı bir ortamdır;: A ship is a crowded, closed environment; an infection can spread quickly and is difficult to manage with limited medical facilities. By maintaining hygiene, the steward prevents illness at the outset. Clean accommodation is critical for health, morale and inspections alike.
Gemi, reefer alanlarında standart 440V/3: The ship provides standard 440 V three-phase sockets (reefer plugs) in the reefer areas. The total number of reefers determines the ship's reefer power capacity (kVA), and the generator load is planned accordingly. The sockets must be water- and corrosion-resistant, earthed and protected by circuit breakers.
Gemi-içi testler laboratuvarın yerini tu: On-board tests do not replace the laboratory but provide early warning and confirmation. The Chief Engineer uses the two as complementary tools.
Gemi-kıyı arasında potansiyel farkı ve s: To prevent a potential difference and static sparks between ship and shore, the use of a bonding cable and/or an insulating flange is arranged in accordance with ISGOTT. Most modern terminals prefer an insulating flange; a wrongly applied bonding cable can cause problems with cathodic protection currents.
Gemi; klas sörveyleri, bayrak devleti de: The ship is subject to various inspections, such as class surveys, flag State inspections, PSC and vetting. Each examines LSA/FFE compliance to a different depth. The Third Officer ensures that, as far as safety equipment is concerned, the ship is always ready for inspection.
Gemide TRB sürecinden sorumlu kişi genel: The person on board responsible for the TRB process is usually the Chief Engineer or a senior engineer designated by the Chief Engineer (training officer). The trainer reads the cadet's entries, verifies that the task was actually done and performed to an appropriate standard, requests corrections if necessary and signs the entries found satisfactory.
Gemide UPS'ler kritik tüketicilere kesin: On board, UPS units supply uninterrupted, clean power to critical consumers: ECDIS, radar, the GMDSS console, automation/IAS servers, cargo control and the VDR. An online (double-conversion) UPS feeds the load continuously through the inverter and carries on without any changeover when the mains supply fails; a line-interactive UPS, which has a short changeover time, is used in simpler applications.
Gemide bakım; kapsül/cradle bütünlüğü, H: Maintenance on board covers the integrity of the canister and cradle, correct fitting of the HRU and weak link, the painter attachment, the last service and HRU dates, and the lashing. Internal servicing is carried out only at an approved station.
Gemide bataryalar farklı görevlere hizme: Batteries on board serve different purposes: GMDSS reserve (communications), emergency/transitional (bridging emergency power), engine start (generator/lifeboat), UPS (critical IT/navigation) and, increasingly, energy storage for hybrid/electric propulsion. The choice of chemistry depends on the purpose: lead-acid (high current, economical), Ni-Cd (wide temperature range, robust), Li-ion (high energy density).
Gemide disiplin, can ve mal emniyetinin: Discipline on board is the foundation of the safety of life and property. The Chief Officer clearly sets out the standard of conduct within the department; PPE use, the drug & alcohol policy, compliance with work permits and respect for the hierarchy are non-negotiable rules. In the event of a violation, the progressive disciplinary process defined in the company SMS (verbal warning → written warning → formal report) is applied.
Gemide disiplin, keyfi değil belgeli ve: Discipline on board follows a documented and fair process, not an arbitrary one. The Master applies warnings, records, the sanctions defined in the SEA/CBA and, in serious cases, repatriation or termination procedures in proportion. The seafarer's right of defence, a written record of the process and witness statements are important. Excessive or arbitrary discipline is both a violation of the MLC and a source of later employment law claims.
Gemide ekipman bakımı genellikle ISM Cod: On board, equipment maintenance is usually defined within the Planned Maintenance System (PMS) under the ISM Code. The cook enters the maintenance tasks for galley equipment in the PMS or coordinates them with the engine department; jobs requiring electrical/mechanical work are left to authorized personnel (electrician, engineer officer).
Gemide globe, gate, butterfly, check (no: On board there are various types of valve, such as globe, gate, butterfly, check (non-return), safety/relief and quick-closing valves. Before an overhaul, the valve is isolated and the system depressurized. The Fitter removes the bonnet by loosening its bolts gradually (crosswise), takes out the internal parts (disc, seat, spindle, gland packing) and inspects them for wear, gouging and erosion.
Gemide gövde (hull), referans toprak gör: On board, the hull serves as the reference earth; all metal equipment enclosures are bonded with protective earthing (PE). This limits the touch voltage in the event of an insulation fault. The ETO periodically checks equipment earthing connections for integrity, corrosion and looseness; earthing of portable equipment and temporary connections in particular is carefully verified.
Gemide içme suyu ya limanda kıyıdan (sho: On board, drinking water is either taken from shore in port (shore bunkering) or produced on board from seawater with an evaporator/RO (reverse osmosis) plant. Water from either source is not taken into the potable water tanks until it has been brought to drinkable quality; shore water is supplied to the tank through a reliable hose/connection, and produced water after mineralization and disinfection. The cook is the person who monitors that water quality is right at the end-user side (galley, mess).
Gemide mess, sadece beslenme değil aynı: On board, the mess is not only a place to eat but also a place to socialize and relax. A well-prepared messhall and attentive service make the crew feel valued; a mess that is untidy, dirty or serves cold food quickly becomes a source of complaints and low morale. The steward therefore treats service not as a mechanical task but as a service that looks after the crew's welfare.
Gemide meydana gelen yaralanmaların önem: A large share of injuries on board is caused by "slip, trip and fall" accidents. Lines left lying about, hand tools left out, spilled oil and paint, loose deck plates and blocked passageways are all low-severity but high-frequency causes of accidents. The Bosun's housekeeping discipline stops these accidents at the source.
Gemide onaylı LSA/FFE arrangement plan (: An approved LSA/FFE arrangement plan (including the fire control plan) is kept on board and kept up to date. Inventory records show the location, quantity, service/expiry date and condition of each item. By planning ahead with the expiry schedule, the Chief Officer arranges servicing/renewal in port.
Gemide saha şartlarında SA 2.5 zor sağla: On board, under site conditions, SA 2.5 is difficult to achieve; most areas are prepared with hand tools to around ST 2 - ST 3. Using a visual reference (color chart), the Bosun records which standard the area to be painted has achieved; this is critical for the paint warranty period.
Gemide su, köpük (foam), kuru kimyevi to: Water, foam, dry powder and CO2 portable extinguishers are carried on board; the extinguisher suited to the class of fire (A – solids, B – liquids, C – gases, D – metals, F – cooking oils) is placed at specific stations. Foam + CO2 in the engine room, foam/wet chemical in the galley and water in the accommodation is a typical distribution (CO2 extinguishers are not placed in accommodation spaces). Res. A.951(23) is the guideline for placement and numbers.
Gemide tatlı su (fresh water) sınırlı ve: On board, fresh water is a limited and valuable resource; it is either bunkered or produced by the fresh water generator. Washing laundry consumes a lot of water, so running full loads, avoiding unnecessary cycles and choosing the correct program are the basis of saving water. Excessive rinsing wastes water; the correct detergent dosage gives adequate cleaning with less rinsing.
Gemide tatlı su sınırlı bir kaynaktır. T: Fresh water is a limited resource on board. Unnecessary water consumption is avoided during cleaning; in particular, in toilets supplied by the seawater system, the flushing and the lines are checked. Wasting water means both cost and load on bunkers/generators.
Gemide tatlı su ve enerji sınırlı kaynak: On board, fresh water and energy are limited resources. The steward avoids starting unnecessary cycles before a full load has been collected; this means saving water/energy and reducing the generator load. When washing is complete, laundry is not left in the machine; it produces damp and odors.
Gemide tipik soğutma uygulamaları: provi: Typical shipboard refrigeration applications are: the provision plant (provision cold rooms), accommodation air conditioning (accommodation HVAC), engine room/control room ventilation and cargo refrigeration on reefer ships. The ETO must know the set temperatures, alarm limits and control logic of each system.
Gemide tıbbi sorumluluk, nadiren kullanı: Medical responsibility on board is a form of preparedness that is rarely used but saves lives when it is. The Second Officer's up-to-date medical chest, refreshed skills and effective use of TMAS are a crew's only medical safeguard in the middle of the ocean.
Gemide uzun seferler, izolasyon, monoton: Long voyages, isolation, monotony and fatigue on board are factors that increase the risk of escaping into alcohol or drugs. The Master takes indirect measures by managing these environmental risks (social activities, means of communication, reasonable rest). The D&A policy and fatigue management (rest hours) complement each other; both are part of fitness for duty.
Gemideki SW/FW santrifüj pompalarında en: In the ship's SW/FW centrifugal pumps, the component that fails most often is the mechanical seal. Seal leakage results from dry running, cavitation or excessive axial force. During maintenance, the seal faces are inspected for scratches/wear, the O-rings are replaced, the shaft sleeve is measured and the bearing clearance is checked with a feeler/dial gauge.
Gemideki yolcu/personel sayısı her zaman: The number of passengers and crew on board must always be current and correct; in an emergency the manifest is the basis of search and rescue (passengers with special needs are flagged).
Gemiden karaya distress alert iletimi iç: For ship-to-shore distress alerting, at least two separate and independent means are required; the failure of a single device must not remove the distress alerting capability completely. This redundancy principle is the fundamental safety philosophy of GMDSS and explains why the equipment inventory looks "redundant".
Gemiler A (çok iyi), B (iyi), C (orta),: Ships are rated A (major superior), B (minor superior), C (moderate), D (minor inferior) or E (inferior). Ships rated D for three consecutive years or E for one year must prepare a corrective action plan.
Gemilerde başlıca yakıt türleri HFO (Hea: The main fuel types on ships are HFO (Heavy Fuel Oil), VLSFO (Very Low Sulphur Fuel Oil), MGO/MDO (Marine Gas/Diesel Oil) and, increasingly, alternative fuels such as LNG. Each has a different viscosity, sulfur content and treatment requirement. ISO 8217 defines marine fuel specifications; fuel received is expected to comply with this specification.
Gemilerde genellikle subay messi (office: On ships, the officers' mess and the crew mess are usually separate; the same standard of hygiene and service is provided in both. Because of watchkeeping, meals are taken at different times; the steward also coordinates keeping a night meal/standby meal ready for those coming off night watches.
Gemilerde gıda atığını öğüten comminuter: Ships may have a comminuter/macerator that grinds food waste; discharging comminuted food waste (below a specified particle size) into the sea is conditionally permitted under Annex V when the ship is far enough from land. The permitted distance is greater for food waste that has not been comminuted. In special areas and near ports/the coast, the rules are much stricter.
Gemilerde gıda harcaması, kişi başı günl: On ships, food expenditure is managed through a daily budget per person (victualling rate, USD/person/day); this rate is set according to company/charter policy and regional prices. The cook must provide the adequate quantity, nutritional value, quality and variety required by the MLC without exceeding this rate. Total budget = victualling rate × number of crew × number of days; the cook fits menus and orders into this framework.
Gemilerde çok uluslu ekipler standarttır: Multinational crews are standard on ships. The Bosun brings ratings of different languages, religions and cultures together in a common safety and work culture. Respect and clear communication are the basic tools. Fairness in mess room arrangements, use of recreation areas and allocation of duties ensures team harmony.
Geminin Minimum Safe Manning Document (M: The ship's Minimum Safe Manning Document (MSMD) is issued by the flag State and specifies the minimum qualified personnel that must be on board. The Chief Officer must assess whether the planned workload can be completed with the personnel available without violating rest hours. During busy periods such as port operations, heavy weather and tank cleaning, the work plan must be prioritized realistically and non-critical work postponed.
Geminin ana güç ve kontrol sistemleri ar: When the ship's main power and control systems fail — blackout, fire, flooding — independent emergency systems with their own power sources are needed to maintain safety. These are located separately from the main systems (usually above the main deck, in a watertight compartment) and can operate without main power. The aim is to maintain basic safety functions even in the worst-case scenario.
Geminin ice class'ı (Polar Class veya Fi: The ship's ice class (Polar Class or Finnish-Swedish ice class) determines in which ice conditions and with what support (unescorted / under icebreaker escort) she may navigate. The Second Officer provides the Master with data to verify that the planned route is within the capabilities of the ship's ice class.
Geminin tüm güverte ilgili sertifikaları: All of the ship's deck-related certificates (Safety Equipment, Load Line, class certificate, hatch cover test reports, LSA/FFE service certificates) must be valid and ready for inspection. The Chief Officer monitors the certificate validity schedule and renews those approaching expiry in good time. A single expired certificate creates a serious finding.
Geminin ve yükün ortak kurtarılması için: If a deliberate sacrifice was made for the common safety of the ship and cargo (general average), the process runs under the York-Antwerp Rules and the protest contributes to the chain of evidence. In situations such as salvage and towage, the protest and records are also of critical importance.
Geminin ölçümünden (ship figure) elde ed: The quantity obtained from the ship's measurement (ship figure) is compared with the shore measurement (shore figure). If the difference exceeds the specified tolerance (e.g. 0.5%), a Letter of Protest is issued; otherwise the defence against later cargo claims is weakened.
Gemiye erişim; rıhtım yüksekliği, freebo: Access to the ship is provided by a gangway, an accommodation ladder or a combination of the two, depending on the height of the quay, the freeboard and the operation. For pilot transfer, a pilot ladder and, where necessary, a combination arrangement (accommodation ladder + pilot ladder) are used. The AB learns from the Bosun/officer which equipment is to be used in which conditions.
Gemiye giriş noktaları (kapılar, havalan: Entry points to the ship (doors, ventilation openings, cable penetrations) are kept rodent-proof; holes must be sealed with metal/filler (rodents can gnaw through wood/plastic but struggle with metal). The cook checks that the galley and food stores are protected in this respect.
Gemiye yeni katılan her personel, görev: Every new joiner receives safety familiarization in accordance with ISM Code Section 6 and SOLAS before taking up duties. The Chief Officer (or an officer the Chief Officer designates) shows the lifejackets, immersion suits, muster station, liferafts/lifeboats, fire extinguisher locations, alarm signals, emergency escape routes and mustering procedures. This training is documented and signed for.
Gemiye yeni katılan personel, vardiyaya: Personnel newly joining the ship receive engine room familiarization before they start keeping watch: escape routes, emergency duties, critical equipment, alarms and communications. The Second Engineer ensures that everyone clearly knows their job description and reporting line. Unclear responsibility leaves a "nobody was responsible" gap when an accident happens.
Gemiyi terk, kaptanın verebileceği en ağ: Abandoning ship is the gravest decision the Master can take and is the last resort. In line with the principle "abandon the ship when it can no longer carry you", every moment the ship stays afloat she is a safer platform than a liferaft. The Master must take the decision to abandon neither too early (abandoning a ship that could be saved) nor too late (a disorderly evacuation at the moment of sinking). When the decision is taken, the abandon ship signal is sounded and the crew assemble at the muster stations with lifejackets and immersion suits.
Genel DP uygulamasında her referans, DP: In general DP practice, each reference is observed independently and compared with the existing references before it is included in the DP model. Before a reference with a growing deviation is simply deselected, the cause is investigated, because the deviating sensor may sometimes be the correct one while the others share a common error.
Genel DP uygulamasında, DP'ye geçmeden ö: In general DP practice, each thruster and main propeller is proved in both directions in manual control before changing over to DP. The command, the feedback and the physical response are compared; the system is not taken over until all three are verified to agree.
Genel acil durum alarmı (general emergen: The general emergency alarm is a signal of seven short blasts plus one long blast on the whistle/bells; it calls everyone to the muster station. The fire alarm, the abandon ship signal and other signals are defined in the SMS. To be sure of noticing an alarm in the high noise of the engine room, the Oiler also watches the visual alarm beacons and follows telephone/UHF communication.
Genel acil durum sinyali yedi veya daha: The general emergency signal is given by seven or more short blasts followed by one long blast on the whistle (and the same pattern on the electric bell); the order to abandon ship is given by the Master verbally/over the PA, and the signal itself is not an order to abandon ship. The AB must be able to tell these signals apart by heart and, on hearing the signal, immediately take their lifejacket and go quickly to the muster station.
Genel denetim bulgusu: kalibre edilmemiş: A general inspection finding: navigational equipment that is not calibrated or whose records are not kept is a regular cause of PSC detentions. Lesson: the chain of records is as important as the equipment itself.
Genel haberleşme: e-posta, teleks, SMS (: General communications: email, telex, SMS (through an LES — Land Earth Station).
Genel hedef olarak kümes eti ve kıyma ≥7: As a general target, poultry and minced meat are cooked to a core temperature of ≥75°C, fish/eggs to ≥63-70°C, and reheated food to ≥75°C. It is essential to confirm by measurement, not by eye, that the target has been reached; a change in color is not conclusive proof that the food is cooked.
Genel kural: plastik, pişirme yağı, inci: General rule: plastics, cooking oil, incinerator ash, operational waste and e-waste must not be discharged into the sea; they are retained on board and delivered ashore. Food waste and non-HME cargo residues may be discharged subject to distance and other conditions.
Genel tanıtımı, sorumlu olunacak ekipman: The general familiarization is followed by detailed familiarization with the equipment the person will be responsible for. For example, the Third Engineer is introduced to the generators, purifiers and boiler, and the ETO to the switchboard, PMS automation and high-voltage systems. Vendor manuals, P&ID diagrams and the notes of previous personnel are used.
Genel tanıtımın ötesinde, her mürettebat: Beyond the general familiarisation, every crew member is familiarised with the equipment specific to his or her duties: the officer of the watch with the make of ECDIS on board, the radar, the autopilot and the GMDSS console; the engineer with the ship's main engine, auxiliary systems and alarm panel. An officer keeping a watch alone without type-specific training is a recurring cause of accidents in MAIB reports.
Genellikle finned tube (kanatlı boru) ti: It is usually of the finned-tube type and cooled by seawater or central cooling water. Large engines may use two-stage cooling.
Genellikle iki kompresör (duty/standby),: Usually two compressors (duty/standby), one condenser (water-cooled), and an expansion valve for each room.
General Arrangement planı, geminin tüm g: The General Arrangement plan shows the layout of all the ship's decks and the engine room. From this plan, the cadet learns which platform/deck each piece of equipment is on, as well as the escape routes, doors and passages. The GA provides quick orientation, particularly on joining a new ship.
General Average (GA), örneğin yangını sö: General Average (GA) is the sharing of sacrifices made to escape a common danger, such as cargo being damaged by water to put out a fire, cargo being thrown overboard (jettison) to refloat a grounded ship, or salvage and towage expenses. When GA is declared, the contribution of all the parties saved (the shipowner and all the cargo owners) to the losses is calculated under the York-Antwerp Rules (commonly the 2016 version).
General emergency alarm, en az yedi kısa: The general emergency alarm is a signal of seven or more short blasts followed by one long blast on the whistle/bell; it must be audible throughout all accommodation and working spaces of the ship. This signal means "go to your muster station"; the order to abandon ship is given by the Master verbally (PA/radio) and has no separate automatic signal.
Generator aşırı yüklendiğinde tüm baranı: To prevent the collapse of the whole busbar (blackout) when a generator is overloaded, preferential tripping comes into action: the least critical consumers (air conditioning, heating, refrigeration compressors) are shed first, in stages, so that essential loads remain supplied. The ETO sets the current setpoints and the stage sequence of the preferential trip relay according to the class-approved load study.
Genleşme elemanı: Basınç düşürerek akışk: Expansion device: lowers the pressure and brings the refrigerant to evaporator conditions.
Genleşme oranı (expansion ratio), köpük: The expansion ratio is the ratio of the volume of foam to the volume of the foam solution. Low expansion (up to 20:1) is used for long-range monitors and nozzles; medium expansion (20–200:1) for limited areas; high expansion (over 200:1) for filling a whole space (the engine room).
Genleşme tankı, devrenin en yüksek nokta: The expansion tank is at the highest point of the circuit; it serves for venting, thermal expansion and topping up. A continuous fall in the tank level points to a leak, a continuous rise to an internal leak from a heat exchanger or a jacket.
Genleşme valfi: Yüksek basınçlı sıvı akı: Expansion valve: the high-pressure liquid refrigerant is throttled to low pressure, which lowers its temperature. A liquid-vapour mixture forms.
Genç personel, deneyimli bir tayfa ile e: Young personnel are paired with an experienced rating and work within a "buddy system". This serves both teaching and safety; a novice is never left alone in a high-risk area.
Gerekli CII değerleri, 2019 referans değ: The required CII values are tightened by 2 percentage points per year relative to the 2019 reference in 2023-2026 (5% in 2023, 11% in 2026).
Gergin halat koptuğunda depolanan enerji: When a line under tension parts, the stored energy is released and the line recoils (snap-back). According to OCIMF MEG4, snap-back zones painted on deck can give a false sense of security, so the whole mooring area is treated as a potential snap-back zone.
Geri bildirim aynı zamanda diyet/alerjen: Feedback also keeps dietary/allergen/cultural needs up to date: the preferences of newly joined crew members are recorded and changing needs (e.g. low salt for health reasons) are reflected in the menu. An open and respectful feedback culture improves both menu quality and the atmosphere in the mess.
Geri bildirim somut, zamanında ve yapıcı: Feedback must be concrete, timely and constructive. Instead of "that was good", specific feedback such as "Your maneuver in the crossing scenario was correct, but you were 3 minutes late; earlier action would have given a much safer CPA" speeds up learning. The Second Officer conveys strengths and areas for improvement in a balanced way.
Geri kazanılamayan slop yalnız liman atı: Slops that cannot be recovered are delivered only to a port reception facility. The transfer is recorded in ORB Part II with the appropriate code (Code J, etc.) and the receipt is kept.
Geri montajda parçalar doğru sırada, doğ: On reassembly, the parts are fitted in the correct sequence, in the correct orientation and to the manufacturer's tightening torque (particularly the lock ring / large nut). Incorrect assembly can lead to imbalance (vibration) and even to a disaster with the bowl flying apart. The alignment marks of the lock ring are lined up; over- or under-tightening is dangerous.
Geride kalan düzeltmeler için UKHO'nun c: For outstanding corrections, the UKHO cumulative/back-correction services (e.g. Annual Summary, NP234 NtM cumulative list) are used; in this way a chart that has not been corrected for a long time can be brought up to date quickly by seeing which notices are missing.
Gerilim altındaki bir halat veya tel kop: When a line or wire under tension parts, it releases its stored elastic energy by recoiling like a whip; the area swept by this recoil is called the snap-back zone. Synthetic lines (especially nylon) recoil far more dangerously because of their high elasticity; in less than a second, the parted end moves fast enough to tear a human body apart. This is why most mooring injuries are fatal or involve the loss of limbs.
Gerilme σ = F/A formülüyle hesaplanır. D: Stress is calculated with the formula σ = F/A. Strain is defined as ε = ΔL/L₀.
Gerçek bir acil durumda insan düşünmez,: In a real emergency, people do not think; they do what they have drilled. This is why drills are critical: the cadet becomes able to put on a lifejacket, respond to the alarm signals and carry out their duty by reflex rather than from memory. Taking part in drills seriously saves lives later.
Gerçek motorda yanma sabit basınçta gerç: In a real engine combustion does not take place at constant pressure, there are heat losses, the gas properties change with temperature and there are friction losses. For these reasons the real efficiency is about 60–70% of the ideal cycle efficiency.
Gerçekçi bir drill; beklenmedik bir sena: A realistic drill includes an unexpected scenario (e.g. "this exit is blocked, find another"), timing, use of real equipment and a debrief afterwards. "Went well / to be improved" notes are written in the drill records, and the gaps found are turned into corrective action. A bad drill creates false confidence, which is more dangerous than not drilling at all.
Gevşek giysi, takı ve açık saç dönen eki: Loose clothing, jewelry and loose hair are a lethal hazard near rotating equipment; entanglement accidents result in serious injury or death. The cadet must get into the habit of checking clothing and accessories when entering the engine room.
Geçerli bir Sea Service Certificate; gem: A valid Sea Service Certificate contains the seafarer's identity details, the ship's name, IMO number, flag, type and tonnage, main engine power (propulsion power — kW), rank/capacity, dates of joining and leaving and the total length of service. The certificate is signed by the Master and bears the ship's stamp.
Geçici onarımlarda (acil sızıntı) boru k: For temporary repairs (an emergency leak), a pipe clamp or a cold repair kit may be used; however, these solutions are temporary and are replaced by a permanent welded/flanged repair at the first opportunity. The class society approves permanent repairs.
Geçici çözüm (clamp, drip tray) ile kalı: A clear distinction is kept between a temporary fix (clamp, drip tray) and a permanent repair (gasket, gland packing, renewal of the line). A temporary arrangement is always recorded and passed on at handover, because a forgotten "temporary" fix is the most frequent cause of fire.
Geçiş ECA içinde tamamlanırsa, gemi bir: If the changeover is completed inside the ECA, the ship will have navigated for some time with sulfur above the limit — this is a violation. Therefore the principle "enter the ECA on compliant fuel" is absolute and is planned with a safety margin.
Geçiş kademeli yapılır: viskozite ve sıc: The changeover is made gradually: because of the viscosity and temperature difference (HFO ~130°C, MGO ~40-50°C), a sudden thermal shock can cause fuel pump plunger seizure and fuel leaks. The changeover rate is controlled with a cooler (MGO chiller); the ramp rate is usually kept below 2°C/min.
Geçiş süresince geçici TBN uyumsuzluğu k: A temporary TBN mismatch is acceptable during the changeover, but on long ECA passages the right choice of cylinder oil is essential. The wrong TBN triggers cold corrosion or deposit problems.
Geçiş sırasında fuel oil sıcaklık değişi: During the changeover, the rate of change of fuel oil temperature is kept below the limit specified by the engine maker (typically around 2 °C/minute). This allows the fuel system components to adapt gradually and prevents mechanical damage.
Geçiş yollarında engel (hortum, kablo, a: No obstacles (hoses, cables, tools, parts) are left on walkways; tripping accidents are at least as common as slipping. Good housekeeping means both cleanliness and order.
Geçiş, sülfür içeriğinin %0.10 altına in: The changeover is considered complete when it has been confirmed that the sulfur content has fallen below 0.10%. For verification, the mixing ratio and the system flushing time are monitored; if there is any doubt, an extra margin is allowed.
Giren kişi, mümkünse harness ile bağlı b: Where possible, the entrant wears a harness attached to a lifeline (rescue line); the standby AB holds the line and watches its slack and condition. Rescue equipment stands ready outside the entrance: spare SCBA, a rescue harness, a tripod/winch recovery arrangement (if required), resuscitation equipment and first aid. The AB knows where this equipment is and how to use it.
Giren personel, sürekli okuyan kişisel g: Personnel entering carry a continuously reading personal gas detector; if the atmosphere deteriorates, it gives an alarm and the space is left immediately. Measurement is not a one-off; conditions can change, so monitoring is continuous.
Giriş prosedürü: alanı izole et ve haval: Entry procedure: isolate and ventilate the space, test the atmosphere (O2, LEL, toxic gases), issue the permit, assign standby personnel, ensure continuous communication and monitoring, keep a rescue plan ready. Nobody may enter until the readings are within the safe range. Oxygen must be around 20.9%, LEL 0% and toxic gases below their threshold limits.
Giriş süresince kapı/menhol başında bir: During entry, a standby person/watchman is present at the door/manhole, continuous communication is maintained and a rescue plan is kept ready. Most enclosed space deaths are caused by low oxygen or toxic gas that comes without warning, and the toll multiplies when a second person goes in unprepared "to help".
Giriş süresince, giriş ağzında bir stand: Throughout the entry, a standby person (attendant) remains at the entrance at all times and is in uninterrupted communication with the team inside (radio, voice, visual or rope signals). The standby person NEVER goes in, but raises the alarm and calls the rescue team if there is a problem. Rushing in alone and becoming the second victim is the main cause of enclosed space deaths.
Giriş öncesi ve giriş süresince atmosfer: Before and during entry, the atmosphere is measured with a calibrated multi-gas detector for oxygen (for entry it must be at the normal level of air, i.e. about 21% by volume [20.9% on the meter]; lower oxygen can cause loss of consciousness and death without warning), flammable gas (LEL — Lower Explosive Limit; the target is usually below 1% LEL) and toxic gases (H₂S, CO in ppm). Testing is done at different levels (top, middle, bottom) because some gases collect at the bottom and others at the top.
Giriş, Birinci Zabitten alınan Enclosed: Entry is made with an Enclosed Space Entry Permit obtained from the Chief Officer. The Bosun passes the permit conditions on to the team, ensures ventilation, organizes atmosphere testing and makes sure that entry does not begin until every step has been completed. Entry without a permit is strictly prohibited.
Giriş/çıkış sıcaklık ve ΔP değerleri düz: Inlet and outlet temperatures and ΔP values are recorded regularly; a deviation from the reference shows fouling. When a plate cooler is opened, the order and orientation of the plates are marked, and the gaskets are checked and renewed if necessary. The seawater strainer is cleaned often, and the plates or tubes are cleaned chemically at planned intervals.
Girişten önce ve giriş boyunca atmosfer: The atmosphere is tested before and throughout entry: oxygen (target 20.9%), flammable gas (LEL), H2S and CO. The gas detector must be calibrated, and measurements must be taken at different levels (top/middle/bottom); some gases collect at the bottom, others at the top. The Bosun makes sure that the testing is done correctly.
Globe ve gate valflerde sızdırmazlık sea: In globe and gate valves, tightness is achieved by the contact surface between the seat and the disc. If there is erosion/pitting, lapping (grinding with lapping compound) is carried out; heavy damage requires replacement of the seat or a new valve. Quick-closing valves (fuel tank quick-closing) are tested as required by SOLAS; a malfunctioning one is a gap in fire safety.
Goose-neck vinçler: Tek bom, elektro-hid: Goose-neck cranes: single jib, electro-hydraulic drive. Standard on modern dry cargo ships.
Grab/vinç tel halat, fren ve hidrolik ba: Grab and crane wire ropes, brakes and hydraulics are maintained according to the PMS; hatch cover hydraulic cylinders and hoses are inspected for leaks.
Gravity davit, filikayı kendi ağırlığıyl: A gravity davit lowers the lifeboat out and down by its own weight (with a brake); it is the most common type. A free-fall davit lets the lifeboat drop freely and uses a separate winch for recovery. The davit must be strong enough to carry the weight of the fully loaded lifeboat safely.
Gravity disc (dam ring), yakıt-su ayrışm: The gravity disc (dam ring) sets the fuel-water interface. Choosing the correct gravity disc for the fuel density is essential; a wrong choice leads to fuel loss or insufficient water separation.
Gravity disc çapı, arıtılacak akışkanın: The gravity disc diameter is selected according to the density of the liquid to be treated. The higher the density, the smaller the disc hole diameter used.
Gravity disc çapı, yakıtın yoğunluğuna g: The diameter of the gravity disc is chosen according to the density of the fuel. Choosing the wrong disc causes fuel to escape through the water outlet or water to mix with the fuel.
Greasing kirli ve kaygan bir iştir; AB e: Greasing is dirty and slippery work; the AB wears gloves, takes care not to slip and does not let grease residue get onto the deck or into the sea. Waste grease and dirty rags are collected as appropriate waste under MARPOL Annex V and are not thrown overboard.
Green normal operasyon; Advisory/Blue di: Green is normal operation; Advisory/Blue means caution and monitoring; Yellow means bringing the activity to a safe stage; Red means stopping or abandoning the activity. The colours are defined in the ship-specific ASOG, and no shift in their meaning between projects is allowed.
Gross observed volume (GOV), ortalama sı: Using the gross observed volume (GOV), the average temperature and the standard density, the gross standard volume (GSV) is obtained with ASTM Table 54B and converted to weight (MT in vacuum/in air) with the WCF (weight correction factor).
Group A (sıvılaşabilir yükler — nickel o: Group A (cargoes that may liquefy — nickel ore, iron ore fines, bauxite fines): TML (Transportable Moisture Limit) tests, the Flow Moisture Point and the cargo declaration are critical. If the TML is exceeded, loading is refused; otherwise liquefaction causes the ship to capsize (MV Bulk Jupiter 2015).
Group A yükler (nickel ore, iron ore fin: Group A cargoes (nickel ore, iron ore fines, bauxite fines) can liquefy; the TML (Transportable Moisture Limit) and the cargo declaration are critical. If the TML is exceeded the Master refuses to load; otherwise the ship can capsize because of liquefaction. Group B cargoes (DRI, sulphur, coal) carry the risks of self-heating, off-gassing and CO; hold ventilation and gas measurements are needed. Group C is low risk.
Group B (kimyasal tehlike — DRI, sulphur: Group B (chemical hazard — DRI, sulfur, coal): risk of self-heating, off-gassing and CO emission. Hold ventilation, surface temperature monitoring, gas detection and the fixed CO2 system must be ready. Group C covers low-risk cargoes (cement, sand, salt).
Group B yüklerde sıcaklık izleme, hold v: With Group B cargoes, temperature monitoring, hold ventilation (on or off as the cargo schedule requires), gas detection and control of ignition sources are applied. Ammonium nitrate-based cargoes need special precautions against fire and explosion.
Guard rail, stanchion, bulwark ve safety: The integrity of guard rails, stanchions, bulwarks and safety chains is checked periodically; missing or loose railings are reported immediately and temporary safety measures (warning, barrier) are taken.
Gypsy (wildcat), zincirin baklalarına bi: The gypsy (wildcat) is a toothed drum profiled so that the links of the chain sit exactly in it. A separate gypsy is needed for each chain diameter; the links sitting fully in the pockets of the gypsy prevents the chain from slipping ("jumping") and being damaged. There is a clutch (dog clutch) between the gypsy and the main shaft; when letting go, the clutch is disengaged and the gypsy runs free.
Gyro arızasında manyetik pusula tek head: If the gyro fails, the magnetic compass may remain the only heading reference; for this reason, an up-to-date and reliable deviation is a redundancy safeguard. It is also checked that no magnetic material is placed near the compass.
Gyro compass, gerçek kuzeyi (true north): The gyro compass is designed to indicate true north; however, a small error (gyro error) may always be present. The error is expressed as "high" (the reading is greater than the true value) or "low", and is found from the difference between the true bearing and the gyro bearing. The Second Officer makes this check regularly and records it in the gyro error book.
Gyro compass, gerçek kuzeyi sağlayan kri: The gyro compass is the critical sensor that provides true north; modern fiber-optic (FOG) or ring-laser (RLG) types are easy to maintain, while traditional mechanical types need careful maintenance. The ETO checks the gyro power supply, heading repeater alignment, the follow-up system and the alarm functions. Because a heading error misleads all navigation equipment, gyro accuracy is critical.
Gyro heading; köprü repeater'ları, dümen: The gyro heading is distributed to the bridge repeaters, the steering, radar/ECDIS, AIS and the autopilot. The repeaters must follow the master gyro exactly; if there is a difference, the synchronisation is checked. The magnetic compass can be read from the bridge through a periscope or reflector.
Gyro pusula bazı sistematik hatalar göst: The gyrocompass shows some systematic errors: latitude (damping) error, speed/course/latitude error (the deviation caused by the ship's speed and latitude) and ballistic deflection during manoeuvres. Modern gyros correct these automatically, but the principle must be known.
Gyro pusula tekrarlayıcıları (repeater): Gyro compass repeaters are located on the bridge, the bridge wings and in the steering gear compartment.
Gyro pusula, yüksek hızda dönen bir roto: The gyrocompass uses the conservation of angular momentum of a rotor spinning at high speed (gyroscopic inertia) and its interaction with the earth's rotation (precession). With a gravity and damping arrangement, the rotor axis seeks true north (north-seeking) and stays there (north-settling). This gives a true north reference independent of the magnetic field.
Görev dağılımında genellikle subay yaşam: In the allocation of duties, officers' accommodation and ratings' accommodation are usually kept to different standards and frequencies, but the level of hygiene must be equal in both. The cabins of the Master, Chief Officer and Chief Engineer and the common areas may be put on a daily program, and some ratings' cabins on a weekly deep-clean program. The steward follows this program using a checklist and records it by signing.
Görev dağılımında winch/vinç operatörü,: In the allocation of duties, the persons who will operate the winch/crane, operate the hatch cover controls, carry out lashing and handle communications are designated. The AB usually takes on more than one role; however, conflicting duties, such as operating machinery controls and working under a load at the same time, are not given. Communication is maintained by hand-held radio or hand signals.
Görev gereksinimi ile geminin gerçek tek: By assessing the task requirements together with the actual technical condition of the ship, the required DP equipment class, level of redundancy, number of personnel and combination of position references are agreed with the client.
Görev hiyerarşisinde ETO, Baş Mühendis'e: In the chain of command, the ETO reports to the Chief Engineer but is the ship's most competent technical person in electrical/electronic matters. The ETO works in coordination with the watchkeeping engineers and acts together with the engine room team, particularly during blackouts, generator paralleling and switchboard switching operations.
Görev için gerekli sınıf sağlanamıyorsa: If the class required for the task cannot be provided, the work is not started. Task Appropriate Mode (TAM) may only be used through an approved, risk-based process and with a reduced operating envelope; it does not automatically make missing redundancy acceptable.
Görev karmaşasını önlemek için Baş Mühen: To prevent confusion over tasks, the Chief Engineer uses a RACI matrix (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed). For example, in a bunkering operation the Chief Engineer may be Accountable, the Second Engineer Responsible and the Third Engineer Consulted on the soundings.
Görev kartları kişiye özel ve dilden bağ: Duty cards are prepared for each individual and independent of language (supported by symbols); with a multinational crew, the IMO standard symbols (Res. A.760(18)) and the ship's working language are used. When a new crew member joins the ship, the station card is prepared at once and handed over during safety familiarization.
Görev kartı; toplanma yeri (muster stati: The duty card specifies the muster station, the lifeboat/liferaft number, the team role (e.g., fire party, boundary cooling, first aid, communications) and the equipment to be carried. At a crew change, each newly joined AB is given familiarization and a duty card before being assigned shipboard duties; this is a legal requirement.
Görev ve su derinliğine göre DGNSS, HPR/: A combination of DGNSS, HPR/USBL, taut wire, laser, microwave or relative PRS is chosen to suit the task and the water depth. It is taken into account that two GNSS units using the same satellite or correction source may not be truly independent.
Görev-özel familiarization ise personeli: Job-specific familiarization relates to the person's actual work: the mooring station, crane operation, the enclosed space procedure, personal protective equipment (PPE), the permit-to-work system and the relevant sections of the company SMS. New personnel are not assigned alone to hazardous work until full familiarization has been completed.
Görev; PSV ikmali, AHTS/anchor handling,: The task is clearly defined as PSV supply, AHTS/anchor handling, diving, ROV/survey, pipe or cable laying, drilling, offshore loading, walk-to-work or heavy lifting. Each type of task brings its own watch circle, combination of references and stop criteria.
Görsel indication 15 saniye içinde reset: If the visual indication is not reset within 15 seconds, the first-stage audible alarm starts on the bridge.
