Görünür kusur yoksa \"clean\" B/L imzala: If there is no visible defect, a clean B/L is signed. If there is a defect, the actual condition is documented by writing it on the B/L (claused/dirty). Pressure to show damaged cargo as clean is a serious legal and ethical trap.
Görüş bozulduğunda Kural 19 gereği hız \: When visibility deteriorates, under Rule 19 the speed is reduced "as far as is practicable"; if necessary, the ship takes all way off. The officer coordinates the decision to reduce speed with the engine room (stand-by engine request) and records it in the deck logbook.
Gösterge \"depth below keel\" mi yoksa \: It must be made clear whether the display shows "depth below keel" or "depth below transducer/waterline"; if the offset is wrong, the depth reading becomes dangerously misleading. On dual-frequency sounders, the appropriate frequency is selected.
Gösterilen fix kalitesi; uydu geometrisi: The quality of the fix shown depends on satellite geometry, the antenna's view of the sky, the ionosphere, multipath, integrity monitoring and the augmentation used. A single "± metres" value does not prove the reliability of the position at that moment.
Gövde altına yerleştirilen hava dağıtıcı: Low-pressure air is supplied from air distributors fitted under the hull. The layer of micro-bubbles formed creates a low-friction interface between the hull and the water.
Gövde onarımı, boru kaynağı, yapısal par: It is widely used in hull repairs, pipe welding, joining structural parts and build-up welding. Classification societies certify welder qualifications.
Gövde ve pervane fouling (kabuklanma), d: Hull and propeller fouling increases resistance dramatically and raises consumption. Regular hull cleaning and propeller polishing can save 3-8% fuel. The Chief Engineer plans the timing of cleaning by looking at the performance trend (rising SFOC, falling speed).
Gövde, korozyona karşı sacrificial anode: The hull is protected against corrosion by sacrificial anodes or Impressed Current Cathodic Protection (ICCP). During the underwater inspection, anode wastage is measured and ICCP system performance (potential readings) is recorded. Insufficient protection accelerates hull and propeller corrosion.
Gövde-boru (shell & tube): Bir akışkan b: Shell and tube: one fluid passes through the tubes and the other through the shell. It withstands high pressure and temperature; it is used for F.O. heaters and steam heaters.
Göz koruması kıvılcım, sıçrayan sıvı ve: Eye protection is used against sparks, splashing liquids and dust, and respiratory protection against dust, fumes and chemical vapors. Respiratory protection is selected according to the MSDS/risk assessment; a dust mask does not stop gas — for gas, a mask with a suitable filter or an air-supplied system is needed. In an enclosed space, only SCBA/SAA is safe.
Gözle: sızıntı, gevşek bağlantı, anormal: Look: leaks, loose connections, abnormal levels, vibration. Listen: unusual knocking, cavitation, rubbing noise. Smell: burnt insulation, oil/fuel vapor, exhaust gas leaks. Touch (carefully): bearing housing temperature, temperature differences between pipes. This sense-based diagnosis reveals early faults that panel readings cannot catch.
Gözlemci, her adımda \"doğru prosedür iz: At every step, the observer notes whether the correct procedure was followed: was the SCBA pre-use check done, was the buddy system applied, was communication clear, was the equipment used correctly? These notes form the basis of the debrief and the record; simply saying "drill held" is not enough.
Gün sonunda Reis, tamamlanan işleri, kul: At the end of the day, the Bosun reports to the Chief Officer on the jobs completed, materials used, jobs left unfinished and observations on site (new rust areas, failed equipment, stock running out). PMS work orders are closed with evidence of completion (photo, measurement).
Güncel meteorolojik veriler (pilot chart: Current meteorological data (pilot chart climatology, seasonal TRS risk), draft restrictions, ECDIS safety settings and company policies (e.g. UKC policy, squat allowance, minimum CPA) are also gathered at this stage. A missing or out-of-date publication invalidates all the stages that follow.
Güncelleme sırasında \"base CD\" (taban: When updating, the distinction between the "base CD" (base data) and the "update CD" (weekly changes) is important: base data arrives at set intervals, updates every week. Loading in the wrong order or a missing permit results in cells not being loaded and the navigation area appearing blank.
Gündüz, bir top/küre (ball) demirli, dik: By day, one ball indicates a ship at anchor, two balls in a vertical line NUC, ball-diamond-ball RAM, a cylinder CBD and a diamond a ship engaged in towing. By reading these shapes and lights without hesitation, the officer correctly assesses the Rule 18 priority and the status of the ship. The range of visibility of lights is defined in Rule 22 according to the ship's length.
Günlük \"toolbox talk\" (vardiya başı br: During the daily "toolbox talk" (start-of-watch briefing), the day's jobs are explained to the ratings and the duty engineer; for each job, the risk assessment, the isolation required, PPE and the need for a standby person are discussed. Work is allocated by matching experience to the job; an experienced person always accompanies an overhaul being done for the first time.
Günlük DSC testi (kıyı/başka istasyonla: The daily DSC test (with a coast station or another station, or a self-test), antenna and coaxial cable checks, and battery and portable VHF tests are carried out, and the radio log is kept. Care is taken not to press the real distress button by mistake during the test.
Günlük blow-down ve su kimyası testleri: Daily blow-down and boiler water chemistry tests are carried out; soot blowing prevents soot build-up. The safety valves are tested annually.
Günlük kontrolde hidrolik yağ seviyesi (: In the daily check, the hydraulic oil level (tank and replenishing tank), leaks at the ram/cylinder seals, leaks at hose/pipe connections and general cleanliness are checked. A leak from a ram seal means loss of oil and a slip/fire hazard on the floor; it also lets air into the system and reduces performance.
Günlük noon report; ana makine/yardımcı/: The daily noon report contains main engine/auxiliary/boiler consumption, steaming hours, distance, average speed, slip and SFOC. ROB by calculation (previous ROB − consumption) is compared with ROB by sounding; any discrepancy (leak, measurement error, calculation error or theft) is investigated. All figures are entered into the company performance system.
Günlük yakıt/yağ tüketimi, sefer raporla: Daily fuel/lube oil consumption is the basic data for voyage reports (noon reports). A deviation from the expected consumption may indicate a decline in engine performance or a measurement/leakage problem. These data are critical for EEXI/CII performance monitoring.
Günlük/haftalık DSC testi, anten/tuner v: Daily and weekly DSC tests, checks of the antenna, tuner and earth system, battery tests and the radio log are carried out. The test is made not on the actual distress frequency but with the appropriate test procedure.
Güvenli bir gemi ağı, fonksiyonlara göre: A secure ship network is divided into segments (VLANs) by function: OT (bridge/engine control), operational IT (company/administrative), the crew welfare network and the guest/passenger network. The ETO ensures that these segments are isolated from each other and that traffic between them is controlled by firewall rules. A flat network allows a breach in one zone to spread to the whole ship.
Güvenli kaldırma, eğitim gerektiren bir: Safe lifting is a skill that requires training: sling angles, center of gravity, equipment selection and signaling have to be learned. Inexperienced personnel work under the supervision of a competent person. Over time, the Oiler/Fitter masters this skill and passes correct practice on to newcomers.
Güvenli olan artan yemek, gıda güvenliği: Safe leftover food can be used at the next meal in line with food safety rules (proper cooling, correct reheating temperature); if it is not safe, it goes into the waste stream. This balance both reduces waste and prevents the risk of foodborne illness.
Güvenli çalışma koşulu: NPSHa > NPSHr (g: Safe operating condition: NPSHa > NPSHr (generally with a margin of at least 0.5 m).
Güvenlik (safety/shutdown) sistemi, kont: The safety (safety/shutdown) system must be independent of the control system: main engine overspeed, low oil pressure and crankcase oil mist (oil mist detector) trips are designed separately from the control PLC and fail-safe (going to the safe state on loss of power). The ETO preserves this independence and tests the trip chain periodically.
Güvenlik ağının eksik gerilmesi, can sim: A safety net that is not properly rigged, no lifebuoy at the access point, failure to monitor tide and draft changes, and inadequate lighting are the main causes of gangway-related falls and drownings. The AB must treat the access point as a fully equipped area that is checked continuously.
Güvenlik olayları yönetimi, kaptanın hem: Managing security incidents is an area in which the Master uses together the composure of command, humane responsibility and knowledge of the regulations. A prepared ship — drilled, with plans, connected to the reporting network — turns these incidents not into panic but into a controlled procedure.
Güvenlik zonları IGF Code (International: Safety zones are defined by the IGF Code (International Code of Safety for Ships Using Gases or Other Low-flashpoint Fuels).
Güverte bakımı, denizciliğin \"görünmeye: Deck maintenance is the "unseen heroism" of seafaring: when it is done well, nobody notices, because the ship stays sound, clean and safe; when it is neglected, it comes back as corrosion, accidents and PSC detentions. The hammer, brush and grease gun in the AB's hands are really tools that extend the ship's life and protect the crew. Quality, safe maintenance is possible with patience, the right sequence and disciplined PPE and risk management.
Güverte bakımı; sadece \"boya atmak\" de: Deck maintenance is not just "slapping on paint". It is a disciplined, systematic and continuous effort to prevent corrosion, extend the service life of equipment, pass inspections with credit and keep the team safe. The Bosun is the on-site leader of this effort; the Bosun's success keeps the ship upright, sound and certified for 10-15 years.
Güverte bakımının büyük kısmı korozyonla: Most deck maintenance is a fight against corrosion. The cadet learns the sequence of rust removal (chipping/needle gun), surface preparation, primer and topcoat application. Paint applied without proper surface preparation soon flakes off; cleanliness and dryness are therefore important. PPE (dust mask, ear protection, goggles, gloves) is used against dust, noise and chemical exposure.
Güverte departmanı tipik olarak Birinci: The deck department typically consists of the Second Officer, Third Officer, Bosun, Able Seamen (AB), Ordinary Seamen (OS) and cadets under the Chief Officer. The Chief Officer organizes navigational watch and cargo operation duties for the officers, while managing the ratings' daily maintenance and operational work through the Bosun. These two channels (watchkeeping system + day work system) must not clash; rest hours must be protected in both.
Güverte düzeni ve temizlik, denizciliğin: Deck housekeeping and cleanliness are among the least noticed but most life-saving duties in seafaring. An open escape route, a working scupper, a freely moving freeing port and a clean deck prevent accidents in routine work and make survival possible in a crisis. The AB's value lies in this continuous, quiet discipline, which stays invisible "when all is well" but safeguards the ship and crew in a fire, in a storm or at the moment someone slips.
Güverte düzeni, geminin Planned Maintena: Deck housekeeping is closely linked with the ship's Planned Maintenance System (PMS) and maintenance program; rust, cracks, broken railings and defective equipment noticed during cleaning are reported into the maintenance system. The AB is not "just a cleaner" but also an observer who detects defects; a small defect reported early prevents large maintenance costs.
Güverte housekeeping; gösteriş için deği: Deck housekeeping is done for life, not for show. A tidy deck means fewer accidents, faster emergency response, cleaner inspections and a more motivated team. The Bosun is both the architect and the guardian of this order; a good Bosun's ship is ready at any moment to receive even an inspector who arrives without notice.
Güverte operasyonlarına katılım, stajyer: Taking part in deck operations is the most tangible area in which the cadet turns theoretical knowledge into real seamanship. Every minute spent at the end of a line, at the anchor cable or at the winch builds both skill and vital safety reflexes. The cadet's duty is never to work outside supervision, to read the risk continuously and to record what has been learned meticulously in the TRB. The discipline acquired on deck forms the foundation of the safety culture of the future deck officer.
Güverte stajyeri vardiya zabitinin gözet: The deck cadet takes part in the bridge watch under the supervision of the officer of the watch, but has no authority to make independent decisions. In every situation, the cadet acts only with the OOW's approval. This hierarchy is not accidental: STCW VIII/2 sets out the principle that the officer in charge of the watch "is primarily responsible at all times for the safe navigation of the ship". The cadet cannot share this responsibility, but prepares for it through observation and limited practice.
Güverte tahliye delikleri (scupper), nor: Deck drain holes (scuppers) normally discharge rain/sea water overboard; however, during bunkering/transfer they are plugged (scupper plugs) to prevent a possible spill from going into the sea. The plugs remain fitted throughout the operation and any accumulated liquid is monitored; when rainwater collects, the clean water is drained off in a controlled manner.
Güverte tarafında en sık PSC bulguları:: The most frequent PSC findings on the deck side are: missing/expired LSA/FFE equipment, an incorrect muster list, emergency lighting not working, a damaged liferaft release unit (hydrostatic release), inconsistencies in records, poor hold/deck maintenance and incomplete permit-to-work files. The Chief Officer closes out these items with a self-check before arrival in port.
Güverte tarafında yağ kirliliği genelde: On the deck side, oil pollution generally comes from bunkering, leaks from hydraulic equipment (cranes, winches, hatch covers) and cargo operations. The Chief Officer verifies that scupper plugs are fitted before bunkering, that drip trays are in place and that the SOPEP gear is ready. Small amounts of oil spilled on deck are cleaned up immediately with absorbent and prevented from going overboard.
Güverte temizliği reisin yönettiği günlü: Deck cleaning is carried out according to the daily/weekly program run by the Bosun: washing off salt deposits (especially after a voyage and before painting), cleaning up spills, checking drains and general tidiness. Because sea salt accelerates corrosion, equipment on the open deck is washed with fresh water. The AB follows the program and reports when it is completed.
Güverte üstü paint, kumlama (grit), kayn: Paint, grit (from blasting), welding slag and other operational waste on deck are prevented from getting into the sea; during deck work, scuppers are checked and waste is collected.
Güverte üstünde taşınan konteyner, keres: Containers, timber, pipes, machinery or project cargo carried on deck are tested by the ship's motions, green water and wind loads. At intervals set by the Bosun, the AB makes a lashing round, tightens slack turnbuckles and reports any signs of damage or shifting. In bad weather, if going out on deck is risky, the check is made on the officer's decision, with safety of life as the priority.
Güverte üzeri su drenajı (scupper) tıkal: When the deck drains (scuppers) are blocked, water collects on deck; this is both a slip hazard and a cause of damage to cargo/stores. The Bosun checks that the scuppers are kept clean and clear. However, during tanker/cargo operations, scupper plugs are fitted because of the risk of pollution; the balance between these two requirements is managed case by case.
Güverte üzeri yük (container, boru, proj: Cargo on deck (containers, pipes, project cargo, timber) is directly exposed to sea conditions. On deck, the Bosun checks that the lashing pattern is correct, the dunnage is sufficient and the cargo distribution is in line with the plan. For special cargoes such as timber deck cargo, the requirements of the TDC Code are applied.
Güverte üzerindeki tüm hareketli/gevşek: All movable/loose equipment on deck turns into lethal projectiles in heavy weather. The Chief Officer checks the lashing of the pilot ladder, gangway, hoses, drums, welding equipment, store hatches and all loose items. Nothing is assumed to "stay put under its own weight"; everything is secured.
Güverte/rampa aydınlatması ve acil aydın: Deck and ramp lighting and the emergency lighting (including low-location lighting) are tested; defective fittings are replaced.
Güvertede bırakılan boya kutusu, takım,: Paint tins, tools, rope reels and equipment left on deck are secured (lashing/securing) so that they do not slide and become dangerous with the ship's motions at sea. Unsecured heavy items cause crushing or impact accidents, or slide overboard, when the ship rolls. The AB puts away or secures every piece of equipment not in use.
Güvertede scupper tıpaları (scupper plug: Scupper plugs are kept fitted on deck so that any spill does not go overboard; spills are collected with absorbent. Sea and air pollution (including VOC emissions) is prevented, and port/terminal rules are followed. Environmental violations lead to heavy fines and detention of the ship.
Güvertede yüksek basınçlı yağ kaçağı cid: A high-pressure oil leak on deck is a serious injury risk; hands or bare skin are never used to look for a leak. Hoses are inspected regularly for age, cracks and kinks.
Güvertedeki dağınık halat, takım, hortum: Loose ropes, tools, hoses, spills and unnecessary materials on deck are the main causes of slip, trip and fall accidents. These accidents account for a significant share of lost workdays and injuries at sea. By tidying the area after every job, putting materials back in place and cleaning up spills, the AB eliminates this risk at its source.
Güverteye binen su hızla tahliye olmalıd: Water shipped on deck must drain away quickly; otherwise the accumulated water (water on deck) endangers stability through both its weight and its free surface effect. The Chief Officer verifies that the freeing ports (openings in the bulwarks) and scuppers are not blocked and that the freeing port flaps (if fitted) open freely. The Load Line Convention makes these mandatory.
Güverteye dökülme olursa: önce kaynağı d: If there is a spill on deck: first stop the source (emergency stop), then limit the spread (absorbent kit, verify that the scuppers are plugged), clean up and report. Even the smallest amount of oil reaching the sea is managed by activating the SOPEP and informing the port authority. Procedure, not panic, is what counts.
Güç diyotları doğrultucu devrelerde AC'y: Power diodes convert AC into DC in rectifier circuits. Reverse voltage rating and current capacity are the selection criteria.
Power diodes are used to convert AC into DC in rectifier circuits. In the excitation system of a brushless generator, a rotating diode set is mounted on the rotor.
Güç türbini: Egzoz gazı enerjisini doğru: Power turbine: converts exhaust gas energy directly into mechanical power.
Güç yönetim sistemi (PMS) yük paylaşımın: The power management system (PMS) optimises load sharing.
Güç ünitesi, kontrol devresi ve ayrım dü: The power units, control circuits and separation arrangements are approved according to the size of the ship and the applicable paragraphs of SOLAS II-1/29. Seeing two pumps is not on its own proof of full independence.
Gıda alerjisi olan mürettebat üyesi, gem: A crew member with a food allergy should declare it when joining the ship (pre-employment medical / familiarization); the cook records this information. The main allergens are gluten, milk, eggs, peanuts, tree nuts, soya, fish and shellfish. The cook prevents cross-contamination in the meals served to this person: a separate cutting board, separate containers, and no shared oil/water.
Gıda güvenliği için depo sıcaklıkları dü: For food safety, the store room temperatures are monitored and recorded regularly; if the cold chain is broken, provisions spoil. Cross-contamination is prevented (raw meat kept separate) and the rooms are kept clean. The MLC requires sufficient and properly stored food.
Gıda güvenliği, görünmediğinde başarılıd: Food safety is successful when it goes unseen. A disciplined cold chain, measured cooking, barriers to cross-contamination and personal hygiene are the first line of defense for crew health in the closed environment of a ship, where a single outbreak can put the whole ship out of action. The temperature records and samples kept by the cook are the basis of both prevention and traceability when a problem arises.
Gıda güvenliğinin kalbi soğuk zincirdir:: The cold chain is the heart of food safety: the chiller (0-4°C), the freezer (-18°C and below) and the dry store (cool, dry) must be kept at their target temperatures. The cook reads these temperatures daily (usually at least once or twice a day) and records them in the cold chain log. A calibrated thermometer/temperature indicator is used; the equipment's own indicator is verified periodically against a reference thermometer.
Gıda güvenliğinin kalbi sıcaklık kontrol: Temperature control is at the heart of food safety. Bacteria multiply rapidly in the "danger zone" between 5°C and 60°C; food left in this range for a long time carries a risk of food poisoning. Hot food is kept at 60°C or above, and cold food at 5°C or below. Bain-marie and cold counter temperatures are checked throughout service.
Gıda israfı doğrudan maliyet ve aynı zam: Food waste is a direct cost and at the same time a MARPOL Annex V waste burden. The cook reduces waste through portion calibration, FIFO/FEFO discipline, safe reuse of leftover food and correct storage. Spoiled products are a loss of both money and nutrients; correct storage prevents this.
H&M poliçesi, geminin kendi gövdesine ve: The H&M policy is a property insurance covering physical damage to the ship's own hull and machinery (hull and machinery damage). It is typically built on standard sets of clauses such as the Institute Time Clauses (Hulls). Deformation of the hull caused by a collision, fire damage in the engine room, bottom plating damage after a grounding, or propeller or shaft damage are covered by H&M. Through the "running down clause" (RDC / 3/4ths collision liability), H&M can also cover a certain proportion of the damage caused to the other ship in a collision.
H&M poliçesinde bir muafiyet (deductible: An H&M policy has a deductible; small damage that stays below this deductible is borne by the ship or the company. The "sue and labour" clause (Marine Insurance Act 1906) provides for the assured to incur reasonable expenses to reduce the loss and for these expenses to be met by the insurer — the Master's efforts to limit the damage after an incident are important in this respect.
HACCP, gıdadaki tehlikeleri (biyolojik,: HACCP is a preventive approach that systematically identifies hazards in food (biological, chemical, physical) and manages them at critical control points (CCPs). The seven principles are hazard analysis, determining CCPs, setting critical limits, monitoring, corrective action, verification and record keeping. In the ship's galley, this brings every stage of the flow under control (receiving → storage → preparation → cooking → cooling → service).
HCP (Sıkı Paket Altıgen): Çinko, magnezy: HCP (hexagonal close-packed): metals such as zinc and magnesium have this structure.
HF, A4 bölgesinde tek güvenilir uzun men: In sea area A4, HF is the only reliable long-range alerting method; on polar voyages outside satellite coverage, the distress alerting function is lost if HF DSC is not kept operational.
HFC'lerin küresel ısınma etkisini azaltm: It provides for a phased reduction in the production and consumption of HFCs in order to reduce their global warming effect.
HFO arıtma sırası: Settling tank → Purif: HFO treatment sequence: settling tank → purifier → clarifier → service tank → engine.
HFO depolama/settling/service tankları v: HFO storage, settling and service tanks and the fuel heaters are heated with steam to lower the viscosity; on tankers, heavy cargoes (asphalt, crude oil) are made pumpable with heating coils. Overheating degrades the fuel or cargo; insufficient heating causes pumping problems.
HFO yaklaşık 130-150 °C'de servis edilir: HFO is supplied at about 130-150 °C, MGO/LSMGO at a much lower temperature. A sudden temperature change creates a risk of thermal shock, seizing and leakage in the fuel pumps and injectors. Therefore the changeover is carried out gradually and under control.
HFO yüksek viskoziteye sahiptir (genelli: HFO has a high viscosity (generally 180–380 cSt at 50 °C). Before use it must be heated to 130–150 °C to bring its viscosity down to 10–15 cSt.
HFO'nun viskozitesi 50°C'de 180-700 cSt: The viscosity of HFO is 180–700 cSt at 50 °C. For use it must be heated to 130–150 °C to bring its viscosity down to 10–15 cSt.
HFO, motorlarda kullanılabilmesi için ço: HFO goes through a multi-stage preparation process before it can be used in engines. This process consists of storage, settling, purification (purifier), the service tank, heating, viscosity control and filtration.
HFO/VLSFO için purifier (centrifugal sep: For HFO/VLSFO, the purifier (centrifugal separator) is operated at an optimum of 90-98 °C. The gravity disc / interface setting is made according to the fuel density. With the viscotherm, injection viscosity is kept within 10-15 cSt (if the fuel viscosity is low, cooling is required; if it is high, heating). An incorrect viscotherm setting causes injector wear and impairs atomization quality.
HMK yapı: α-demir (ferrit), krom, molibd: BCC structure: α-Fe (ferrite), chromium, molybdenum. Can become brittle at low temperature. FCC structure: γ-Fe (austenite), copper, aluminum, nickel. Ductile and easily formed. HCP structure: zinc, magnesium. Limited ductility.
HRU (Hydrostatic Release Unit): 1.5-4 m: HRU (Hydrostatic Release Unit): releases the bracket when it reaches a depth of 1.5–4 m; the EPIRB floats to the surface and is activated by water.
HRU değişimi, sal servisine denk getiril: HRU replacement can be timed to coincide with the raft service, but it must also be tracked independently. Incorrect installation (mixing up the weak link and the strong point, attaching the painter to the HRU incorrectly) leads either to the raft not deploying at all or to it being dragged down with the sinking ship.
HRU, gemi battığında yaklaşık 1.5–4 m de: The HRU is a pressure-activated device which, when the ship sinks, cuts the lashing securing the liferaft at a depth of about 1.5–4 m by water pressure, allowing the liferaft to float free. Most HRUs (e.g. Hammar H20) are disposable and are replaced every 2 years; the expiry date is printed on them. The Safety Officer records the expiry date of each HRU in the inventory.
HRU, liferaft kapsülünü krezete (cradle): The HRU automatically cuts the lashing that secures the liferaft canister to its cradle when the sinking ship reaches a certain depth of water (about 1.5–4 m), by water pressure. The canister is freed and floats to the surface; as the painter is still attached to the ship, the raft inflates automatically.
HT (yüksek sıcaklık) devresi ana makine: The HT (high-temperature) circuit circulates the main engine jacket water and typically works in the 80–90 °C range; the temperature is controlled by a three-way thermostatic valve. Running too cold leads to cold corrosion and fuel residue deposits on the liner surface.
HV elektrik kazasında, kurtarıcı önce ka: In an HV electrical accident, the rescuer does not touch the victim before isolating the source. The rescue is carried out after the circuit has been made safe; CPR and first aid for burns are given. The ETO knows the emergency procedure and the isolation points in the HV area.
HV sistemlerde gerilime asgari yaklaşma: On HV systems, the minimum approach distances to live parts are strictly observed. Insulating gloves are checked before each use with an air leak (inflation) test, undergo periodic dielectric testing and are worn with leather over-gloves for mechanical protection. The ETO keeps track of the certificate and test validity dates of the HV PPE inventory.
HV switchgear üzerinde yalnızca yetkin v: Only competent, specially trained (HV authorized) personnel may work on HV switchgear. The ETO gains this competence through STCW A-III/6 and vendor training; special equipment such as GIS (Gas Insulated Switchgear) also requires manufacturer-approved training.
HV ve yüksek enerjili sistemlerde izolas: On HV and high-energy systems, working earths (earthing/grounding) are applied after isolation as protection against residual/induced voltage. The ETO deliberately earths the section to be worked on with the earthing switch or a portable earthing set; in this way, accidental energizing or capacitive/inductive voltage does not endanger the person working. The earthing is removed as the last step when the work is finished.
HV çalışması, sıkı bir işlem sırasıyla v: HV work is carried out under a Permit to Work, following a strict sequence of operations: disconnect the load, open the circuit (open breaker), withdraw the breaker truck (rack out / isolate), lock and tag, verify the absence of voltage and apply earthing. Each step is taken in order and verified; skipping a step can have fatal consequences.
HV çalışmasında uygun sınıf yalıtkanlı e: For HV work, insulating gloves of the appropriate class (Class 2/3), an arc-flash suit, a face shield and insulating footwear/mats are used. PPE is tested regularly (glove inflation test); damaged insulating PPE is a life-threatening risk. The ETO checks the PPE before every use.
HVAC merkezinde bir soğutma çevrimi (chi: At the heart of the HVAC system is a refrigeration cycle (chiller or direct expansion); the compressor, condenser and evaporator remove heat with the refrigerant. The air handling unit (AHU) cools or heats the air, dehumidifies it and distributes it to the spaces through ducts. The return air is mixed with fresh air.
HVAC nemli yüzeyleri ve su soğutmalı kul: Damp HVAC surfaces and water-cooled towers are environments where Legionella can grow; regular cleaning, disinfection and filter changes are essential for health. A dirty filter reduces both air quality and system efficiency.
HVAC ve soğutma, gemi elektrik yükünün ö: HVAC and refrigeration account for a significant part of the ship's electrical load. The ETO optimizes energy consumption by running compressors and fans on load-following VFD control, by keeping the condenser clean (poor heat transfer increases energy use) and by not keeping set temperatures unnecessarily low. This contributes to the MARPOL Annex VI CII efficiency targets.
HVAC, yaşam mahallini konforlu ve MLC st: The HVAC keeps the accommodation comfortable and in line with MLC standards. Filter cleanliness, fan/damper operation and air quality are monitored. A clogged filter both reduces comfort and increases energy consumption.
HVSC yüksek gerilim taşır; interlock, to: HVSC carries high voltage; interlocks, earthing and LOTO discipline are followed strictly. Emergency disconnection is kept ready.
Haberleşme yöntemi önceden kararlaştırıl: The method of communication is agreed and tested in advance. Personnel inside give a regular "all OK" signal; if the signal stops, the emergency procedure starts. The Chief Officer makes sure that the standby person fully understands the duty.
Hafif slime tabakası bile sürtünme diren: Even a light layer of slime can increase frictional resistance by 7–10%. Moderate fouling causes a 20–30% and heavy fouling a 40–50% increase in resistance.
Haftalık general alarm testi, tüm gemide: The weekly general alarm test verifies that the alarm can be heard throughout the ship and that it works from the standby power source (battery). The crew are informed in advance, so that it is not mistaken for a real emergency. The PA (public address) system must work intelligibly on every deck and in every space; if dead spots are found, a defect is raised.
Haftalık lifeboat ve launching appliance: In the weekly visual inspection of the lifeboat and launching appliance, the lifeboat and davit are inspected visually, and the condition of the falls, the presence of the release gear and hook connection, and the visual condition of the embarkation ladder and brake are checked. If a deficiency is noticed, it is recorded at once and, if necessary, a defect is raised.
Haftalık ve aylık testler, emniyet siste: Weekly and monthly tests are the "pulse" of the safety system: when they are carried out regularly, the equipment is always ready, the records are continuous and inspections pass without problems. The Safety Officer's disciplined test schedule is the strongest guarantee against the surprise of "it didn't work" in a real emergency.
Halat ayarlarken usta gemici gergin hat: When adjusting lines, the AB does not stand on or in front of a taut line; they position themselves clear of the snap-back zone, at a point with an escape route. PPE is worn and care is taken against sudden changes in tension. Rushing with a line under tension can lead to a fatal accident.
Halat kesip iş halatı (heaving line, gan: Cutting rope to make utility lines (heaving lines, gantlines, lashings) is also part of store management. The Bosun does not waste leftover pieces; by heat-sealing or whipping the ends, the Bosun turns them into useful short lengths of rope.
Halat türleri: Polipropilen (PP), poliam: Types of rope: polypropylene (PP), polyamide (nylon), polyester, HMPE (Dyneema) and wire rope. The different types have different elongation and breaking properties; using them mixed is dangerous.
Halat winch drum'a sarılırken \"turn\"la: When the line is wound onto the winch drum, the turns must lie evenly without riding over one another; a riding turn causes the winch to jam and leads to loss of control. The Bosun checks that enough turns (usually 3-4) are on the drum and that the line is able to render.
Halatlar aşınma, kesik ve UV hasarı açıs: Lines are inspected for wear, cuts and UV damage; retirement criteria are followed through the line management plan. Tails and fenders are checked.
Halatlar aşınma/kesik açısından denetlen: Lines are inspected for wear and cuts, and the condition of the fenders is checked. Because of the frequent operations, the retirement criteria are followed closely.
Halatlar bollard'a (rıhtım babası) \"eye: Lines are put over the shore bollard by the eye; if there are lines from more than one ship on the same bollard, the "dip the eye" technique is used: the eye of the ship arriving later is passed up through the eye of the earlier ship's line from below, so that each ship can let go its own line independently.
Halatlar düzenli olarak elden geçirilir:: Lines are inspected regularly for abrasion, cuts, glazing (heat damage), internal fiber breakage and UV degradation. The MEG4 retirement criteria (replacement when residual strength falls below 75%) are applied. A worn line increases the risk of snap-back.
Halatlar toplandıktan sonra düzgün ranza: After the lines have been taken in, they are stowed neatly on the racks, the fairleads are cleared and the winch is disengaged. The Bosun brings the station to the "secured for sea" condition and reports to the bridge.
Halatın doğru sarılması ve istifi de bak: Correct coiling and stowage of ropes are also part of maintenance; a kinked rope wears quickly and creates a hazard during operations. The AB coils ropes neatly in a figure-of-eight or another suitable coil and stores them where air can circulate.
Halatın fairlead'den çıkış açısı (lead a: The sharper the angle at which the line leaves the fairlead (lead angle), the greater the friction and wear. In an ideal arrangement the line leaves the fairlead as straight as possible. A wrong angle both wears the line and causes uneven winding on the winch drum.
Ham petrol kendi tortusunu çözen bir çöz: Crude oil is a solvent for its own deposits; the heavy residue sticking to the tank walls (clingage) is dissolved by jets of crude oil under pressure and discharged with the cargo. This produces much less waste (slops) than water washing and lets more cargo reach the terminal (higher outturn).
Hamamböcekleri sıcak, nemli ve karanlık: Cockroaches like warm, humid and dark places; the galley, the dishwashing area and the stores are the main high-risk areas. They are very commonly brought on board in cardboard packaging, so provision cartons are not taken into the stores or are disposed of quickly. Control uses monitoring with sticky traps, filling cracks and crevices, rigorous cleaning (leaving no food source overnight) and, if necessary, gel bait/professional treatment.
Hamamböceği gıdayı patojenle (Salmonella: Cockroaches can contaminate food with pathogens (Salmonella etc.); their presence is a serious food safety threat. Since even a single insect may be a sign of an established population, a sighting is never underestimated and action is taken immediately.
Harcama kontrolünde \"total cost of owne: A "total cost of ownership" approach is fundamental to spending control: a cheap but low-quality (e.g. non-OEM) spare can turn out more expensive in the long run because of its short life and failure risk. The Chief Engineer sets the quality-cost balance according to equipment criticality.
Harita ve nautikal yayın yönetimi, seyir: Chart and nautical publication management is one of the invisible but most fundamental layers of navigational safety; a correct route is worthless when it is drawn on a chart that is not up to date. The Second Officer's task is not only to apply corrections but to keep all navigational information, paper and digital, complete, traceable and ready for the voyage. A correction routine carried out with discipline, promptly and completely, is the quiet but strongest defense that breaks, right at the start, the "uncorrected chart" and "unreliable source data" chain that recurs in grounding statistics.
Harmonik filtreleme için pasif filtre, a: Passive filters, active filters or multi-pulse rectifiers (12-pulse, 18-pulse) are used to filter harmonics.
Harness ve lanyard kullanım öncesi kontr: The harness and lanyard are checked before use: if there is cut or worn webbing, cracked or deformed buckles or karabiners, or rusty snap hooks that do not lock, they are not used. A harness that has been shock-loaded (has arrested a fall) is taken out of service. The equipment must be certified and periodically inspected.
Hasar fotoğraflanır, konum/zaman kaydedi: Damage is photographed, its position and time are recorded and a Letter of Protest is issued. The condition is documented by clausing the mate's receipt; the source of wetting (rain, hatch leakage, sweat) is identified.
Damage is photographed, its position and time are recorded and a Letter of Protest is issued to the party concerned. The condition is documented through the mate's receipt and clausing.
Hasar tespit raporları (survey reports),: Survey reports are the basis of compensation and of the apportionment of liability. The Master also documents independently the extent and nature of the damage observed by the surveyor; consistency is sought between the surveyor's report and the ship's own records. Whether the damage was "pre-existing" or caused by this incident is often disputed; for this reason the ship's regular maintenance and class records (to prove the condition before the damage) are critical.
Hasarlı conta veya compression bar su gi: A damaged seal or compression bar leads to water ingress; the cargo is wetted by rain/waves (hygroscopic/grain cargoes in particular suffer serious damage).
Hasarlı ekipman onarılmaya çalışılmaz (ö: No attempt is made to repair damaged equipment (especially slings and shackles); the standard is to discard the damaged item and replace it with a new certified one. An attempt to "repair it and use it" leaves an invisible weakness.
Hassas yüklerde yükleme öncesi ultrasoni: For sensitive cargoes, an ultrasonic test before loading is the safest evidence against wet-damage claims.
Hasta mürettebatın veya bulaşıcı şüphesi: The bedding of a sick crew member, or of a person suspected of having an infectious disease, is collected separately, handled with gloves and washed at high temperature without being mixed with other laundry. Mattresses and pillows are aired periodically; damp and mold are the most frequent complaints.
Hastanın gemide tedavi edilemeyeceği dur: When the patient cannot be treated on board, medevac (by helicopter or by diversion to the nearest port) is planned on TMAS advice. The Second Officer contributes to coordination with the MRCC, preparation of the patient, documentation and, if applicable, deck preparation for the helicopter operation. The decision rests with the Master; coordination is carried out together with the team.
Hat basınçlı tutulur (wet pipe); su deşa: The line is kept pressurised (wet pipe); when water is discharged, the alarm valve operates.
Hat doğrulandıktan sonra terminal limiti: Once the line-up is confirmed, the rate is increased to the bulk rate, up to the terminal limit; the IGS positive pressure is maintained. When a tank is 90% full, the rate is reduced to the topping-up rate and the final ullage is followed by manual/closed gauging.
Hat üzerinde basıncı koruyan jokey pompa: There may be a jockey (pressure maintenance) pump and a hydrophore tank that keep the main pressurised.
Hata zinciri yaklaşımı kurum kültürüne y: When the error chain approach is embedded in the organisation's culture, teams move from the question "who made the mistake?" to "which barrier did not work, and why?"; this gives sustainable safety.
Hatch coaming, track, bilge well, hold l: Hatch coamings, tracks, bilge wells, hold ladders and light fixtures are cleaned separately; these details often make the difference in an inspection. Cleaning the bilge wells and strainers is important for water drainage and cargo safety.
Hatch coaming, tuz suya en açık bölgeler: The hatch coaming is one of the areas most exposed to salt water. The Bosun plans periodic washing to remove salt/water accumulated in the drainage recesses. When the onset of rust is seen, a local touch-up is not applied straight away; surface preparation is done first (ST 3), then epoxy primer + topcoat are applied.
Hatch cover operasyonu sırasında ezilme: The risk of crushing and falling during hatch cover operations is high. No crew member may be between a moving cover and the fixed structure; a "no-go zone" must be clearly defined and supervised. Nobody stays under or in the path of a cover while it is moving.
Hatch cover panelleri, coaming ve güvert: Hatch cover panels, coamings and deck openings are monitored for corrosion; advanced corrosion creates both a structural risk and a tightness risk. The Bosun includes corrosion spots in the painting program and reports serious deformation to the Chief Officer.
Hatch cover su geçirmezliği hose test ve: Hatch cover weathertightness is verified periodically by hose test or ultrasonic test. Before heavy weather, it is checked that the drainage non-return valves are working and that the compression bars are making contact. This double check eliminates the most common cause of water ingress.
Hatch cover su geçirmezliği; rubber pack: Hatch cover weathertightness depends on the integrity of the rubber packing (seal), compression bar, drainage channel/non-return valve and the cleat/quick-acting cleat system. The Chief Officer regularly checks the seals for permanent set, the compression bars for corrosion and the cleat adjustment. On bulk carriers and container ships, water ingress means cargo damage and a stability risk.
Hatch cover sızdırmazlığı, ambardaki yük: Hatch cover tightness protects the cargo in the hold from seawater and protects the ship's integrity against water ingress. A leaking cover leads to cargo damage (especially grain, steel, sensitive cargo), mold/wetting and large claims. The Bosun knows that the maintenance preserving this tightness is, directly, cargo safety.
Hatch cover ve weather deck sızdırmazlık: Hatch cover and weather deck tightness maintenance is one of the Bosun's most concrete tasks in protecting the cargo and the ship from the sea. Clean gaskets, open drains, working cleats and sound deck openings ensure that the holds stay dry even in heavy weather and that the cargo is carried safely.
Hatch cover üstü (on-deck) istif, hold i: Stowage on hatch covers (on-deck) requires different lashing from stowage in the hold (in-hold); wind and wave loads are much higher on deck. When the tier limit is exceeded, a single lashing is not enough; double lashing or a lashing bridge comes into play.
Hatch cover'ın su geçirmezliği, geminin: The weathertightness of the hatch covers is a basic element of the ship's seaworthiness; water entering the hold damages the cargo and endangers stability. After closing, the AB checks that the rubber packing, drain channels, compression bars and cleats are correctly seated. Old or crushed rubber, rusty compression bars and clogged drains cause leaks.
Hatch cover'ın weathertight (su geçirmez: A weathertight hatch cover protects the cargo in the hold from seawater. The Bosun checks the condition of the rubber gaskets, compression bars, drainage channels and non-return valves. Water entering a loaded hold is critical, as it damages the cargo and causes stability/strength problems for the ship.
Hatch cover; rubber gasket, compression: The hatch cover consists of rubber gaskets, compression bars, cleats, hydraulic cylinders and drainage channels. Tightness tests (chalk test, hose test, ultrasonic test) are carried out by the Chief Officer + Bosun. Seawater ingress into the hold is a forerunner of major casualties such as the MOL Comfort.
Hava distribütörü, motor ateşleme sırası: The air distributor sends air to the correct cylinders in turn, according to the firing order of the engine. Air is admitted only to cylinders whose pistons are just past top dead centre.
Hava emiş filtreleri ve engine room vent: Air intake filters and engine room ventilation also affect performance; a high intake temperature (hot climate) leads to a wrong diagnosis if it is not evaluated with ambient correction.
Hava hattındaki emniyet supabı ve patlam: The safety valve and bursting disc in the air line prevent overpressure.
Hava işleme ünitesi (AHU): Hava filtrele: Air handling unit (AHU): filters, cools or heats, and humidifies or dehumidifies the air.
Hava muhalefeti, liman beklemesi (anchor: Adverse weather, waiting off port (anchorage) or a machinery breakdown can extend the voyage. The cook always keeps an "emergency provisions" buffer for a set number of days; he or she must be able to produce at least several days' additional menu from dry and canned stores. If the voyage is extended, portion discipline is tightened, waste is reduced to zero and durable ingredients are favored.
Hava penceresi (weather window) ve tide: The weather window and the tide window are assessed together; for example, entry into a bar harbor is tied to a particular tide time so that there is enough height of water. The Second Officer builds the time dimension of the plan by matching these windows with the ETA calculation.
Hava sakinleştiğinde Birinci Zabit güver: When the weather calms down, the Chief Officer carries out a deck inspection: hatch covers, lashing condition, cargo damage, water ingress, freeing ports and deck equipment are checked. Damage is photographed, hold soundings are taken and the necessary repairs/re-lashing are carried out. If there is cargo damage, a Letter of Protest and a damage report are prepared.
Hava sirkülasyonu için raflar tıka basa: Shelves are not packed full, to allow air circulation; circulating cold air keeps product temperatures uniform. The area in front of the evaporator and near the door is exposed to temperature fluctuations; the most sensitive products are placed away from these areas. The door is kept open for as short a time as possible.
Hava soğutucu serpantinde yoğuşan nem al: Moisture condensing on the air cooling coil is removed (dehumidification); if necessary the air is reheated for comfort. Too much humidity causes mould and corrosion, too little causes discomfort. Humidity and temperature are controlled by thermostats and humidistats.
Hava tahmini ve dalga durumu izlenir; ağ: The weather forecast and sea state are monitored; speed and course are adjusted in heavy weather. With Group A cargoes (which may liquefy), moisture and cargo behaviour are monitored and the route is changed if necessary.
Hava takibi, geminin ne zaman gideceğini: Weather monitoring is the discipline that tells not when the ship should go but when she should wait. The Second Officer's task is not just to read forecasts but to translate the data into the ship's specific sensitivities, see the worst-case scenario early and give the Master a clear, reasoned recommendation. Good weather monitoring is less about getting through a storm than about never entering it; this is the strongest safety strategy.
Hava uygun olduğunda seyir, rutin temizl: When the weather is suitable, the passage is an opportunity for routine cleaning and tidying; however, the safety constraints (harness, weather window, supervision) are tighter than in port.
Hava şişeleri (25-30 bar), ana başlatma: It consists of the air receivers (25–30 bar), the master starting valve, the starting air distributor, the cylinder starting valves and the pneumatic control circuit.
Hava şişeleri ve kompresörler safety val: Air bottles and compressors are protected by safety valves; a fusible plug releases the air at excessive temperature. If draining is not done regularly, condensed water may lead to corrosion, and accumulated oil to an explosion in the air line. The cadet learns the importance of the draining routine.
Hava şişelerinin doluluğu kritiktir: yet: The pressure in the air bottles is critical: without sufficient starting air the engine cannot be started, or maneuverability is lost. The cadet learns to monitor bottle pressure and the logic of automatic filling by the compressors.
Hava şişesi emniyet valfi, basınç şişeni: The air receiver safety valve opens when the pressure exceeds the receiver's design pressure.
Hava şişesinden gelen yüksek basınçlı ha: High-pressure air from the air receiver goes through the main starting valve and the air distributor to the cylinder starting valves; it is admitted to the cylinders in the correct order and turns the engine. Wrong timing or a leaking starting valve can cause a blowback or an explosion.
Hava, güç, thruster, PRS veya hortum ger: If the limits for weather, power, thrusters, PRS or hose tension are exceeded, the transfer is stopped, the lines are disconnected and the ship moves to a safe distance.
Havacılıkta 'sterile cockpit' kuralı kri: In aviation the "sterile cockpit" rule prohibits unnecessary conversation during critical operations. In the same way, focus must be maintained in the engine room during manoeuvring.
Havacılıktaki CRM (Crew Resource Managem: The CRM (Crew Resource Management) concept from aviation was adapted to the maritime sector as BRM. With the STCW 2010 Manila Amendments, ERM was added to the mandatory training syllabus for engineer officers.
Havalandırma sürekli çalışır; giriş boyu: Ventilation runs continuously and the atmosphere is monitored throughout the entry. The standby person waits at the entrance, keeps continuous communication and never leaves the post. No entry is made until the rescue plan and rescue equipment (tripod, winch, SCBA, resuscitator) are ready.
Havuz suyu filtre edilir ve klor/pH süre: Pool water is filtered and its chlorine level and pH are monitored continuously; circulation and water renewal are ensured. In water parks and jacuzzis, Legionella and microbiological control are critical.
Havuzlamada pervane yüzeyi parlatılır (p: During dry-docking the propeller surface is polished (for efficiency), damage to the blade edges is repaired and the balance is checked. On a CPP the hub sealing and the pitch mechanism are tested. The rope guard and the propeller boss are checked.
Hazır/işlenmiş ürünlerin etiketleri aler: Labels of ready-made/processed products are read for allergens; "may contain" warnings are heeded. When in doubt, the cook prepares a separate meal for the person with the allergy from basic ingredients known to be safe. In case of a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis), the location of the adrenaline auto-injector in the ship's medical locker and the telemedicine contact must be known.
Hazırlanan malzeme, kullanılana kadar uy: Prepared ingredients are kept at a suitable temperature until they are used; ingredients left at room temperature for a long time enter the danger zone. Raw meat/poultry is prepared last or in a separate area, and surfaces are sanitized afterwards.
Hazırlanan menü döngüsü ve haftalık menü: The menu cycle and the weekly menu prepared are usually submitted to the Master or the chief steward for approval. Approval is a checkpoint both for the budget (the daily victualling rate per person) and for crew satisfaction. The approved menu is posted in the mess room; this provides transparency and also strengthens the cook's daily preparation discipline.
Hazırlanan plan önce İkinci Zabit tarafı: The prepared plan is first reviewed by the Second Officer; the cadet's calculations, chart corrections and waypoints are checked. The plan is then submitted to the Master; until the Master approves it, the plan remains a "draft". The whole bridge team holds a briefing on the plan before the voyage; by attending this briefing, the cadet grasps the plan as a whole.
Hazırlık tamamlanınca Reis, ambarın iste: When preparation is complete, the Bosun checks that the hold is up to the required standard and reports to the Chief Officer. The condition is documented with photos/video; in a cargo dispute, this record is the evidence that the hold was handed over clean.
Hazırlığın en kritik ve en çok ihmal edi: The most critical and most neglected part of the preparation is preparing the crew for the inspection. Every crew member must be able to show his or her muster station, fire and abandon ship duties, and the use of the EEBD and immersion suit. When the inspector stops a randomly chosen rating (an oiler, an AB) and asks "what do you do when the fire alarm sounds?", an unhesitating and correct answer is the strongest proof that the system works.
Hazırlığın kalbi alarm sistemidir. Tüm k: The heart of the preparation is the alarm system. It is verified that all critical alarm setpoints are correctly set and active; the transfer of alarms to the bridge and the engineers' cabins (extension alarm) is tested. If any alarm is suppressed (inhibit/override), the reason for it and the risk are assessed.
Haşere yönetimi öncelikle önlemeye dayan: Pest management is based first on prevention: cutting off access to food (closed containers, cleaning up spilled food immediately), cutting off access to water and eliminating harborage points. Rodents (rats/mice), cockroaches, stored-product insects (flour/grain) and flies are the main pests on board. The cook detects infestation early through regular visual inspection: droppings, gnaw marks, eggs/larvae, odor.
Head line: Baş taraftan rıhtıma ileriye: Head line: a line leading forward from the bow to the quay. It holds the ship in towards the quay.
Head-up, course-up ve north-up gösterim: The head-up, course-up and north-up display modes and the difference between relative motion and true motion are concepts the cadet must understand clearly. The cadet learns how own ship's and the targets' true movements appear in north-up + true motion mode, and how risk of collision is more easily assessed in relative motion mode.

The difference between the head-up, course-up and north-up display modes, and between true and relative motion, is taught. In relative motion, own ship is fixed and the targets move; in true motion, both show their true movement. In assessing collision avoidance, reading the relative motion and the relative track is essential.
Head/stern line, breast line ve spring l: Head and stern lines, breast lines and spring lines restrain the ship's fore-and-aft and sideways movement; they are sent out in the order of the pilot's and Master's plan. The condition of the lines and their MBL/SWL are checked.
Heading (gyro) verisi özellikle kritikti: Heading (gyro) data is particularly critical: the radar ARPA, ECDIS, AIS and autopilot all depend on the gyro. The ETO keeps the heading distribution redundant (gyro + magnetic + GPS heading) and verifies changeover to the correct source in the event of a sensor failure.
Heading/speed input kaybında radar ekosu: When the heading or speed input is lost, radar echoes may still be present but the stabilisation and the reliability of the ARPA true data are lost. The user isolates the faulty layer, reverts to relative measurements and manual plotting or other radar and visual methods, informs the Master and records the fault.
Heat dedektörleri iki tipte çalışır: fix: Heat detectors work in two ways: fixed temperature (e.g. a 57°C or 78°C threshold) and rate-of-rise (sensitive to the rate of temperature increase, e.g. >8°C/minute). Heat detectors are used instead of smoke detectors in normally hot or steamy spaces such as the galley, the laundry and the engine room. Flame detectors detect UV/IR radiation and are used for fast-flaring fires in open areas such as a tanker deck.
Heated washing line, viskoz ürünler için: A heated washing line supplies water at 60–80 °C for viscous products.
Heating coil sızıntı testi yapılır (karg: The heating coils are leak-tested (water or steam leaking into the cargo causes contamination). The heat-up rate is controlled according to the cargo instructions and the temperature is kept within the target range.
Helmsman (dümenci) görevinde AB, OOW vey: As helmsman, the AB keeps the ship on the required course by repeating back the course/helm orders given by the OOW or the pilot and carrying them out correctly. Even when the autopilot is engaged, the helmsman stands by so that a change-over to hand steering can be made immediately in narrow waters, traffic separation schemes and maneuvering situations.
Hem stowaway hem de gözaltına alınan şüp: Humane treatment is mandatory both for stowaways and for suspects held in custody. The Master strikes the balance between the security of the ship and human rights within the framework of the regulations; excessive force, ill-treatment or putting the person in danger are unacceptable and create heavy liability.
Her FFE kalemi PMS'te bir job ile izleni: Each FFE item is tracked in the PMS with a job: monthly extinguisher checks, quarterly hose/nozzle checks, annual SCBA service, five-yearly extinguisher hydro-test and so on. All checks, maintenance and refills are recorded with the date + the person responsible + the findings. Maintenance without a record is considered "not done" in an inspection.
Her MLC kapsamındaki gemi, Maritime Labo: Every ship covered by the MLC carries a Maritime Labour Certificate and, attached to it, a Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance (DMLC). DMLC Part I is issued by the flag state and summarises the relevant requirements of national law. DMLC Part II is prepared by the shipowner and describes the concrete measures applied on board for each item in Part I; the flag state approves it.
Her Multi-Function Workstation, dokunmat: Each Multi-Function Workstation consists of a touch screen and an operator computer that runs silently because it needs no fan. Each MFW runs all applications in parallel and all are connected to redundant networks, which removes any concern about a single point of failure.
Her abandon ship drill'de muster, can ye: Each abandon ship drill includes mustering, correct donning of lifejackets, assembling at the lifeboat/liferaft stations, explaining the embarkation procedure and lowering at least one lifeboat. Lifeboats are launched and maneuvered in the water every 3 months (free-fall lifeboats every 3 months by free-fall or by the secondary means of launching; in addition, a free-fall launch or simulated launching at intervals of not more than 6 months). The rescue boat is launched and maneuvered in the water every month as far as possible, and in any case at least once every 3 months (SOLAS III/19).
Her acil durum görevi (yangın ekibi, fil: Every emergency duty (fire team, lifeboat, first aid) and muster station is assigned; at a crew change the muster list is updated and posted. Familiarisation is carried out.
Her acil durum ve drill, log book ve inc: Every emergency and drill is recorded in the log book and an incident report: what happened, what action was taken, what the outcome was, what lesson was learned. These records are used in class, insurance and company investigations and in future training.
Her akşam kaptan, ertesi 24 saatlik sefe: Every evening the Master writes specific instructions for the next 24 hours of the voyage in the night order book: the expected course alteration points, the expected weather, traffic information, when to call the Master and ETA updates. Night orders are the most practical tool for helping the officer of the watch with decisions during the night.
Her alarm tarihi, saati ve değeri ile lo: Every alarm is logged with its date, time and value.
Her ana filtrede bir diferansiyel basınç: Every main filter has a differential pressure (DP) gauge, which shows the difference between the filter inlet and outlet pressures. On a clean filter the DP is low; as particles accumulate, the DP rises. When the threshold set by the manufacturer (e.g. 0.8-1.5 bar) is exceeded, the filter is cleaned or replaced.
Her arayüz ünitesi, bağlandığı iticinin,: Each interface unit can be placed near the thruster, reference system or sensor to which it is connected. The result is a marked reduction in cabling, which means lower cost in newbuilding and better feasibility in a retrofit.
Her armatür için bir kayıp katsayısı (K): A loss coefficient (K) is defined for each fitting, and the loss is K multiplied by the velocity head. The K values of all fittings are added to find the total local loss, which is added to the friction loss.
Her ağır kaldırma öncesi plan yapılır: y: A plan is made before every heavy lift: the weight and center of gravity of the load, the equipment to be used and its SWL, the lifting points, the sling angle, the route of travel and the allocation of tasks are determined. The load is slung so that it is balanced; if the center of gravity is misjudged, the load rotates or slips. Soft edge protectors (softeners) are used.
Her bakım işi öncesi, ekip kısa bir tool: Before each maintenance job, the team holds a short toolbox talk: the steps of the job, the hazards (falls from height, sparks, chemicals, enclosed spaces, slippery surfaces), the control measures and what to do in an emergency are discussed. If the risk is high (work at height, overside work, enclosed space, hot work), a Permit to Work is also issued.
Her ballast alımı, deşarjı, BWMS treatme: Every ballast uptake, discharge, BWMS treatment and failure is recorded in the BWRB. The entry includes time, position, quantity and treatment status. Like the ORB, this book is examined during inspections and must be consistent with reality.
Her bağlama teçhizatı periyodik görsel k: All securing gear undergoes periodic visual inspection: deformation, cracks, excessive corrosion, damaged threads. A damaged item is removed from the inventory immediately and placed in the "out of service" box, so that it cannot come back into circulation.
Her belge türünün yasal saklama süresi v: Each type of document has a statutory retention period: the ORB 3 years, the garbage record book 2 years, the deck and official log books, depending on the flag state, generally a long time after the event. Completed books are handed over to the company and archived. At a change of Master (handover), all active and completed books, certificates and files of ongoing disputes are handed over to the new Master with a signed record.
Her bulgu için Baş Mühendis bir root cau: For each finding, the Chief Engineer draws up a root cause analysis and a corrective action plan. This aims not only to fix the problem but also to prevent it from recurring, and is entered into the company SMS.
Her büyük limanda P&I kulübünün bir corr: In every major port the P&I club has a correspondent (local representative). The correspondent is like the Master's eyes, ears and hands in that port: arranges surveyors, engages local lawyers, negotiates security, handles communication with the authorities and collects the necessary documents. When an incident occurs, one of the Master's first calls (with the company's approval) should be to the P&I correspondent in that port; the correspondent list is kept up to date on board.
Her changeover, ayrı bir fuel changeover: Every changeover is recorded in a separate fuel changeover log: date/time, ship's position (lat/long), changeover start and finish times, tanks/fuel types, ROB figures. During a PSC inspection, this record is the primary evidence of MARPOL Annex VI compliance. Entering an ECA before the changeover is complete is a ground for detention.
Her ciddi olay, filo için bir öğrenme fı: Every serious incident is a learning opportunity for the fleet. Corrective actions are applied not only on that ship but throughout the company. A modern safety culture focuses not on "whom shall we blame" but on "how can we strengthen the system". The Master's honesty after an incident is the basis for preventing future accidents.
Her cihaz tipi için IMO bir performans s: IMO publishes a performance standard (Resolution) for each type of equipment; for example A.424(XI) for the gyro compass and MSC.333(90) for the VDR. Equipment must be type approved to these standards and carry the "wheelmark". The Second Officer verifies that the equipment approval certificates and calibration documents are on board.
Her dedektör periyodik olarak gerçek uya: Each detector is periodically tested with a real stimulus: smoke detectors with test aerosol/smoke, heat detectors with a test heat source and MCPs with a test key. The test must verify that the alarm appears on the panel with the correct address/zone and that the sounders sound. SOLAS and the company SMS typically require a weekly panel check, monthly testing of a sample of detectors and an annual full test.
Her deficiency veya observation için ISM: For every deficiency or observation a root cause analysis is carried out under the ISM. Using "5 Whys" or similar methods, the managerial or systemic cause beneath the surface technical failure is found. For example, the root cause of the finding "the emergency fire pump did not work" is often not the pump itself but a maintenance item missing from the PMS, untrained personnel or an insufficient stock of spare parts.
Her deficiency, bir konu koduna (örn. 01: Each deficiency is linked to an area code (e.g. 01 certificates, 04 emergency systems, 07 fire safety, 10 safety of navigation, 15 ISM) and to one or more action codes. The action code says what the inspector requires of the ship: 17 = "rectify before departure", 15 = "rectify at next port", 16 = "rectify within 14 days", 18 = "rectify within 3 months" and, the gravest, 30 = "grounds for detention / ship detained".
Her denetimin odak alanı farklıdır: PSC: Each inspection has a different focus: PSC focuses on deficiencies and detention; vetting measures the risk profile; class checks structural integrity and the validity of certificates. Knowing what each inspection looks for, the Chief Officer prepares the documents and the physical condition of the ship.
Her denizci, imzalı bir Seafarers' Emplo: Every seafarer must have a signed Seafarers' Employment Agreement (SEA); one copy is held by the seafarer and one is kept on board. The SEA contains the identities of the parties, the start date and duration, the position, wages, hours of work, annual leave, repatriation rights, health and social security, and the conditions for termination. The Master verifies that the SEA of every seafarer on board is present, legible and valid; it is one of the first documents PSC asks for.
Her drill official log book'a ve ayrıca: Every drill is entered in the official log book and also in a detailed drill record. The record includes the date, drill type, scenario, participants, equipment used, observations, deficiencies and corrective actions. Under SOLAS III/19.5, the dates and details of drills are recorded; if a drill is incomplete or shortened, the reason is also recorded.
Her drill sonrası debrief yapılır: ne iy: A debrief is held after every drill: what went well, what needs improving, what deficiencies were identified. These outputs shape the scenario of the next drill.
Her drill sonrası debrief'te ortaya çıka: Organizational errors revealed in the debrief after each drill are reflected in a revision of the muster list and station cards. The Safety Officer updates all copies at the same time (the list on the notice board, the cabin cards, the bridge and MCR copies); an old version left on display causes confusion.
Her durakta beş duyu kullanılır: göz (sı: At every stop, all five senses are used: sight (leaks, levels, color), hearing (abnormal noise, knocking), touch (bearing/casing temperature — the limit that can be felt with the back of the hand is ~60°C), smell (burnt oil, electrical burning, exhaust) and the feel of vibration. This sensory check picks up early signs that no sensor can detect.
Her dış yardım salvage değildir. Gemi ac: Not all outside assistance is salvage. If the ship is not in immediate danger but needs assistance (for example being towed to port after an engine failure, a dead tow), this is carried out under a towage contract. BIMCO's standard contracts Towcon (lump sum) and Towhire (daily hire) are used for this purpose. The distinction between salvage and towage is important, because a salvage award can be much higher than a towage fee.
Her ekipmanda running hour counter bulun: Each item of equipment has a running hour counter, which is updated regularly in the PMS. When the running hour threshold is reached, the PMS generates a work order automatically.
Her enclosed space entry permit, atmosfe: Every enclosed space entry permit is archived with the atmosphere measurement results, instrument calibration record, standby assignment and entry/exit times. These records are among those most often examined in PSC inspections, vetting and accident investigations. The Chief Officer makes sure that the records are complete and reflect reality.
Her familiarization, şirket SMS'inde tan: Each familiarization is conducted using a checklist defined in the company SMS; each item is ticked off when it has been shown, and at the end both the new crew member and the person giving the familiarization (Safety Officer) sign. The signature is a statement that "it was shown and I understood"; in an ISM audit, this document is evidence of safe operation.
Her gemi hava koşullarına farklı tepki v: Every ship responds differently to weather conditions; a container ship is more susceptible to parametric rolling, a bulk carrier to deck flooding, a tanker to green water, and a ro-ro to list and cargo shift. The Second Officer knows the thresholds for wind, wave height (Hs), wave period and swell direction set by the company/for the ship type and interprets the forecasts against these thresholds.
Her gemi klas onaylı bir Cargo Securing: Every ship carries an approved Cargo Securing Manual; this manual contains the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) values of the lashing equipment and the approved lashing patterns. Annex 13 of the CSS Code provides a method of calculating forces for non-standardised cargo. The Master checks that the lashing plan is consistent with the manual and adequate for the expected weather.
Her gemi onaylı bir SOPEP (Shipboard Oil: Every ship carries an approved SOPEP (Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan); ships carrying noxious liquid substances have an SMPEP (which also covers them). The plan contains the reporting flow (coastal state, P&I, company), the response equipment and the allocation of duties. The Master is the person who makes the first report and coordinates the response when a spill occurs. SOPEP drills are held periodically (at least once a year).
Her gemi, bayrak devleti/klas onaylı bir: Every ship carries a Cargo Securing Manual approved by the flag State/class; this manual specifies how each cargo is to be secured and with how many lashings. The AB works to this approved plan, not to personal habit. For non-standard or heavy/high cargoes, the officer issues a special lashing plan.
Her gemi, gemiye özgü bir Garbage Manage: Every ship carries a ship-specific Garbage Management Plan, which defines how waste is to be segregated, stored, processed and delivered ashore. A person in charge of garbage management is appointed (usually an officer); the cook is the hands-on implementer of this system for galley waste and is obliged to act in line with the plan and to support the record keeping.
Her gemi, klas onaylı Cargo Securing Man: Every ship carries a class-approved Cargo Securing Manual (CSM). This manual contains the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) values of the lashing equipment and the approved lashing patterns and methods. The Bosun ensures that the lashing applied on deck complies with this manual; "improvised" lashing causes accidents and cargo loss.
Her gemi, klas onaylı bir Cargo Securing: Every ship must carry a class-approved Cargo Securing Manual. This manual contains the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) values of the lashing equipment, examples of lashing patterns and calculation methods. There are separate chapters for container, ro-ro, project cargo and heavy lift.
Her gemi, klas/bayrak devleti onaylı bir: Every ship must carry a Stability Booklet and Loading Manual approved by class/the flag State. These documents contain the hydrostatic tables, cross curves (KN values), tank capacity tables, free surface moment values, allowable bending moment/shear force envelopes and the standard loading conditions (departure full load, arrival ballast etc.). By comparing the actual loading condition with these standard conditions, the Chief Officer continuously monitors the safety margin.
Her gemiadamının, güvensiz bir durum gör: Every seafarer has the right (and the duty) to stop work when they see an unsafe situation. When a job becomes unsafe (missing permit, defective PPE, an unexpected hazard), the Oiler stops the job and informs the engineer; this is not "cowardice" but professionalism. No commercial/time pressure overrides this right.
Her generator breaker'ı bir dizi koruma: Each generator breaker is equipped with a set of protection relays: reverse power (32), overcurrent (50/51), under/overvoltage (27/59), under/overfrequency (81), differential (87) and, on large machines, negative sequence (46). The ETO sets the setpoints of these relays according to the class-approved protection coordination study and verifies them periodically with a secondary injection test set.
Her geçişin bir geri dönüş yolu olmalıdı: Every changeover must have a way back. If unexpected behaviour is seen in DP, reverting to joystick or manual control must be a movement that has been thought through and practised in advance. Regular testing of the independent joystick path is therefore an operational requirement.
Her güverte operasyonu öncesinde, ISM/SM: Before every deck operation, a risk assessment is carried out as required by ISM/SMS; by taking part in this process, the cadet learns to recognize hazards and the control measures taken. A Permit to Work (PTW) is also issued for work such as hot work, enclosed space entry, work at height and overside work. The cadet observes why a PTW is needed, which signatures are obtained and why the validity of the permit is time-limited.
Her haftalık baskı, o hafta etkilenen ha: Each weekly edition gives the list of charts affected that week (chart index) and the texts of the corrections. The Second Officer compares this list with the charts in the ship's folio and selects and applies only the relevant corrections.
Her haritanın sol alt köşesindeki \"Smal: The last NtM number entered on the "Small Corrections" line in the bottom left-hand corner of each chart shows up to which date the chart is corrected. The cadet learns to check this line before using a chart for navigation and to complete any missing corrections. The cadet understands that for larger changes made by block correction (tracing), the tracing must be pasted onto the chart in exact alignment.
Her hydrant'ta hortum ve çift maksatlı (: Each hydrant has a hose and a dual-purpose (jet/spray) nozzle. Hoses are pressure-tested regularly; the jet, spray and shut-off functions of the nozzles are checked. The equipment must be easily accessible and marked.
Her iki akışkan aynı yönde akar. Girişte: Both fluids flow in the same direction. The temperature difference is greatest at the inlet and decreases towards the outlet. The outlet temperature of the cold fluid cannot exceed the outlet temperature of the hot fluid.
Her iki sistem de \"compact operator sta: Both systems can be delivered as a "compact operator station" or a "console" version; the console version is available in several configurations to suit the need. The JX system can easily be upgraded to DP 0, because the thruster and sensor cabling and interface are the same in both systems.
Her iki sistemde de gözlem (observation): In both systems, if an observation is raised, it is closed out through root cause analysis and corrective action. The Chief Officer coordinates the closing of deck-related observations.
Her inspection'ın bulguları (foto dahil): The findings of each inspection (including photographs) are recorded and the trend is followed. A recurring finding (e.g. increasing deposits on a particular unit) triggers a root cause investigation. The Second Engineer uses these records to guide maintenance decisions.
Her istasyonun kendi ekipmanı ve kendi t: Each station has its own equipment and its own cleaning responsibility: color-coded cutting boards and knives at the cold preparation station, range/oven/deep fryer at the cooking station, bain-marie and hot-holding units at the service station. The cook sets up the mise en place according to this station logic; in this way a one- or two-person team can serve three meals on time.
Her izin, bir Job Safety Analysis (JSA): Every permit starts with a Job Safety Analysis (JSA) or Risk Assessment. The job is broken down into steps; for each step the hazard is identified and a risk score is calculated by multiplying likelihood by severity.
