Kaldırma donanımı periyodik olarak proof: Lifting gear is tested periodically with a proof load (a test load above the SWL) and documented in the Register of Lifting Appliances and Cargo Handling Gear (cargo gear register). Examination by a competent person is required by ILO Convention 152.
Kaldırma donanımı proof load testinden g: Lifting gear undergoes a proof load test and is documented in the Register of Lifting Appliances and Cargo Handling Gear; examination by a competent person is required by ILO Convention 152. The certificates are checked by PSC and in inspections.
Kaldırma donanımı; tel halat (wire rope): Lifting gear consists of wire ropes, blocks and sheaves, hooks, slings, shackles and swivels. Each item has its own SWL, and the weakest item in the chain sets the limit for the whole system.
Kaldırma donanımı; tel halat, blok/makar: Lifting gear consists of wire ropes, blocks and sheaves, hooks, shackles, slings and swivels. Each item has its own SWL; the weakest item in the chain sets the limit for the whole system. The larger the sling angle, the higher the load in each leg.
Kaldırma ekipmanı kuru, temiz ve korozyo: Lifting equipment is stored dry, clean and protected from corrosion; slings are kept hanging (not dragged along the floor), and chain blocks are lubricated and stored covered. Equipment left carelessly in a damp/oily environment deteriorates and is unsafe at its next use. Maintenance is included in the PMS program.
Kaldırma sırasında işaretçi (signalman/b: During lifting, a signalman (banksman), taglines, keeping clear of the area under the load and clear communication are essential. Snatch lifting, overloading and uncontrolled swinging are prohibited. Stability and list are checked during heavy lifts.
Kaldırma sırasında tek bir yönlendirici: During the lift, a single signaller (banksman/signaller) directs the operation with clear hand/verbal signals; mixed orders are dangerous. Absolute rule: no one stands under a suspended load or in its path. If a taut rope/chain parts, the snap-back is lethal.
Kaldırma ve taşıma ekipmanı güvenliği, m: Lifting and handling equipment safety prevents the most fatal accidents in the engine room. Meticulous checking of every sling, every shackle and every brake, correct slinging and the discipline of "never go under a suspended load" make working with heavy parts safe. A good Fitter is someone who lifts even the heaviest part in the safest way, does not use any equipment they have doubts about and keeps complete records. There is no shortcut here; there is only the right way.
Kalibrasyon kaydı her sensör için tutulu: A calibration record is kept for each sensor: the as-found and as-left values, the certificate number of the reference instrument used, and the date. These records are critically important at class surveys and in recurring fault analysis.
Kalibrasyon sertifikaları, denetimlerde: Calibration certificates are requested at inspections (class, PSC, company); the ETO keeps them in an orderly, accessible and up-to-date file (digital and/or printed). Each certificate is matched to its instrument; the certificate number and the calibration and expiry dates are recorded. A missing or expired certificate is assessed negatively at an inspection.
Kalibrasyon, bir ölçüm cihazının çıktısı: Calibration is the comparison of the output of a measuring instrument with a known reference standard to determine its deviation. A wrongly calibrated pressure sensor or gas detector leads to wrong decisions and safety risks. The ETO ensures that calibration is traceable to national/international standards; the certificate documents this chain of traceability.
Kalorifer (calorifier): elektrik veya bu: Calorifier: an electrically or steam-heated hot water tank.
Kalıcı düzeltmeler haritanın üzerine mür: Permanent corrections are entered on the chart in ink and remain in force. T notices report a temporary situation (e.g. a navigation light temporarily extinguished, a temporary buoy), while P notices give advance information on something that will soon become permanent (e.g. a new berth under construction). T&Ps are entered in pencil because they must be erased when they are canceled.
Kalıcı düzeltmeler standart hidrografik: Permanent corrections are entered using the standard hydrographic symbols (with reference to INT1 / NP5011 "Symbols and Abbreviations used on Admiralty Charts"). Violet (or black) fine-point ink is used; erasures or smudges are not acceptable, because the chart is a legal document.
Kalıcı seal değişimi genellikle drydock: Permanent seal replacement usually requires drydock or an in-water seal repair (possible with some types). The Chief Engineer records the leak, coordinates with class/the company and plans the repair.
Kalın metal kesimi için oksi-asetilen (g: Oxy-acetylene (gas cutting) or plasma cutting is used to cut thick metal. Cylinder pressures (oxygen/acetylene) and the flashback arrestors are checked; the acetylene cylinder is always kept upright. Before cutting, the surrounding area is made safe against fire.
Kalıntı yakıtlar: RMA, RMB, RMD, RME, RM: Residual fuels: RMA, RMB, RMD, RME, RMG, RMK – classified by viscosity.
Kam mili → kam takipçisi (follower) → it: Camshaft → cam follower → push rod → rocker arm → valve. The spring force keeps the valve closed.
Kamara temizliği \"yukarıdan aşağıya, ku: Cabin cleaning follows the principle "top to bottom, dry work before wet work". First the door is opened for ventilation (respecting the crew member's privacy is essential; personal belongings are not touched). Dusting then starts with high surfaces (tops of lockers, shelves, light fittings), tables and frequently touched surfaces (door handles, switches, telephone) are disinfected, and finally the floor is swept and mopped.
Kamara ve ortak alanlarda yangın/sigara: Fire/smoking safety in cabins and common areas is a valuable monitoring task that arises from the steward's constant presence in the accommodation. Ashtray discipline, fire door and detector awareness, reporting of risky appliances and early alarm protect the accommodation from being the area where fires most often start.
Kamaralarda izinsiz elektrikli alet (ısı: If unauthorized electrical appliances (heaters, high-power devices), uncontrolled multi-socket adapters or naked flame sources are found in cabins, the steward reports them immediately. These devices can cause overloading and fire. Company policy usually prohibits certain appliances.
Kamarot servis sırasında nazik, temiz ve: During service, the steward presents a courteous, clean and tidy appearance: clean uniform, apron on and, when necessary, gloves/hairnet. Untidiness raises food hygiene concerns. When coughing/sneezing during service, the steward turns away from the food and hygiene is maintained.
Kamarot yaşam mahallinde çok dolaştığı i: Because the steward moves around the accommodation a great deal, the steward may be the first person to notice signs of fire (smoke, smell, heat). In such a case, the steward raises the alarm immediately and acts according to the procedure. Early detection and a quick alarm prevent a fire from growing.
Kamarot çoğu zaman yaşam mahallinde tek: The steward often works alone in the accommodation and during quiet hours; the steward is therefore often the first person to notice smoke, a burning smell, abnormal heat or a water leak. Any abnormality is reported immediately to the officer of the watch/bridge; even a smell that seems "minor" is never ignored without being investigated.
Kamarot, Station Bill'e göre yaralı bakı: In accordance with the Station Bill, the steward may assist the casualty care party (stretcher, first-aid support) or the head count. As the steward knows the accommodation well, the steward plays a valuable role in checking cabins and confirming that no one has been left behind.
Kamarot, aşçının talimatıyla basit ön ha: On the cook's instructions, the steward does simple preparation: washing, peeling and chopping vegetables and fruit, weighing ingredients and taking them out of the refrigerator. Vegetables are washed thoroughly to remove dirt and any residues; this is part of food safety. Chopping is done to the size and arrangement the cook requires.
Kamarot, denetim öncesi son kontrolde öz: In the final check before an inspection, the steward reviews in particular the high-touch surfaces, the stock of consumables, the cleanliness of the garbage bins and the integrity of escape routes/fire doors. Order must be continuous; the essential thing is to maintain the standard every day rather than doing a one-off clean because "an inspection is coming".
Kamarot, hasta bakımı ve revir temizliği: During patient care and sick bay cleaning, the steward also protects their own health, using PPE and paying attention to hand hygiene. The steward's health is important for continuity of service and for protecting the rest of the crew.
Kamarot, kirli çamaşır ve kimyasallarla: When working with dirty laundry and chemicals, the steward uses personal protective equipment: gloves and, when necessary, an apron and mask. Hands are always washed after handling laundry, and especially after contact with contaminated textiles. The laundry is kept physically and operationally separate from food preparation; the steward pays attention to hand hygiene when moving between the two.
Kamarot, stok hareketlerini (ikmal, tüke: The steward records stock movements (resupply, consumption). This record shows the consumption trend and makes planning the next resupply easier. A regular inventory prevents both waste and shortages.
Kamarot, tıbbi sorumlu zabit (genelde İk: The steward works in coordination with the officer responsible for medical care (usually the Second Officer/Medical Officer) and reports changes in the patient's condition (not eating, fever, deterioration). Cleanliness of the sick bay and patient comfort are teamwork that complements medical care.
Kamarot, vardiyaya başlamadan önce sorum: Before starting duty, the steward turns their area of responsibility into a clear "cleaning route". A typical route starts with the officer cabins, continues with the alleyways and stairways, covers the messhall and pantry, and then ends with the common toilets/showers (common sanitary) and the dayroom/recreation room. To prevent cross-contamination, the basic principle is to work from clean areas towards dirty areas (cabin → toilet); work is never done in the reverse direction.
Kamarot; banyo/tuvaletleri, ortak alanla: The steward regularly cleans and disinfects bathrooms/toilets, common areas (mess, saloon, alleyways) and high-touch surfaces (door handles, handrails, switches). The correct disinfectant is used with the correct contact time; a hasty wipe does not disinfect.
Kamarot; gelen surveyor, denetçi, acente: The steward provides courteous and professional service to visiting surveyors, inspectors, agents and guests. Drinks/refreshments are prepared, the meeting area is set up and the guests' comfort is ensured. Professional hospitality reflects the ship's corporate image.
Kamarot; revirin zemini, yatak/yatak tak: The steward regularly cleans and disinfects the sick bay floor, berth/bedding, worktop, washbasin and instruments. Sanitation checks (ventilation, odor, hygiene) are carried out. Medical instruments and surfaces are kept clean so as to reduce the risk of infection.
Kamarot; temizlik kimyasalları (deterjan: The steward monitors cleaning chemicals (detergent, disinfectant, glass/surface cleaner), paper products (toilet paper, paper towels), soap/hand sanitizer, laundry supplies and general accommodation consumables. The current stock (ROB) and rate of consumption of each item are recorded.
Kamarot; çamaşır deterjanı, ağartıcı, de: The steward stores laundry detergent, bleach, disinfectants and cleaning chemicals in accordance with the SDS information. Incompatible groups (acids/alkalis, oxidizers) are kept apart, containers are correctly labeled and chemicals are kept in their original containers. A chemical stored unlabeled or in the wrong container is a serious accident risk.
Kamarotun temel ekipmanı; mikrofiber bez: The steward's basic equipment consists of a set of microfiber cloths, a mop and bucket system (preferably with two buckets, separating clean and dirty water), a broom, a vacuum cleaner, a squeegee, a set of brushes, a garbage trolley and personal protective equipment (gloves, apron and, when necessary, a mask). The equipment itself is also a hygiene factor: dirty cloths and mops become carriers of bacteria. Cloths and mop heads are washed and dried after each use and are not left to go moldy in damp, closed lockers.
Kamarotun yaşam mahalli temizliğindeki b: The steward's success in cleaning the accommodation directly determines the health and dignity of the environment in which the crew rest, eat and work every day. This work, which demands unseen meticulousness, is the cornerstone of the ship's quality of life, from infection control to fire safety and from MLC compliance to crew morale. Maintaining the standard every day, not just on "inspection day", is the most fundamental professional principle of the steward's job.
Kanal dönüşlerinde, görüşün engelli oldu: At bends in the channel and in areas where the view is obscured, the ship proceeds with caution and sounds one prolonged blast in accordance with Rule 34(e). Anchoring in a narrow channel is avoided. For overtaking within the channel, the officer applies the Rule 9(e) signal arrangement and agreement with the other ship.
Kanal sistemi: supply ve return; her mah: Duct system: supply and return; a grille/diffuser and damper in each space.
Kanal sistemi: İşlenmiş havayı kompartım: Duct system: distributes the treated air to the compartments.
Kanat üzerindeki basınç buhar basıncının: When the pressure on the blade falls below the vapour pressure, the water turns into vapour bubbles (cavitation); the bubbles collapse in the high-pressure region, eroding the blade surface (erosion), producing noise and vibration and reducing efficiency. Overloading, a damaged blade or a wrong pitch increases cavitation.
Kapak açılırken sıcak yakıt/yağ fışkırma: There is a risk of hot fuel/oil spraying out when the cover is opened; it is therefore verified that the pressure has been fully released, a drip tray is placed and suitable PPE (gloves, goggles) is worn. The cartridge is removed and its contents are examined (metal swarf, water or unusual residue is reported to the engineer), a new/clean cartridge is fitted, the O-ring is checked and the lever is left in the "standby" position.
Kapak kilitleme (interlock): Furnace kap: Door interlock: the burner cannot operate while the furnace door is open.
Kapak mekanizmaları: Açma/kapama ve sızd: Hatch cover mechanisms: opening/closing and tightness check.
Kapaklar hidrolik silindir, zincir veya: The covers are moved by hydraulic cylinders, chains or wire ropes. Once closed, the cleats and quick-acting cleats press the panels down onto the coaming and compress the packing. The weathertightness of the cover depends on this pressing force.
Kapaklar hidrolik/wire ile maker prosedü: Hatch covers are opened and closed hydraulically or by wire, following the maker's procedure; cleats, rubber packing and drainage are checked. On closing, all cleats are secured.
Kapalı alan girişi, kurallara harfiyen u: Enclosed space entry is an operation that is safe when the rules are followed to the letter and lethal at the slightest deviation. The Chief Officer's success lies in applying the permit-test-standby-rescue chain in full for every entry, ensuring the reliability of the instruments and instilling in the team the culture of "never enter without testing, never rush blindly into a rescue". This discipline directly saves lives.
Kapalı alan girişi, ölümlerin en sık yaş: Enclosed space entry is the type of work in which deaths occur most often; a significant proportion of the victims are second persons who go in to rescue. Before entry, O2 (a steady 21% by volume), LEL/flammable gas (target 0%), H2S and CO are measured with a calibrated multi-gas meter. Measurements are taken at different levels of the space (top–middle–bottom) because gases stratify according to their density.
Kapalı alan ile ilgili near-miss'ler (ör: Near-misses involving enclosed spaces (e.g. instrument failure, ventilation interruption) are reported and analyzed. The Chief Officer continuously reinforces the culture that "an enclosed space is never entered without testing". This culture is vital in an area where a single lapse in discipline can bring death.
Kapalı alan, giriş öncesi ve giriş süres: An enclosed space must be supplied with fresh air by continuous mechanical ventilation (forced ventilation) before and during entry. Natural ventilation is insufficient. Ventilation must reach all corners of the space (no dead zones), and if it stops, entry must be suspended immediately. The Chief Officer confirms the adequacy of ventilation by measurement; ventilation is maintained so that "the atmosphere stays safe".
Kapalı alanlar (tanklar, cofferdam, ball: Enclosed spaces (tanks, cofferdams, ballast tanks, bilges, chain lockers, boilers) may contain invisible lethal atmospheres: oxygen deficiency, toxic gases (H2S), explosive vapors (LEL) and carbon monoxide. Human senses cannot detect most of these hazards; therefore atmosphere testing before and during entry is vital.
Kapalı araç güvertesinde DG yangını hızl: A dangerous goods fire spreads quickly on a closed vehicle deck; segregation and access are never neglected.
Kapalı devre suyunun kimyasal şartlandır: Chemical treatment of the closed-circuit water prevents corrosion and cavitation erosion. The typical parameters measured are the nitrite/inhibitor level, pH and chloride content; the limits are taken from the ranges set by the chemical supplier and the engine maker.
Kapalı döngü iletişim (closed-loop commu: Closed-loop communication is used: the order is given → the receiver repeats it → the sender confirms. Standard terminology is used to prevent misunderstandings.
Kapalı döngü sistemde çıkış değeri sürek: In a closed-loop system the output is measured continuously and compared with the reference value (set point). The deviation (error signal) is fed to the controller, which applies a corrective action.
Kapalı mekan (enclosed space); sınırlı g: An enclosed space is a space with limited means of entry and exit, without continuous ventilation and not designed for continuous occupancy: ballast/fuel/cargo tanks, cofferdams, double bottoms, the chain locker, the pump room, empty holds, waste water tanks, and some cofferdams and void spaces. These spaces may have an oxygen-deficient, toxic or flammable atmosphere.
Kapalı mekan girişi hazırlığı, Reisin \": Preparing for enclosed space entry is the Bosun's most serious duty, one where "a single skipped step means death". Full compliance with the permit, continuous atmosphere monitoring, a standby person who does not rush in and a rescue team ready to act bring this invisible hazard under control and ensure that the team comes out alive.
Kapalı mekan kazalarının en trajik örünt: The most tragic pattern in enclosed space accidents is that people who jump in unprepared to rescue the first casualty also die; in one case, several people died one after another in a tank, each trying to rescue the one before. The standby AB's discipline of "alarm first, never enter without SCBA" breaks this chain.
Kapalı mekan standby ve kurtarma desteği: Enclosed space standby and rescue support is the most vital duty an AB can take on. A standby who waits attentively outside, never loses communication and, in an emergency, applies the protocol instead of instinctively diving in saves the life of the shipmate inside as well as their own. One lesson sums up everything in this duty: an enclosed space is unforgiving, and heroic rescues kill; alarm first, then entry with preparation. Here, discipline directly means life.
Kapalı mekan ölümlerinin ortak nedenleri: The common causes of enclosed space deaths are: atmosphere testing skipped or inadequate, "quick" entry without a permit, inadequate ventilation, neglect of the standby duty and loss of communication. Most cases began with the thought "I was only going in and out for a second" and ended in death.
Kapalı mekana giriş, sorumlu zabit (gene: Entry into an enclosed space is made with an enclosed space entry permit approved by the responsible officer (usually the Chief Officer). The permit states the atmosphere test results, the ventilation status, the entry duration, the job description, the standby and rescue arrangements and the communication method. The permit is time-limited and conditional; it is canceled if conditions change.
Kapalı mekânlardaki tehlike görünmezdir: The hazard in enclosed spaces is invisible and cannot always be detected by smell: oxygen deficiency, toxic gas (H2S, CO) or an accumulation of flammable gas. In low oxygen, a person can lose consciousness within seconds without any warning. That is why even a tank that "looks fine" can be deadly; entry is made only after testing and with a permit.
Kapalı sistemde sınırdan kütle geçişi yo: In a closed system no mass crosses the boundary; only energy (heat and work) can cross it. An example is a piston-cylinder arrangement: as the piston moves, the mass of gas inside does not change, but work is done through the change in volume and heat is added or removed.
Kapalı, nemli kamaralar küf ve kötü koku: Closed, damp cabins produce mold and bad odors. Ventilation is provided whenever possible, damp textiles are not put in lockers before being dried, and signs of mold are dealt with by early action.
Kapalı/kapalı mahaller (ambarlar, balast: Enclosed spaces (cargo holds, ballast tanks, cofferdams, chain lockers, empty tanks) are among the most lethal causes of accidents at sea; oxygen deficiency and toxic or flammable gas can be fatal. The cadet learns that an enclosed space is NEVER entered without a permit, without gas testing and without an attendant. Ventilation, gas testing (oxygen 20.9%, toxic and flammable gas limits) and a PTW are mandatory before entry.
Kapama sonrası compression mark (rubber': After closing, the compression mark (the even impression of the rubber) is checked; uneven compression indicates a gasket or bar adjustment problem. Cleating is done correctly and tightly; a loose cleat at sea means cover damage and water ingress in bad weather.
Kapasite testi, discharge sırasında rate: A capacity test is carried out by measuring the rate during discharge; falling performance points to seal or impeller wear. A high rate at a low level causes cavitation.
Kapatılmayan veya geç kapatılan iş emirl: Work orders that are not closed, or are closed late, fall into the "overdue" list. Too many overdue jobs damage both class CMS compliance and the impression given to PSC; maintenance is therefore recorded as soon as it is done.
Kapağı kapalı tutan cleating/securing me: The cleating/securing mechanism that keeps the cover closed (cleats, wedges, hydraulics) is lubricated and kept in working order. Cleating that does not hold may allow the cover to open in heavy weather and the hold to flood.
Kaptan değişiminde, gelen kaptanın gemiy: When the Master changes, the first days are vital for the incoming Master to grasp the ship, the SMS, the crew and the open risks quickly. An incomplete handover puts the new Master into a risk he or she does not know about; this is why the outgoing Master is obliged to make an honest and complete handover rather than hiding problems to "look good".
Kaptan için \"denetime hazır gemi\", den: For the Master, an "inspection-ready ship" is not a ship hastily tidied up on the morning of the inspection but a ship kept in an inspectable condition every day. When the discipline of the certificate matrix, the honesty of the self-audit, the depth of the root cause analysis and the genuine competence of the crew all come together, PSC and vetting are merely outside confirmation of this continuous preparation. The best Master is the one who saw and corrected what the inspector sees long before; for him or her the inspection is not an examination but the confirmation of a result already known.
Kaptan için temel ilke şudur: bir bulgu,: The basic principle for the Master is this: a finding recorded honestly is a manageable problem; concealed, it turns into a crime that ends careers and freedom. Preparing for an inspection does not mean "making an ugly truth look good" but "correcting the truth before the inspection and documenting it honestly". Falsification is a risk greater than any deficiency could ever create.
Kaptan kendisini köprüüstüne çağırma kri: The Master writes the criteria for calling the Master to the bridge clearly in the Master's Standing Orders. Typical criteria: if visibility falls below 2 miles, if the CPA comes within 1 mile, if the ECDIS fails, if bad weather develops differently from expected, on any equipment failure, before a narrow passage, before the expected pilot boarding time, and so on. This list must be tailored to each ship and voyage.
Kaptan komutayı pilota devretmez. Pilotu: The Master does not hand over command to the pilot. The pilot's advice is assessed professionally; advice contrary to safety is rejected. The pilot is an adviser who does not know the ship; the Master is the person who knows the ship best.
Kaptan ve SSO, SSAS test prosedürünü (ge: The Master and the SSO know the SSAS test procedure (usually coordinated in advance with the authorities) and test the system periodically. An SSAS alert triggered by mistake must be cancelled at once by notifying the centres concerned; otherwise an unnecessary search and rescue operation or military intervention may be triggered. The SSAS message contains the ship's identity, its position and an indication that its security is under threat.
Kaptan ve SSO, SSP'nin güncel, manipülas: The Master and the SSO ensure that the SSP is up to date and protected against tampering (with authorised access if it is electronic), and that the security equipment on board (CCTV, lighting, access barriers, metal detector) is in working order. The Continuous Synopsis Record (CSR — SOLAS XI-1/5) keeps the ship's "identity history" (flag, name, owner, ISM/ISPS certificate history) and is kept on board.
Kaptan ve zabitler, stajyere yapılandırı: The Master and officers give the cadet structured training modules. The cadet completes them, asks questions and records what was learned in the TRB. Active participation — doing and asking rather than watching — makes learning last.
Kaptan, \"general impression\" faktörünü: The Master must not underestimate the "general impression" factor: a rusty deck, lighting that does not work, an untidy lifeboat station, watertight doors left open, a dirty engine room — all of these give the inspector the impression that "the system on this ship is weak" and deepen the inspection. The impression made in the first 15 minutes sets the tone and the length of the inspection.
Kaptan, B/L imzalanmadan önce yükün mikt: Before the B/L is signed, the Master has the quantity and apparent condition of the cargo checked against the documents. The Chief Officer's and tally records, draft survey or ullage measurements and the Mate's Receipt are the basis of this verification. If there is visible damage, a shortage or a discrepancy, the B/L is claused (a remark is added).
Kaptan, BWMS'in çalışır durumda olduğunu: The Master checks that the BWMS is in working order, that D-2 compliance is achieved and that the BWRB is kept correctly. The USA (USCG) has its own approval regime; ships entering US waters need additional compliance.
Kaptan, D&A programının tüm ayak izini k: The Master keeps a record of the whole footprint of the D&A programme: signed policy and familiarisation forms, the random test selection method and results, observation reports for for-cause and post-incident tests, breathalyser calibration documents, records of test kit stock and expiry dates, and correspondence on positive results. These records must be ready both for internal audits and for PSC and vetting.
Kaptan, DMLC Part II'yi günlük yönetimin: The Master uses DMLC Part II like a "user manual" for daily management: it states which procedure and which form are applied, and how often, on each subject. If a PSC inspector finds a contradiction between what is observed on board and the DMLC Part II declaration, this counts as a non-conformity. Even if the certificate is valid, the ship can be detained if there is an actual violation.
Kaptan, DPA'ya ulaşmak için hiçbir izne: The Master needs no permission to reach the DPA and can do so 24/7, day and night. The DPA's contact details (telephone, e-mail, satellite line) must be posted visibly on the bridge and in the SMS documentation. PSC inspectors often ask "who is the DPA and where is the number?"; crew not knowing this can be raised as an ISM non-conformity.
Kaptan, Giglio Adası'na yakın \"salute\": The ship ran aground while the Master was making a "salute" maneuver close to Giglio Island. 32 dead. The investigation revealed an unsafe distance off the coast and deficient BRM.
Kaptan, ISPS güvenlik kayıtlarını (güven: The Master keeps the ISPS security records (changes of security level, DoS documents, security drills and exercises, equipment tests, incident reports) for the specified minimum period and keeps them available for PSC and security inspections. Security drills are held at least every three months, and more comprehensive exercises (with the participation of the company or the PFSO) at least once a year.
Kaptan, ORB kayıtlarını periyodik olarak: The Master signs the ORB entries periodically and checks the accuracy of every page. A "magic pipe" (an OWS bypass) is the gravest environmental crime; the Master's duty is to guarantee that no such system exists on board and that the records match the actual operations exactly.
Kaptan, SOF'taki çelişkili veya gemi ale: Before signing, the Master corrects any contradictory entry or entry against the ship in the SOF; if it is not corrected, he or she signs with the remark "signed under protest, time as per ship's log". This remark ensures that the ship's records are taken as the basis in any later arbitration.
Kaptan, Sea Protest'i not ettirirken (no: When noting the Sea Protest, the Master reserves the right to extend it later; additional evidence is then submitted in an "extended" protest. A Sea Protest does not by itself remove liability; as a formal and timely declaration, however, it places on record the ship's good faith and the facts. The Master applies protest practice under company/P&I guidance.
Kaptan, acente aracılığıyla yürütülse de: Although the FAL documents are handled through the agent, the Master must check their content because he or she signs them personally. In particular, undeclared tobacco, alcohol or cash in the Ship's Stores and Crew's Effects declarations leads to heavy fines ("manifest violation") in the USA and many other countries. Passport and seaman's book details in the Crew List are critical for immigration.
Kaptan, acenteye pre-arrival mesajı ile: Through a pre-arrival message the Master informs the agent of the ETA, draught, gross and net tonnage, the last 10 ports, the crew list, waste quantities, supply requirements and special requests (MEDEVAC, repatriation, spare parts). He or she asks for all the agent's expenses to be documented transparently with the PDA/FDA (Proforma / Final Disbursement Account) and questions suspicious items.
Kaptan, beklenen PSC veya vetting öncesi: Before an expected PSC inspection or vetting, the Master carries out a systematic internal audit using the ship's own VIQ/RISQ/PSC checklist. This audit covers the deck, the engine room, the life-saving appliances (LSA), the fire-fighting appliances (FFA), the bridge, the paper and electronic records and the competence of the crew. The findings are entered in a "snag list"; each item is assigned to a responsible person and a deadline.
Kaptan, bilişsel tuzaklara (tunnel visio: The Master must be alert to cognitive traps (tunnel vision, plan continuation bias, fixation on a wrong picture of the situation). As in the El Faro case, clinging to the first plan when it is no longer valid is fatal. Keeping the "challenge and response" culture on the bridge during a crisis as well is the strongest safeguard covering the Master's blind spots; an officer being able to say "shouldn't we reconsider this?" saves lives in a crisis.
Kaptan, bir bulgunun action kodunu rapor: The Master must always read the action code of a finding before signing the report, because the difference between "rectify before departure" (17) and "detained" (30) is an operational and commercial chasm that keeps the ship from sailing. A code 30 is a sign not only of that finding but of a systemic doubt about the safe operation of the ship.
Kaptan, bu sürecin \"tek karar verici\": The Master knows that in this process he or she is not the "sole decision-maker" but the "manager on site and the one who reports". The safety decision (removal from duty) belongs to the Master at once; but termination of employment and legal representation are handled together with the company. This clarity both protects the Master and ensures that the seafarer's rights are protected.
The Master approves the cargo plan with his or her signature. This signature is not a formality; it is written evidence that the Master has actually reviewed the plan for consistency with the ship type, the charter party terms and the strength curves. In a dispute, the record that "the Master saw and approved the plan" is evidence that both protects and binds.
Kaptan, denetim öncesi bir \"tatbikat br: Before the inspection the Master holds a preparation briefing: with crew members who face a language barrier, the English wording of the key answers is refreshed, and the location and testing of critical equipment are repeated. But this is not imposing rote learning; it is reminding people of what they really know, because an answer learned by heart but not understood falls apart at the first follow-up question and creates distrust in the inspector.
Kaptan, denetim öncesi bir self-assessme: Before an inspection the Master carries out a self-assessment (PSC self-assessment) and closes beforehand the items that frequently lead to detention (defects in LSA/FFA equipment, missing records, emergency equipment not working, security gaps). A serious systemic ISM finding leads to the ship being detained and the company falling into "targeted" status, which brings an additional inspection burden on the whole fleet.
Kaptan, denetim öncesi kendi MLC dosyası: Before an inspection the Master keeps his or her own MLC file ready (certificate, DMLC Parts I and II, sample SEAs, rest hour records, payroll, accommodation inspection records, complaint procedure). Consistent and honest records speed up the inspection; contradictory or incomplete records create a risk of detention. Findings that can be corrected are closed in port; serious or repeated violations get the ship detained.
Kaptan, durumu doğru sınıflandırır: gerç: The Master classifies the situation correctly: if there is no real peril and negotiation is possible, a towage contract is preferred because it has a known and fixed cost. However, if the situation deteriorates during a towage operation and a real peril arises, it can turn into salvage. The Master coordinates the type of contract and the basis of payment with the company and the P&I club.
Kaptan, gemi ve şirket adına hukuki süre: The Master is the primary point of contact on site for legal proceedings on behalf of the ship and the company. After an incident, notices from courts or authorities (writ, arrest warrant, subpoena), requests for investigation from the port or coastal state and legal correspondence from the other party reach the Master first. Before signing or replying to these documents, the Master always contacts the company and the FD&D or legal department of the P&I club. A hasty signature or statement can weaken the ship's legal position.
Kaptan, geminin kurtarılabilir mi yoksa: When deciding whether the ship can be saved or must be abandoned, the Master must read the time correctly: abandoning too early can cause unnecessary loss of life, abandoning too late can be fatal. The principle "the ship carries the people, not the people the ship" is the guide; but if staying on board is still safer than a liferaft (the ship being a rescue platform as long as it does not sink), the Master weighs this too.
Kaptan, geminin yasal temsilcisidir (mas: The Master is the legal representative of the ship (master as agent). A document the Master signs is not just a confirmation; it is a legal undertaking binding the ship, the shipowner and in some cases the charterer. The signature on a bill of lading (B/L) starts the contract of carriage, the signature on the NOR starts the laytime clock, and a letter of protest is a declaration reserving rights against the other party. The Master must therefore know the legal consequence of every document he or she signs.
Kaptan, gemiye yeni katılan her personel: The Master checks that familiarisation is carried out in accordance with the SMS for every new crew member joining the ship; this is a direct requirement of ISM section 6. No one may be assigned to a watch or a critical operation until familiarisation is complete. This check is an area that PSC and vetting inspections often look at, especially on ships with high crew turnover.
Kaptan, gerektiğinde \"can test\" (IMSBC: When necessary, the Master has the "can test" (the IMSBC complementary test) carried out and does not rely blindly on the shipper's TML declaration. In the Bulk Jupiter case (2015) a bauxite cargo with too high a moisture content lost its stability (the phenomenon later described as dynamic separation); the ship capsized and 18 people died.
Kaptan, göreve özgü familiarization'ı bi: The Master runs duty-specific familiarisation through a checklist and a responsible senior officer (the chief officer for the deck, the chief engineer for the engine room). The critical point is timing: a person may take on a duty alone (e.g. a solo navigational watch) only after familiarisation has been completed and his or her competence confirmed. The "he will learn on his first watch" approach is unacceptable.
Kaptan, haksız gördüğü bir detention'a k: The Master can use the right of appeal against a detention he or she considers unjust through the flag state and the company; but moving the ship without the inspector's permission during this process is a serious violation. The appeal, too, proceeds with documents and reasons.
Kaptan, ilaç dolabının envanterini, son: The Master checks the inventory of the medicine chest, the expiry dates and the narcotics records; missing or expired medicines are replaced in port. In a serious case, TMAS is consulted and, if necessary, a MEDEVAC is arranged (by helicopter or by deviating to the nearest port); this decision lies within the Master's overriding authority and is taken despite any commercial loss.
Kaptan, kadronun yorgunluk seviyesini sü: The Master continuously monitors the fatigue level of the crew; the STCW A-VIII/1 and MLC limits (at least 10 hours of rest in 24 hours, at least 77 hours in 7 days) are only a floor, not a target. Intensive port rotations, frequently broken watches and critical operations (cargo, anchoring, canal) increase fatigue cumulatively. Before critical operations the Master actually verifies that the key personnel are rested.
Kaptan, kendi \"Master's Review\" (ISM): The Master includes MLC compliance in his or her own Master's Review (ISM) process and reports the deficiencies found and the corrective actions to the DPA. The MLC becomes sustainable when it is managed together with the ISM; keeping the two systems apart creates duplicate records and gaps.
Kaptan, kriz boyunca bir olay günlüğü (i: Throughout the crisis the Master keeps an incident log: time-stamped decisions, messages and changes in the situation. This record both makes operational coordination easier and is critical evidence for the subsequent investigation, insurance and legal proceedings. Memory is unreliable in a crisis; a written record is reliable.
Kaptan, müdahale ekibinin güvenliğini ya: The Master considers the safety of the response team as important as putting out the fire. The SCBA air time is monitored (BA control — the air control board), the team enters in pairs, and a withdrawal signal and a back-up team are ready. Because of the risk of re-ignition, the area continues to be watched and its temperature monitored after the fire has been extinguished. The principle is not one person's heroics but a disciplined response that can always be withdrawn.
Kaptan, mürettebatın dinlenme ve toparla: The Master looks after the crew's need for rest and recovery (including MLC rest hours). Returning to normal operations with an exhausted team after a crisis invites new errors; if necessary, additional personnel or port support is requested.
Kaptan, mürettebatın refahını (welfare): The Master must treat the welfare of the crew — long contracts, missing their families, isolation, mental health — as a visible priority. An open-door policy, a complaint procedure that really works and a person's ability to raise his or her voice safely when struggling are required by the MLC and are the basis of operational safety. A happy and respected crew is a safe crew.
Kaptan, müster listesinin (muster list —: The Master confirms that the muster list (SOLAS III/8) is up to date, that every crew member knows his or her duties in an emergency (fire party, rescue party, first aid, preparing liferafts) and that the equipment assignments (radios, EEBDs, hoses) are correct. When the crew changes, the muster list is updated at once.
Kaptan, olaydan hemen sonra delilleri si: Immediately after an incident the Master systematically preserves and collects the evidence: deck and engine log book entries (time-stamped and true), the bell book / movement book, ECDIS and radar records, the data of the VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) saved and preserved, the GMDSS log, weather reports, photographs and video, and the crew's notes as witnesses. If the VDR record is not saved immediately after the incident, it can be overwritten and lost; securing the VDR is therefore a priority of the first minutes.
Kaptan, olayın tüm zaman çizelgesini (lo: The Master preserves the whole timeline of the event (log, ECDIS replay, statements of the lookouts) and prepares for a formal sea protest. The lesson of the Wakashio case is clear: deviating from the passage plan for personal reasons (closing the coast) is a trigger of major accidents. Crisis management covers not only the moment of the event but also the records and the legal process afterwards.
Kaptan, periyodik konaklama denetimi (ac: The Master carries out periodic accommodation inspections; the MLC requires these inspections to be carried out frequently (generally at least weekly, regularly under most SMSs) and recorded. The inspection covers cleanliness, working fittings, pest and rodent control, and the condition of the laundry and the hospital. Findings are closed with corrective action.
Kaptan, pilotun bir hareketinin gemiyi t: If the Master becomes convinced that an action of the pilot endangers the ship, he or she intervenes at once and, if necessary, takes the con directly. This is not disrespect towards the pilot but the Master's legal duty. The event is recorded.
Kaptan, repatriation hakkı doğan denizci: For a seafarer whose right to repatriation has arisen, the Master coordinates with the agent and the company; the air ticket, visa, transit and settlement of wages are arranged. During the COVID-19 period hundreds of thousands of seafarers were stranded on ships because of the "crew change crisis"; this was a period in which the MLC's repatriation provision was tested on a global scale, and joint IMO/ILO statements stressed seafarers' status as "key workers".
Kaptan, resmi soruşturma (flag, coastal,: The Master is honest in statements to official investigations (flag, coastal state, MAIB) but knows the right to avoid, without legal advice, statements amounting to an admission of guilt. In many countries the criminalisation of the Master after an accident (criminalization of seafarers) is a real risk; the P&I "loss prevention" department provides legal support on this.
Kaptan, sefer çıkışından önce lashing ti: Before departure the Master confirms that the tightening of the lashings has been completed and that the "lashing certificate" (where applicable) is ready. On voyages where bad weather is expected, he or she gives instructions for additional lashing. For heavy lift and project cargo, an engineering calculation and class approval are required.
Kaptan, sertifikaların (Safety Construct: The Master tracks the validity dates and survey windows of the certificates (Safety Construction, Safety Equipment, Safety Radio, IOPP, ISM/SMC, ISSC, MLC/DMLC); an expired or conditional certificate is a reason for PSC detention. "Condition of class" (CoC) items identified in communication with the class surveyor are closed in time.
Kaptan, taciz/zorbalık iddialarını ciddi: The Master takes allegations of harassment or bullying seriously and investigates them confidentially and fairly, protecting the victim and preventing retaliation. With the growing number of women seafarers, sexual harassment and a safe environment have come to the fore; many companies now provide a clear zero-tolerance policy and reporting channels (including off-ship and anonymous lines). Good welfare management means creating a safe climate in which problems are not hidden.
Kaptan, tehlike (peril) durumunda LOF im: In a situation of peril the Master has the authority to sign LOF; but where possible he or she first contacts the company and the P&I and H&M insurers. If time is critical and there is no communication, the Master signs LOF for the safety of the ship and crew — this authority is supported by the priority given to safety in SOLAS and by maritime custom. After signing, the company and the insurers are informed at once.
Kaptan, tüm bulgu-RCA-CA/PA döngüsünü şi: The Master enters the whole finding–RCA–CA/PA cycle into the company's SMS reporting system (usually a non-conformity / CAR form) and passes it to the DPA. This record is not just a bureaucratic requirement; it is the concrete answer to the question "how did you close your last finding?" at the next inspection, and an input to the company's management review. Unclosed actions come up again and again at vetting and PSC.
Kaptan, vardiya planını (watch system) b: The Master sets up the watch system in the light of these limits and has the rest hour records kept daily. Port operations, drills, PSC/vetting inspections and emergencies carry a high risk of upsetting rest hours. Fatigue is among the leading causes of accidents in MAIB reports; the Master plans honestly so as not to create a crew that is "compliant on paper but tired in reality".
Kaptan, vetting öncesi bir iç denetimle: Before vetting, the Master closes the gaps in the programme with an internal audit (self-assessment): an expired calibration, missing familiarisation signatures and unrecorded random tests are the most common findings. This preparation considerably reduces the stress of the inspection day and the number of observations.
Kaptan, voyage charter'da SOF'u (Stateme: Under a voyage charter the Master keeps the SOF (Statement of Facts) meticulously: NOR tendered/accepted times, pilot on/off, all fast, hose connected, commenced/completed loading, weather stoppages, equipment breakdowns. The demurrage/despatch calculation is made entirely from these records. Every "remark" in the SOF signed with the charterer's surveyor can make a difference of thousands of dollars later.
Kaptan, şikâyetleri kayda geçirir, taraf: The Master records complaints and deals with them impartially and on time, and protects the seafarer's right to be accompanied or represented. The procedure includes the flag state's contact details and those of the port state authority; PSC checks whether the complaint procedure includes these final levels. A well-managed complaint procedure prevents small problems from turning into a major crisis (ITF intervention, PSC detention).
Kaptan; Notice of Readiness (NOR — gemin: The Master approves or authorises the Notice of Readiness (NOR — notice that the ship is ready to load or discharge, which starts laytime), the Statement of Facts (SOF — the timeline of operations), the cargo manifest and the related customs documents. These documents are evidence in demurrage and commercial disputes.
Kaptan; TML aşımı şüphesi, mis-declared: The Master can stop the cargo operation because of a suspected TML exceedance, mis-declared DG, a missing VGM, exceeded stability or strength limits, unsafe practices by the terminal, a risk of pollution or the weather. This authority is the expression, in cargo operations, of the "overriding authority" in SOLAS V/34-1 and ISM 5.2.
Kaptan; kişinin bulunma koşullarını, kim: The Master documents the circumstances in which the person was found, his or her identity details (if any), state of health and the supervision arrangements. The P&I Club is informed early (stowaway costs are covered by P&I). Disembarkation and return are carried out in coordination with the states concerned and the agent.
Kaptan; tank ve bölme soundinglerini ald: The Master has the tanks and compartments sounded (to detect flooding), compares the draft readings, calculates the high-water window from the tide tables and, if necessary, prepares a refloating plan with salvage and class advice. If there is a risk of pollution, the SOPEP is activated and the authorities are informed. A controlled and calculated refloating plan, rather than hasty decisions, protects both the ship and the environment.
Kaptanı çağırma kriterleri (calling the: The criteria for calling the Master (calling the master) are applied clearly and without hesitation: entering or approaching restricted visibility, failure to achieve the planned CPA, traffic density becoming unmanageable, an unexpected danger (drifting object, distress signal), equipment failure, uncertainty about the position, deteriorating weather and any situation of "any doubt". The officer must never hesitate to call the Master and must not put off the decision to call.

The criteria for calling the Master are one of the most important lists a cadet must memorize: the Master is called immediately when visibility falls below a set limit, when traffic density increases, when there is doubt about the navigation, in the event of equipment failure or when the specified CPA cannot be maintained. The cadet internalizes the principle that "if in doubt, call the Master" is never a weakness but a professional reflex.
Kaptanın SIRE 2.0 hazırlığı, dosya düzel: The Master's preparation for SIRE 2.0 goes beyond tidying files: an officer must be able to answer the question "how do you apply this procedure?" by describing the real practice on his or her own ship. Because of photographic evidence and the real-time recording system, "show it and put it away" is not possible. In SIRE 2.0 negative findings are reported as "observations"; each observation must be closed by the company with a root cause and corrective action, otherwise the way to the next charter is not open.
Kaptanın bu aşamadaki rolü, 2. Zabit'in: The Master's role at this stage is to read critically the appraisal prepared by the Second Officer (usually the navigating officer). It is the Master's duty to find the points where the route requested by the charterer conflicts with the seasonally safe route and to report them, with reasons, to the company and the charterer. For example, in the North Atlantic winter a great circle may look economical, but in the light of sentinel buoy data and a weather routing service (e.g. WNI, AWT) it may be necessary to keep further south.
Kaptanın burada hassas olması gereken no: The point on which the Master must be careful here is the difference between "blame" and "root cause". "The AB was negligent" is not a root cause but an accusation; the real root cause may be "this item was not in the AB's job description" or "familiarisation was inadequate". RCA based on a just culture is a precondition of an honest reporting culture that does not hide the real cause.
Kaptanın buradaki rolü çift yönlüdür: he: The Master's role here is twofold: to lead as the head of the team, and to create an environment in which the team can "challenge" him or her. A junior officer being able to say "the CPA looks too close to me" is a sign that the team really works. If this culture is not built, even the most competent team will miss the danger seen by a junior who stays silent.
Kaptanın hafife almaması gereken nokta,: A point the Master must not underestimate is that "the sum of several small findings" can lead to detention just as much as "one big failure". If the inspector sees a picture of findings that are each small but together prove that the SMS has collapsed, he or she can detain the ship under the ISM (code 15). In other words, the ship can be detained on the grounds that "none of them is fatal on its own, but together they show that there is no system".
Kaptanın halefiyet (succession) perspekt: The Master is expected to have a succession perspective: today's second officer is tomorrow's chief officer; today's chief officer is tomorrow's Master. A good Master sees training people who could fill his or her own place not as a threat but as a professional duty. This is the only real source of sustainable competence for the fleet.
Kaptanın iletişim altyapısı GMDSS (DSC,: The Master's communication infrastructure covers GMDSS (DSC, Inmarsat-C, MF/HF/VHF, EPIRB, SART) and commercial satellite systems (FleetBroadband, VSAT, Starlink and similar). In distress, urgency and safety traffic the correct channel and procedure are vital: MAYDAY (distress), PAN-PAN (urgency), SECURITE (safety). The listening watch on VHF Ch 16 and the discipline of Ch 13 (bridge-to-bridge manoeuvring) are a daily routine at sea.
Kaptanın iletişim becerisi, \"kibar yazı: The Master's communication skill is not "polite correspondence" but the discipline of passing the right message to the right party at the right time, with documents. Keeping the DPA line alive, managing charterer pressure professionally and maintaining the discipline of signatures and statements towards third parties protect the Master both legally and in terms of safety. The principle not to be forgotten is this: commercial pressure is temporary, but the accident and legal consequences of badly managed communication are permanent. A seasoned Master is the one who, even at moments when saying "yes" is easy, can say the "no" that safety requires, with reasons and with documents.
Kaptanın kadro ve eğitim yönetimi, tek b: The Master's management of manning and training goes beyond the limits of a single ship; the appraisals he or she gives, the officers he or she trains and the competence gaps he or she reports feed the company's fleet-wide human resources planning. By reporting training needs and certificate gaps to the company regularly, the Master ensures that the next rotation is better prepared.
Kaptanın kadro ve eğitim yönetimindeki b: The Master's success in managing manning and training is not a shiny list but a reality that shows itself in a crisis: everyone knowing his or her place when the alarm sounds, a junior officer being able to speak up about a danger he or she sees, a tired crew having been rested beforehand, and an error being reported rather than hidden. None of these results is a coincidence; all are the product of the disciplined follow-up of competence, genuine familiarisation, realistic drills and fair leadership that the Master maintains every day. A good Master knows that even the best equipment comes down to people, and counts training those people as the most important duty.
Kaptanın kritik kavramı \"survey window\: A critical concept for the Master is the "survey window": it forms a window from 3 months before to 3 months after the anniversary date (±3 months for the annual survey). The renewal survey must be completed within the 3 months before the expiry date. Going outside the window breaks the harmonised survey regime, and a certificate falling "out of window" directly produces a deficiency at PSC. The Master must plan the port rotation with the company so as to catch the survey windows.
Kaptanın night order book'una saat değiş: The clock change is written clearly in the Master's night order book: in which watch, by how many minutes and in which direction. The night watchkeeper applies the change on the bridge clock and enters it in the deck logbook. At the briefing, the Second Officer tells the officer on the night watch clearly how and when the change is to be made.
Kaptanın pratik çıkarımı şudur: geminin: The practical conclusion for the Master is this: the ship's past deficiencies and the company's record directly determine how often she is inspected today. A single detention can lower the company's performance rating (e.g. from high or medium to low or very low) and increase the likelihood of every ship in the fleet being targeted. This is why the Master is not content with saying "I passed my own inspection"; he or she knows that every finding affects the company's record and the risk of the fleet.
Kaptanın rolü, standartları yalnızca \"b: The Master's role is not only to "know" the standards but to ensure that they are actually applied on board, to prove it and to correct deviations. Since the philosophy of the MLC is "decent working and living conditions for seafarers", the Master's leadership style directly determines whether these rights are realised.
Kaptanın sorumluluğu, bu tanıtımın \"for: The Master's responsibility is to ensure that this familiarisation is not just "getting a form signed". The newcomer must really know where to go when the alarm sounds; this is why good familiarisation includes a physical walk-through on board: the person actually walks to the muster station, is shown the nearest exit and puts on a lifejacket with it in hand.
Kaptanın yorum becerisi, ham sinoptik ha: The Master's interpretive skill is being able to translate raw synoptic weather data (the 500 hPa pattern, the jet stream, the position of the polar vortex) into ship performance. The modern bridge shows weather and wave data as an ECDIS overlay; but the data is updated every 6 hours and can be wrong at the micro scale.
Kapı/rampa kapandıktan sonra çok sayıda: After the door or ramp is closed, a large number of hydraulic or mechanical locking devices (cleats) press the panel tightly against the hull. All locks must be fully engaged; incomplete locking can lead to the door opening at sea and the ship taking in water.
Karar alındığında: log book'a tam metin: Once the decision is made, it is entered in full in the log book, notified by email to the company's DPA and operations manager, and notified to the charterer. This threefold record is the strongest evidence protecting the Master and the company in any future legal dispute.
Karaya oturma anında ilk refleks makiney: At the moment of grounding, the first reflex may be to try to get off by going astern on the engine; this is often a mistake. The Master first assesses the situation: where the ship is aground (bow, stern, full length), the type of bottom (sand, mud, rock), hull integrity, flooding, the state of the tide and the environmental risk. Going astern hastily can tear the damaged area open and multiply flooding and pollution; moreover, a damaged ship that slides off into deep water can sink.
Karaya oturmalar büyük çevre felaketleri: Groundings can turn into major environmental disasters (Exxon Valdez 1989, Wakashio 2020). The Master gives priority to the condition of the fuel tanks; if necessary, he or she reduces the risk of pollution by internal transfer (moving cargo or fuel into intact tanks). The SOPEP/SMPEP contains the initial response equipment and the notification list. The port or coastal state, class and the P&I club are informed quickly; a surveyor is appointed.
Karbon fiyatlandırma: IMO düzeyinde tart: Carbon pricing: under discussion at IMO; the EU ETS for shipping started in 2024.
Karbon fiyatı dalgalanır; 2024 başı itib: The carbon price fluctuates; as of early 2024 it was in the range of approximately 60-90 €/ton CO₂. This adds 187-280 € per ton to the fuel cost (HFO basis, where 100% of the emissions are covered).
Kargo ambarlarında, her ambardan sürekli: In cargo holds, sample extraction smoke detection is used, drawing air samples continuously from each hold to detectors at a control station; the same system may be combined with the CO₂ extinguishing line. The pipes must not be blocked and must be correctly marked for each hold.
Kargo hasarında, hasarın gemiye yüklenme: In cargo damage, distinguishing whether the damage occurred before the cargo was loaded (clausing / a remark on the Mate's Receipt) or during carriage determines liability for compensation. The Master documents observations of damage during loading and discharging with a Letter of Protest and a survey. These records are used directly in the P&I club's defence of the cargo claim.
Kargo manifoldu, gemi hatlarının termina: The cargo manifold is the central point where the ship's lines are connected to the terminal's loading arms or hoses. With multi-grade cargoes, each parcel must be carried with its own set of pumps, lines and valves (segregation); commingling is not acceptable. The valve arrangement and the line diagram are settled before the operation.
Kargo tankından gelen patlayıcı gazın ma: To prevent flammable gas from the cargo tanks escaping back to the generating side in the engine room, the deck water seal and a mechanical non-return valve work together. This double barrier prevents flame or vapour from flashing back; the water level in the deck seal is maintained continuously.
Kargo, kirlilik veya yaralanma içeren ol: In incidents involving cargo, pollution or injury, the scene is preserved as far as possible until the surveyor arrives. The Master takes photographs of the damaged areas, records the measurements (soundings, draft, ullage) and gathers all the documents in a single "casualty file". This file is the basic source for any later P&I claim, the GA adjustment and court proceedings.
Kargo/balast operasyonları ORB Part II'y: Cargo/ballast operations are entered in ORB Part II in time and completely with the relevant codes. Each completed operation is signed by the officer in charge and each completed page by the Master; the records are kept on board for at least three years.
Karmaşık arızalar, üst mühendise yapılan: Complex failures are reported to the senior engineer in a structured way: what was observed, when it started, which values changed, what action was taken and what state the equipment is in. Presenting measured data and a timeline instead of a vague "it broke down" speeds up the right decision.
Karmaşık değişiklikler için tracing (ase: For complex changes, the tracing technique (acetate copy) is used: the tracing attached to the NtM is aligned with reference points on the chart (e.g. a lat/long intersection or a prominent light), and the new symbols are transferred to the chart by pressing through with a pencil. This is the most reliable method of avoiding position errors.
Karter veya ayrı yağ tankından alınan ya: Oil taken from the sump or a separate oil tank is pressurised by a pump, passes through the cooler and a full-flow filter and is distributed to the engine bearings. The return oil comes back to the tank and the cycle continues.
Karşılıklı izleme, birbirini suçlama değ: Mutual monitoring is a culture of protecting each other, not blaming each other.
Kaskad kontrolde iki iç içe döngü bulunu: Cascade control has two nested loops: the outer (master/primary) loop controls the main process variable; the inner (slave/secondary) loop controls an intermediate variable that changes faster.
Kasırga rotasında ısrar, 33 ölü. Ders: e: Persisting on a track into a hurricane; 33 dead. Lesson: the most current weather information and official hurricane advisories must not be ignored; a junior officer's "challenge" must not be suppressed.
Katalizör ince parçacıkları (Al+Si) aşın: Catalyst fines (Al+Si) cause wear and must be removed by the purifier. Asphaltenes can block fuel filters. Mixing incompatible fuels causes sludge formation.
Kategoriye uygun prewash yapılmadan lima: Leaving port without a prewash appropriate to the category is a serious violation. The most common mistake in the field is leaving residues in a tank because the stripping line test was skipped.
Katı atık (kağıt, gıda) charge door'dan: Solid waste (paper, food) is loaded through the charging door; after preheating, the flame burns it.
Kauçuk (cutless rubber) yatak malzemesi: Rubber (cutless rubber) bearing material is used. It is lubricated by seawater. It has environmental advantages (no risk of oil leakage).
Kauçuk contalar (rubber packing), compre: The rubber packing, compression bars, cross-joints and drains together provide weathertight integrity; renewing only the packing does not correct a misaligned panel or poorly adjusted cleats.
Kavitasyon (pompa emişinde basınç düşmes: Cavitation (vapor bubbles forming because of a pressure drop at the pump suction) produces a typical gravel-like rattling sound and wears the pump impeller rapidly. A clogged suction filter or a low tank level is a common cause; the Oiler recognizes the sound and reports it to the engineer.
Kavitasyon türleri: Sheet (yüzey), tip v: Types of cavitation: sheet, tip vortex, bubble, cloud and supercavitation.
Kavitasyon, akışkan basıncının buharlaşm: Cavitation is the formation of vapour bubbles when the fluid pressure falls below the vapour pressure, and their collapse in the high-pressure region, causing material damage, noise and loss of performance. It causes pitting and erosion on the impeller vanes.
Kavitasyonu azaltmak için kanat profili: To reduce cavitation, the blade profile is optimised, the blade tips are shaped and the propeller is loaded appropriately.
Kaydın sahte veya abartılı olmaması esas: It is essential that entries are not false or exaggerated. Entering in the TRB a job in which the cadet did not actually take part is a serious disciplinary offense; these tasks are also questioned in the oral examination, and superficial entries are exposed. The TRB is the mirror of the cadet's real competence.
Kaynak, kesme (oksi-asetilen, plazma), t: Hot work such as welding, cutting (oxy-acetylene, plasma), grinding and open flames is the work with the highest risk of fire and explosion. The hot work permit documents that the area has been cleared of combustible materials, that a gas test has been carried out (especially around tanks/fuel), that firefighting equipment is ready and that a fire watch has been assigned.
Kaynak, taşlama, kesme gibi sıcak işler,: Hot work such as welding, grinding and cutting is a major source of fire in the engine room. A hot work permit requires gas-free measurement (LEL 0%, surroundings cleared of combustibles), a fire watch, extinguishers ready, isolation of nearby fuel/oil and the approval of the Master + Chief Engineer. The fire watch is maintained at the end of the job and for 1 hour afterwards.
Kaynak/taşlama bittikten sonra metal saa: After welding or grinding is finished, the metal stays hot for hours and can start a hidden fire. The fire watch keeps the area under watch for at least 30–60 minutes after the work ends; concealed voids that sparks may have reached are checked. The permit is closed only when the area has fully cooled down and is clean.
Kaynaklı bağlantı yapılacaksa kaynak ağz: If a welded joint is to be made, a weld bevel is prepared; for a flanged joint, the flange type (slip-on, weld-neck) and the pressure class are selected to match. On threaded joints, threads are cut (threading) and tightness is achieved with suitable flax/Teflon tape plus sealing compound.
Kayıt \"gerçek zamanlı ve dürüst\" olmal: Entries must be "real-time and honest". Logs filled in later from memory or padded with "copied" values make failure analysis impossible and destroy trust during inspections.
Kayıt defterlerindeki kayıtların doğrulu: The accuracy of the entries in the record books is the Master's personal responsibility. In the USA, magic pipe cases are generally brought on the basis of false ORB entries (false statements), resulting in prison sentences for the Master and the chief engineer and fines of millions of dollars for the company.
Kayıt sahteciliği — özellikle ORB'de \"m: Falsification of records — especially concealing a "magic pipe" in the ORB (oily water discharged overboard bypassing the OWS) — is among the crimes punished most severely in maritime law. In the USA, under APPS (Act to Prevent Pollution from Ships), entering a US port with a false ORB is a crime in itself even if the pollution did not actually occur in US waters; fines of millions of dollars, imprisonment of the Master and denial of departure clearance for the ship can follow.
Kayıt tutarlılığı, denetimin en kırılgan: Consistency of records is the most fragile point in an inspection. If a lifeboat engine has been run, the logbook must show the date, the duration, the person who ran it and the observations. A contradiction between the records and the physical condition (e.g. the logbook says "tested" but the HRU has expired) produces a PSC deficiency directly.
Kayıtlar dürüst ve zamanında tutulur; so: Records are kept honestly and on time; filling them in afterwards in bulk (pencil whipping) is prohibited and, if found during an inspection, leads to serious sanctions. Although alarm and data logging on modern ships is done by automation (AMS), the responsibility for manual verification and signature remains.
Kayıtlar gerçek zamanlı, silinmeden (düz: Entries are made in real time, without erasures (corrections by a single line + initials) and completely. A complete, correct and up-to-date ORB is the first checkpoint of a PSC and USCG inspection. Gaps, late entries or a mismatch with reality are the most common causes of deficiencies and prosecutions.
Kayıtlar gerçek, zamanında ve düzeltilme: Entries must be true, timely and unaltered (no false data). If a parameter goes outside its limits, both the value and the action taken are recorded. These records have evidential value in Port State Control (PSC) inspections, insurance investigations and casualty investigations.
Kayıtlar survey ve PSC için kritik delil: Records are critical evidence for surveys and PSC; however, the real aim is not to pass the inspection but to build a team that is ready for a real emergency. A well-kept drill record based on reality gets the ship through both the inspection and a real crisis.
Kayıtlar, MLC 2006 denetimi, liman devle: The records are examined during MLC 2006 inspections, by Port State Control (PSC) and by the port health authority (Ship Sanitation). Well-kept records both protect the ship legally and allow fast diagnosis when a problem arises.
Kayıtlar, yalnızca uyum için değil, soru: Records matter not only for compliance but also for responsibility: in an investigation after an accident, these logs show which correction the chart was up to date with on which date. A blank, late or backdated log is a serious weakness.
Kayıtların gizliliği ve saklama süresi ş: The confidentiality and retention period of the records follow the company procedure; since they are personal data, access is restricted. Summaries of results (how many tests, how many positives) can be reported in anonymised form; individual results, however, are shared only with authorised persons.
Kayıtların operasyonla ve tank sounding: In an inspection, the records being consistent with the operations and with the tank soundings is more decisive than the equipment simply being in working order.
Kayıtların tutarlılığı kritiktir: deck l: Consistency of records is critical: the position in the deck log, the ECDIS, the GPS and the SOF must not contradict each other. A contradiction leads an investigation to conclude that "the records are unreliable" and destroys the insurance defence. The Master periodically cross-checks the consistency of the records.
Kayıtta bir sapma (örn. soğutucu 4°C üst: When a deviation is seen in the record (e.g. the chiller has risen above 4°C), the cook starts corrective action: checking the door/seal/filling level, moving the products to another unit if necessary, reporting the fault and assessing/destroying the affected food. A product suspected of having had its cold chain broken is not risked. These actions are the practical application of "critical control point" management in HACCP terms (details in the food safety task).
Kaza sonrası kaptan ve mürettebat, medya: After an accident the Master and the crew make NO statements to the media, to shore surveyors, to the other party's lawyers or on social media. All external communication goes through the spokesperson appointed by the company and through P&I and the lawyers. An early and thoughtless sentence ("I think the speed was too high") becomes evidence against the ship in criminal and compensation cases. This discipline is explained to the crew beforehand in a briefing.
Kazan en kritik emniyet sistemlerinden b: The boiler is one of the most critical safety systems. Low-low water level cut-out, flame failure protection, high pressure protection and safety valves are mandatory. Low water can cause the tubes to overheat and burst.
Kazan safety valve'i, aşırı basınca karş: The boiler safety valve is the last safeguard against overpressure and is tested/adjusted regularly. The flame failure device prevents an explosion by shutting off the fuel if the flame is lost. The Second Engineer verifies that these safety devices are working; if one of them is defective, the boiler cannot be operated safely.
Kazan suyu kimyasal olarak şartlandırılı: Boiler water is chemically treated; chloride, phosphate, alkalinity (pH) and condensate hardness tests are carried out regularly. Incorrect water chemistry leads to internal boiler corrosion, scale and carry-over. Test results are entered in the water treatment log.
Kazan suyu testleri (pH, kloride, fosfat: Boiler water tests (pH, chloride, phosphate and so on) are carried out regularly; deposits are removed by daily blow-down. Soot blowing prevents soot build-up.
Kazan suyu; korozyon, kireç (scale) ve k: Boiler water is treated to prevent corrosion, scale and carryover (foaming). pH/alkalinity, chloride, phosphate and dissolved oxygen are tested regularly and controlled by chemical dosing and blow-down. Hardness and oxygen corrosion directly affect the life of the tubes.
Kazan, separatör ve hava kompresörü bakı: Boiler, separator and air compressor maintenance is the Second Engineer's daily discipline that keeps the engine room safe and efficient. Correct water treatment, working safety devices and well-maintained auxiliary systems protect both safety and the health of the main engine together.
Kazan/Ekonomizer: Besi suyu ısıtılır, bu: Boiler/economiser: the feed water is heated, evaporated and, if necessary, superheated. In marine applications the heat source is mostly the main engine exhaust.
Kazandan çıkan buhar, dağıtım hattıyla t: Steam from the boiler goes through the distribution line to the consumers (HFO heater, tank heating coils, calorifier, fuel module). Having given up its heat, the steam condenses; the condensate returns through the condensate line to the cascade/hotwell tank and is pumped back into the boiler by the feed pump. The closed circuit minimises water losses.
Kazayı önleyen unsur çoğu zaman büyük te: What prevents an accident is often not a major technical intervention but a small act of discipline: the right note, the right confirmation, escalation at the right time.
Kazıma (scrape-down) yağ analizi, demir: Scrape-down oil analysis is the most practical feedback, through its iron content and residual alkalinity, on whether the feed rate is correct.
Kaçak yolcu tespitinde FAL Konvansiyonu: When a stowaway is found, the guidance procedures of the FAL Convention and IMO Res. FAL.13(42) are applied. The Master ensures the person's safety, enters the identity details and the circumstances of discovery on the standard stowaway report form, and notifies the flag state, the next port state, the company and the P&I Club. A stowaway is not made part of the crew; but humane treatment and safety are provided.
Kaçak; düşen performans, sık şarj ihtiya: A leak shows itself through falling performance, frequent need for recharging, bubbles in the sight glass, unusual noise or temperature imbalance. Leak points are searched for with an electronic detector or a bubble test. A leak both reduces performance and creates environmental/legal liability.
Kaçınma her zaman tam mümkün olmayabilir: Avoidance may not always be fully possible; when heavy seas are expected, lashing/securing is checked, movable equipment is secured, watertight closures are made and the crew is briefed. The risk of parametric rolling and synchronous rolling is managed by adjusting speed/course.
Kaçış aydınlatması (escape lighting, low: Escape lighting (low-location lighting) and direction signs must be visible and working; they are not covered with paint or materials. The AB reports defective escape lighting or worn-off signs. During drills, the escape routes are physically checked, and any obstruction found is removed.
Kaçış yolları (escape routes) ve acil çı: Escape routes and emergency exits are kept clear at all times; cleaning trolleys, mop buckets or garbage bags are not left in these routes. Access to fire extinguisher lockers, hydrants, EEBDs and lifejacket stowage positions is never obstructed. These points are inspected under SOLAS and ISM.
Kaçış yolları (escape routes), koridorla: Escape routes, corridors, emergency exit doors and stairways are always kept open, unobstructed and marked. The AB immediately removes any material left in an escape route, because in a corridor filled with smoke during a fire, even the smallest obstacle causes a fatal delay. Emergency exit doors are not locked and are never blocked.
Kaçış yolunun malzeme ile kapatılması, k: Blocking escape routes with stores, leaving escape lighting defective and incorrect head counts at muster lead to people left inside being overlooked. The AB must keep escape routes clear, be honest in the head count and report every deficiency they see.
Kağıt haritalar, haftalık yayımlanan Adm: Paper charts are kept up to date with the weekly Admiralty Notices to Mariners. The cadet learns how to read NtMs, which chart they affect and how the correction is applied to the chart (in violet ink, with the NtM number written in the margin). T&P (Temporary & Preliminary) notices are kept in a separate file and announce temporary changes (for example, a light temporarily out of service).
Keep the muster list current and practis: Keep the muster list current and practise assigned fire, man-overboard (MOB), abandon-ship and enclosed-space rescue duties. Demonstrate rescue arrangements without exposing unprotected crew to a hazardous atmosphere. Record lessons and verify corrective actions.
