Liner iç çapı, üst (TDC yakını), orta ve: The liner bore is measured at the top (near TDC), middle and bottom, in both the athwartships and the fore-and-aft directions. The measurement is made with an inside micrometer or a dial gauge.
The liner bore is measured with a micrometer. The wear rate is expressed in mm per 1000 hours. In good conditions 0.03–0.05 mm per 1000 hours is acceptable.
Liner çapı iç mikrometre ile ölçülür. Ov: The liner bore is measured with an inside micrometer. Ovality and taper are calculated. The liner is renewed when the wear limit set by the maker is reached.
Lint atığı da düzenli toplanır; çöpe atı: Lint waste is also collected regularly; when it is disposed of, it is borne in mind that it is combustible, and it is kept away from heat/sources of ignition. By separating waste correctly, the steward contributes to the ship's compliance with the Garbage Management Plan.
List, transverse ağırlık dengesizliğinde: List results from transverse weight imbalance or from negative GM. Before correcting a list by ballast transfer, the Chief Officer first diagnoses the cause: unbalanced cargo, free surface or negative GM? A list caused by negative GM (loll) can get dangerously worse if ballast is taken on the wrong side.
Loading instrument (LoadMaster, Cargomax: The loading instrument (LoadMaster, Cargomax, BluePrint etc.) is calibrated with these data and verified by class every year. Even if the instrument fails, the Chief Officer must be able to construct the GZ curve by hand from the hydrostatic tables and KN values; this competence may be questioned during a PSC inspection.
Loading instrument, her kademede longitu: The loading instrument shows longitudinal bending moment and shear force at each stage as a percentage of the permissible envelope. Above 85% is the alarm zone; exceeding 100% means a risk of structural damage. On bulk carriers, during alternate hold loading, shear force peaks at the critical bulkhead positions; therefore only the approved sequence is followed.
Loading sequence ve ballast planı BLU Co: The loading sequence and ballast plan are prepared in line with the BLU Code; the loading rate must match the deballasting capacity. Otherwise the SF/BM limits are exceeded or the operation is delayed.
Local Mean Time (LMT), belirli bir boyla: Local Mean Time (LMT) is the mean solar time at a given meridian; it changes by 4 minutes for each degree of longitude (360° / 24 hours = 15°/hour = 4 minutes/degree). LMT is used for sunrise/sunset, twilight and moon observations. When planning star sights for night navigation, the Second Officer works from LMT, because twilight times depend on longitude.
Local/remote, emergency stop, pitch-to-z: The local/remote, emergency stop, pitch-to-zero and drive protection functions are returned from the test state to the operational position. A derated or unavailable thruster is correctly defined in the DP model and the capability plot and consequence analysis are updated.
Lock-Out/Tag-Out (LOTO), bir ekipman üze: Lock-Out/Tag-Out (LOTO) is the procedure that prevents equipment from starting or becoming energized unexpectedly while work is being done on it. The electrical supply is isolated, valves are closed and pressure is released; these isolation points are then secured with a lock, and a tag with the warning "work in progress, do not operate!" is attached. The key of the lock stays with the person doing the work.
Log hatası, ECDIS dead reckoning, ETA he: Log error affects ECDIS dead reckoning, the ETA calculation and squat estimates. The Second Officer monitors consistency by regularly comparing the log readings with the GNSS SOG and records any discrepancies.
Log kalibrasyonu genelde üretici/servis: Log calibration is usually carried out by the manufacturer/service company on a measured mile or by comparison with GNSS. The Second Officer carries out a verification by comparing log speed with GNSS SOG in open, calm water; a large difference is a sign of transducer fouling or a fault.
Lokal müdahale yetersizse, makine daires: If local firefighting is insufficient, the engine room is completely cleared of personnel, all openings are closed and the fixed extinguishing system is activated. With a CO2 total flooding system, the gas is not released until the head count has been fully confirmed — asphyxiation is a fatal risk.
Lokal referanslarda en sık görülen kayıp: The most common cause of losing a local reference is that the target can no longer be seen: shadowing of the reflector or transponder, the angle closing as the ship moves, or a structure or crane boom coming in between. With satellite-based references, ionospheric scintillation, jamming and spoofing can affect all satellite-based sources at the same time.
Lokasyon öğrenimi, General Arrangement ç: Learning these locations is reinforced by matching the General Arrangement drawing with the actual spaces. The cadet develops the skill of "finding on site what I see on the drawing"; this is a true engineering competence.
Lookout görevi; çevredeki tüm gemilerin,: The lookout's duty is to watch for all ships, small craft, buoys, coastlines, ice/debris/floating objects, navigation lights and sound signals in the vicinity and to report them to the OOW at once. The AB does not make decisions; they report what they see, and the decision to maneuver belongs to the OOW. This separation is the basic discipline of the watch: the lookout "reports", the officer "interprets and maneuvers".
Loop arızaları üç ana tipte görülür: ope: Loop faults are of three main types: open circuit (broken line/loose terminal), short circuit (cable short, water ingress) and earth fault (breakdown of cable insulation, leakage to earth). An addressable panel shows the address of the fault or the segment between two addresses, which speeds up fault finding. In a conventional system, the ETO works zone by zone, measuring terminal by terminal.
Low-location lighting marks approved esc: Low-location lighting marks approved escape routes near deck level when higher signs are obscured. Applicable SOLAS requirements, FSS Code chapter 11 and IMO resolution A.752(18) govern the arrangement. Check the approved plan, condition, visibility and power or photoluminescent performance; ordinary decorative lighting is not a substitute.
MARPOL 73/78, deniz kirliliğini altı ek: MARPOL 73/78 regulates marine pollution under six annexes: Annex I (oil), Annex II (noxious liquid substances), Annex III (harmful substances in packaged form), Annex IV (sewage), Annex V (garbage) and Annex VI (air pollution). The Chief Officer deals directly with Annex I in particular (deck oil operations, bunkering), Annex V (garbage) and Annex IV; bilge/sludge transfers are carried out in coordination with the engine department.
MARPOL Annex I gereği, makine dairesi ya: Under MARPOL Annex I, engine-room oil operations are recorded in the Oil Record Book Part I: bunkering, internal fuel/oil transfers, pumping bilge water overboard through the OWS, sludge disposal (incinerator/ashore/tank) and tank cleaning. Each operation is recorded under specific code letters (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I) with the date, quantity and details, and signed by the responsible engineer.
MARPOL Annex I yağı, Annex II zararlı sı: MARPOL Annex I regulates oil, Annex II noxious liquid substances, Annex III harmful substances in packaged form, Annex IV sewage, Annex V garbage and Annex VI air emissions. For each annex the ship carries the relevant record book, certificate and management plan (IOPP, ORB, GMP, SEEMP, etc.). The Master knows which annexes apply to the ship and whether the current certificates are valid.
MARPOL Annex I, makine dairesi sintine s: MARPOL Annex I requires that engine-room bilge water may be pumped overboard only through the OWS and at less than 15 ppm. Every bilge transfer is recorded in the Oil Record Book Part I. The cadet learns this recording logic; unlawful bilge discharge (magic pipe) is one of the most severely punished maritime offenses.
MARPOL Annex I, tüm bu işlemlerin Oil Re: MARPOL Annex I requires all these operations to be recorded in the Oil Record Book (ORB Part I); the quantities delivered/incinerated, the tank levels and the dates must be consistent. The Wiper provides observation and on-site support for these operations; the accuracy of the records is the engineer's responsibility.
MARPOL Annex I, yağlı suyun denize deşar: MARPOL Annex I subjects the discharge of oily water into the sea to strict criteria (e.g. an instantaneous rate of discharge of oil not exceeding 30 litres per nautical mile, a total limit, distance from land, ship en route). The ODME (Oil Discharge Monitoring Equipment) measures the oil content continuously; if the criteria are exceeded, it stops the discharge automatically and keeps a record (Oil Record Book).
MARPOL Annex IV, lağım suyu deşarjını dü: MARPOL Annex IV regulates the discharge of sewage: sewage treated in a type-approved STP (Sewage Treatment Plant) may be discharged to sea under certain conditions; untreated sewage may be discharged only more than 12 nm from land, with the ship en route and at a certain speed. The biological process (activated sludge) and disinfection performance of the STP are monitored.
MARPOL Annex IV, pis su deşarjını düzenl: MARPOL Annex IV regulates the discharge of sewage: effluent treated in an approved sewage treatment plant may be discharged under certain conditions; untreated sewage may be discharged at a moderate rate at least 12 nm from land while the ship is en route at more than 4 knots. From the deck side, the Chief Officer monitors that the treatment plant is in working order and that the discharge conditions are complied with.
MARPOL Annex V kapsamında güverte atıkla: Under MARPOL Annex V, deck waste (plastics, metal, food, operational waste) is collected separately; the Bosun checks that the garbage stations on deck are kept in order and that waste is segregated correctly. Working records are kept on deck for the Garbage Record Book entries.
MARPOL Annex V, gemilerden kaynaklanan t: MARPOL Annex V regulates the management of all garbage from ships. The basic principle is that the discharge of plastics into the sea is completely prohibited and that other wastes may be discharged into the sea only under certain conditions (distance, speed, category). The 2013 revision of Annex V tightened the rules and moved to the approach "discharge generally prohibited, exceptions defined".
MARPOL Annex V, çöpü kategorilere ayırır: MARPOL Annex V divides garbage into categories: plastics (A), food waste (B), domestic waste (C), cooking oil (D), incinerator ash (E), operational waste (F), animal carcasses (G), fishing gear (H), e-waste (I) and cargo residues (J: non-HME, K: HME). The Chief Officer ensures that labeled, color-coded garbage bins are placed at suitable positions on deck and that the crew segregates waste correctly.
MARPOL Annex VI EEXI ve CII çerçevesinde: Within the framework of MARPOL Annex VI EEXI and CII, optimizing the electrical load on board helps reduce fuel consumption and emissions. The ETO controls unnecessary pump/fan running with VFDs, converts lighting to LED and optimizes the PMS settings so that generators run in their most efficient load range (70–85%).
MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 14, kullanılan yakı: MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 14 requires the sulfur content of the fuel used to be within the limit and this to be demonstrated by the BDN, the fuel sample and the changeover record. During PSC inspections, sulfur compliance is verified by sample analysis and examination of the records.
MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 18, manifold'da con: MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 18 makes it mandatory to take a continuous drip sample at the manifold (4-way sampler). The sample is divided into 4 bottles: the one retained by the ship (MARPOL bottle, sealed, kept for at least 12 months), the supplier's copy, the one sent to the laboratory and the ship's own commercial sample (ship's sample). The seal number of each bottle is written on the BDN and on the barge's copy; both parties sign.
MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 27 (eski Reg. 22A): Applied since 2019 under MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 27 (formerly Reg. 22A). Ships report their annual fuel consumption, distance traveled and hours spent at sea.
MARPOL Annex VI kapsamında EEXI (Energy: Under MARPOL Annex VI, the EEXI (Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index) and the annual CII (Carbon Intensity Indicator) rating are in force. The performance data kept by the Second Engineer (SFOC, speed-power curve, fouling trends) directly affects the ship's CII rating and provides the justification for SEEMP Part III actions (hull cleaning, derating, trim optimization).
MARPOL Annex VI kapsamında kullanılan ya: Under MARPOL Annex VI, the sulfur content of the fuel used (BDN), flowmeter readings and the required records are kept. The Third/Fourth Engineer records the changeover in the logbook with the time and position.
MARPOL Annex VI, ECA (Emission Control A: MARPOL Annex VI sets the sulfur limits in ECAs (Emission Control Areas) and in general waters (global limit 0.50% m/m, within an ECA 0.10% m/m). The cadet learns which fuel is used in which area, the fuel changeover procedure and the importance of the BDN (Bunker Delivery Note) record.
MARPOL Ek V uyumu PSC ve liman otoritele: MARPOL Annex V compliance is inspected by PSC and port authorities; inconsistencies between the GRB and the actual waste flow lead to heavy penalties. By segregating galley waste correctly and reporting it correctly, the cook keeps the first link in the ship's compliance chain sound. The principle "when in doubt, do not discharge to sea: store it and deliver it ashore" is the safest rule.
MARPOL Ek V, gemi çöpünü kategorilere ay: MARPOL Annex V divides ship's garbage into categories and places strict rules on the discharge of each into the sea. The categories that concern the cook most are food waste and galley-generated plastics/packaging/oil. The general principle is that "the sea is kept clean": plastics are the strictest category, prohibited from discharge into the sea in all circumstances, while food waste may be discharged into the sea only under certain conditions (such as a minimum distance from land and being comminuted).
MARPOL Reg. 28 kapsamında yan/dip yarala: Side and bottom damage scenarios under MARPOL Reg. 28 are checked with the damage module of the loading computer; the final condition must meet both the intact and the damage criteria.
MARPOL VI Reg. 14, küresel yakıt sülfür: MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 14 reduced the global fuel sulphur limit to 0.50% from 1 January 2020 and to 0.10% in the ECAs (the Baltic, the North Sea, North America, the US Caribbean and, since 1 May 2025, the Mediterranean). The ship either uses compliant low-sulphur fuel (VLSFO/MGO) or achieves equivalent compliance with a scrubber (EGCS). The Master checks the Bunker Delivery Note (BDN) and the retention of the samples (12 months).
MARPOL bazı atıkların gemide yakılmasını: MARPOL prohibits the incineration of certain wastes on board, such as those containing PCBs, wastes containing heavy metals, refined petroleum products containing halogen compounds and residues of cargoes subject to Annex I, II or III. PVC may be incinerated only in an incinerator with an IMO type approval certificate. General garbage (paper, food waste residues), sludge and waste oil may be incinerated. Incineration is recorded in the Garbage Record Book / Oil Record Book.
MARPOL numunesi mühürlü olarak alınır ve: The MARPOL sample is taken sealed and kept for the specified period (e.g. 12 months). The contents of the BDN are verified and entered in ORB Part I with the appropriate code (Code H).
MARPOL'ün tüm ekleri (I-VI) makine daire: All the annexes of MARPOL (I-VI) concern the engine room. In the USA, APPS makes keeping a false Oil Record Book a federal crime; seafarers can be given a "whistleblower" award (up to 50% of the fine). For this reason, a report by a single crew member can bring the company a fine of millions of dollars and a prison sentence for the responsible officer.
MARPOL, bazı denizleri (örn. Akdeniz, Ba: MARPOL regards certain seas (designated "special areas", e.g. the Mediterranean, the Baltic, the North Sea and the Antarctic area) as sensitive, and the waste rules there are much stricter; the distance and conditions for discharging food waste into the sea are tighter, and in some cases delivery ashore is in practice the only option. The cook confirms the rules for the area the ship is in with the responsible officer and plans storage/delivery accordingly.
MARPOL, her changeover için yazılı kayıt: MARPOL requires a written record for each changeover: the start and end date/time of the changeover, the ship's position (lat/long), the fuel volume in each tank and the type of fuel used. This record is the legal proof that the ship entered the ECA on compliant fuel.
MARPOL, makine dairesi sintine suyunun d: MARPOL allows machinery space bilge water to be discharged into the sea only under these conditions: the ship is en route, the oil content is 15 ppm or less, and the approved OWS and monitor are in operation. The rules are stricter in special areas.
MARPOL, yıkama sonrası tankın yeterince: MARPOL requires the tank to be sufficiently dry after washing; the bottom is drained with the help of trim and the last liquid is removed by stripping. This reduces the amount of slops and the contamination of later ballast water.
MBL (Minimum Breaking Load), halatın kop: The MBL (Minimum Breaking Load) is the load at which the line parts. The Ship Design MBL (SDMBL) is the reference MBL for which the mooring system is designed. The winch brake is set to slip (render) before the line parts, so that the brake gives way rather than the line.
MBR (Membrane Bioreactor): biyolojik pro: MBR (Membrane Bioreactor): biological process + ultrafiltration membrane; the effluent is of very high quality.
MDO (DMB sınıfı): Distile yakıta az mikt: MDO (DMB grade): distillate fuel with a small amount of residual fuel mixed in. Its viscosity can be up to 11.0 cSt at 40 °C. It may need slight heating.
MDO: ECA dışı bölgelerde ekonomik distil: MDO: an economical distillate option outside ECAs; used as the continuous fuel in some auxiliary engines.
MDoH, geminin son uğraklarında ve seyir: The MDoH (Maritime Declaration of Health) is the official declaration reporting to the port authority cases of illness or death that occurred at the ship's last ports of call and during the voyage, the sanitary conditions and known health risks. The Master prepares the declaration accurately and completely; concealment or a false declaration creates serious liability.
ME üstündeki tavan vinci (overhead trave: The overhead travelling crane above the ME and the monorail are fixed equipment designed for lifting heavy engine parts; their SWL is marked on their rails/girders. Inspection looks for: rail condition, trolley movement, limit switches, brake, hook and hoist wire/chain, and operation of the control pendant. Periodic load testing and certification are required.
MEG4, eski \"boyalı snap-back zone\" yak: MEG4 has revised the old "painted snap-back zone" approach: zones are no longer treated as individual painted lines but as "the whole mooring deck being a potential danger zone", because the direction of snap-back can change with the lead angle of the line and with fairlead failure. The Chief Officer forbids personnel to stand inside a bight, in line with a fairlead, or between the line and the bollard while a line is under tension.
MEG4, halatların bir Line Management Pla: MEG4 recommends that lines be tracked with a Line Management Plan (retirement criteria, usage records). The AB helps to record at which station and for how long each line has been used; periodically turning the lines end-for-end evens out the wear.
MES, lifeboat ve life raft koordineli ku: The MES, lifeboats and liferafts are used in a coordinated way; passenger guidance, mustering and counting are practised. The evacuation time and bottlenecks are assessed.
MF (yaklaşık 1.6-4 MHz) gündüz ground wa: MF (about 1.6–4 MHz) gives a range of about 150–300 miles by day through the ground wave; at night the range increases through the sky wave. HF (3–30 MHz) reaches thousands of miles, even global range, by reflection from the ionosphere (sky wave); but the range varies with the frequency, the time of day and ionospheric conditions.
MF DSC tehlike frekansı 2187.5 kHz'tir;: The MF DSC distress frequency is 2187.5 kHz; on HF there are separate DSC distress frequencies in the 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16 MHz bands. The distress alert is sent by DSC on a suitable frequency and received automatically by the coast station. Radiotelephony and NBDP (telex) distress frequencies are also defined.
MF DSC: 2187.5 kHz; MF voice: 2182 kHz.
MF/HF DSC cihazları da günlük dahili tes: MF/HF DSC equipment also requires a daily internal test. The distress and safety frequencies (2187.5 kHz MF DSC, 8414.5 kHz and the other HF DSC bands) are monitored continuously in scan/watch mode. The Second Officer verifies that the scanning receiver scans the correct set of frequencies.
MF/HF performansı büyük ölçüde anten ve: MF/HF performance depends largely on the integrity of the antenna and the earthing (earth/ground). The Second Officer visually checks the tension of the antenna wires, salt/dirt build-up on the insulators, the antenna tuner connections and the earth connection. Corrosion or a loose connection reduces transmit power dramatically.
MF/HF, uzun tel/whip anten ve otomatik a: MF/HF sets are matched to the different frequencies with a long wire or whip antenna and an automatic antenna tuner (ATU). A good RF earth (ground) system (hull/sea earth) determines efficiency; a poor earth reduces range and output power. An ATU fault prevents transmission on certain bands.
MGO (DMA sınıfı): Tamamen distile edilmi: MGO (DMA grade): a fully distilled fuel, clear and bright in appearance. Its viscosity is 2.0–6.0 cSt at 40 °C. It needs no heating and can be fed directly to the injection system.
MGO/LSMGO viskozitesi HFO'dan çok düşükt: The viscosity of MGO/LSMGO is much lower than that of HFO. For lubrication of the fuel pumps and injectors, the injection viscosity must not fall below a minimum value (generally ~2 cSt); otherwise pump seizure and injector wear occur. This is why some ships use a fuel cooler / chiller.
MGO: ECA bölgelerinde ana yakıt, acil je: MGO: the main fuel in ECAs, emergency generator fuel, pilot fuel for the auxiliary boiler. It is preferred while waiting in port.
MLC (Standard A2.3), çalışma ve dinlenme: The MLC (Standard A2.3) provides two alternative limits for hours of work and rest; STCW A-VIII/1 sets only minimum hours of rest. Minimum rest: at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period and at least 77 hours in any 7-day period. Rest may be divided into no more than two periods; one of them must be at least 6 hours long without interruption, and the interval between consecutive rest periods must not exceed 14 hours. Alternatively, the ILO 180 maximum hours of work limit (max. 14 in 24 hours, max. 72 in 7 days) may be applied; the flag State states in the DMLC which one it has chosen.
MLC 2006 Regulation 3.1 ve Standard A3.1: MLC 2006 Regulation 3.1 and Standard A3.1 require suitable facilities on board for the crew to wash their laundry and maintain personal hygiene. Keeping the laundry working, clean and accessible is the employer's obligation; the steward is the one who delivers this facility on the ground. A broken washing machine or a dirty laundry is a direct finding (deficiency) in an MLC inspection.
MLC 2006 Regulation 3.1, gemideki yaşam: MLC 2006 Regulation 3.1 requires the accommodation and recreational spaces on board to be of a "decent" standard and to be kept clean and healthy at all times. Standard A3.1 requires an accredited person (usually the Master or an officer authorized by the Master) to inspect the accommodation at regular intervals and the results to be recorded. The steward is the front-line implementer for this inspection; the quality of cleaning directly determines MLC compliance.
MLC 2006 Regulation 3.2, mürettebata ücr: MLC 2006 Regulation 3.2 requires the crew to be provided, free of charge, with food that is sufficient in quantity, nutritious and suitable in quality and variety, and with clean drinking water. Standard A3.2 requires food to be provided with respect for religious and cultural diversity and catering staff to be trained. The steward implements this standard on the ground; the quality of service is the visible face of MLC compliance.
MLC 2006 Standard A2.3 ve STCW Code A-VI: MLC 2006 Standard A2.3 and the STCW Code A-VIII/1 set two basic limits for seafarers' rest hours: at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period and at least 77 hours of rest in any 7-day period. The 10 hours of rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours uninterrupted; the interval between two consecutive rest periods must not exceed 14 hours.
MLC 2006 Standard A3.2, belirli müretteb: MLC 2006 Standard A3.2 requires ships operating with more than a prescribed number of crew (usually 10) to carry a trained and qualified ship's cook. The cook must have been trained in food preparation, food and personal hygiene, food storage, stock control and environmental protection. The flag State issues the Ship's Cook Certificate in accordance with national legislation.
MLC 2006 ve STCW gereği minimum dinlenme: Minimum rest under MLC 2006 and STCW: 10 hours in any 24-hour period (which may be divided into two periods, one of them at least 6 hours long) and 77 hours in any 7-day period.
MLC 2006 ve STCW, yorgunluk (fatigue) yö: MLC 2006 and STCW make fatigue management mandatory: a minimum of 10 hours of rest in any 24 hours and a minimum of 77 hours in any 7 days. Rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours uninterrupted.
MLC 2006'nın mürettebat refahı (welfare): The emphasis of MLC 2006 on crew welfare encourages treating alcohol and drug dependence as a health problem as well as a disciplinary one. Some companies offer "self-referral" (asking for help voluntarily): if a seafarer asks for help before a positive test, he or she is referred to rehabilitation. The Master supports the existence and the confidentiality of such a channel.
MLC 2006, gıda ve içme suyu alanının düz: MLC 2006 requires the food and drinking water areas to be inspected and the inspections recorded regularly; the Ship Sanitation Control Certificate documents that the ship is acceptable from a public health point of view. The cook ensures that these records are always up to date and ready for inspection. Missing/falsified records are a serious nonconformity and can lead to detention of the ship.
MLC 2006, kaptanın \"iyi niyetle\" değil: MLC 2006 is an area in which the Master must manage "with documents", not "in good faith": every right, from the rest hour record to the payroll, from the accommodation inspection to the complaint procedure, must be visible through a record. But the real spirit of the MLC lies not on paper but in the people on board; keeping compliant records while creating a crew that feels tired, unpaid and undervalued both defeats the purpose of the MLC and sooner or later turns into a safety accident. A sensible Master knows that by protecting the crew's rights he or she is also making the strongest investment in safety: a crew that is rested, paid, healthy and treated with dignity is the most reliable line of defence at sea.
MLC 2006; barınma, beslenme, sağlık, eğl: MLC 2006 sets minimum standards on matters such as accommodation, food, health, recreational facilities and paid leave. The Chief Officer looks after the deck personnel's living conditions in the accommodation, laundry/cleaning arrangements and general welfare, and finds solutions by passing problems on to the Master. Crew satisfaction reduces turnover and preserves accumulated experience.
MLC 2014 değişiklikleri (2017'de yürürlü: The 2014 amendments to the MLC (in force since 2017) introduced two new mandatory financial securities: (1) insurance or a guarantee covering repatriation, outstanding wages and essential needs in the event of the seafarer's abandonment; (2) financial security for contractual compensation arising from occupational injury, illness or death. The ship must carry the certificates proving this security (usually from a P&I Club) and post them in a visible place.
MLC Title 3, kamara büyüklüğü, havalandı: MLC Title 3 sets concrete standards for cabin size, ventilation/air-conditioning, lighting, noise and vibration limits, beds, sanitary facilities (ratio of toilets and showers), laundry, the hospital and recreational facilities. These standards are largely met at the building or refit stage, but the Master is responsible for maintaining them (maintenance, cleanliness, function). Air-conditioning not working, noise above the limits or too few toilets and showers are real welfare problems.
MLC denetimi ve şirket gözetimi her iki: MLC inspections and company oversight check both sides: the adequacy/quality of the food and spending discipline. By keeping menu, order, cost and satisfaction records, the cook proves both nutritional quality and budget compliance.
MLC denetiminde galley hijyeni, bulaşık: During an MLC inspection, galley hygiene, the order of the dishwashing area, equipment cleanliness and storage are checked. A greasy, dirty or untidy galley results directly in an MLC finding and undermines confidence in the ship's food safety management.
MLC içeriği beş Title altında düzenlenir: The content of the MLC is organised under five Titles: Title 1 — minimum requirements for seafarers to work on a ship (minimum age, medical certificate, training, recruitment); Title 2 — conditions of employment (SEA, wages, hours of work and rest, leave, repatriation, compensation for the ship's loss, manning, career); Title 3 — accommodation, recreational facilities, food and catering; Title 4 — health protection, medical care, welfare and social security; Title 5 — compliance and enforcement (DMLC, inspection, complaints, PSC). The Master is the "supervisor on site" for each of the five Titles.
MLC ve ILO ilkeleri; ırk, renk, cinsiyet: MLC and ILO principles prohibit discrimination based on race, colour, sex, religion, political opinion, or national or social origin. Guidance developed since 2016 (the ICS/ITF Guidance on Eliminating Shipboard Harassment and Bullying) deals explicitly with preventing harassment and bullying on board. In multinational crews, cultural sensitivity, discipline in the use of a common (working) language and equal treatment are part of the Master's daily management.
Under the MLC, the Master's defence is the "record". Rest hour sheets are kept daily and confirmed by the seafarer; when back-filling is detected, the reliability of all the records collapses. Accommodation inspections, water tests, the medicine chest inventory, payroll and complaint records are kept with dates and signatures. These records are evidence for PSC, the flag state and any later employment law case.
MLC, denizcilere karadakine eşdeğer, müm: The MLC aims to provide seafarers with medical care comparable to that available ashore, as far as possible free of charge. On board there is a medical chest, a medical guide (the WHO International Medical Guide for Ships or equivalent) and access to medical advice by radio/satellite (TMAS — Telemedical Maritime Assistance Service). Ships carrying 100 or more persons and ordinarily engaged on international voyages of more than 3 days carry a doctor; on other ships, an officer responsible for medical care (usually the Master or the Second Officer, trained in STCW medical care) is assigned.
MLC, denizcilere ücretsiz, yeterli mikta: The MLC guarantees that seafarers are provided, free of charge, with food and drinking water of sufficient quantity and nutritional value that respect cultural/religious diversity. Catering staff (cooks) must be trained and at least 18 years old; on ships with a prescribed manning of 10 or more, a fully qualified ship's cook (certified ship's cook) is required. The Master checks menu variety, adequacy of portions, food stocks, the cold chain and storage hygiene.
MLC, denizcilerin ücretsiz işe alınmasın: The MLC guarantees that seafarers are recruited free of charge: a seafarer may not be charged for finding a job (the manning agency's commission may not be passed on to the seafarer). Using licensed or regulated recruitment and placement services is essential. The Master watches that seafarers joining the ship have been employed through a legal and transparent process and have not come in situations resembling debt bondage.
MLC, denizcinin belirli durumlarda ücret: The MLC guarantees the seafarer's right to be repatriated free of charge to his or her home country (or an agreed place) in certain circumstances: expiry of the SEA, illness or injury, loss of the ship, justified termination of the SEA by the shipowner or the seafarer, the seafarer being sent to a war zone, and so on. The maximum period of service on board (after which the right to repatriation arises, generally 11 months) is set by flag state law. It is prohibited to recover repatriation costs from the seafarer (by advance deductions), except in cases of serious default by the seafarer.
MLC, gemide çalışmak için asgari yaşı 16: The MLC sets the minimum age for working on a ship at 16; there are restrictions on night work and hazardous work for seafarers under 18. Every seafarer must hold a valid medical fitness certificate (generally valid for 2 years, 1 year for those under 18); a separate period applies for duties requiring colour vision. The Master personally verifies the validity of the medical and STCW certificates of every seafarer joining the ship.
MLC, her gemide adil, etkili ve hızlı bi: The MLC requires every ship to have a fair, effective and quick on-board complaint procedure. A seafarer has the right to take a complaint first to his or her immediate superior and, if it is not resolved, step by step to the Master and, if necessary, to an authority ashore (DPA / company / flag state / port state official). The procedure is given to every seafarer in writing (together with the SEA), and victimisation of a seafarer for making a complaint is strictly prohibited.
MLC, ücretin düzenli (en az ayda bir) ve: The MLC guarantees that wages are paid regularly (at least monthly) and in full; the seafarer is given a monthly wage statement (payslip) and is able to send money to his or her family (allotment). The Master monitors that wage payments on board are made in accordance with the SEA/CBA, on time and with documents; late payment is the most concrete and quickest cause of complaint for a seafarer.
MMSI numarası bayrak devleti tarafından: The MMSI number is assigned by the flag state and is unique.
MOB anında ilk eylemler: \"MAN OVERBOARD: First actions on a MOB: "MAN OVERBOARD" is shouted, a lifebuoy (with light and smoke signal) is thrown to the side the person fell, the MOB button is pressed (marking the GPS position), the rudder is put over to the side the person fell (to swing the propeller away from the person), and a lookout keeps the person in sight continuously and never loses sight of him or her. The Master is called to the bridge and chooses a suitable turning manoeuvre: the Williamson turn (person out of sight, returning along the same track), the Anderson turn (person in sight, quickest turn) or the Scharnow turn.
MOB durumunda Safety Officer, rescue boa: In a MOB situation, the Safety Officer may coordinate the preparation and launching of the rescue boat and directs the rescue team. A fast and organized response is critical because survival time in cold water is limited. MOB equipment (lifebuoy, light, smoke signal) is thrown overboard quickly.
MOB olayları çoğu zaman güverte çalışmas: MOB events usually arise from preventable causes such as work on deck, seasickness or not using a safety harness. After the event the Master investigates the root cause (overboard work permit, harness use, maintenance of the guardrails) and prevents recurrence; prevention is as much a part of crisis management as rescue.
MOB senaryosunda muster list; gözcü (kaz: In a MOB scenario, the muster list assigns the lookout (the person who keeps pointing at the person in the water), the person who releases the MOB marker/lifebuoy, the rescue boat crew (boat commander, engine operator, helmsman), the bridge maneuvering team and the person in charge of communications. Having the rescue boat crew designated and trained in advance is decisive in the golden minutes of the rescue.
MOC formu; değişikliğin tanımı, gerekçes: The MOC form covers the description of the change, its justification, the risk assessment, the approvals required (the Master and usually the company/DPA), the implementation steps and a review after the change. TMSA 3 (OCIMF's self-assessment for tankers) explicitly measures MOC as a performance indicator. Through MOC discipline, the Master prevents a temporary solution (e.g. a workaround for faulty equipment) from becoming a permanent norm.
MOL Comfort vakası, mukavemet limitlerin: The MOL Comfort casualty showed that ignoring strength limits can lead to the loss of the ship.
MR üzerinden Bill of Lading hazırlandığı: Since the Bill of Lading is prepared from the MR, the condition recorded on the MR is reflected directly in the B/L. Failing to record damage makes the ship/company liable for that damage. The Chief Officer's careful cargo inspection is therefore critical for legal protection.
MSB genellikle makine kontrol odasında (: The MSB is usually located in the engine control room (ECR). Safe access must be provided at the front and rear.
MSB yangın ve su hasarından korunmalıdır: The MSB must be protected against fire and water damage.
MSB, hava kesiciler (ACB), bara sistemi,: The MSB consists of air circuit breakers (ACB), the busbar system, measuring instruments (voltmeter, ammeter, wattmeter, frequency meter), the synchroscope, protection relays and control panels.
MSB; jeneratör panelleri, bara sistemi,: The MSB consists of generator panels, the busbar system, distribution panels, measuring instruments, protection relays and control circuits. The main busbar is usually made of copper or aluminium conductors, and the generators and load circuit breakers are connected to this busbar.
MSC.1/Circ.1432 kapsamında tüm yangın ko: Under MSC.1/Circ.1432, all fire protection equipment (detectors, CO2, fire pumps, portable extinguishers, BA sets, fire dampers) is placed on a maintenance/test schedule and entered in the PMS. These records are the primary evidence at the class annual survey and in a PSC inspection; a missing record is a deficiency.
MSL (Maximum Securing Load), bir lashing: MSL (Maximum Securing Load) is the maximum load that a lashing item can safely carry and is usually defined as a proportion of the item's breaking load (e.g. 80% of BL for wire, 50% for web lashing). In calculations, a safety factor is also applied to obtain the CS (Calculated Strength); CSS Code Annex 13 standardizes this calculation.
MSMD bir \"yeterlilik\" değil \"asgari\": The MSMD is a document of the "minimum", not of "adequacy"; on routes with heavy cargo operations, frequent port calls, canal transits or tiring passages, the minimum manning may in practice be insufficient. If the Master finds that the actual workload is forcing the minimum crew into breaches of rest hours, he or she must report this to the company with reasons and request additional personnel or rotation. A crew at minimum manning that is "compliant on paper" but "tired in reality" is the classic beginning of an accident chain.
MT'nin Bridge Mate Integrated Bridge Sys: MT's Bridge Mate Integrated Bridge System holds DNV NAUT-AW type approval, the most comprehensive bridge class notation in the industry. When used together with MT's conning display and ECDIS, the Bridge Mate Autopilot obtains Wheel Mark approval and track control steering certification.
MT, bu sağlam tasarımın özellikle servis: MT stresses that this robust design matters especially on ships where a service engineer and a system specialist are not available around the clock. Offshore, the maker's engineer is often hours or days away when a fault occurs; it is critical that the system can stay up on its own.
Madde 5, şirket SMS'inde kaptanın görevl: Section 5 requires the company's SMS to define the Master's duties clearly, to give the Master the authority to implement the SMS on board and to report deviations to the company, and to confirm the "overriding authority" in writing. In other words, the company must explicitly give the Master the authority to put safety and environmental protection above any commercial consideration. This written confirmation is among the first pieces of evidence looked for in internal and external audits.
Madde 6 ayrıca, geminin emniyeti ve çevr: Section 6 also requires ensuring that duties critical to the safety of the ship and the protection of the environment are understood by the personnel; this covers a common working language, the comprehensibility of instructions and the effectiveness of training. In a multinational crew, the adequacy of the common working language (usually English) is a subject questioned directly in ISM audits and accident analyses.
Magnetronlu veya solid-state verici, sca: A magnetron or solid-state transmitter sends electromagnetic energy through the scanner. The round-trip time of the echo returning from a target gives the range; the azimuth position of the antenna gives the relative bearing. When the gyro heading is added, true bearings and a north-up/course-up presentation can be produced.
Main bearing, crankpin ve thrust bearing: Main bearing, crankpin and thrust bearing temperatures and the sump LO level are monitored. The crankcase oil mist detector (OMD) must be in working order; a high oil mist alarm is a warning of an impending crankcase explosion — the engine is slowed down/stopped immediately, and the crankcase is not opened until it has cooled down sufficiently.
Major NC, denetim bitmeden veya çok kısa: A major NC must be closed before the end of the audit or within a very short time; otherwise the certificate may be suspended and the ship may be prevented from sailing. In the case of a major NC, the Master informs the DPA immediately, takes immediate containment measures and implements the permanent corrective action plan within the time set. A serious ISM-related finding in a PSC inspection is recorded as an "ISM-related detention" and brings additional inspection pressure on the company's whole fleet.
Makine daireleri için CO₂ miktarı, korun: For machinery spaces, the quantity of CO₂ is calculated to fill a certain percentage of the protected volume (and the casing); for machinery spaces SOLAS requires CO₂ corresponding to about 40% of the gross volume (or a larger calculation including the casing). A different (lower) ratio is used for cargo spaces.
Makine daireleri için gazın büyük kısmı: For machinery spaces, most of the gas must be discharged in a short time (about 2 minutes) so that the concentration reaches the extinguishing level quickly and re-ignition is prevented. The pipe diameters and nozzle design provide this flow.
Makine dairesi A-class divisions (A-60/A: The engine room is enclosed by A-class divisions (A-60/A-30/A-0). Fire dampers and the skylight and ventilation closing (quick-closing) arrangements are there to cut off the air and smother the fire in the event of fire. Quick-closing valves (fuel/oil tank outlets) can be closed from outside the engine room (remotely, usually from the fire control station).
Makine dairesi alarmları kademelidir: ön: Engine room alarms are graded: first a warning (alarm), then slow-down (automatic speed reduction) and finally shut-down (automatic stop). Critical alarms (LO low pressure, jacket water high temp, scavenge fire, overspeed) trigger automatic intervention to protect the engine. The cadet learns the meaning of each alarm and the action it triggers.
Makine dairesi bilge suyu, ancak 15 ppm: Engine room bilge water may be discharged only through a 15 ppm Oily Water Separator (OWS), monitored by the oil content meter, with the ship en route (in special areas the equipment must also stop the discharge automatically; in the Antarctic area no discharge is allowed). All transfers, discharges and sludge operations are entered in ORB Part I with time, position and quantity. On tankers, cargo and ballast operations are entered in ORB Part II.
Makine dairesi dışından (köprü/fire stat: Emergency stops that can be activated from outside the engine room (bridge/fire station): remote stop of fuel/oil transfer pumps, separator/booster pump stop, ventilation fan stop and quick-closing valves. These arrangements cut off the fuel supply to a fire. All remote stops are tested periodically and must be clearly labeled.
Makine dairesi dışından uzaktan durdurul: Equipment that must be stoppable remotely from outside the engine room: fuel transfer and booster pumps, lubricating oil pumps, separators, ventilation fans and the boiler burner. This emergency stop arrangement isolates the space from fuel and air.
Makine dairesi emniyeti, tek bir ekipman: Engine room safety is not about a single piece of equipment; it is the management of the continuous soundness of the prevention, detection, containment and response barriers. The Chief Engineer's task is to make sure that none of these barriers is taken out of service "temporarily" and that each of them has been tested in a provable way. A shortcut in safety is a price that is paid sooner or later.
Makine dairesi housekeeping'i, İkinci Mü: Engine room housekeeping is the most visible and most continuous test of the Second Engineer's leadership quality. Disciplined order reduces the risk of fire and accidents, makes environmental compliance easier, increases equipment reliability and shapes a positive impression of the ship at every inspection. A well-managed engine room marks the ship as "well operated" before a single record has been examined.
Makine dairesi kaynaklarının yönetimi, g: Management of engine room resources, allocation and prioritisation of tasks, effective communication, leadership and teamwork, situational awareness, decision-making and problem solving.
Makine dairesi merdivenleri dik ve metal: Engine room ladders are steep and made of metal; a film of oil on them leads to serious falls. The Wiper gives priority to keeping ladder steps, handrails and walkways clean and dry, and checks that anti-slip surfaces remain effective.
Makine dairesi sintinesi, tank içleri, k: The risk of electric shock increases in damp/conductive environments such as the engine room bilges, the inside of tanks, the boiler room and the open deck. In these spaces, low-voltage (e.g. 24 V) hand lamps, double-insulated or earthed portable tools and, where necessary, an isolating transformer are used. The ETO verifies that portable equipment is suitable for these spaces.
Makine dairesi skylight'ları, kapıları v: The engine room skylights, doors and other openings must be able to be closed in a fire; there are remote closing or quick manual closing arrangements. The closing sequence and the people responsible are defined in the fire plan and the emergency procedure.
Makine dairesi sıvı yakıt yangınları içi: For liquid fuel fires in the engine room there may be a fixed high-expansion foam system or a local application system; there are also portable foam applicators supplied from the fire main.
Makine dairesi tahliye edildikten ve tüm: Once the engine room has been evacuated and everyone has been accounted for, the fixed CO₂ or FM200 (HFC-227ea) extinguishing system can be released.
Makine dairesi tahliye/CO₂ salımı öncesi: Before the engine room is evacuated and CO₂ released, the remotely operated emergency shutdowns are activated: the quick-closing valves of the fuel service/settling tanks are closed (cutting off the fuel supply), the fuel transfer/booster pumps, ventilation fans and purifiers are stopped remotely, and the ventilation flaps/dampers are closed. These are generally operated from a panel/box outside the engine room.
Makine dairesi terk edilmeden önce kapsa: Before the engine room is left unmanned, a thorough inspection round is made, all systems are checked, the alarm system is tested and the UMS checklist is completed.
Makine dairesi ve kargo bölgesi sabit CO: Fixed CO2/clean agent systems for the engine room and the cargo area are subject to annual inspection and periodic weighing/pressure checks. The Chief Officer (usually in coordination with the Second/Third Engineer) monitors the cylinder fill percentage, the distribution piping, the alarm/time delay and the functioning of the release mechanism. An inadvertent release is fatal; this is why the alarm that clears personnel from the space before release, and the interlock, are critical.
Makine dairesi ve kargo mahalleri için f: Fixed CO2 (or foam/water-mist/aerosol) systems are provided for the engine room and cargo spaces. The Safety Officer checks the cylinder pressures, release manifold seals, the alarm-before-release system, the ventilation/fuel shut-off interlocks and the warnings at the bottle room entrance. Before CO2 is released, the sequence of clearing all personnel from the space + alarm + ventilation stop must always be followed.
Makine dairesi ventilasyonu hem yanma ha: Engine room ventilation is critical both for combustion air and for personnel; clogged intake grilles and dirty filters adversely affect both engine performance and the ambient temperature. The Second Engineer includes the cleaning of the ventilation and the hoods in the housekeeping program.
Makine dairesi yakıt kayıtları ile köprü: A daily reconciliation should be made between the engine room fuel records and the bridge navigation data; discrepancies should be corrected before they are carried into the DCS/MRV reports. This discipline increases the reliability of the CII rating.
Makine dairesi yangın emniyeti, yakıt/ya: Engine room fire safety includes the quick-closing valves of fuel/oil tanks (which shut off the fuel flow remotely in a fire), the remote emergency stops of pumps, and the ventilation damper/fan stop functions. These devices are tested periodically; it is verified that the fire pump, fuel shut-off and air shut-off can be operated from a single point in a fire. They are covered by SOLAS II-2 and are a focus of PSC inspections.
Makine dairesi yangınları genellikle yük: Engine room fires usually start when a high-pressure fuel/oil leak comes into contact with a hot surface (exhaust, T/C, manifold). Early detection (fire detection, flame detectors) and rapid response (portable extinguishers, fire team) are critical.
Makine dairesi yangınlarının büyük çoğun: Most engine room fires start when a pressurized oil/fuel leak sprays onto a hot surface (>220°C) such as an exhaust manifold, a turbine casing or a steam line. Oil accumulated on the floor and on equipment becomes the fuel for this fire, which then spreads rapidly. A clean engine room removes this fire load.
Makine dairesi yangınlarının çoğunluğu,: Most engine room fires start when a pressurized fuel/oil leak sprays onto a hot surface (exhaust manifold, turbine casing >220°C). Fuel sprayed as a fine mist ignites instantly. By catching leaks early (routine rounds), the Oiler prevents a fire before it starts; this is the first defense.
Makine dairesi yangını en tehlikeli gemi: An engine room fire is one of the most dangerous fires on a ship; fuel, oil and hot surfaces are present together. The response includes the steps of shutting off the fuel supply (quick-closing valves), shutting down the ventilation (ventilation flaps), withdrawing personnel, closing off the space (boundary cooling) and activating the fixed smothering system (CO2/foam/water mist). A personnel count is always carried out before the fixed system is released.
Makine dairesi yangını kontrol edilemezs: If an engine room fire cannot be controlled, the fixed CO₂ total flooding system is activated. This system extinguishes the fire by smothering it of oxygen; however, CO₂ is lethal to people. For this reason, before release, the engine room is completely evacuated, a head count is made and all openings (ventilation flaps, doors) are closed.
Makine dairesi yangınında ana yangın pom: In an engine room fire, the main fire pump may be unusable; in that case the emergency fire pump, located outside the engine room and with its own power source, is started and pressurizes the fire main. The Oiler knows the location of the emergency fire pump, its starting procedure and its suction line.
Makine dairesi yüksek gürültü, sıcak yüz: The engine room is an environment with high noise, hot surfaces, rotating equipment and slip hazards. The cadet uses safety shoes, a hard hat, ear protection (mandatory in zones above 85 dB(A)), a boiler suit and, where necessary, eye/face protection. Loose clothing, jewelry and loose hair are a lethal hazard near rotating parts.
Makine dairesi; sıcak yüzeyler (egzoz ma: The engine room is a high-risk space where hot surfaces (exhaust manifold, turbine, boiler), high-pressure fuel/oil lines and electrical equipment are found together. A fuel/oil leak dripping onto a hot surface is the main fire scenario of SOLAS II-2 and the leading cause of engine room fires. Housekeeping is the first line of defense that reduces the "ignition probability" of this scenario.
Makine dairesinde biriken yağlı sintine: Oily bilge water accumulated in the engine room must not be discharged directly into the sea; it is first processed by the Oily Water Separator (OWS / 15 ppm bilge separator). The OWS separates the water from the oil, and the Oil Content Monitor (OCM / 15 ppm alarm) continuously measures the oil content of the water leaving it. If 15 ppm is exceeded, the three-way valve automatically redirects the discharge back to the bilge tank (not to the sea).
Makine dairesinde en az iki bağımsız kaç: The engine room has at least two independent escape routes, and these must be unobstructed at all times. The Second Engineer ensures that tools, materials, hoses or temporary storage left in passageways are removed immediately; an escape route is never a storage area.
Makine dairesinde gürültü seviyesi tipik: The noise level in the engine room is typically between 90 and 110 dB(A). The IMO Noise Code (MSC.337(91); formerly A.468(XII)) sets the noise limits: machinery spaces max 110 dB(A), control room max 75 dB(A).
Makine dairesinde güvenlik, ekibin ekipm: Safety in the engine room depends on the team knowing the equipment and the risks. The Second Engineer sees training not as a formality but as the foundation of accident prevention and operational continuity. A well-trained team acts correctly both in routine work and in an emergency.
Makine dairesinde kullanılan başlıca kal: The main lifting equipment used in the engine room comprises chain blocks / lever hoists, overhead travelling cranes and monorails (overhead crane above the ME), wire rope slings, chain slings, textile/web slings (polyester webbing slings), shackles, eye bolts and trolleys. Each has its own SWL, limits of use and inspection criteria.
Makine dairesinde santrifüj (cooling wat: The engine room has centrifugal pumps (cooling water, ballast), positive displacement pumps (FO/LO transfer, screw/gear) and eccentric screw pumps (sludge). The cadet learns which pump type is used in which system and why (according to pressure/flow/viscosity requirements).
Makine dairesinde soğutma suyu sıcaklık: Cooling water temperature control in the engine room is a typical example of a closed loop: the temperature sensor measures → the controller compares → the thermostatic valve is adjusted.
Makine dairesinde su yükselmesi; sea che: A rising water level in the engine room may result from a sea chest/sea valve leak, a cooler tube rupture, shell plating damage or a burst pipe. The bilge high-level alarm gives early warning; the Chief Engineer quickly finds the source and isolates it.
Makine dairesinde tehlikeler katmanlıdır: Hazards in the engine room come in layers: physical (noise, vibration, temperature, pressure), mechanical (rotating shafts, belts, couplings, rotating machine tools), chemical (fuel vapor, oil, coolant, cleaning chemicals, battery acid), electrical (high-voltage panels) and atmospheric (O₂ deficiency in enclosed spaces, toxic/flammable gas). Each type requires its own control method.
Makine dairesinde temel PPE her zaman gi: Basic PPE is always worn in the engine room: steel-toe safety shoes (non-slip soles), coveralls (non-flammable/cotton, not loose-fitting), a safety helmet (falling objects/impact) and, in the engine room, hearing protection. Job-specific PPE is added on top: a face shield and leather apron for welding/grinding, chemical gloves for chemicals, heat-resistant gloves for hot work.
Makine dairesinde tipik yaralanmalar: ya: Typical injuries in the engine room are burns (hot surfaces/steam/fluids), cuts/crushing (tools, rotating equipment), eye injuries (swarf/chemical splashes), chemical contact and electric shock. The Oiler knows where the nearest first-aid cabinet, eye wash and emergency shower are.
Makine dairesinde water mist hem total f: In the engine room, water mist is used both for total flooding and as local application for high-risk equipment (burners, separators, main engine); it quickly controls fires from oil leaks.
Makine dairesinde yangının üç temel bile: In the engine room, the three basic components of a fire are present together: fuel (oil/fuel leaks), oxygen (forced ventilation) and an igniting hot surface (exhaust manifold ~400°C, turbine casing, steam pipes). Fuel spraying onto a hot surface from a crack in a high-pressure fuel line (HP fuel line) turns into a major fire within minutes.
Makine dairesinde yüksek gerilim panolar: There are high-voltage panels and circuits in the engine room. The Oiler/Fitter does not undertake electrical work for which they are not authorized; electrical work is done by an authorized person after isolation, locking and testing (LOTO + voltage test). Using power tools on a wet floor, damaged cables and unearthed equipment carry a risk of electric shock.
Makine dairesinde, en yüksek kapasiteli: The engine room has an emergency bilge suction that takes suction directly through the largest-capacity pump. The valve position, accessibility and working condition of this arrangement are verified during drills; material stowed in front of it is a typical finding.
Makine dairesine kontrolsüz su girişinde: In the event of uncontrolled water ingress into the engine room (cooler burst, sea valve failure, hull damage), the source is isolated first, then the bilge pumps and, if necessary, the emergency bilge suction are brought into use. The bridge is informed, and if necessary the effect on stability/draft is assessed. This scenario is drilled regularly.
Makine dairesine su girişi; deniz suyu h: Water may enter the engine room as a result of a burst sea water line, a sea chest/valve failure, hull damage, a crack in a cooling line or back-flooding. The bilge high-level alarm gives early warning. When the Oiler notices water ingress, they immediately raise the alarm, try to identify the source (which valve/line) and isolate it if possible.
Makine dairesinin en az iki ayrı kaçış y: The engine room has at least two separate means of escape, at least one of which is protected (escape trunk). The Oiler knows by heart the normal and alternative escape routes, the locations of the EEBDs (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) and the emergency lighting. An EEBD provides ~10-15 minutes of breathing for escape from a smoke-filled space; it is used for escape, not for firefighting.
Makine dairesinin en az iki bağımsız kaç: The engine room has at least two independent escape routes; one of these may be a protected (fire-protected) escape trunk. The cadet must know the escape routes well enough to find them with eyes closed, because in a real fire smoke can reduce visibility to zero. Emergency lighting and photoluminescent signs then show the way.
Makine departmanı; black-out recovery, e: The engine department takes part in black-out recovery, engine room fire, flooding, steering gear failure and enclosed space rescue drills. The Chief Engineer plans and observes these drills and reports any deficiencies. Drills must be run with realistic scenarios and must not turn into a routine "form-filling" formality.
Makine her gün sonunda boşaltılıp temizl: At the end of each day, the machine is drained and cleaned; cleaning the filter, checking for scale and emptying the strainer are routine maintenance. A clogged filter both impairs washing and produces odors and bacteria. A machine fault (not heating, not filling with water) is reported immediately; dishes washed at low temperature are not sanitized.
Makine kayıtları sadece geçmişi belgelem: Engine records do not just document the past; they manage the future. Wrong or invented data leads to wrong maintenance decisions, unexpected breakdowns and loss of trust during inspections. The Third/Fourth Engineer does not fill in a value that could not be measured with an estimate; the value is either measured or noted as "could not be measured".
Makine personeli eğitimi, İkinci Mühendi: Training of engine personnel is the most valuable investment the Second Engineer makes in the team and in the safety of the ship. Proper familiarization, sound safety training and realistic emergency drills make the engine room both efficient in routine operation and resilient in a crisis.
Makine personelinin yönetimi, Baş Mühend: Managing engine personnel is the most visible reflection of the Chief Engineer's technical leadership. A well-managed team produces fewer accidents, higher maintenance quality and a stronger safety culture. The modern Chief Engineer is as much a mentor, planner and human resources manager as an engineer.
Makine sistemlerini öğrenmek, ekipman is: Learning machinery systems is not memorizing equipment names but understanding the path of the fluid, the conversion of energy and the dependencies between systems. When the cadet learns each system in terms of "purpose, flow, failure, protection", the engine room stops being a puzzle and becomes a meaningful whole. This holistic understanding lays a solid foundation for fault diagnosis and operational management later on.
Makine stajyeri için deniz hizmeti, maki: For the engine cadet, sea service means the period of structured training and supervised duties in the engine room. This period is not just "being on board" but the active period during which the training program (TRB) is carried out. This is why Sea Service and the TRB complement each other: one proves the duration, the other the content.
Makine stajyerinin bakım desteğindeki ge: The engine cadet's real gain from assisting with maintenance is not just dismantling and reassembling a pump, but experiencing planning, isolation, measurement, precision and documentation together. Manual skill is gained through repetition, technical language through curiosity and safety awareness through discipline. The meticulousness learned under supervision today is the signature discipline of the engineer who will carry out maintenance independently tomorrow.
Makine stajyerinin vardiya katılımındaki: The engine cadet's success in watch participation comes not from moving fast but from observing correctly, reporting on time and respecting the limits of authority. The discipline learned under supervision today forms the basis of the safety culture of the engineer who will keep an independent watch tomorrow. A good cadet learns what is "normal" so well that he or she notices what is "abnormal" before anyone else.
Makine tarafında turboşarj verimi, enjek: On the engine side, turbocharger efficiency, injector balance, air cooler cleanliness and hull and propeller condition become more critical with limited power; even a small loss of efficiency can turn into a deviation from the schedule.
Makine vardiyası, görünmeyen bir başarı: An engine room watch is an art of invisible success: on a well-kept watch nothing happens, because the engineer has caught problems before any alarm sounds, read the trends and acted in time. The Third/Fourth Engineer's disciplined rounds, honest records and correct reporting reflex are the engine room's first line of defense.
Makine yedek parça ve sarf bütçesi, gemi: The engine spare parts and consumables budget is a significant item of the ship's annual OPEX. The Chief Engineer spends within the annual budget approved by the company (Superintendent) and reports the actual vs budget variance monthly. Unplanned major breakdowns strain the budget; anticipating failures through predictive maintenance is therefore a direct cost saving.
Makine üreticisinin (OEM) bakım el kitap: The sectional and assembly drawings in the machinery manufacturer's (OEM) maintenance manuals show the internal construction of a piece of equipment part by part. In a pump overhaul, these drawings give the dismantling/assembly sequence of the parts, torque values and part numbers.
Makine ısıtılır, yakıt geçişi yapılır, h: The engine is warmed up, the fuel is changed over, the air receivers are full and the telegraph test is carried out. With frequent manoeuvring, disciplined preparation is especially important.
Makine, pompa ve boru yüzeyleri temiz tu: When machinery, pump and pipe surfaces are kept clean, a new leak (weeping) is noticed immediately; clean equipment is therefore also a diagnostic tool. During cleaning, electrical panels, cable connections and hot surfaces are not exposed to water/chemicals.
Makine, pompa ve filtre altlarındaki dri: The drip trays and save-all trays under machinery, pumps and filters are designed to collect leaking oil; however, when they become full, they overflow and stop doing their job. The Wiper empties these trays regularly and keeps them clean. The oil removed is always transferred to the sludge/waste oil tank and is never mixed into the bilge or the sea.
Makinelerin döndüğü (rotasyon kontrolü): It is verified that the machines are rotating (rotation check) and that the nozzles are not blocked; low pressure or a machine that does not rotate prevents effective washing.
Makro fouling (yosun, midye, deniz lales: Macro-fouling (weed, mussels, barnacles): 10–40% increase in resistance.
Malzeme gemiye geldiğinde Reis, teslimat: When material arrives on board, the Bosun compares the delivery note with the order list: items, quantities and specifications are checked, and the goods are checked for damage. Missing, wrong or damaged items are written on the delivery note as a "remark" and reported to the Chief Officer; a shortage accepted silently later becomes the ship's problem.
Malzeme israfı, hem maliyet hem de denet: Waste of materials is a problem in terms of both cost and inspections. The most common sources of waste are: paint mixed incorrectly and thrown away, epoxy left to dry in the open, cutting unnecessarily long lengths of rope, lost hand tools and undisciplined drawing of consumables. The Bosun records the issue of materials, so that "who took how much" is known.
Malzemenin ısıl iletkenliği, ısı transfe: The thermal conductivity of the material is the critical parameter that determines the accuracy of heat transfer calculations.
Management of Change (Değişim Yönetimi),: Management of Change ensures that any permanent or temporary change on board (equipment, procedures, crew composition, software, structure) is assessed in a controlled way. For example, if the type of a critical valve is to be changed, a procedure is to be bypassed or an experienced officer is to be replaced by a new one, the MOC process is triggered. The aim is to prevent a change that "looks small" from creating hidden risks.
Manevra bitince tug çözülür. Gergin tug: When the maneuver is completed, the tug is let go. A tug line under tension is never cast off by hand; the bridge passes "ease the line" to the tug, and once the tension is off, the AB lets go the line under control and returns it to the tug. If a quick-release arrangement is fitted, the AB knows how to use it and in which situations it is to be used.
Manevra boyunca emirler tekrar edilerek: During manoeuvring orders are repeated back before they are carried out; the bell book is kept. Continuous running in the barred speed range is avoided.
Manevra durumlarında (liman giriş-çıkış,: During maneuvering (entering/leaving port, narrow channels), the engine room goes to standby: an extra generator is put in parallel, the main engine is switched from UMS to manual control and the EOOW stands by in the control room. The cadet observes the coordination between telegraph orders, speed requests from the bridge and the "stand by engines / finished with engines" orders.
Manevra evresinde yalnızca standard mari: Only the Standard Marine Communication Phrases should be used during manoeuvring; no order should be carried out before the "order – read-back – confirmation" loop has been completed.
Manevra komutları, vana operasyonları, e: Manoeuvring orders, valve operations, electrical switching operations, emergency procedures. Without closed-loop communication, mistakes such as opening or closing the wrong valve can happen.
Manevra sırasında \"double watchkeeping\: During manoeuvring the principle of "double watchkeeping" is applied: the position is checked by ECDIS, by radar parallel indexing and by visual bearings. Relying on a single instrument is flagged in MAIB reports as a "single point of failure".
Manevra sırasında ani komut değişiklikle: During maneuvering, the engine room is ready for sudden changes of order, many starts/stops and crash astern maneuvers; starting air consumption and scavenge temperature are watched closely.
Manevra sırasında pilot, köprüüstüne kom: During maneuvering, the pilot gives orders to the bridge; the bridge passes them to the station by radio ("heave away forward spring", "slack head line", "make fast", "let go aft"). The Bosun confirms these orders by read-back and carries them out at the station. If an order is not understood, "say again" is used; no action is taken on guesswork.
Manevra sırasında sürekli iletişim hattı: A continuous communication line is kept open during manoeuvring. Critical orders are recorded in the Engine Log Book.
Manevra vardiyasında en az iki kişi akti: At least two people should be kept active during a manoeuvring watch: one for the telegraph and carrying out orders, the other for following alarms and the continuity of auxiliary systems. This division of duties should be confirmed with a written card before the watch.
Manevra ve bağlama gözlemi, güverte staj: Observing maneuvering and mooring gives the deck cadet the opportunity to learn the most dynamic moments of seafaring live. Observing the phases, understanding the maneuvering data and the discipline of observing safely prepare the cadet to become an officer who will make their own maneuvering decisions with confidence in the future.
Manevra öncesi \"stand-by main engine\": Before maneuvering, on a "stand-by main engine" request, the engine is put into maneuvering mode: the second generator is on line, the starting air receivers are full, FO heating is correct, the control test (ahead/astern) has been carried out and the telegraph test has been completed. Throughout the maneuver, the Third/Fourth Engineer closely monitors the telegraph orders and the engine's response.
Manevra öncesi 5 dakikalık ortak brifing: In a 5-minute joint briefing before the manoeuvre, the critical set of orders, the expected sequence and possible reversing orders should be made clear.
Manevra öncesi Birinci Zabit, baş üstü e: Before maneuvering, the Chief Officer gives a toolbox briefing to the forward mooring team (bosun + deck ratings): who will operate the winch, who will throw the heaving line, who will hold the stopper and who will handle communications. Everyone must know their task and their own snap-back zone. The radio channel between the bridge and the forward/aft stations must be clear and confirmed.
Manevra, ağır hava, bunker ve kritik bak: In situations such as maneuvering, heavy weather, bunkering and critical maintenance, additional personnel are called to duty. The Second Engineer plans these call-outs in advance (e.g. adjusting rest according to the port arrival time) and keeps the arrangement consistent with the emergency muster list. In an emergency, the engine room roles (fire team, bilge/flooding, blackout recovery) are clearly assigned.
Manevra, dar su geçişi, yoğun yük operas: Before manoeuvring, passages through narrow waters, intensive cargo operations or bad weather, the personnel concerned are made sure to be rested. The Master plans the port programme and the allocation of duties so as to reduce fatigue; if necessary, operations are slowed down or extra rest is given.
Manevra, liman ve düşük devirli seyirde: During manoeuvring, in port and at low engine speeds, the shaft generator output falls or it is disconnected; in these phases the load is transferred to the auxiliary diesel generators. A seamless changeover depends on the PMS (power management system) logic.
Manevrada geminin atalet, dümen/pervane: During maneuvering, the ship's inertia, the response to rudder/propeller, the effect of wind/current, the use of tugs and team coordination can all be observed at the same time. The cadet sees textbook knowledge in real motion. Good observation lays the foundation for the cadet's own maneuvering decisions in the future.
Manifestteki hata veya eksiklik, gümrükt: An error or omission in the manifest can lead to a customs fine, the cargo not being released and delay to the ship. The Master confirms that the manifest matches the B/Ls and the actual cargo.
Manifold bolt'ları yıldız (çapraz) sıray: The manifold bolts are tightened in a star (cross) pattern with the torque increased in stages; tightening on one side crushes the gasket and causes a leak. All bolt holes must be filled; no connection is made with bolts missing.
Manifold, tanker güvenliğinin en yoğun r: The manifold is the point of highest risk for tanker safety; what matters here is not speed but verifying every flange one by one.
Manila değişiklikleriyle birlikte STCW T: With the Manila amendments, STCW Tables A-II/1 and A-II/2 made Bridge Resource Management and Bridge Team Management competences mandatory for Masters and officers. These competences are not just theoretical knowledge; they are behavioural skills: keeping the hierarchy without undermining safety, a "challenge and response" culture, sharing situational awareness, and awareness of human factor risks.
Manlı (manned) makine dairesinde tur tip: In a manned engine room, rounds are typically made every hour, or at the latest every two hours; in UMS mode, daytime checks + alarm-based response apply. A round follows a systematic route: main engine platform, generator flat, boiler and FO unit, purifier room, pump flat, separator/OWS area, shaft tunnel and steering gear.
Manning planlaması ile rest hours yöneti: Manning planning and rest hour management are two sides of the same coin: an insufficient crew makes breaches of rest hours mathematically inevitable. If the Master has to choose between "making the records look clean" and "really letting the crew rest", he or she must choose the latter and send the company a written request for the manning or rotation that would make the former possible.
Manual call point (yangın ihbar butonu),: A manual call point (fire alarm button) allows a person to raise the fire alarm manually; it is of the break-glass or push type and is located along escape routes at intervals complying with SOLAS. The ETO periodically tests the electrical continuity of the MCPs and the operation of the glass/button mechanism.
Manual fix yalnız sembol koymak değil; s: A manual fix is not just placing a symbol; it is a record of the source, time, accuracy and any discrepancy. When a position jump or freeze, spoofing or jamming, a datum mismatch or a misalignment of charted objects is seen, reliance on track control is stopped, the Master is called and the safe speed and sea room are reassessed.
Manuel pozisyon girilen cihazlarda en ge: On equipment where the position is entered manually, the position must be updated at least every 4 hours. In A2/A4 areas, this is a point that is often skipped in practice on MF/HF DSC equipment but is questioned at inspections.
Manuel sounding, seviye transmitter arız: Manual sounding is done when a level transmitter fails or for verification. A sounding pipe and a sounding tape are used. The measurement is taken as ullage (empty distance) or innage (filled depth).
Manuel yağlama noktaları (greasing point: Manual lubrication points (greasing points) — fan bearings, valve spindles, door hinges, crane/winch bearings — are greased with a grease gun according to the PMS schedule. Over-lubrication is at least as harmful as under-lubrication (strain on seals, dirt sticking). The Oiler uses the correct type of grease (according to temperature/application).
Manuel ölçümde dahi vapour'a maruz kalma: Even manual gauging carries a risk of exposure to vapour; the correct PPE (gas detector, suitable respiratory protection where needed) and standing upwind are essential. Additional precautions are taken with cargoes containing H2S.
Manuel, joystick ve DP operasyonlarının: Manual, joystick and DP operations are all brought together at one point. The DP Chair is available with DP 1 and DP 2 operator stations and can replace or complement the conventional stand-alone DP consoles on the bridge. Chair configurations with a dedicated DP operator station and a Multi-Function Workstation for bridge applications are also available.
Manyetik pusula manyetik kuzeyi gösterir: The magnetic compass points to magnetic north. The angle between true north and magnetic north is the variation, taken from the chart with its annual change. The error caused by the ship's own magnetic field is the deviation; it changes with the ship's heading and the cargo, and is given for each compass heading by the deviation card.
Manyetik pusula, gemideki demir ve çelik: The magnetic compass has a deviation error caused by the iron and steel structures of the ship. This error is corrected with the Flinders bar, soft-iron spheres and magnets (compass adjustment).
Manyetik pusula, geminin çelik gövdesi v: The magnetic compass deviates from magnetic north (deviation) because of the local magnetic field created by the ship's steel hull and electrical equipment. This deviation is different for each heading and is shown on the "deviation card" (deviation table). Total compass error = variation + deviation.
Marine Technologies, LLC 2002'de kuruldu: Marine Technologies, LLC was founded in 2002, and its initial aim was to develop a DP system that met the IMO guidelines for DP class 2. The first ship equipped by MT received a DP-2 classification from ABS within 16 months. The company has since delivered more than 100 DP systems, most of them on DP class 2 ships.
Marş düzeni akü, hidrolik akümülatör vey: The starting arrangement may be batteries, a hydraulic accumulator or an independent air receiver; in every case it is essential that it is not supplied from the main source of power and that it keeps its capability for consecutive starts.
