Marş hattında flame arrester (alev tutuc: The starting air line has a flame arrester, and each receiver has a safety valve and a bursting disc. Air receivers are subject to class survey; internal corrosion and thickness are checked.
Marş havası genelde ~30 bar gerektirir;: Starting air generally requires about 30 bar; compressing in a single stage causes overheating and a loss of efficiency. Two-stage compression is therefore used: the first stage raises the air to an intermediate pressure, the intercooler cools it and the second stage brings it to the final pressure. Cooling increases efficiency and reduces carbonisation of the oil.
Marş havası şişeden basınç düşürücü (red: Starting air from the receiver is fed to the control and service lines through a reducing valve. Because a loss of control air can paralyse critical automation, continuity is ensured with a separate control air receiver (reserve).
Masalar ve sandalyeler dezenfekte edilir: Tables and chairs are disinfected, the floor is swept and mopped, and condiment sets and jugs are cleaned and refilled. The mess is set up again in mise en place for the next meal, so that the next service always starts ready.
Master's Review (kaptanın SMS değerlendi: The Master's Review (the Master's evaluation of the SMS) is the Master's periodic feedback on the effectiveness of the system on board and a critical input to the management review. Here the Master reports honestly any gaps of the "it's on paper but not working in practice" kind; this honesty is the only way for the system really to improve. A Master's Review that hides the reality on board is one of the most dangerous management failures.
Master's Review, ISM'in kalp atışıdır. Y: The Master's Review is the heartbeat of the ISM system. At least once a year (generally every six months), the Master evaluates the effectiveness of the SMS on board and reports deficiencies and suggestions for improvement to the company in writing. These reports are reviewed by the DPA (Designated Person Ashore) and are an input to the company's management review.
Mate's Receipt (MR), yükün gemiye fiilen: The Mate's Receipt (MR) is the internal record documenting that the cargo has actually been received on board and its "apparent order and condition". The Chief Officer checks the quantity (by draft survey/tally) and the condition of the cargo loaded. If the cargo shows visible damage, wetness, rust or shortage, the Chief Officer writes the appropriate reservations (clausing/remarks) on the MR.
Mate's Receipt, yükün gemiye alındığını: The Mate's Receipt is the preliminary document showing that the cargo has been received on board, and it forms the basis of the B/L. Reservations about the cargo (clausing) are first entered on the mate's receipt; these reservations are carried over to the B/L. The Cargo Manifest is the list of all the cargo (by B/L) with port, consignee, quantity and description, and it is the basis of the customs declaration.
Mate's Receipt, yükün gemiye fiilen alın: The Mate's Receipt is the internal record documenting that the cargo has actually been received on board and its condition (apparent order and condition). The Bill of Lading is prepared from it. If the cargo is damaged or short, it is "claused"; otherwise a clean B/L is signed and the ship/company becomes responsible for that condition.

The Mate's Receipt is the internal record documenting that the cargo was actually received on board and its condition; the B/L is issued on the basis of this receipt. The remarks (damage notes) on the Mate's Receipt must be carried over to the B/L. The Master checks that this chain is consistent.
Matkap tezgahında (drill press) iş parça: On the drill press, the workpiece must always be secured with a vise/clamp; a part held by hand spins when the drill bit grabs it and is flung around like a whip, causing injury. The correct drill bit (HSS, suitable for the material), the correct speed and cooling are used. The machine is stopped to remove the bit.
Mauritius açıklarında karaya oturma, doğ: Grounding off Mauritius: approaching the coast for a birthday celebration and an unplanned route to get a Wi-Fi signal. Lesson: any deviation from the passage plan needs written justification; "small" personal motives trigger major accidents.
Mechanical seal montajı pompanın en hass: Fitting the mechanical seal is the most delicate operation on a pump: the seal faces must not be touched by hand, scratched or run dry. Incorrect fitting results in early seal failure and leakage. The cadet learns the importance of clean assembly, correct orientation and proper lubrication.
Mechanical seal ve bearing PMS aralıklar: Mechanical seals and bearings are replaced at the PMS intervals; impellers are inspected for wear and erosion. Vibration analysis is used to detect failures early.
Megger (insulation resistance tester), D: A megger (insulation resistance tester) measures the resistance between the conductor and the hull by applying a DC test voltage (500 V, 1000 V or 2500 V).
Megger (insülasyon tester), ölçülen devr: A megger (insulation tester) applies a DC voltage to the circuit being measured and measures the leakage current between the conductor and earth. The insulation resistance is calculated from the measured current.
Megger testi ile hat bazında izolasyon d: The insulation resistance of each line is measured with a megger test and the faulty circuit is found.
Mekanik bakımların büyük çoğunluğu PMS (: Most mechanical maintenance is triggered through the PMS (Planned Maintenance System); jobs such as valve overhauls, opening up pumps and cleaning coolers are planned by running hours or by calendar. The Fitter reads the work order and verifies that the necessary spare parts, gaskets, O-rings, packing and consumables are in stock; if anything is missing, the Fitter informs the engineer.
Mekanik bakımın kalitesi doğru ölçümle b: The quality of mechanical maintenance begins with correct measurement. The Fitter uses instruments such as calipers, micrometers, feeler gauges, dial gauges and bore gauges skillfully. Bearing clearances, shaft diameter, ovality (oval wear) and flatness are compared with the manufacturer's tolerances; a part outside the limits is replaced.
Mekanik kayıplar: Yağlama optimizasyonu,: Mechanical losses: lubrication optimisation, friction reduction.
Mekanik montajda üretici tork değerleri,: In mechanical assembly, the manufacturer's torque values are applied with the correct spanner and a torque wrench; tightening by eye/feel is not accepted on critical connections. When the job is complete, the system is re-energized, a leak test is carried out and the parameters (pressure, temperature, current, vibration) are monitored on the first start.
Mekanik salmastra hassas bir parçadır; m: A mechanical seal is a precision part; when it is fitted, the faces must be perfectly clean and free of scratches, and the correct compression must be applied. On pumps with gland packing, a slight drip is normal and provides cooling; tightening the packing until it is completely leak-free burns it.
Mekanik soğutma çevrimi dört temel bileş: The mechanical refrigeration cycle is based on four basic components: the compressor (compresses the gas), the condenser (rejects heat and liquefies the gas), the expansion valve (reduces the pressure) and the evaporator (absorbs heat and provides cooling). The ETO manages the electrical control (compressor motor, fan motors, valve solenoids, sensors) and the safety devices of this cycle.
Mekanik temizlik tek başına yetmez; tuz: Mechanical cleaning alone is not enough; salt deposits draw moisture under the paint and cause early breakdown. This is why the prepared surface is washed with fresh water to remove the salt and then left until completely dry. Oil/grease stains are removed with a suitable solvent or detergent; otherwise the paint will not adhere.
Menhol/kapı başında bir standby kişi sür: A standby person is always present at the manhole/door, keeps in constant communication with the personnel inside and monitors the situation. If there is a problem, the standby person does not rush in, but raises the alarm and calls in the rescue team/SCBA standing by. The rescue line (lifeline) and harness allow the personnel inside to be pulled out.
Menzil yüksekliğe bağlıdır; SART ne kada: The range depends on height; the higher the SART is held (e.g. raised on a pole in the liferaft), the greater the range. It is typically detected at about 8 miles from a ship and much farther from an aircraft. Close to the water surface the range of the SART falls.
Menü döngüsü, sipariş hesabının temelidi: The menu cycle is the basis of the order calculation: the shopping list is drawn up by adding up the ingredients needed for the recipes in the planned menu. In this way, neither too much (waste/spoilage) nor too little (running out) is ordered. Existing stock is deducted; only the shortfall is ordered.
Menü planlaması, seferin süresi, rota üz: Menu planning is based on the length of the voyage, the provisioning ports on the route and the crew composition. The cook usually prepares a 7-, 10- or 14-day "menu rotation" (cyclic menu); this rotation prevents menu fatigue while making stock planning and order quantities predictable. On long ocean passages (e.g. a transpacific crossing of 14-21 days), the menu is staged according to the order in which fresh produce runs out: the first days are planned mainly around fresh vegetables/fruit and fresh meat, and the last days mainly around frozen and canned food.
Menü rotasyonu (örn. 7/10/14 günlük döng: A menu rotation (e.g. a 7/10/14-day cycle) prevents menu fatigue while making budget and stock planning predictable. By keeping the cycle long enough and enriching it with theme days/special-occasion menus (see the morale task), the cook balances both variety and cost control. The rotation also makes it easier to balance the macro/micronutrient distribution over the week.
Merdiven korkulukları (handrail) sık dok: Stair handrails are high-touch surfaces and are disinfected. When emergency exit signs, fire equipment lockers and lighting are cleaned, care is taken that they are never blocked by materials/equipment.
Merkez Mandeville, Louisiana (ABD); ayrı: The headquarters are in Mandeville, Louisiana (USA), with further offices in Egersund (Norway) and Singapore. This three-region structure is taken into account in planning, as it determines how close service and spare-parts support are to the area of operation.
Merkezi soğutma sistemi (central cooling: On ships with a central cooling system, sea water cooling and fresh water cooling (high/low-temperature circuits) are monitored separately. The temperature difference between the plate cooler inlet and outlet shows the heat transfer efficiency; if the difference is falling, the cooler is clogging or fouling.
Merkezi soğutmada deniz suyu (SW) yalnız: In central cooling, seawater (SW) goes only to the central cooler and returns overboard from there. The machinery is cooled by fresh water (FW) circuits with low salinity and inhibitor. The high-temperature (HT) circuit cools the main engine jackets; the low-temperature (LT) circuit cools the L.O. cooler, the charge air cooler and the auxiliaries. A thermostatic three-way valve keeps the temperature constant.
Mesafe ve durum köprüüstüne sürekli rapo: Distance and status are reported to the bridge continuously: "Two shackles to go", "All gone forward" (all lines forward have been let go), "Made fast forward" (the forward station is made fast). Without this feedback the bridge carries out the maneuver blind; clear and timely reporting by the AB is the eyes of the maneuver.
Mesajlar genelde standart bir yapı izler: Messages usually follow a standard structure: warning type, area affected, position/movement of the system, expected wind and sea state. The Second Officer transfers these messages to the passage plan and passes the critical ones to the Master and the officers of the watch.
Mess'teki sürekli açık çay/kahve istasyo: The tea/coffee station in the mess is always open and accessible to the crew 24/7. The steward keeps this station clean, stocked and working; the machines are cleaned regularly, and milk, sugar and other consumables are never allowed to run out. These small details make a big difference to morale.
Mess, dinlenme ve sosyalleşme alanıdır;: The mess is a place to relax and socialize; the steward ensures that it stays clean, tidy and welcoming. Dirty plates piling up around the tables are cleared promptly, and spills are wiped up immediately. Temperature, ventilation and lighting are kept comfortable.
Messhall (yemek salonu) ve dayroom (dinl: The messhall and the dayroom are the most heavily used common areas and need cleaning several times a day. Tables are disinfected before meals; after meals, leftovers are cleared, tables are wiped again and the floor is mopped. Shared touch points in these areas, such as the TV, game tables and armchairs, are part of infection control.
Metallerde üç temel kristal yapı gözleml: Three basic crystal structures are seen in metals: body-centred cubic (BCC), face-centred cubic (FCC) and hexagonal close-packed (HCP).
Mevcut gemilerde MT, DP, köprüüstü enteg: On existing ships MT retrofits DP, integrated bridge and thruster control systems. A midlife upgrade typically involves replacing the control computers, operator stations, network switches and software, while the existing IO cabinets and cabling infrastructure are kept.
Mevcut haritalar, sailing directions, ti: The charts, sailing directions, tide and current data, weather and port information are collected; alternative routes and risky passages (TSS, narrow channels) are identified.
Mevcut ticari gemilerin çoğunda R-404A (: Most existing merchant ships use R-404A (medium/low temperature), R-134a (air conditioning) and R-407C. On newbuildings the use of R-744 (CO₂) and R-717 (ammonia) is increasing.
Mevzuat sürekli güncellenir (IMO MSC ve: The regulations are updated continuously (the IMO MSC and MEPC each meet twice a year). The Master regularly follows amendments to SOLAS, MARPOL and STCW, IMO circulars, P&I bulletins and MAIB and TSB reports. Company bulletins, vetting reports (RightShip, OCIMF SIRE) and class technical bulletins are the Master's daily reading list.
Michell tipi kaymalı yatak en yaygın tip: The Michell-type plain bearing is the most common type. Tilting pads form a hydrodynamic oil film between themselves and the shaft surface.
Mikro besinler (vitaminler ve mineraller: Micronutrients (vitamins and minerals) are invisible but critical: vitamin C is needed for immunity and tissues, the mineral Fe to prevent anemia, calcium/vitamin D for bones, and B-group vitamins for energy metabolism. The cook ensures this balance by keeping fresh fruit/vegetables, red meat, pulses, dairy products and whole grains on the menu. Variety is the natural guarantee of adequate micronutrient intake.
Mikrodalga, fırın, mikser, et kıyma maki: Equipment such as the microwave, oven, mixer and meat mincer is cleaned after use; equipment that can be dismantled is taken apart and washed. Care is taken with hot surfaces, and electrical equipment is unplugged before cleaning.
Minimum kabul değeri: 1 MΩ (genel kural): Minimum acceptable value: 1 MΩ (general rule). A temperature correction is applied for motors and generators.
Minimum seviyenin altına düşen veya yakl: Items that fall below or approach the minimum level are reported in good time to the Second Engineer (and, when necessary, to the Chief Engineer). The report includes the part name, the IMPA/maker part number, the current ROB, the quantity required and the urgency. Late reporting means that a critical spare cannot be supplied within the port window.
Mixed mooring (aynı yönde hem tel hem se: Mixed mooring (using both wire and synthetic lines in the same direction) is not recommended by MEG4, because lines of different elasticity do not share the load equally and the stiffer one parts first. The Bosun prevents this error; lines of similar elasticity are used in the same service.
Model çevresel kuvvetleri öğrenene kadar: The ship is held steady long enough for the model to learn the environmental forces, and the actual performance is monitored. Work does not start until the capability plot, the consequence analysis and the footprint show the expected behaviour.
Modem, uydu link'ini kurar ve IP trafiği: The modem establishes the satellite link and manages IP traffic; its configuration (satellite/transponder settings, IP plan, QoS) is provided by the service provider. The ETO backs up the modem configuration, applies firmware updates in a controlled manner and uses the modem logs for fault diagnosis. A wrong configuration leads to loss of the link.
Modern ALCAP (Alfa Laval) ve EPC-50/60 (: The modern ALCAP (Alfa Laval) and EPC-50/60 (Mitsubishi) systems do not need a gravity disc; they work with automatic interface detection.
Modern Alpha Lubricator / SIP (Swirl Inj: Modern Alpha Lubricator / SIP (Swirl Injection Principle) systems adjust the feed rate automatically according to engine load and sulfur. Feed rate is usually 0.6-1.4 g/kWh; the minimum guaranteed feed rate is maintained in accordance with the engine maker's specification. Scrape-down (drain) oil analysis is the basis for feed rate optimization.
Modern Alpha lubricator feed rate yöneti: Modern Alpha lubricator feed rate management adjusts the dosage automatically according to engine load and fuel sulfur content. Drain oil analysis (Fe, Sn, Pb, Cu metal trends, BN reserve) is carried out monthly; a rising trend indicates liner/ring/piston wear.
Modern FWG'ler plakalı (plate) ısı eşanj: Modern FWGs use plate heat exchangers: one plate pack heats and evaporates the seawater with jacket water (the evaporator), the other condenses the vapour with seawater (the condenser). They are compact, efficient and easy to clean.
Modern IAS sistemleri Ethernet tabanlı y: Modern IAS systems use an Ethernet-based redundant ring or star topology. At field level, sensors and actuators communicate via Modbus, Profibus or CANbus, while at control level data is shared between controllers via Ethernet/IP.
Modern LNG gemilerinde DFDE (Dual Fuel D: On modern LNG carriers, DFDE (Dual Fuel Diesel Electric) or ME-GI/X-DF engines are replacing the steam turbine system.
Modern PLC ve kontrolörler oto-tuning fo: Modern PLCs and controllers have an auto-tuning function. The system determines the process dynamics automatically with a relay feedback test and calculates the PID parameters. However, auto-tuning does not always give the optimum result; manual fine-tuning is needed for critical loops.
Modern PMS sistemlerinde her work order,: In modern PMS systems, every work order automatically deducts (issues) the spare parts used from stock. This integration makes actual consumption traceable and reduces the margin for manual error. When a work order is closed, the Chief Engineer checks that parts consumption has been entered correctly; otherwise inventory reliability suffers.
Modern SMS, \"her kritik ve rutin dışı o: A modern SMS is based on the principle of a written risk assessment before every critical and non-routine operation. The common methodology is a 5×5 risk matrix: likelihood (1–5) times severity (1–5) equals the risk score. High-scoring jobs (generally above 12) are either cancelled or brought down to an acceptable level with additional barriers (control measures). The Master checks that the risk assessment team is made up of the right people (including those who will actually do the job) and that the ALARP principle (as low as reasonably practicable) is observed.
Modern ana makinelerde safety system, pa: On modern main engines, the safety system monitors the parameters and, when a threshold is exceeded, first gives an alarm and, if the condition continues, applies a slowdown or shutdown. Some hazards (e.g. low LO pressure, overspeed) are linked directly to a trip, because any delay would wreck the engine. In certain situations, the bridge may temporarily override a shutdown for the safety of maneuvering (e.g. in confined waters); however, this is a conscious acceptance of risk and is recorded.
Modern bir gemi mürettebatı genellikle ç: A modern ship's crew is usually multinational and multicultural. The Master ensures respect for differences of language, culture, religion and tradition, the prohibition of discrimination (MLC) and equal treatment. In an isolated environment, morale is maintained through the quality of the food, rest, internet and communication facilities, a fair distribution of work and a respectful atmosphere. Low morale is as dangerous an accident factor as fatigue.
Modern bir tanker veya bulk carrier'in a: The main engine of a modern tanker or bulk carrier is typically a 2-stroke crosshead engine from the MAN B&W ME-C, WinGD X or Wärtsilä RT-flex series. These engines burn HFO (Heavy Fuel Oil), MGO (Marine Gas Oil) or VLSFO (Very Low Sulfur Fuel Oil); LNG dual-fuel and methanol options have become increasingly common since 2020.
Modern dizel makinelerde yataklardaki mi: In modern diesel engines, the minimum oil film thickness in the bearings is in the order of microns; even a 10-20 micron particle can break through the oil film and cause metal-to-metal contact. For this reason, the filter mesh size (e.g. 25-40 microns for ME LO, finer for the injection line) is selected in strict accordance with the manufacturer's specification.
Modern elektronik overload röleleri ek k: Modern electronic overload relays provide additional protection: phase loss (single phasing), phase imbalance, earth leakage and motor winding temperature monitoring through a thermistor (PTC) input. The ETO verifies that these functions are active and that the trip class (usually Class 10 or 20) suits the motor characteristics.
Modern gemi ekipleri çok-uluslu ve çok-d: Modern ship crews are multinational and multilingual. The Chief Engineer makes sure that the common working language (usually English) is used clearly in safety-critical communication. Toolbox talks, permit-to-work briefings and drills are conducted in a way that everyone understands.
Modern gemi galley'lerinde fritöz ve piş: In modern ship galleys, a fixed wet chemical extinguishing system is installed over the fryer and the cooking line. The system directs nozzles at the oil surface, the cooking appliances and the hood/duct entrance. When activated, the wet chemical agent forms a vapor-tight soapy blanket on the oil through saponification; this both cuts off oxygen and cools the surface, preventing re-ignition.
Modern gemiler merkezi soğutma sistemi k: Modern ships use a central cooling system: sea water (low temp sea water) cools the fresh water circuit through a central cooler, and the fresh water (LT/HT fresh water) in turn cools the engine and auxiliary equipment. This keeps the corrosive effect of seawater away from the equipment. The cadet learns the difference between the LT and HT circuits.
Modern gemilerde CCTV; makine dairesi, k: On modern ships, CCTV allows the engine room, cargo areas, mooring stations and security areas to be monitored from the bridge. In some systems, CCTV is integrated with fire detection: when a zone goes into alarm, the relevant camera automatically appears on the bridge monitor so that the fire can be confirmed visually. The ETO is responsible for the technical maintenance of the cameras, the recorder (DVR/NVR), the network switches and the monitors.
Modern gemilerde HMPE (High Modulus Poly: On modern ships, HMPE (High Modulus Polyethylene — Dyneema/Spectra) lines and mixed polyester/polyamide lines are common. The steel wire + synthetic tail combination is used particularly on tankers. The Chief Officer verifies that the line's MBL is within 100–105% of the SDMBL and that the tail is stronger than the main line (generally 125–130% of the SDMBL).
Modern gemilerde Kongsberg, Praxis veya: On modern ships, alarm/monitoring systems such as Kongsberg, Praxis or Lyngsø collect all parameters every second. The Second Engineer reviews the trend screens of this data daily, focusing on the "rate of change" rather than the absolute value. For example, a rise of 20-30°C in the exhaust temperature of a single cylinder, even while the absolute value is still within limits, is a warning sign of a fuel valve (fuel injector) fault.
Modern gemilerde LED seyir fenerleri kul: Modern ships use LED navigation lights. LED lights have a life of 50,000+ hours and low power consumption.
Modern gemilerde LSA kayıtları hem fizik: On modern ships, LSA records are kept both in a physical logbook and in the electronic PMS (Planned Maintenance System). Each inspection is opened as a job and closed when done; expiry dates are tracked in a separate "expiry tracker" table. The Safety Officer's golden rule: work that has not been done is not recorded, and work that has not been recorded is considered not done.
Modern gemilerde PMS, AMOS, TM Master ve: On modern ships, the PMS is run with AMOS, TM Master or similar software, and the data are synchronized with the shore office. The Third/Fourth Engineer learns to enter work orders against the correct equipment, to update running hours and to verify that the records are complete before synchronization.
Modern gemilerde döner hidrolik jib/knuc: On modern ships, slewing hydraulic jib or knuckle-boom cranes give fast cargo handling with a single operator. The classic derrick system carries the load between fixed points with two derricks in a union purchase arrangement; it is cheap, but slow and limited in its movements.
Modern gemilerde high-pressure water mis: On modern ships, a high-pressure water mist system (HI-FOG etc.) is an alternative or supplement to total flooding; very fine water droplets provide both cooling and oxygen dilution, and it is safer than CO2 (personnel do not need to leave the space). Local application water spray covers high-risk points such as the top of the main engine, the purifiers and the boiler.
Modern gemilerde köprüüstü kumandası pot: On modern ships the bridge control produces a potentiometer or synchro signal. This signal is sent to the steering gear by electric cable and controls the electro-hydraulic servo valve.
Modern gemilerde mooring rope olarak HMP: On modern ships, HMPE (Dyneema), polyester, polyamide (nylon) and mixed lines are used as mooring line. Each line has a Line Design Break Force (LDBF) and a certificate; under OCIMF MEG4, lines are entered in the inventory with their type, diameter, length, date of manufacture and MBL. The Bosun tracks the lines in use and the spare lines in the store separately.
Modern gemilerde mürettebat çoğunlukla f: On modern ships the crew is usually made up of different nationalities (e.g. a mix of Filipino, Indian, Turkish, Ukrainian and Chinese). The cook considers the crew's religious requirements (halal, vegetarian, beef/pork restrictions) and eating habits. In practice, offering an alternative protein or a neutral option (e.g. chicken/fish) alongside the main dish at each meal is the standard way of resolving conflicting preferences within a single menu.
Modern gemilerde mürettebat çoğunlukla ç: On modern ships the crew is mostly multinational and multicultural (Filipino, Indian, Ukrainian, Chinese, Indonesian and so on). The Master's welfare management covers clear communication in the common working language (usually English), respect for religious and cultural practices (menu, prayer times, holidays), equal treatment and preventing cliques and exclusion. Cultural sensitivity is a leadership skill that reduces tension on board and strengthens the safety culture.
Modern gemilerde otomasyon, drive ve hab: On modern ships, automation, drive and communication systems are based on PCBs (printed circuit boards) and modules. The ETO stocks at least one spare of each critical board (controller CPU, I/O boards, drive control board, AVR board). Replacing a board usually requires parameters/software to be loaded; the ETO backs up these configurations.
Modern gemilerde su sisi (water mist) ve: On modern ships, water mist and local application foam systems tackle a fire around the ME/AE/incinerator without the engine room having to be evacuated. Water mist works through both cooling and oxygen dilution and is less hazardous than CO₂. The Oiler knows the manual release points of these systems and the areas they cover.
Modern gemilerde tamamen kapalı (totally: Totally enclosed lifeboats are standard on modern ships; they are watertight, self-righting and motorized. Free-fall lifeboats are released into the sea from a ramp at the stern; they allow rapid abandonment and are common on bulk carriers/tankers. Tankers carrying cargoes with a flashpoint not exceeding 60 °C must carry fire-protected lifeboats.
Modern gemilerde tüm tank seviyeleri mer: On modern ships all tank levels are transmitted to the central alarm and monitoring system (AMS). Level transmitters communicate through 4–20 mA or digital signals (HART, Modbus).
Modern gemilerde yüksek mukavemetli HMPE: On modern ships, high-strength HMPE (Dyneema) and polyester blend ropes are common. After every voyage, the rope is checked visually for chafe, glazing (heat damage), kinks, broken yarns and UV fading. Under OCIMF MEG4, ropes are kept on record with regard to LDBF (Line Design Break Force), MBL and the use of "tails".
Modern gemilerde ırgat genellikle baş ka: On modern ships the windlass is usually on the forecastle, above the forepeak, with a separate gypsy (wildcat) for each anchor. In some designs the windlass and the forward mooring winches share a common drive unit (windlass-mooring winch combination).
Modern gemilerin çoğu 5 yıllık özel sörv: Most modern ships are managed under the CMS program within the 5-year special survey cycle. Each item of equipment is surveyed once every 5 years; PMS records are used as evidence. The Chief Engineer keeps crank deflection measurements, exhaust valve overhaul records, T/C overhaul records and ME safety device test records ready for the class surveyor.
Modern gemilerin çoğu CMS programıyla yö: Most modern ships are managed under a CMS program: machinery items are surveyed in turn under a program spread over five years, so that each item is surveyed once every 5 years. This removes the burden of stopping all the machinery at once.
Modern gemilerin çoğu UMS (E0/AUT notati: Most modern ships are classed for UMS (E0/AUT notation); the engine room runs without a watch at night and alarms are relayed to the ECR and the bridge. The Duty Engineer is responsible through the call system (dead-man alarm, engineer's call). On ships with traditional watchkeeping, a 4-hour watch system (0000-0400, 0400-0800 etc.) is used.
Modern gemilerin çoğu UMS (Unattended Ma: Most modern ships are UMS (Unattended Machinery Space) certified; the engine room may be left unmanned at night and alarms are routed to the bridge and to the duty engineer's cabin. The cadet learns how the engine room is monitored in both attended (manned) and unattended periods.
Modern gemilerin çoğu UMS (Unmanned Mach: Most modern ships are UMS (Unmanned Machinery Space) certified; at night the engine room is left unmanned and the alarms are routed to the bridge and to the cabin of the duty engineer. However, during maneuvering, port operations, passages through narrow waterways and critical maintenance, the engine room is "manned" and the oiler is present on site at all times.
Modern gemilerin çoğu klas tarafından 5: Most modern ships are managed by class in a 5-year Continuous Survey of Machinery (CMS) cycle. In this cycle each machinery item is surveyed at least once within 5 years; about one fifth of the surveys are completed each year. On ships with an approved PMS (Approved Planned Maintenance Scheme), class accepts the Chief Engineer's PMS records (chief engineer survey) instead of opening up and surveying certain equipment.
Modern iki zamanlı motorlar uniflow (tek: Modern two-stroke engines use uniflow scavenging. Fresh air enters through the ports at the bottom of the cylinder and the exhaust gas leaves through the exhaust valve at the top. This arrangement gives the most effective scavenging.
Modern kuru yük gemilerinde folding (kat: Folding, side-rolling and pontoon (lift-off) type hatch covers are common on modern dry cargo ships. Each type has its own hydraulic/mechanical controls and safety pin system. Before a cover is opened, the AB confirms that the cleats, wedges and safety locks have all been removed; otherwise the hydraulics are overstressed and damage or collision results.
Modern köprüüstü; ECDIS, track control (: The modern bridge is highly automated, with ECDIS, track control (autopilot), ARPA and an integrated bridge system. This creates the risk of automation complacency: assuming the system is working correctly, the team relaxes its monitoring. In this complacency, GPS spoofing/jamming, an ENC error or a sensor failure progresses unnoticed. The Second Officer stresses that automation is a tool and that responsibility always remains with people.
Modern motorlarda elektronik performans: On modern engines, the electronic performance monitoring system (PMI) provides automatic analysis.
Modern mürettebat çok uluslu ve farklı b: Today's crews are multinational, with different dietary needs: religious requirements (halal, vegetarian, pork-free/alcohol-free), allergens (nuts, gluten, seafood) and medical diets (diabetes, low salt) are taken into account during service. Together with the cook, the steward keeps track of these special needs and clearly labels/separates dishes that contain allergens.
Modern oil monitorlar tamper-proof (kayı: Modern oil monitors are designed to be tamper-proof (logged and sealed); they record when, at what ppm and how much was discharged overboard. This log is cross-checked with the ORB. In special areas (Mediterranean, Baltic, Black Sea etc.), discharge at ≤15 ppm is permitted only while the ship is en route, through an approved OWS with a 15 ppm alarm and automatic stopping; discharging overboard in the Antarctic area and inside ports is prohibited.
Modern panellerde her dedektörün hassasi: On modern panels, the sensitivity of each detector and, if necessary, an alarm delay (e.g. day/night mode) can be configured. The cause-and-effect matrix defines which outputs are triggered when a detector goes into alarm (ventilation shutdown, fire damper, pre-warning of fixed gas release). The ETO ensures that this matrix remains consistent with the manufacturer's class-approved configuration.
Modern programlar, online portal üzerind: Modern programs provide results, trend charts and expert comments through an online portal. The Chief Engineer combines these comments with his or her own observations on site to make the final decision and does not trust the report blindly.
Modern separatörler purifier/clarifier m: Modern separators perform automatic water monitoring and self-cleaning (sludge discharge) in purifier/clarifier mode. Series operation (two units) increases separation security for heavy fuels (high density/water content).
Modern separatörler self-cleaning (otoma: Modern separators work with self-cleaning (automatic bowl discharge) and water content monitoring (water transducer); without a gravity disc, the water discharge is controlled by the sensor. This reduces the need for manual adjustment over a wide density range.
Modern seyir planlaması IMO A.893(21) il: Modern passage planning is defined by IMO A.893(21) in four stages: Appraisal, Planning, Execution and Monitoring. In the appraisal stage all relevant information is gathered; in the planning stage the detailed route is laid down; execution is the ship carrying out the plan, and monitoring is the continuous checking of adherence to the plan. The cadet supports the Second Officer especially in the first two stages (appraisal and planning) by collecting data and making preliminary plots.
Modern slavery ve insan kaçakçılığı risk: The risk of modern slavery and human trafficking is real in shipping; a breach of the free recruitment principle is the first sign of it. In a suspicious case the Master coordinates with the DPA and the CSO; keeping a seafarer's passport against his or her will (passport retention) is a violation of the MLC and of human rights.
Modern stern tube seal'leri genelde lip-: Modern stern tube seals are usually of the lip-seal type; the aft seal (sea side) uses more than one lip to prevent water ingress and oil leakage. As the lips wear, sealing deteriorates; most systems allow an adjustment that changes the contact point of the lip on the liner.
Modern turboşarjerlerin toplam verimi %6: The overall efficiency of modern turbochargers is between 65% and 72%. Turbine efficiency × compressor efficiency × mechanical efficiency = overall efficiency.
Modern uydulardan elde edilen besttrack: Best-track data from modern satellites makes the Master's job easier, but uncertainty is high in forecasts beyond 72 hours. With the "1-2-3 rule", the Master adds a safety margin of 100/200/300 NM to the forecast radius at 24/48/72 hours.
Modern uygulamalarda thyristor doğrultuc: In modern applications precise DC motor control is provided by thyristor rectifiers or chopper circuits.
Modern vinçlerde yük momenti sınırlayıcı: Modern cranes have a load moment limiter (overload/moment limiter), speed limiting, hose burst valves and an emergency stop. When the load exceeds the SWL, the system stops automatically.
Monitoring modunda active route/leg, cro: In monitoring mode, the active route and leg, cross-track distance, next waypoint and turn, the selected position, heading and speed sensors, the chart scale and the alarms are monitored at the same time. If there is a track-control/autopilot connection, mode awareness and readiness for manual takeover are particularly maintained.
Monitoring, gerçek pozisyonun planlanan: Monitoring is comparing the actual position with the planned route and noticing deviations early. In the ECDIS the route monitoring, XTD, anti-grounding and depth alarms must be set correctly. A situation briefing is always given at watch changes, and standard phrases such as "I have the conn" and "You have the conn" are used.
Monkey's fist içine asla metal/ağır cisi: Metal or heavy objects are never put inside the monkey's fist; this can seriously injure the person ashore. MEG4 and COSWP require the weight of a heaving line to be soft and of limited mass. Warning the people on the quay when throwing ("heads up — line coming over") is good practice.
Montaj sonrası coupling alignment (laser: After assembly, coupling alignment is carried out (with a laser or dial gauge); misalignment leads to vibration, bearing wear and seal failure. The cadet learns that alignment is a measured value, not something that "looks aligned".
Montaj sonrası valf, hidrostatik veya pn: After assembly, the valve is tested for tightness by a hydrostatic or pneumatic test. Safety/relief valves are adjusted to the set pressure and sealed. All bolts are tightened to the manufacturer's torque values in a crosswise sequence.
Mooring güvenliği büyük ölçüde ekipman d: Mooring safety depends to a large extent on the condition of the equipment. The AB regularly checks lines for wear, cuts, glazing (shine caused by heat) and internal fiber damage, and wires for broken wires, birdcaging, rust and loosening. Damaged lines/wires are reported and taken out of service; the "it will hold a bit longer" mindset produces snap-back accidents.
Mooring halatları (HMPE, polyester, mixe: Mooring lines (HMPE, polyester, mixed) and wires are inspected regularly for external wear, internal abrasion, UV degradation, splice integrity and elongation. Every line must have retirement criteria under a "line management plan". OCIMF MEG4 is the industry standard for managing line service life and LDBF (Line Design Break Force).
Mooring halatı doğrudan rıhtıma uzanamay: Because the mooring line is too heavy to reach the berth directly, a light heaving line is thrown first; the weight at its end (monkey's fist) carries it ashore, and the mooring gang ashore hauls in this line to bring the eye of the main line onto the berth. The AB coils the heaving line neatly, takes half of it in the throwing hand, aims according to the target and the wind, and throws.
Mooring head/breast/spring sırasıyla ver: The mooring lines are sent out in the order head, breast and spring lines. Line tension and snap-back zones are managed in accordance with MEG4; no one stands in a snap-back zone.
Mooring istasyonunda zorunlu PPE: baret,: Mandatory PPE at the mooring station: safety helmet, steel-toe safety shoes, mooring gloves (a type that gives grip but will not get caught in a roller), coveralls and, for night operations, a reflective vest. The choice of gloves is important; loose or torn gloves increase the risk of being caught by the drum.
Mooring vinçleri: Çalıştırma ve fren tes: Mooring winches: running and brake test.
Mooring watch sırasında gangway güvenliğ: During the mooring watch, gangway safety, unauthorized access and the condition of the quay and surroundings are also watched. The AB reports any abnormal situation (chafed line, fire, leak, unauthorized person) to the bridge.
Mooring winch controls permit heaving, p: Mooring winch controls permit heaving, paying out and braking. Operate only on an understood command identifying the line and action. Automatic-tension operation can move a line unexpectedly and alter load sharing; use it only under the approved mooring arrangement and operating instructions.
Mooring winch fren tutma kapasitesi, bra: The holding capacity of the mooring winch brake is verified by a brake holding test; the target is generally about 60% of the wire/line MBL (depending on the design). If brake rendering is not set correctly, either the line parts or the brake fails to hold; both are dangerous. Test results are recorded.
Mooring winch'ler brake holding capacity: Mooring winches are set according to their brake holding capacity; MEG4 recommends keeping the brake rendering point at 60% of the SDMBL (for steel) or 80% (for synthetic). A brake test (brake holding capacity test) must be carried out regularly and recorded. A brake set too tight leads to the line parting; a slack brake lets the ship move off the berth.
Mooring ölümlerinin büyük kısmı, AB'nin: Most mooring deaths result from an AB standing in the recoil zone of a line under tension. In some cases, the person started in the right area, but the direction of recoil changed because the line was bent around a fairlead. Lesson: do not rely on a single "safe line"; treat the whole deck as dangerous while lines are under tension and keep the escape route clear.
Motor Control Center (MCC), bir geminin: The Motor Control Center (MCC) is the modular switchboard that houses all of a ship's motor starters. Each starter module contains a main switch/fuse, contactor(s), a thermal overload relay, a control transformer and indicators/push buttons. The ETO periodically checks the thermal condition of the MCC, the condition of the contactors and the integrity of the control circuits.
Motor alt yapısını oluşturur. Ana yatakl: It forms the base structure of the engine. The main bearings are in the bedplate. It is of welded steel or cast construction.
Motor hızı çıkış frekansına doğrudan bağ: The motor speed depends directly on the output frequency (n = 120f/P). Keeping the V/f ratio constant gives constant torque over the whole speed range.
Motor ilk olarak yıldız bağlantıyla çalı: The motor is first started in star connection; the voltage applied to the windings falls by a factor of 1/√3 and the current to 1/3. When the motor has accelerated, it is switched to delta. A brief current peak may occur at the changeover.
Motor kontrol ve güç elektroniği bakımı,: Maintenance of motor control and power electronics calls for an unseen but continuous discipline: a correctly set overload relay saves a motor from burning out, while regular megger and vibration trending turn unplanned failures into planned maintenance. The ETO's mastery in this area is measured by keeping the ship's hundreds of items of rotating equipment running quietly and by making a tangible contribution to energy efficiency.
Motor sargı yalıtımı, nem, sıcaklık ve y: Motor winding insulation deteriorates with moisture, temperature and aging. The ETO isolates the motor and measures the winding-to-earth insulation resistance (IR) with a 500 V megger (LV motor). Under IEEE 43, the minimum acceptable IR depends on the winding voltage; in practice, 1 MΩ + 1 MΩ per kV of rated voltage is a practical lower limit, but the trend is more important.
Motor yükü düştüğünde SFOC (özgül yakıt: When the engine load falls, the SFOC (specific fuel oil consumption) rises, but the total consumption still decreases.
Motor çalışma noktası surge line'dan yet: The engine's operating line must be at a sufficient distance from the surge line (surge margin).
Motorlu gemilerde ana makine egzoz gazın: On motor ships the waste heat of the main engine exhaust gas is used to produce steam in a fire-tube or water-tube economiser. At sea it greatly reduces the fuel consumption of the auxiliary boiler.
Motorun ileri/geri kavramaları (eğer güv: The ahead/astern engagement of the engine is tested separately (if it is safe, when the boat has been lowered into the water, not in the davit). The running time, observations and battery condition are entered in the logbook.
Move/heading change talepleri küçük artı: Move and heading change requests are carried out in small steps, with confirmation from ROV control at each step. On loss of telemetry, excessive umbilical tension or DP degradation, the recovery or abandon criteria are applied.
Muayene, kapsamlı muayene ve proof-load: The scope of inspections, thorough examinations and proof load tests is not taken from a fixed table found on the internet; it is verified from the flag state's requirements, SOLAS II-1/3-13, MSC.1/Circ.1663, the applicability of ILO Convention 152 and the ship's Register of Lifting Appliances/Cargo Gear Book.
Multi-Function Workstation'da DP dışında: On a Multi-Function Workstation, it must be ensured that DP monitoring continues without interruption while applications other than DP are open. The screen brightness is set through central dimming to a level that does not spoil night vision; the alarm volume is not turned down.
Multi-grade (çoklu parsel) yüklerde her: With multi-grade cargoes, each parcel must be carried in its own cargo system (pumps, lines, set of valves) and segregated so that commingling is prevented. The use of the slop tanks and intermediate tanks affects the integrity of the plan.
Muros (2016): ECDIS'te yanlış safety con: Muros (2016): with an incorrect safety contour on ECDIS and an inadequate route check, the ship ran aground on a shoal. Lesson: the ECDIS settings must be verified for the ship, and the route check output must be reviewed.
Muster List, SOLAS III/8 gereği gemide g: Under SOLAS III/8, the muster list is posted in conspicuous places on board (bridge, engine room, corridors, cabins) and shows who does what for each type of emergency (general emergency, fire, abandon ship, man overboard, pollution). From the card on their cabin door and at the muster station, the AB learns their duty, team and muster station.
Muster list (genel) ile bireysel station: The muster list (general) and the individual station card (a personal card posted on the cabin door) complement each other. The station card reminds each crew member of their muster station, their abandon ship duty, the equipment they are to carry and which survival craft they are to board. The Safety Officer checks that every cabin has an up-to-date station card.
Muster list (station bill), her acil dur: The muster list (station bill) sets out where each person goes and what they do in each type of emergency (fire, flooding, abandon ship, man overboard). The duties of the Oiler/Fitter are generally engine-room-focused, such as fire party membership, boundary cooling, operating the emergency generator/pump or closing shut-off valves.
Muster list (toplanma cetveli), her müre: The muster list shows where each crew member is to go and which duty they will take on in an emergency. Under SOLAS III/8 it must be posted in conspicuous places on the bridge, in the engine control room and in the crew accommodation. The general alarm signal, the abandon ship signal, each person's duty and their substitute are shown on the muster list.
Muster list ve emergency instruction'lar: The muster list and emergency instructions must be in a working language understood by the crew; with multinational crews they are supported by IMO standard symbols (Res. A.760(18) / A.1116(30)). Every cabin must have lifejacket donning instructions and directions to the muster station.
Muster list'in başarısı, hiçbir acil dur: The success of the muster list stays invisible as long as no emergency occurs. In a real abandonment, fire or MOB, however, the lives of the crew depend on exactly how this list works on deck: on everyone knowing their station and duty by reflex. The paper on the notice board is only the start; being able to say "everyone knows their station, the equipment is being carried, the head count is complete" means the job is done.
Muster list, her mürettebata acil durum: The muster list shows each crew member's emergency duty, muster station and the meaning of the signals. When personnel change, the Chief Officer updates the muster list and posts it in conspicuous places. Everyone who joins receives safety familiarization within 24 hours: donning a lifejacket, finding the muster station, recognizing the alarms and using LSA are demonstrated.
Muster list, kaptanın yokluğunda kimin y: The muster list also defines who takes charge in the Master's absence and the persons responsible for using the LSA and radio equipment. The Safety Officer continuously checks that the list matches the persons actually on board, one for one; at a crew change the list must be updated immediately, otherwise in an emergency some people end up with "no duty" and others with "two duties".
Muster station (toplanma yeri), acil dur: The muster station is the designated place where the crew assemble in an emergency. The muster list shows each person's duty in an emergency (fire party, liferaft, first aid, etc.). The cadet must know their own muster duty and station by heart; this is learned during familiarization and reinforced through drills.
Muster station'da isim sayımı (head coun: The head count (roll call) at the muster station is a critical stage; if anyone is missing, a search team is sent. The AB reports their own presence and, if assigned to communications, maintains the flow of information between the bridge and the muster station by radio/PA. A wrong count leads to someone left inside being overlooked.
Mutfak ekipmanlarının bakımı, görünmeyen: Galley equipment maintenance is an unseen but decisive discipline: regular cleaning and preventive maintenance ensure both that meals are served without interruption and that burns, cuts and electrical accidents are prevented. As the person who knows the limits of his or her authority, catches faults early, reports them correctly and carries out user maintenance with discipline, the cook is the guarantee that the galley operates continuously and safely.
Mutfak gibi normalde duman/buhar olan ye: Heat detectors are used where there is normally smoke or steam, such as the galley; smoke detectors in cabins and corridors; and a combination of flame, smoke and heat detectors in the engine room. The wrong type causes either false alarms or late detection.
Mutfak ve depo düzeni, görünürde basit a: Galley and store organization is a discipline that looks simple but has big consequences: a well-organized galley is faster, safer and more hygienic; it is the first line of defense against pests, fire and food spoilage. The cook's habit of "constant order" is the quiet guarantee of both crew health and inspection compliance.
Mutfak yangın emniyeti, aşçının en hayat: Galley fire safety is one of the cook's most vital responsibilities, because the galley is the space with the highest fire risk on board. Prevention (cleaning, supervision, switching off) is the first line of defense; knowing the right extinguisher and the fire blanket is the second; automatic suppression, damper control and an organized response are the third. Basic reflexes, such as never tackling an oil fire with water, make the difference between a minor incident and a disaster in a galley fire.
Mühendis sadece göstergelere bakmaz; beş: The engineer does not just look at the gauges but uses all five senses. Abnormal noise (knocking, cavitation, bearing hum), vibration, oil/water/fuel leaks, smells (burnt insulation, hot bearing), heat (hot spots) and traces of leakage are detected. Suspect points are measured with a thermometer/IR gun.
Mühürlü MARPOL numunesi alınır ve saklan: A sealed MARPOL sample is taken and retained; the BDN is checked and entered in the appropriate record book (ORB). The sulphur content must suit the area where the fuel will be used.

Mükemmel termodinamik özelliklere sahipt: It has excellent thermodynamic properties and a high COP. It is used in large industrial and ship refrigeration plants.
Mümkün olduğunda slop'taki yağ fazı, bir: Where possible, the oil phase of the slops is recovered by loading the next cargo on top of it (load-on-top); this gives both environmental and commercial advantages.
Mümkünse rota değişimi (alter course) te: If possible, an alteration of course is preferred, because it is more readily apparent on radar and visually than a change of speed; however, if there is enough sea room, a change of speed can also be used. After the maneuver, it is monitored that the ship passes at a safe distance until the danger is completely past, and further action is taken if necessary.
Mürettebat \"knowledge\" testi de yapılı: A crew "knowledge" test is also carried out: the inspector asks a randomly chosen rating about the fire station, releasing a liferaft or enclosed space rescue. This is why the quality of familiarization and drills directly affects the outcome of the inspection.
Mürettebat beslenme kalitesi ve bütçe yö: Managing crew nutrition quality and the budget is the task that demands the highest level of the cook's skill: providing nutrition that is balanced, varied and sustainable in terms of micronutrients within a limited victualling rate. Correct ordering, low waste, choosing economical, good-quality sources, foresight that prevents deficiencies such as scurvy, and a satisfaction/rotation system together protect crew health, morale and budget compliance at the same time. A good cook uses the budget not as a constraint but as a framework that brings discipline to quality.
Mürettebat embarkasyon güvertesinde fili: The crew board the lifeboat at the embarkation deck; when the davit brake is released, the lifeboat descends under control. The brake (centrifugal/band brake) limits the speed of lowering. When the boat is waterborne, the release is opened and the boat moves away from the ship on the painter. The whole procedure must be known thoroughly from drills.
Mürettebat rotasyonu (crew change) sürek: Crew rotation (crew change) carries a constant risk of losing information; the handover of the Master, the chief officer and the chief engineer in particular is critical. A good handover covers a realistic account of open issues, unclosed findings, ongoing maintenance items, charterer and company instructions, the particularities of critical equipment and the dynamics of the team. A written handover note is standard and, where possible, the handover is made face to face (with an overlap).
Mürettebat ruh sağlığı (yalnızlık, izola: Crew mental health (loneliness, isolation, stress) is receiving more and more attention; shared mealtimes strengthen social interaction and a sense of belonging in the mess room. By offering menus that appeal to everyone's taste in a multinational team, the cook creates a dining culture in which no one is left "outside". This is a quiet but real contribution to welfare.
Mürettebat sertifikaları (CoC, GMDSS, me: The Master keeps a tracking matrix for crew certificates (CoC, GMDSS, medical, STCW courses) and ship certificates (SMC, ISSC, class, statutory). Documents about to expire are included in port and class planning. Sailing with an invalid certificate carries the risk both of PSC detention and of insurance cover being prejudiced (P&I cover prejudice).
Müster listesi (muster list — SOLAS III/: The muster list (SOLAS III/8) shows each crew member's duty in an emergency, the muster station, the equipment assigned and the meaning of the alarm signals. The general emergency alarm consists of seven or more short blasts followed by one long blast. The Master continually confirms that the muster list is up to date and that each person knows his or her duty (fire party, rescue party, first aid, liferaft preparation, bridge support).
NAVTEX (518 kHz uluslararası İngilizce,: NAVTEX (518 kHz international in English, 490/4209.5 kHz national) and EGC SafetyNET (Inmarsat) are the main channels for receiving these warnings. The Second Officer filters the warnings received according to whether they are relevant to the voyage and transfers the relevant ones to the plan/chart.
NAVTEX (518 kHz) seyir uyarılarını alır;: NAVTEX (518 kHz) receives navigational warnings; the ETO checks the condition of the receiver and antenna. The EPIRB (406 MHz COSPAS-SARSAT) and the SART (Search and Rescue Transponder) require checks of the test function (battery/GPS self-test), the battery expiry date and the hydrostatic release unit (HRU). The EPIRB is tested annually and undergoes maintenance at an approved shore-based facility at intervals not exceeding 5 years; the battery and the HRU are replaced by their expiry dates.
NAVTEX (518/490/4209.5 kHz), kıyıya yakı: NAVTEX (518/490/4209.5 kHz) broadcasts gale warnings, storm warnings and forecasts for areas near the coast (category B = met warning, E = met forecast). In the open sea, outside NAVTEX coverage, Inmarsat EGC/SafetyNET provides the same METAREA information. The Second Officer verifies that both sources are programmed for the correct area.
NAVTEX (Navigational Telex), GMDSS kapsa: NAVTEX (Navigational Telex) is an automatic system within the GMDSS that broadcasts MSI (Maritime Safety Information) on 518 kHz (international, in English), 490 kHz (national language) and 4209.5 kHz. The cadet learns the B1-B4 character coding of NAVTEX messages: B1 is the station identity, B2 the message type (A=navigational warning, B=meteorological warning, D=SAR, etc.), and B3-B4 the message serial number.
NAVTEX, 518 kHz (uluslararası İngilizce): NAVTEX broadcasts navigational warnings, weather reports and SAR information by NAVAREA/METAREA on 518 kHz (international, in English), 490 kHz (national language) and 4209.5 kHz (tropical). The Second Officer verifies that the correct NAVAREA stations and message categories (A=navigational, B=met warning, D=SAR, etc.) are selected.
NOA ve gerekli liman bildirimleri zamanı: The NOA and other required port reports are made on time; the pre-arrival checklist (equipment tests, ECDIS, steering gear test) is completed. NAVTEX navigational warnings are followed.
NOR uyuşmazlıkları laytime davalarının ç: NOR disputes make up most laytime cases. Situations such as "NOR tendered when the ship was not actually ready", "tender before free pratique was granted" or "tender at the wrong place" invalidate the NOR. The Chief Officer confirms all readiness conditions before tendering NOR; the wording "NOR tendered without prejudice" is used under some C/Ps but does not always give protection.
NOR verilme yeri (berth, anchorage, \"Wh: Where the NOR is to be given (berth, anchorage, "Whether In Berth Or Not — WIBON") and how it is to be given (in writing, e-mail, letter, telegram) are defined in the C/P. The Chief Officer prepares the NOR in exact accordance with the C/P terms, tenders it with a time stamp and keeps proof of delivery.
NOR, geminin yüke/boşaltmaya fiilen ve h: The NOR gives notice that the ship is physically and legally ready to load/discharge. The ship must have arrived at the correct berth/anchorage, completed the necessary free pratique and customs formalities and have its holds/tanks ready. An NOR given before these conditions are met is considered invalid and laytime does not start; this leads to loss of demurrage.
NOR, geminin yükleme/boşaltma için her b: The NOR is the document notifying the charterer or receiver that the ship is ready in all respects to load or discharge, and it starts the laytime clock. For the NOR to be valid, the ship must be physically and legally ready (free pratique granted, customs formalities completed, access to the cargo open). An NOR tendered too early or invalidly upsets the laytime calculation and leads to demurrage/despatch disputes.
NOx Technical Code kapsamında Tier II/II: Under the NOx Technical Code, Tier II/III compliance requires injection timing, EGR/SCR systems and engine group parameters to be kept in line with the EIAPP/Technical File. The Second Engineer ensures that setting changes remain within the approved limits and that the Record Book of Engine Parameters is kept up to date.
NOx emisyonu motorun yanma sıcaklığına b: NOx emissions depend on the combustion temperature of the engine. For Tier III, SCR (Selective Catalytic Reduction — with urea/AdBlue) or EGR (Exhaust Gas Recirculation) is used. Every engine is certified with a NOx Technical File; the setting parameters (injection timing, nozzle, cam) must be kept within the range permitted by this file. Unauthorized "tuning" is a NOx violation.
NOx: Tier I (2000-2010), Tier II (2011+): NOx: Tier I (2000–2010), Tier II (2011 onwards), Tier III (in NOx ECAs, 2016 onwards).
NPSHavailable: Sistemin emme noktasında: NPSH available: the pressure head that the system can provide at the suction point. NPSH required: the minimum pressure head the pump needs to work without cavitation (given in the maker's catalogue).
Narkotik/kontrollü ilaçlar kilitli, ayrı: Narcotic/controlled drugs are kept locked, recorded separately (controlled drugs register) and generally used under the supervision of two persons. The use, quantity and reason are recorded; missing stock or unrecorded use is a serious legal problem.
Navigation light panel (seyir feneri pan: The navigation light panel provides a dual supply (main + emergency) for each light, on/off monitoring and a lamp failure alarm. The ETO verifies that each light is fed from two independent sources, that spare lamps are ready and that the lamp failure alarm works.
Near-miss (ramak kala olay), bir kazaya: A near miss is an event that could have led to an accident but passed without consequences. MSC-MEPC.7/Circ.7 encourages near-miss reporting, because beneath every serious accident lie dozens of near misses and hundreds of unsafe acts (the Heinrich/Bird pyramid). The Master creates a non-blaming environment that encourages the crew to report near misses; a high number of near-miss reports is not bad but, on the contrary, a sign of a healthy safety culture.
Near-miss (ramak kala), yaralanma/hasar: A near-miss is an event that did not cause injury or damage but could have. The Heinrich/Bird pyramid shows that beneath every serious accident there are dozens of near-misses and hundreds of unsafe acts. Collecting near-misses is the cheapest way to prevent accidents.
Near-miss (ramak kala), zarara yol açmam: A near-miss is an event that did not cause harm but could have. Every near-miss is a forerunner of an accident that can be prevented in the future. According to the accident pyramid principle, behind a large number of reported near-misses lies a smaller number of serious accidents; by managing near-misses, serious accidents are prevented.
Near-miss kültürünün en büyük düşmanı ko: The greatest enemy of a near-miss culture is fear: the perception that "reporting is punished" kills reporting. The Third Officer stresses that reporting is a tool for learning, not for blame, and builds an environment focused on solutions, not punishment. Open reporting is the sign of a living safety culture.
Near-miss raporlamasının canlı olması, b: Lively near-miss reporting is the most reliable indicator of a ship's safety culture. A ship from which no near miss is ever reported is not a ship where "everything is perfect" but one where "nothing is reported because of fear". The Master encourages reporting, protects the person who reports and draws a systemic lesson from every report.
Near-miss ve hazard raporlama teşvik edi: Near-miss and hazard reporting is encouraged; the data is used to improve the system.
Near-miss ve unsafe condition raporlaman: The "just culture" approach, in which reporting near misses and unsafe conditions is not punished but encouraged, is passed on from the very beginning. New crew members knowing that they can report without fear is the foundation for keeping the safety culture on board alive.
Nem ve sıcaklık boyanın yapışmasını doğr: Humidity and temperature directly affect paint adhesion. Painting just above or below the dew point traps moisture on the surface; this is why the Bosun usually does not paint in the morning before the dew has lifted or in the evening once the moisture settles. The AB does not start painting without asking: "Is the surface really dry and clean?"
Net yük = (final displacement − light sh: Net cargo = (final displacement − light ship − ballast − fuel − fresh water − constant). All tanks are carefully sounded; the constant must be consistent with previous surveys. A density correction is made.
New Edition ile \"Reprint\" farklıdır: r: A New Edition is different from a "Reprint": a reprint is a reissue that contains only the existing corrections and may not need any further correction, whereas a New Edition contains new navigational information and requires the old edition to be withdrawn from use.
Ni-Cd bataryalar dayanıklıdır, geniş sıc: Ni-Cd batteries are robust, operate over a wide temperature range and tolerate deep discharge better than lead-acid batteries; this is why they are preferred for GMDSS and engine start applications. The ETO tops up the electrolyte (potassium hydroxide, KOH, alkaline) with pure water and monitors cell voltages. Because KOH is alkaline, alkali safety precautions are required, not acid precautions.
Ni-Cd'de SG, kurşun-asitteki gibi şarj d: In Ni-Cd batteries, SG does not indicate the state of charge as it does in lead-acid batteries; the KOH density does not change significantly with discharge. The state of charge is therefore assessed by voltage and capacity tests. The ETO maintains capacity through the periodic full charge/discharge cycle recommended by the manufacturer.
Nitrit/pH/kloride değerleri haftalık tes: Nitrite, pH and chloride values are tested weekly; the correct inhibitor dosage prevents corrosion. Cleaning the coolers keeps the heat transfer efficient.
Nitrit/pH/kloride haftalık test edilir;: Nitrite, pH and chloride are tested weekly; the inhibitor dosage is maintained. On cold-climate routes the antifreeze concentration is checked in the circuits concerned.
Nitrite, pH and chloride are tested weekly; the inhibitor dosage is maintained. Cleaning the coolers keeps the heat transfer efficient.
No-go area; geminin draught ve UKC polic: No-go areas are shallow/dangerous areas that the ship must never enter, given her draft and the UKC policy. On ECDIS these areas are displayed through the safety contour and safety depth settings; on a paper chart they are marked by hatching. The plan is built so that it keeps the ship in safe water at all times.
Noon report verileri, charterer'ın gemi: Noon report data are used by the charterer to assess the ship's performance (good weather speed/consumption warranty). Bad weather, current and fouling increase consumption; the Chief Engineer explains these factors in the report.
Noon report, flowmeter, bunker delivery: If the noon reports, flow meters, bunker delivery notes and port operation data do not agree, CII management becomes misleading. Data quality should therefore be followed as a separate performance metric.
Noon report, her gün öğlen (12:00 local/: The noon report gives, every day at noon (12:00 local/UTC), the ship's position, the distance covered in the last 24 hours, average speed, main engine rpm, slip, weather/sea conditions, fuel consumption (HFO/VLSFO, MGO, cylinder oil, system oil) and ROB.
Noon report; mil/gün, ortalama hız, ME/A: The noon report includes miles/day, average speed, ME/AE/boiler FO and DO consumption, LO consumption, slip percentage and weather/sea conditions. The Second Engineer calculates the specific fuel oil consumption (SFOC, g/kWh) and compares it with the shop-test/sea-trial reference curve. A persistent increase in SFOC indicates fouling, injection faults, loss of T/C efficiency or governor deviation.
Normal (σ) ve kayma (τ) gerilmelerinin b: In a plane stress state where normal (σ) and shear (τ) stresses act together, the equivalent stress is calculated and compared with the yield strength. σvm < σyield / SF must hold.
Normal stern tube yağ tüketimi düşük ve: Normal stern tube oil consumption is low and steady. An increase in consumption indicates a leak; an increase of water in the oil (in the analysis) indicates seawater ingress through the aft seal. The Chief Engineer assesses these two indicators together.
Norovirus, deri enfeksiyonları ve solunu: Norovirus, skin infections and respiratory pathogens spread easily via contaminated textiles. During outbreaks (COVID, norovirus, etc.), the laundry handling protocol is tightened: separate collection, high temperature, extra disinfection and increased use of personal protective equipment.
Numune alımından sonuca kadar gözetim zi: The chain of custody is maintained from sample collection to result: who took the sample, how it was stored and who tested it are recorded. This ensures that the result remains valid against challenges, especially when it is positive. Disposal records are also kept.
Numune alırken hattı flush etmemek, kirl: Not flushing the line when taking a sample, using a dirty bottle or filling in the label wrongly spoils the analysis result and leads to wrong decisions. Accidentally mixing drained oil into the bilge is a direct violation of MARPOL.
Numune kabı temiz, etiketleme doğru (eki: The sample container must be clean, the labeling correct (equipment, date, running hours, oil brand), and the sampling point must be flushed beforehand. A wrong sample leads to a wrong diagnosis and to unnecessary or insufficient action.
Numune steril/temiz kaba alınır, üzerine: The sample is taken in a sterile/clean container, labeled with the name of the dish, the date and the time, and stored in a separate compartment (protected from cross-contamination). When the retention period ends, it is disposed of safely. In an outbreak investigation, this discipline both protects the ship (evidence) and allows a fast root-cause analysis.
Numune şişesi etiketlenir, her iki taraf: The sample bottle is labelled, signed by both parties (ship and supplier) and sealed.
Numune şişesi temiz, kuru ve doğru etike: The sample bottle must be clean, dry and correctly labeled: ship's name, engine, date, running hours, oil grade, last top-up information. A sample exposed to contamination (dirty funnel, wet bottle) gives a wrong result and causes unnecessary alarm/cost.
Numune, manifold hattına bağlı sürekli d: The sample must be taken by continuous drip sampling connected to the manifold line throughout the bunkering operation. A spot sample is accepted only when drip sampling is not possible.
Numune, yakıt manifoldu veya transfer ha: The sample is taken by continuous drip sampling from the sampling valve on the fuel manifold or transfer line, or with an automatic sampler. A grab sample taken at a single point is considered inadequate.
Numuneler, akredite ve denizcilik ekipma: Samples are sent to a laboratory that is accredited and familiar with marine equipment (e.g. the oil supplier's program or an independent analysis service). Using the same laboratory consistently is important for reliable trends.
Nöbetçi mühendis taşınabilir alarm cihaz: The duty engineer takes the portable alarm unit with them and remains available to be called.
O-ring ve seal ring'ler her açımda kontr: O-rings and seal rings are checked every time the bowl is opened and renewed if necessary. An old/hardened O-ring leaks and impairs the seal. The Oiler inspects all the seals removed and replaces any that are worn.
OCIMF SIRE 2.0, klasik checklist yerine: OCIMF SIRE 2.0 is a digital vetting system that, instead of the traditional checklist, works with risk-based, ship-specific questions (Core, Rotational and Campaign questions). The inspector uses a tablet and assesses the hardware, human and process dimensions together. The Chief Officer is expected to show knowledge of each procedure "by doing it, not from paper".
OCM 15 ppm'i aşarsa 3-way valve geri yol: If the OCM reading exceeds 15 ppm, the three-way valve returns the water to the bilge; discharge takes place only with the ship en route and when the MARPOL conditions are met (it is prohibited in the Antarctic area). Entries are made in ORB Part I with the correct code.
OCM 15 ppm'i aşarsa 3-way valve sintiney: If the OCM reading exceeds 15 ppm, the three-way valve returns the bilge water to the tank; discharge takes place only with the ship en route and when the MARPOL conditions are met (it is prohibited in the Antarctic area). Entries are made in ORB Part I with the correct code.
OMD alarmı asla \"false alarm\" varsayıl: An OMD alarm is never silenced on the assumption that it is a "false alarm". When mist is detected, the engine is slowed down/stopped, and the crankcase doors are kept closed for at least 20–30 minutes (so that the hot spot cools down and a sudden inflow of air does not trigger an explosion) before an inspection is made. This procedure is reinforced through drills.
OMD, ana/yardımcı makine karterindeki ya: The OMD monitors the oil mist density in the crankcase of the main/auxiliary engines. Excessive oil mist is a sign that a bearing/surface is overheating and vaporizing the oil; if this mist reaches its ignition limit, a crankcase explosion occurs. When the mist density rises above the threshold, the OMD triggers a slowdown/shutdown and prevents a major disaster.
OOG yükler genelde flat-rack/platform üz: OOG cargo is usually carried on flat racks or platforms; it is planned with additional lashings (chain or web), lashing angles and an MSL calculation. The overhanging dimensions affect the use of neighbouring slots.
OOW (Engine) Certificate of Competency (: An application for an OOW (Engine) Certificate of Competency (CoC) requires several documents to be brought together: approved Sea Service certificates, a completed TRB, mandatory STCW course certificates (Basic Safety, Advanced Firefighting, Survival Craft, Medical First Aid, Security Awareness, etc.), a valid medical certificate and the training institution's diploma/approval. A missing document holds up the application.
OOW (Engine) yeterlilik belgesine giden: On the way to the OOW (Engine) certificate of competency there are three chains of evidence: (1) approved sea service (Sea Service), (2) a completed TRB, (3) mandatory courses (firefighting, survival, medical first aid, security awareness, etc.), and finally the certificate of competency examination. The TRB is the middle link of this chain; if it is incomplete, the other links are not sufficient.
OOW rotayı appropriate largest scale/usa: The OOW reviews the route visually leg by leg on the appropriate largest scale/usage band, resolves and justifies every alarm and indication, and uses it as a protected route after the Master's approval. A last-minute route revision goes through the same chain of appraisal, check, visual review and approval.
OOW sürekli look-out yapar; radar/ARPA i: The OOW keeps a continuous lookout, assesses risk with radar/ARPA and applies COLREG. Rest hours and a clear handover are ensured; when in doubt, the Master is called.
OOW sürekli uygun gözcülük yapar; radar/: The OOW keeps a proper lookout at all times; risk of collision is assessed by radar/ARPA and by sight. Action is taken early and is substantial, in accordance with COLREG.
OOW; kısıtlı görüş (sis, yağmur, kar), g: The OOW calls for additional lookouts when factors such as restricted visibility (fog, rain, snow), darkness, heavy traffic, narrow channels/canals, navigation close to the coast, concentrations of fishing boats or fatigue arise. The AB is called to duty with orders such as "stand by the wheel" or "extra lookout on bridge wing".
ORB I ile fiili operasyon arasındaki tut: A discrepancy between ORB entries and the actual operation leads to heavy penalties. PSC and coastal states compare the records with physical evidence (soundings, tank condition).
ORB Part I (machinery space operations): ORB Part I (machinery space operations) and Part II (cargo/ballast — on tankers) are filled in under MARPOL Annex I immediately after each operation, with the relevant coded item (codes A to I in Part I). Discharges of slops, bilge water, sludge and through the oily water separator (15 ppm), internal transfers and deliveries of waste are recorded. Every page is signed by the Master.
ORB Part I (makine dairesi operasyonları: ORB Part I (machinery space operations) records every oily waste operation: ballasting/cleaning of fuel tanks, bilge water disposal, sludge disposal, bunkering, OWS use, accidental/exceptional discharge. Each entry is made with time, position, quantity and tank identification and is signed by the officer in charge; each page is signed by the Master.
ORB hataları PSC'de en sık ve en ciddi b: ORB errors are among the most frequent and most serious PSC findings; suspicion of a "magic pipe" can lead to criminal consequences. Legal records are the most sensitive part of technical reporting.
ORB tutarsızlığı (örn. sludge üretimi il: An inconsistency in the ORB (e.g. an imbalance between sludge production and delivery or incineration) immediately raises suspicion at PSC and US Coast Guard inspections. Most "magic pipe" (illegal bypass) cases came to light through a contradiction between the ORB and the actual situation.
ORB, GRB ve BWRB kayıtları PSC, klas ve: The ORB, GRB and BWRB entries are the first documents looked at in PSC, class and vetting (SIRE, CDI) inspections. An inconsistency between the records and the actual operations (e.g. a mismatch between the sludge quantity and the tank level) is a reason for a "deficiency" or detention. The Master guarantees that the records reflect the truth and that no retrospective "corrections" are made.
OWS (genelde gravity coalescer + ikinci: The OWS (usually a gravity coalescer + second-stage filter) separates oil from bilge water. The discharge water is measured continuously by the 15 ppm Oil Content Meter (OCM/oil monitor); when 15 ppm is exceeded, the three-way valve automatically returns the water to the bilge tank (it cannot be pumped overboard). This is the core of the MEPC.107(49) standard.
OWS bypass'ı ağır cezalı kriminal suçtur: Bypassing the OWS is a criminal offence with heavy penalties; the ORB Part I entries must agree with what actually happened.
Bypassing the OWS is a criminal offence with heavy penalties; the records must agree with what actually happened.
