Rest hour sheets that "look perfect but are unrealistic" are a red flag for the inspector.
Rest hours kayıtları, gerçek dinlenmeyi: Rest hour records must reflect real rest. Keeping false records to show compliance (record falsification) is both a violation of the MLC and a collapse of the safety culture, because it hides real fatigue and makes the risk invisible. The Master insists on honest records.
Rest-hours kayıtları (work/rest record): Rest-hours records (work/rest record) are kept daily and signed by the crew member and the person responsible; where there is a violation, its reason and how it was compensated are recorded. These records are examined during PSC and MLC inspections; systematic violation is a serious finding.
Restricted visibility (Kural 19) özel ol: Restricted visibility (Rule 19) is given particular emphasis; in this situation there is no stand-on/give-way distinction, and every ship makes an early and substantial maneuver based on radar plotting. The Second Officer clearly teaches that in fog an alteration of course to port for a ship forward of the beam (other than a ship being overtaken) and an alteration of course towards a ship abeam or abaft the beam are to be avoided, and that speed must be reduced to a safe level.
Reverse power rölesi özellikle paralel ç: The reverse power relay is particularly critical in parallel operation: if a generator loses fuel, it goes into motoring mode and draws power from the other machine; the relay detects this and opens the breaker (typical setpoint 2–6% of rated power, 3–5 s delay). The ETO records the pickup and timing value of each relay in the annual test schedule; these records are requested at PSC inspections and class surveys.
Revir temizliği ve tıbbi yardım desteği,: Sick bay cleaning and medical support is a task through which the steward contributes directly to the recovery of sick crew members and to the ship's MLC compliance. A sick bay that is always ready, attentive patient care and meticulous infection control protect both the individual's health and the hygiene of the whole ship.
Revir, hasta/yaralı bakımı için ayrılmış: The sick bay is a space set aside for the care of sick/injured persons and must be clean, tidy and ready for use at all times. A dirty or untidy sick bay both puts patient care at risk and results directly in an MLC non-conformity finding during inspections. The steward ensures this readiness of the sick bay every day.
Revir; hasta/yaralı bakımı için ayrılmış: The sick bay is a space set aside for the care of sick or injured persons; it must be hygienic, heated/ventilated and provided with the necessary equipment. The Second Officer ensures that the sick bay is clean, tidy and ready for use; the berth, oxygen, stretcher and first-aid equipment are kept accessible.
Revirde yatan hasta mürettebata kamarot;: For sick crew members confined to the sick bay, the steward brings meals, drinks and basic necessities and ensures the comfort of the room (temperature, ventilation, cleanliness). Suitable food for the patient (light/diet food if necessary) is coordinated with the cook. This support contributes to the patient's recovery and morale.
Reynolds sayısı akışkan hızı, karakteris: The Reynolds number depends on the flow velocity, the characteristic length and the kinematic viscosity.
RightShip kabulü için RISQ (RightShip'in: For RightShip acceptance a physical inspection based on RISQ (RightShip's inspection questionnaire) may also be carried out. The Master's practical task is to ensure, together with the company, that the ship's data on the RightShip platform (survey dates, PSC history, accident and incident records) is up to date and correct, and to take every finding seriously, knowing in particular that PSC detentions pull the score down for months.
RightShip, ağırlıklı olarak dökme yük (b: RightShip is the platform through which charterers in the dry bulk segment mainly (traditionally iron ore, coal, grain) make their ship acceptance decisions. It assigns a ship a Safety Score (1 to 5, similar to stars) and also a GHG Rating (A–G, rating the ship's carbon efficiency relative to comparable ships). A low safety score or a poor GHG rating leads to the ship dropping off the nomination lists of the big mining and energy companies.
Riser angle monitoring ile DP pozisyon t: Riser angle monitoring and the DP position trend are watched together; a relaxed position or heading is used only within the approved envelope. On the WCF, drive-off/drift-off or an environmental limit, the secure well, disconnect and escape route sequence is followed.
Risk değerlendirmesi (risk assessment),: Risk assessment means identifying the hazards before a job and planning control measures. The cadet learns hazard identification, likelihood/severity assessment and the logic of the hierarchy of controls (elimination, substitution, engineering, administrative, PPE). This way of thinking is the basis of safety throughout a career.
Risk değerlendirmesinde sıcak yüzey, bas: The risk assessment identifies hot surfaces, pressurized fluids, heavy parts falling (trapping/crushing), sparks, chemicals and enclosed space risks, and sets out mitigation measures (PPE, crane/slings, ventilation).
Risk profili yüksektir: yakıt yanıcıdır: The risk profile is high: fuel is flammable (fire/explosion), hot fuel/oil carries a risk of spraying, and if either enters the sea it constitutes a pollution offense. When learning these systems, the cadet must understand both the technical operation and the safety and environmental aspects together.
Riskler bir öncelik sırasıyla kontrol ed: Risks are controlled in order of priority: first removing the hazard (elimination), then substitution, engineering controls (guarding, ventilation, isolation), administrative controls (procedures, training, permits) and finally PPE. PPE is the weakest defense because it depends on the individual and can fail; it is therefore regarded as the "last line of defense".
Ro-Ro ve PCC (Pure Car Carrier) gemileri: On Ro-Ro ships and PCCs (Pure Car Carriers), the openings where water can enter (bow/stern doors), low GM and the lashing of vehicles are critical. The Estonia (1994) and Golden Ray (2019) cases show the importance of stability and door safety on this type of ship.
Ro-Ro'da trailer ve self-propelled units: On Ro-Ro ships, trailers and self-propelled units are secured to deck pad-eyes with webbing/chains at no fewer than 4 points. For heavy lift cargo (transformers, generators, crane structures etc.), a detailed lashing plan and engineering calculation are made (usually coordinated between the shipper and the 1/C). The plan requires the approval of the Master and class.
Ro-ro gemilerinde araç/trailer'lar güver: On Ro-Ro ships, vehicles and trailers are secured to the deck lashing points with web slings or chains and tensioners; wheel chocks are added. The lashing angle and number are chosen for the vehicle weight in accordance with the CSM.
Ro-ro gemilerinde stern ramp/door (kıç),: Ro-Ro ships have a stern ramp/door aft, a bow visor and bow ramp forward, side ramps and internal ramps or lifts. The ramps serve both as the cargo route and, when closed, as a watertight barrier. They are usually moved by hydraulic cylinders or winches.
RoRo gemilerinde araç ve trailer'lar, de: On RoRo ships, vehicles and trailers are secured to deck pad-eyes/D-rings with web or chain lashings. The CSM sets the minimum number and the angle of lashing points according to vehicle type and weight; heavy self-propelled units are secured at no fewer than four points, and at more points depending on weight and acceleration. The lashing angle (vertical/horizontal component) directly affects safety.
Rock dumping'de survey doğrulamasıyla ço: In rock dumping, a multi-pass plan is used with survey verification; in cable work, the catenary and the minimum bend radius are followed. If the vehicle snags, tension rises, telemetry is lost or DP degrades, the stop and recovery plan is applied.
Rocket parachute flare, hand flare ve bu: The expiry dates of rocket parachute flares, hand flares and buoyant smoke signals (generally 3–3.5 years from manufacture) are tracked carefully. Expired items are disposed of or handed over properly; the ship does not sail with expired pyrotechnics. They count as visual distress signals under LSA (SOLAS III, LSA Code).
Rota optimizasyonu minimum yakıt tüketim: Route optimisation is carried out for one or more of the following objectives: minimum fuel consumption, minimum voyage time or maximum safety.
Rota, ardışık waypoint'ler (dönüş noktal: A route consists of successive waypoints (turning points) and the legs joining them. For each leg, the cadet learns to calculate the course, distance, planned speed and estimated time on the leg. Calculating the ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) from the total distance and the average speed is critical for charterer reporting and the tidal window.
Rotor (dönen alan) dizel motor tarafında: The rotor (rotating field) is driven by the diesel engine and produces a magnetic field with DC excitation current. The stator windings produce an EMF (electromotive force) in this rotating field.
Rotor hızı senkron hızdan her zaman düşü: The rotor speed is always lower than the synchronous speed. This difference is called slip.
Route planner ile waypoint'ler girilir;: Waypoints are entered with the route planner; the check route function produces warnings for no-go areas, shoals and prohibited areas. Each warning is assessed one by one; an automatically generated route is never approved without a manual check.
Route, berth-to-berth hazırlanır; waypoi: The route is prepared berth to berth; waypoints and legs, turn radius and wheel-over, the speed plan, XTD, clearing ranges/PI, reporting points, no-go and limiting danger lines, abort points, contingency anchorages and pilotage notes are linked in a single passage plan.
Route-based folio yönetiminde, geminin t: In route-based folio management, a "standard folio" is defined for the ship's typical routes; if a new voyage goes outside this standard, additional charts are obtained. In AVCS this is handled as digital folio and cell permit management; license periods and renewal dates are monitored.
Royal Majesty (1995): GPS anten arızası: Royal Majesty (1995): the GPS antenna failure went unnoticed, the ship deviated from the planned track for hours and ran aground. Lesson: do not rely on a single position source; cross-check with the depth and with independent fixes.
Royal Majesty (1995): GPS anten bağlantı: Royal Majesty (1995): the GPS antenna connection came apart, the positioning fell back to DR mode and the ship deviated for hours without the team noticing; because there was no confirmation with the echo sounder and independent fixes, she ran aground. Lesson: cross-check the equipment and do not rely on a single source.
Rubber seal/conta hasar açısından denetl: Rubber seals and packing are inspected for damage; the locks must close fully and give compression. The drainage and bilge alarm systems are tested.
Rule 5 tüm uygun araçlarla gözcülük; Rul: Rule 5 requires a lookout by all available means; Rule 6 a safe speed; Rule 7 determining risk of collision with all available means; Rule 8 early, substantial and safe action to avoid collision. A bearing that remains steady or does not change appreciably, together with a decreasing range, is a sign of serious risk; at close range risk may exist even if the bearing changes.
Rutin \"kâğıt doldurma\" tatbikatı tehli: A routine "form-filling" drill is dangerous; it is of no use in a real emergency. Every drill must rehearse what the team will actually do and expose the weak points.
Rutin operasyonlarda katılımcı veya dele: In routine operations a participative or delegating style increases motivation and learning.
Römorkör kullanılıyorsa Reis, tug line'ı: If tugs are used, the Bosun ensures that the tug line is taken on board safely and made fast to the correct bitt/SPM point, and that the crew keep clear while it is under tension. A parting tug line, or one loaded at the wrong angle, causes serious injuries. Work with the tug is coordinated within the bridge–pilot–tug master triangle.
Römorkör yardımlı manevralarda Birinci Z: In tug-assisted maneuvers, the Chief Officer supervises the safe securing of the tug line (usually with the tug's own gear or the ship's messenger) to the ship's bitt/fairlead. A Panama lead, a closed chock or a bollard marked with its SWL is used. The SWL of the fairlead through which the tug line passes must not be exceeded.
Rüzgâr ve akıntı (leeway/set) gemiyi rot: Wind and current (leeway/set) push the ship off its course; even if the helmsman holds the heading on the compass, the ship may be set sideways. In pilotage and narrow waters, the OOW/pilot compensates for this using transits/leading lines and helm orders; the helmsman carries out the orders given exactly and reports any persistent offset noticed (e.g., "she's carrying port helm").
Rüzgâr, dalga, akıntı ve görüş koşulları: Wind, waves, currents and visibility are taken into account. In large waves the added resistance can increase fuel consumption by 10–30%.
S-101, S-100 tabanlı yeni nesil ENC ürün: S-101 is the next-generation ENC product based on S-100 and cannot be opened on every existing S-57 ECDIS. MSC.530(106) accepts either MSC.232(82) or the new standard for equipment installed between 1 January 2026 and 31 December 2028; ECDIS installed from 1 January 2029 will comply with the new, S-100-capable standard. This does not mean that all ships' ENCs switch to S-101 overnight.
S-N eğrisi, uygulanan gerilme genliği (S: The S-N curve shows the relationship between the applied stress amplitude (S) and the number of cycles to failure (N). In steel, fracture does not occur below a certain stress (the fatigue limit); this is generally about 40–50% of the tensile strength.
S-VDR (Simplified), tam VDR'ye göre daha: The S-VDR (Simplified VDR) records less data than a full VDR (for example the radar picture may not be mandatory); it was used on existing (retrofit) ships for reasons of cost. A full VDR is standard on new ships.
S-lay'de joint boyuna uygun incremental: In S-lay, incremental moves match the joint length; in J-lay and reel-lay, approved low-speed auto-track is used. In the event of a welding or production delay, loss of tension, a DP excursion or the WCF, the hold, laydown or abandon procedure is started.
SART (Search and Rescue Transponder), 9: The SART (Search and Rescue Transponder) responds to a 9 GHz X-band radar signal and produces a line of 12 dots on the rescue ship's radar. Battery expiry and the self-test are checked. Replacement of the EPIRB battery and HRU is documented with service records.
SART (Search and Rescue Transponder), ca: The SART (Search and Rescue Transponder) is a device carried in a liferaft/lifeboat which, when triggered by a 9 GHz radar, produces a line of 12 dots on the display. The Second Officer keeps a record of the SART battery expiry date and, where required, of the periodic test (against a radar).
SART (Search and Rescue Transponder), ra: A SART (Search and Rescue Transponder) is either a radar SART or an AIS-SART. A radar SART responds to the 9 GHz radar of a searching ship and produces a line of 12 dots (blip line) on the PPI display. An AIS-SART transmits its position as an AIS target. The Second Officer carries out the monthly self-test and monitors the battery expiry.
SBAS (Satellite Based Augmentation Syste: SBAS (Satellite Based Augmentation System): satellite-based correction systems such as WAAS (USA), EGNOS (Europe) and MSAS (Japan) improve accuracy regionally.
SBT kontaminasyonu ağır MARPOL ihlalidir: Contamination of segregated ballast is a serious MARPOL violation; the line segregation is maintained carefully during maintenance.
SBT, kargo tanklarından tamamen ayrıdır: Segregated ballast tanks are completely separate from the cargo tanks and never mix with cargo. Ballast is discharged during loading and taken on during discharge; each step is checked in the loading computer for SF/BM/GM.
SCBA seti: tüp, basınç regülatörü, deman: An SCBA set includes a cylinder, pressure regulator, demand valve, full face mask, back frame and low-pressure whistle.
SCBA tipik 1200/1800/2000 L hava ile 30–: An SCBA typically gives a working time of 30–45 minutes with 1200/1800/2000 L of air.
SCBA tüpleri belirli aralıklarla hydrost: SCBA cylinders are subject to hydrostatic testing at set intervals (composite ~5 years, steel ~10 years — determined by the manufacturer/flag). There must be at least two spare charged cylinders or a compressor on board. The mask and regulator are sent to an authorized service provider annually.
SCBA, fireman's outfit'in parçasıdır; ya: SCBA is part of the fireman's outfit; it allows the fire team to work in smoky/toxic atmospheres. The Safety Officer checks the cylinder pressure (usually ~300 bar when full), the low-pressure whistle (~50-55 bar), mask tightness, demand valve function and the condition of the harness. The cylinder is refilled after every use.
SCBA; yüksek basınçlı hava tüpü (genelde: An SCBA consists of a high-pressure air cylinder (generally about 6–9 L, about 300 bar), a pressure reducer and demand valve, a full face mask, a back frame, and a pressure gauge with a low-pressure whistle. The mask is kept at positive pressure to prevent smoke getting in.
SCOPIC (Special Compensation P&I Clause): SCOPIC (Special Compensation P&I Clause) is a mechanism that can be added to LOF and comes into play especially in salvage operations involving an environmental risk. Under the classic "no cure – no pay" logic, a salvor can make a loss when salving a ship that threatens the environment but has a low commercial value; SCOPIC pays the salvor reasonable expenses plus a certain margin regardless of success. SCOPIC compensation is typically paid by the P&I club.
SCOPIC devreye alındığında, P&I'ın atadı: When SCOPIC is invoked, an SCR (Special Casualty Representative) appointed on behalf of the P&I side joins the operation and monitors the salvage expenses. The Master works in coordination with the SCR and the salvage master; the ship's crew usually give practical support to the salvage operation (for example the towing connection, pumping, damage control). Throughout, safety and protection of the environment have priority.
SCR (Selective Catalytic Reduction): Üre: SCR (Selective Catalytic Reduction): converts NOx into N₂ and H₂O with a urea solution.
SCR (Silicon Controlled Rectifier), gate: An SCR (Silicon Controlled Rectifier) is a three-terminal semiconductor device that is turned on by a gate trigger signal and conducts until the current falls to zero. The DC output voltage can be adjusted by controlling the gate firing angle.
SEEMP (Ship Energy Efficiency Management: The SEEMP (Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan) and the company's environmental management system (in some cases ISO 14001) continuously monitor and improve energy and waste performance. On the engine room side, the Chief Engineer is the data provider and implementer for these systems; trend reports are shared with the superintendent.
SEEMP Part II, yakıt tüketim verisinin (: SEEMP Part II defines the method for collecting fuel consumption data (IMO DCS); Part III contains the CII targets and the implementation plan for achieving them. The Chief Engineer ensures that the data are collected consistently, completely and in line with the approved plan.
SEEMP: the energy efficiency management plan.
SFOC, exhaust gas spread, T/C devri, sca: SFOC, exhaust gas spread, T/C rpm, scavenge air pressure and oil analysis results are presented as monthly trends. It is not a single day's data that is assessed, but the rolling average and the direction of the trend.
SIRE 2.0, OCIMF'in 2024'te tam yürürlüğe: SIRE 2.0 is OCIMF's new tanker vetting regime, fully introduced in 2024. Instead of the old static VIQ, it works with tablets, a question bank and a vessel-specific risk profile. When the inspector arrives on board, he or she sees the set of questions the system has selected for that ship; the questions are divided into the Hardware (equipment), Process (procedures and records) and Human (crew competence) dimensions. The weight given to the human factor has greatly increased the importance of the interviews with the Master and the officers.
SIRE 2.0; sabit soru setinden, gemiye/du: SIRE 2.0 has moved from a fixed set of questions to a dynamic set specific to the ship and the situation, with the inspector reporting in real time on a tablet. The hardware, process and human (behaviour) dimensions are assessed separately.
SMS, gemide somut olarak bir dizi el kit: On board, the SMS lives concretely as a set of manuals, checklists, forms and records: the Safety Management Manual, procedures for critical operations (enclosed space entry, hot work, mooring, bunkering, navigation), risk assessment templates, the permit-to-work system and the records archive. The Master's task is to confirm that these documents are at the latest revision on board (controlled document register), that old revisions have been withdrawn, and that the crew can access the relevant procedures.
SOF, limandaki tüm olayların (varış, dem: The SOF is the time-stamped chronological record of all events in port (arrival, anchoring, berthing, NOR tendered, start and completion of cargo, waiting times, weather stoppages, breakdowns). The agent prepares it; the Master checks and signs it. The SOF is the basis of the demurrage/despatch calculation through the time sheet; for this reason the cause of every delay (rain, no cargo, awaiting documents) must be written clearly.
SOF, terminal/charterer ile birlikte tut: The SOF is the timeline of the operation, kept jointly with the terminal/charterer. If a dispute arises, demurrage is calculated from this document. The Chief Officer issues a Letter of Protest (LOP) whenever necessary: slow loading rate, equipment breakdown, weather delays, etc.
SOLAS A Pack, LSA Code'daki tam emergenc: The SOLAS A pack is the full set of emergency equipment in the LSA Code; the list of items and quantities is verified from the service certificate and the pack marking.
SOLAS B Pack yalnız Administration'ın iz: The SOLAS B pack is a reduced pack only for short international voyages permitted by the Administration; it is not chosen on an arbitrary "24-hour" limit.
SOLAS Bölüm II-1 Kural 42 gereği acil ay: Under SOLAS Chapter II-1, Regulation 42, emergency lighting must come on automatically after the loss of main power. An uninterrupted operating time of 36 hours is required on passenger ships and 18 hours on cargo ships.
SOLAS Bölüm II-1 Kural 42-44'e göre tüm: Under SOLAS Chapter II-1 Regulations 42-44, all passenger ships and cargo ships of 500 GT and above must have an emergency source of power. The emergency generator must come on line automatically within 45 seconds of loss of main power.
SOLAS Chapter II-2, kaçış yollarının her: SOLAS Chapter II-2 requires escape routes to be kept open and unobstructed at all times. The Bosun checks that no material is stowed in front of corridors, stairways, doors and emergency exits. In a fire, one extra meter along a smoke-filled corridor is the difference between life and death.
SOLAS Chapter III ve ISM madde 8, düzenl: SOLAS Chapter III and ISM section 8 make regular drills mandatory: abandon ship and fire drills every month (within 24 hours of leaving port if more than 25% of the crew did not take part in drills the previous month), enclosed space entry and rescue drills at least every two months, and also damage control, oil spill (SOPEP), man overboard, steering gear failure, security (ISPS) and other scenarios. The Master keeps the schedule of these drills and records that they have actually been carried out.
SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 19, gemi tona: SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 19 lists the navigational equipment that must be carried according to the ship's tonnage and area of operation (gyro compass, magnetic compass, radar/ARPA, ECDIS, AIS, echo sounder, speed/distance log, GNSS, BNWAS, VDR). The Second Officer monitors that this equipment is not only on board but also working in a condition that meets the performance standards.
SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 27, geminin y: SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 27 requires the ship to carry adequate and up-to-date nautical charts and publications for the intended voyage. Being up to date means having been corrected in accordance with the latest published Notices to Mariners; "adequate" means charts of a resolution and scale that cover all areas from the start to the end of the voyage.
SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 34, her sefer: SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 34 requires every voyage to be planned before it starts, and the plan to cover the whole voyage without a break, from berth to berth, including pilotage waters, maneuvering areas and the open sea. When preparing this plan, the Second Officer works on the "berth-to-berth" principle; the anchorage, the pilot boarding ground and narrow channel transits are an integral part of the plan.
SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 5, akit devle: SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 5 obliges Contracting Governments to provide weather warnings, synoptic analyses and forecasts, and ships to receive and assess this information. The Second Officer ensures that the gale/storm warnings issued for the METAREA the ship is in are received and passed to the bridge.
SOLAS II-1 Reg. 3-8 ve MSC.1/Circ.1175,: SOLAS II-1 Reg. 3-8 and MSC.1/Circ.1175 require the SWL of towing and mooring fittings to be marked on board and documented. The Chief Officer must know the marked SWL of every bitt and chock in use and must not exceed it. Choosing the wrong chock (e.g. excessive load at a narrow angle) can tear the fitting out of the deck.
SOLAS II-1, çarpışma/oturma sonrası bölm: SOLAS II-1 introduces the criterion attained subdivision index A ≥ required index R for watertight subdivision and damage stability after collision/grounding. The Chief Officer monitors the status of watertight doors/manholes and whether the loading condition is consistent with the damage control plan.
SOLAS II-2, makine daireleri, kargo bölg: SOLAS II-2 requires machinery spaces, cargo areas, cabins, corridors and escape routes to be protected by fixed fire detection. FSS Code Chapter 9 sets out the design, testing and approval criteria for the system: detectors must be designed so that they retain the ability to give an alarm in the event of a fault or loss of power, and the system must be supplied from both the main and the emergency source of power.
SOLAS III ve II-2, geminin can kurtarma: SOLAS III and II-2 require the ship to keep its life-saving and fire-fighting equipment ready for use at all times. Even though the Chief Officer assigns the daily LSA/FFE checks to junior officers, the Chief Officer remains ultimately responsible for readiness, the accuracy of records and compliance with the service schedule. When a finding is raised at inspection, the Chief Officer is the one held accountable.
SOLAS III/19 gereği abandon ship ve fire: Under SOLAS III/19, abandon ship and fire drills are held at least once a month; each drill tests the muster list under real conditions. During the drill the Safety Officer times the muster, notes people who are left without a duty or are confused, identifies conflicting duties and revises the muster list based on these findings.
SOLAS III/19, fire ve abandon ship drill: SOLAS III/19 makes fire and abandon ship drills mandatory every month (weekly on passenger ships) and enclosed space entry and rescue drills at least every two months. In addition, the company SMS plans MOB, pollution (SOPEP), grounding, blackout, steering failure, helicopter operation and security drills. The Master fits the drill schedule to the voyage programme and ensures that no drill is done only "on paper".
SOLAS III/19, giriş veya kurtarma görevi: SOLAS III/19 requires enclosed space entry and rescue drills at least once every two months for personnel with entry or rescue duties. The Bosun ensures that the team drills realistic rescue scenarios, because in a real incident a correct and rapid rescue is only possible with a reflex built up through drills.
SOLAS III/19, her mürettebat üyesinin ay: SOLAS III/19 requires every crew member to take part in at least one abandon ship drill and one fire drill every month. If more than 25% of the crew have not taken part in drills on board in the previous month, an abandon ship drill and a fire drill must be held within 24 hours of the ship leaving port. On ships with a high crew turnover, this rule requires the Safety Officer to build the drill plan around the voyage schedule.
SOLAS III/19.3.2 gereği, mürettebatın %2: Under SOLAS III/19.3.2, if more than 25% of the crew have not taken part in drills on board in the previous month, a drill is held within 24 hours of the ship leaving port. The Safety Officer makes sure that new crew members take an active role in their first drill; the knowledge taught in familiarization is reinforced by rehearsing a real scenario.
SOLAS III/19.3.2, gemiyi terk (abandon s: SOLAS III/19.3.2 requires every crew member to take part in abandon ship and fire drills at least once a month; if more than 25% of the crew have not taken part in drills on board in the previous month, a drill is held within 24 hours of the ship leaving port. Enclosed space entry and rescue drills are held at least once every two months (III/19.3.3) and security (ISPS) drills at least once every three months; man overboard and pollution scenarios are planned according to the company SMS.
SOLAS III/19.3.3 gereği enclosed space e: Under SOLAS III/19.3.3, an enclosed space entry and rescue drill must be held at least once every 2 months; the planning and content of the drill are based on III/19.3.6 and the recommendations of IMO Res. A.1203(33). Enclosed space accidents are usually multiplied by the deaths of the "second person rushing to the rescue"; this is why the attendant never goes in, but raises the alarm and waits for the equipped rescue team.
SOLAS III/19.3.3, kapalı mekan giriş ve: SOLAS III/19.3.3 requires enclosed space entry and rescue drills to be held at least once every two months. In these drills, atmosphere testing, use of the permit, donning SCBA, recovering a casualty with a lifeline and resuscitation are simulated. In these drills, the AB acquires the reflexes to act without thinking in a real emergency.
SOLAS III/20.6 ve III/20.7 gereği filika: Under SOLAS III/20.6 and III/20.7, lifeboats are subject to a weekly visual inspection and engine run and to a monthly detailed inspection. In the weekly inspection, the lifeboat and launching appliance are inspected visually, and the engine is run for a total of at least 3 minutes. In the monthly inspection, the completeness of the inventory, running of the engine for at least 3 minutes, and the condition of the davit and falls are checked.
SOLAS III/8 ve III/37, muster list'in yo: SOLAS III/8 and III/37 require the muster list to be prepared before the voyage and posted in conspicuous places on board (bridge, engine control room, crew accommodation). The list clearly shows the details of the general alarm and abandon ship signals, the action each person is to take when the alarm sounds, the muster stations, the persons assigned to close watertight doors, fire doors and valves, and the persons responsible for preparing the survival craft and fire-fighting equipment.
SOLAS V, seferin tamamını kapsayan, günc: SOLAS V requires the ship to carry official charts that cover the whole voyage, are up to date and are of adequate scale. On ships using ECDIS, this is achieved by subscribing to an official ENC service (UKHO ADMIRALTY, NOAA, Primar, etc.) and updating regularly. The Second Officer is the person actually responsible for keeping them up to date.
SOLAS V/14 ve IMO Res. A.1047(27) uyarın: Under SOLAS V/14 and IMO Res. A.1047(27), every ship carries a Minimum Safe Manning Document issued by the flag state. This document defines the minimum manning — by position and certificate level — needed for the safe navigation of the ship, the safety of life, the protection of the marine environment and safe operation. The Master must ensure that the actual manning on board never falls below this document.
SOLAS V/19, derinlik ölçüm cihazı taşıma: SOLAS V/19 makes it mandatory to carry an echo-sounding device. The shallow water alarm gives an audible and visual warning when the depth falls below the selected safe depth; it is kept active on the bridge.
SOLAS V/19, gemi tonajına göre zorunlu s: SOLAS V/19 lists the mandatory navigational equipment according to ship tonnage: gyro, radar (two radars above a certain tonnage), ECDIS (with backup), AIS, VDR/S-VDR, echo sounder, speed log, BNWAS, LRIT. The ETO ensures that this equipment is working and type-approved; the failure of one item can be a cause of navigational restrictions (PSC detention).
SOLAS V/19, tonaja göre bir veya iki rad: SOLAS V/19 requires one or two radars depending on tonnage (the second normally S-band). The performance monitor (PM) is used to check the transmitter power and receiver sensitivity on the screen; tuning and the PM are checked regularly.
SOLAS V/28, seyirle ilgili tüm faaliyetl: SOLAS V/28 makes it mandatory to record all navigational activities and incidents; a clock change is also a navigational event that must be recorded. The Second Officer enters the clock change in the deck logbook with these elements: the moment of the change (old ship's time and new ship's time), the amount and direction of the change (e.g. "Clocks retarded 30 min"), the new zone description and the reference of the Master's approval.
SOLAS V/34, geminin sefere çıkmadan önce: SOLAS V/34 clearly states that, before the ship proceeds to sea, the Master must ensure that the intended voyage has been planned (passage plan) using the appropriate charts and nautical publications. The plan must be prepared on a berth-to-berth basis; route selection, adequate depth, expected weather and currents, traffic density, anchorages, abort points and contingency anchorages must be included as integral parts of the plan. It is not enough for the Master simply to "sign" the plan; the Master is expected to actually review whether the plan is suitable for the ship type, the nature of the voyage and the competence of the crew.
SOLAS VI/2 (2016 değişikliği), konteyner: SOLAS VI/2 (2016 amendment) requires the Verified Gross Mass (VGM) of containers to be declared before loading; a container without a VGM is not loaded. The Chief Officer checks that the VGM data are consistent with the stowage/stability calculation. A wrongly declared weight corrupts the stability and strength calculations (the MSC Napoli case of 2007 showed poor weight declaration).
SOLAS VI/2 uyarınca shipper, yüklemeden: Under SOLAS VI/2 the shipper must provide accurate and sufficient cargo information before loading (IMSBC group, TML, MSDS, density / stowage factor, DG class). The Master does not accept this information passively; in case of inconsistency, missing documents or a suspicious declaration, he or she asks for additional verification, has a Letter of Protest issued and, if necessary, stops loading.
SOLAS VI/2 ve MSC.1/Circ.1475, her dolu: SOLAS VI/2 and MSC.1/Circ.1475 make a VGM declaration mandatory for every packed container. A container without a VGM cannot be loaded on the ship. The VGM is obtained either by weighing (Method 1) or by an approved calculation (Method 2). The Master knows that a missing VGM or implausible values are a reason to stop loading; a mis-declared weight corrupts the lashing and stability calculations (MSC Napoli, 2007, is the case usually cited).
SOLAS VI/5.6 ve VII, konteynerler dahil: SOLAS VI/5.6 and VII require all cargo units, including containers, to be stowed and secured in accordance with a ship-specific Cargo Securing Manual approved by the Administration/class. The CSM contains the ship's lashing equipment inventory, the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) of each item, approved lashing patterns, securing device arrangement plans and calculation methods. MSC.1/Circ.1353 is the guideline for its preparation.
SOLAS gemilerinde en az üç (300 GT ve üz: SOLAS ships carry at least three (at least two on cargo ships of 300 GT and upwards but less than 500 GT) waterproof portable VHF radios (survival craft two-way VHF). These are for on-scene communication from survival craft. The primary battery is sealed and for emergency use only; a separate rechargeable battery is for routine/test use.
SOLAS gereği acil jeneratör haftalık ola: The emergency generator is test-run regularly (usually weekly) under the periodic testing of the emergency source of power required by SOLAS. Automatic starting, taking load and the alarm functions must be verified.
SOLAS gereği drill'ler (abandon ship ve: As required by SOLAS, drills (abandon ship and fire monthly — weekly on passenger ships; enclosed space entry/rescue at least every two months, etc.) are carried out on time and recorded in detail; the scenario, participants, duration, deficiencies found and corrections are written down. Writing "done" is not enough; the inspector questions quality and realism. Familiarization records for newly joined personnel must also be ready.
SOLAS gereği en az 8 saatlik yakıt kapas: Under SOLAS it must hold at least 8 hours' supply of fuel. There is a water detection and alarm system with automatic sensors.
SOLAS ve klas kuruluşları gemilerde PMS: SOLAS and the classification societies make a PMS (Planned Maintenance System) mandatory on ships.
SOLAS, belirli drill'leri zorunlu frekan: SOLAS requires certain drills to be carried out at mandatory intervals: abandon ship and fire drills every month (SOLAS III/19.3.2); every week on passenger ships (SOLAS III/30.2). Personnel joining the ship are given training in the life-saving and fire-fighting appliances within two weeks at the latest (SOLAS III/19.4.1). An enclosed space entry/rescue drill is carried out at least every 2 months, lifeboat launching and maneuvering in the water at least every 3 months, and rescue boat launching monthly as far as practicable and in any case at least every 3 months (SOLAS III/19.3). The Master plans this schedule and ensures that drills are carried out realistically and not just "on paper".
SOLAS, filikaların düzenli denize indiri: SOLAS requires lifeboats to be launched regularly and their engines run; the davit brake, winch and release system are subject to periodic load tests. Abandon ship drills are held regularly; the crew know their duties and stations (muster list).
SOLAS, geminin bir çalışma dili (working: SOLAS requires the ship to establish a working language and the muster list and emergency instructions to be written in that language (and in additional languages where necessary). With a multinational crew, the Safety Officer confirms that the instructions are understood by everyone; where necessary, the language barrier is overcome with IMO standard symbols and illustrated instructions.
SOLAS, limandan ayrılmadan 12 saat içind: SOLAS requires the steering gear to be tested within 12 hours before leaving port and an emergency steering drill to be held every 3 months. The Chief Engineer ensures that these tests are carried out and recorded.
SOLAS, çeşitli tatbikatları zorunlu kıla: SOLAS makes various drills mandatory: abandon ship and fire drills (every month; and within 24 hours of leaving port if more than 25% of the crew have not taken part in drills on board that ship in the previous month), enclosed space rescue (every two months), steering gear test; pollution/SOPEP drills are required by the SOPEP and the SMS. The Safety Officer keeps the drill schedule, varies the scenarios and makes them realistic.
SOPEP (Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency: The SOPEP (Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan) locker contains absorbent pads/pillows, shovels, rags, plastic bags, dispersant (if appropriate) and warning material. Before bunkering, this material is moved close to the manifold. If a spill occurs, the plan is activated immediately: stop the source, limit the spread, collect and report (Master, terminal, port authority).
SOPEP ekipmanı (absorbentler, scupper pl: The SOPEP equipment (absorbents, scupper plugs, shovels, drums and so on) is kept quickly accessible; the notification list (coastal state, company) must be up to date.
SOPEP tatbikatları düzenli yapılır; her: SOPEP drills are carried out regularly; every crew member's role in a spill (reporting, shutting off the source, applying absorbent, rigging booms) is defined. The Chief Officer organizes the drill, identifies weaknesses and keeps records. In a real spill, speed and coordination determine the environmental and legal outcome.
SOPEP, sahil otoritesi irtibat listesini: The SOPEP contains the list of coastal State contacts and the company's emergency contacts; this list must be kept up to date. On tankers certified to carry NLS (chemical tankers), a combined SMPEP (covering Annex I + II) may be carried instead of the SOPEP.
SOx emisyonu doğrudan yakıt sülfürüne ba: SOx emissions depend directly on fuel sulfur; the global limit of 0.50% and the ECA limit of 0.10% apply (see the Fuel Management section). Ships with scrubbers use HSFO, but EGCS washwater must be kept within the pH, PAH and turbidity limits (MEPC guidelines) and monitored continuously. Some ports prohibit open-loop scrubber discharge.
SOx emisyonu sıfıra yakındır; NOx emisyo: SOx emissions are close to zero; NOx emissions can meet Tier III without additional treatment (in low-pressure gas engines). PM emissions are negligible.
SOx uyumu BDN kükürt içeriği veya scrubb: SOx compliance is demonstrated by the BDN sulfur content or by the scrubber's exhaust SO₂/CO₂ ratio monitoring data; for NOx, the engines are set in accordance with the Technical File. In ECAs, the stricter limits are applied.
SSSCL, \"ben doldurdum\" değil \"birlikt: The SSSCL works on the principle of "we verified it together", not "I filled it in". Every item is physically checked and marked with the codes A (agreement), P (permission) and R (re-check).
STCW 2010 Manila değişiklikleri, vardiya: The STCW 2010 Manila amendments explicitly require watchkeeping personnel to be "fit for duty". Section A-VIII/1 requires Administrations to establish an alcohol limit of not more than 0.05% (0.5 g/L) blood alcohol concentration (BAC) or 0.25 mg/L alcohol in the breath. Many commercial operators tighten this further, applying 0.04% (OCIMF upper limit) or 0.00% on board.
STCW A-VIII/2, gündüz ve uygun koşullard: STCW A-VIII/2 may permit the officer to keep watch as the sole lookout in daylight and in suitable conditions; however, this applies only after the situation has been fully assessed and provided that assistance is immediately available to be summoned to the bridge when needed. When visibility decreases, as night approaches, in heavy traffic or whenever any doubt arises, the officer must immediately call for an additional lookout.
STCW Bölüm A-III/1, makine vardiya mühen: STCW Section A-III/1 requires completion of a structured onboard training program in order to become an engineer officer in charge of a watch. The TRB is the evidence that this program has been implemented and assessed. The Administration (flag State) issues the candidate's certificate of competency only together with an approved TRB and valid sea service.
STCW Code A-VI/1, gemiye atanan herkesin: STCW Code A-VI/1 requires everyone assigned to a ship to complete basic safety familiarization before taking up duties: mustering in an emergency, recognizing the alarm signals, the location and donning of lifejackets, how to raise the alarm, and knowing the escape routes. This is the maritime world's "life-saving on day one" training.
STCW Kod A-VIII/2, vardiya zabitinin (OO: STCW Code A-VIII/2 states clearly that the officer of the watch (OOW), as the Master's representative, is primarily responsible for the safe navigation of the ship. The officer remains solely responsible for the watch until the Master comes to the bridge and formally takes over the con; the Master's presence alone does not relieve the officer of responsibility, and this handover must be made clearly and verbally and entered in the deck logbook.
STCW Manila değişiklikleri ile resmileşe: The ETO certificate (A-III/6), formalized by the STCW Manila amendments, brings together electrical, electronic and control engineering competences. The ETO is responsible for the operation, monitoring and maintenance of power generation systems, for automation and control systems, for the technical maintenance of navigation/communication electronics and for the ship's security/IT systems.
STCW Manila değişiklikleri, ECDIS'i prim: The Manila amendments to STCW require officers on ships using ECDIS as the primary means of navigation to have completed generic ECDIS training (IMO Model Course 1.27); in addition, the ISM Code (6.3) and STCW Regulation I/14 require type-specific familiarization with the particular ECDIS model on board. The Second Officer verifies that an officer newly joining the ship has completed both and personally carries out the type-specific familiarization.
STCW Reg. I/14, şirketleri gemiye atanan: STCW Reg. I/14 holds companies responsible for ensuring that the certificates of seafarers assigned to the ship are valid and appropriate to their duties, that records complying with STCW are kept on board, and that familiarisation and emergency coordination are provided. The extension of this responsibility on board is the Master; the company sets the policy, the Master applies it on site and reports deviations.
STCW Table A-III/1 ve A-III/2 kapsamında: Under STCW Tables A-III/1 and A-III/2, engineer officers must demonstrate the following ERM competences:
STCW ayrıca alkol ve uyuşturucu kötüye k: STCW also considers the prevention of alcohol and drug abuse together with fatigue management under the heading of fitness for duty. A typical rule for alcohol before a watch is a window of at least 4 hours of abstinence before the start of the watch; but under dry ship policies this is not even a matter of discussion, because alcohol is prohibited on board.
STCW dinlenme saatleri (her 24 saatte mi: STCW rest hours (min. 10 hours in any 24-hour period, min. 77 hours in any 7-day period) directly affect lookout effectiveness; a tired lookout is a hazard. If the AB feels too tired to perform their duty, they are obliged to inform the OOW.
STCW sertifikası asgari standardı belgel: An STCW certificate documents the minimum standard; but two officers with the same certificate can show very different competence in practice. From the first watches the Master observes each officer's real level: discipline in fixing the position, application of COLREG, command of the equipment, speed of decision-making and behaviour under pressure. This observation builds a real competence profile of each officer.
STCW sertifikası bir zabitin generic (ge: An STCW certificate documents an officer's generic competence; however, every ship has a different make of ECDIS, a different radar/ARPA interface and a different bridge layout. For this reason, STCW Regulation I/14 and ISM Code Section 6 require seafarers to receive ship-specific familiarization before taking up their duties. The Second Officer carries out the navigational equipment part of this familiarization and records it.
STCW ve ISM gereği, gemiye yeni katılan: Under STCW and the ISM, everyone newly joining the ship — whether a seafarer, a riding crew member or a contractor — goes through a basic safety familiarisation before starting work: he or she learns the muster station, the alarm signals, where the lifejacket and immersion suit are and how to put them on, the escape routes, the watertight doors and the basic "dos and don'ts". This familiarisation must be completed before the ship berths or before the first critical moments of the voyage.
STCW ve MLC 2006, mürettebatın asgari di: STCW and MLC 2006 regulate the minimum hours of rest for the crew: at least 10 hours of rest in any 24 hours and at least 77 hours in any 7 days; rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours uninterrupted. The Bosun does not plan work in a way that would breach the team's work/rest hours records.
STCW'ye göre ECDIS kullanan zabit gerekl: Under STCW, an officer using ECDIS must have the required generic ECDIS competence. On joining a ship, familiarisation with that maker and model, the menu logic, alarms, route transfer, sensor selection and the back-up is required under the ISM/SMS. In any case it should not be written as if a separate, uniform international certificate called a "type-specific certificate" were mandatory; flag and company requirements are checked separately.
STCW, OOW (Engine) için belirli bir asga: STCW prescribes a minimum period of approved seagoing service for OOW (Engine) (within a structured training program accepted by the Administration). Knowing the target period, the cadet plans voyages and tracks the time still outstanding; before applying for the examination, the cadet makes sure the period has been completed.
STCW, gelen mühendisin vardiyayı devralm: STCW requires the relieving engineer to be fully informed about the condition of the equipment, operations in progress and potential hazards before taking over the watch. If the relieving engineer feels physically or mentally unfit for duty, the watch is not taken over. By observing this, the cadet internalizes the professional discipline of this standard.
STCW, yeterlilik belgesi için \"qualifyi: STCW defines "qualifying seagoing service" for certificates of competency. This covers periods when the ship is actually at sea on voyages and the candidate serves in a position relevant to the duties. Time waiting in port, in the shipyard (lay-up) and periods without duties are generally not counted at the same rate; the rules of the flag Administration determine this distinction.
STCW, zabit yeterliliği için belirli sür: STCW requires a specified period of approved seagoing service for officer certification. The Sea Service Certificate is the official proof of this period. However good the training and the TRB may be, undocumented sea service delays or prevents entitlement to certification.
STCW/MLC; her 24 saatte en az 10 saat ve: STCW and the MLC require at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period and at least 77 hours in any 7-day period. Rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours without interruption, and the interval between consecutive periods of rest must not exceed 14 hours. The Master sees to it that these limits are not breached.
STP biyolojik/kimyasal arıtma ile çıkış: The STP brings the effluent up to the required standards by biological and chemical treatment; discharge complies with the distance and area rules. Discharge is restricted in special areas.
STS operasyonu onaylı bir STS plan ve ri: An STS operation is carried out under an approved STS plan and risk assessment. The POAC takes on overall advisory control; the Masters of the two ships keep responsibility for their own ships. Weather and sea limits and abort criteria are defined in advance.
STS transferde Birinci Zabit, OCIMF/ISGO: In STS transfers, the Chief Officer supervises the arrangement of the primary (Yokohama) fenders and secondary fenders in accordance with the OCIMF/ISGOTT STS guide. The number of fenders is determined by the size of the ships and the maximum berthing speed; their positions are distributed evenly along the parallel body. The approach speed is a critical parameter and is generally kept at about 0.1–0.3 m/s.
SW tarafı en hızlı kirlenen bölümdür. St: The SW side is the part that fouls fastest. The strainers are cleaned regularly; the plates or tubes are descaled periodically with chemicals (acid) and brushed mechanically. Chlorination (MGPS — marine growth prevention system) suppresses marine growth.
SWL (Safe Working Load) veya WLL (Workin: SWL (Safe Working Load) or WLL (Working Load Limit) is the maximum load that a piece of equipment can lift safely, and it is marked/labeled on the equipment. This value is obtained by dividing the breaking load of the equipment by a safety factor (usually 4:1, 5:1, or 7:1 for textile slings). The SWL is never exceeded.
SWL (Safe Working Load), vincin emniyetl: The SWL (Safe Working Load) is the maximum load the crane can lift safely. But the SWL is not fixed: as the radius increases, the overturning moment increases and the load that can be lifted decreases. The load moment (M = load × radius) cannot exceed the crane's design moment.
Saat değişim planı yazılı hazırlanır ve: The clock change plan is prepared in writing and submitted to the Master for approval. The plan states clearly the amount of change for each day (e.g. +30 min × 2 watches), on which night and over which watches it will be distributed, the ZD of the new ship's time relative to UTC, and when it will be announced to the crew.
Saat değişim planı, gemi saatinin varış: The clock change plan is calculated backwards so that, at the end of the voyage, ship's time matches the legal time of the arrival port exactly. The Second Officer establishes the standard time of the arrival port (including DST), finds the total difference from the current ship's time and divides it over the remaining days of the voyage. In this way, when the ship arrives in port, the crew's body clock is close to port time and the ETA and operation times are consistent.
Saat değişimi bu limitleri doğrudan etki: Clock changes directly affect these limits, because rest hours are calculated not on the basis of "actual elapsed time" but from records kept in ship's time. When the clocks are advanced on an eastbound passage and the 24-hour window is effectively reduced to 23 hours, it becomes harder for a crew member to complete 10 hours of rest in that window. The Second Officer must anticipate this squeeze in the plan and distribute the change so that the rest periods are protected.
Saat değişimi yönetimi, denizci dinlenme: Managing clock changes is a task that looks simple but has a high margin for error, because it affects seafarers' rest, record integrity and operational timing at the same time. The Second Officer's job is not just to put the clocks forward or back; it is to run a disciplined process that protects the MLC 2006 rest limits and does not break the continuity of the navigational record, by keeping the UTC reference fixed, distributing the change fairly and documenting every change consistently. A well-planned clock change both reduces fatigue-related errors by the crew and presents a flawless chain of records in PSC inspections and company audits.
Saat değişimi, mürettebatın en az etkile: So that the crew is affected as little as possible, the clock change is usually split between the night watches (00:00–04:00 and 04:00–08:00). A common practice is to divide a one-hour change into two half-hours over two night watches; for example, half an hour in the 00–04 watch and half an hour in the 04–08 watch. In this way no single watchkeeper carries the whole burden, and the rest periods are preserved in a more balanced way.
Saat değişimi, onaylandıktan sonra tüm g: Once approved, the clock change must be announced to the whole ship; otherwise confusion arises on the bridge, in the engine room and in the catering department. The common practice is to announce the direction, amount and time of the change with a "Notice to Crew" on the previous day or on the morning of the change. The notice is posted in the mess room and on the notice boards, and is also entered in the bridge night order book.
Saat geri alındığında (retard) aynı saat: When the clocks are retarded, the same hour is passed through twice, so a note such as "2nd time" is made against the second pass, or the UTC equivalent is written, to avoid confusion in the log entries. When the clocks are advanced, no blank line is left for the skipped hour; the entries continue without a break and the line of the change is clearly marked.
Saat geri alındığında, geri alınan saat: When the clocks are retarded, the hour that is put back is lived twice; for example, if ship's time is put back from 03:00 to 02:00, the period 02:00–03:00 is passed through twice. This must be stated clearly in the deck logbook, and a note made for the second pass, so that events in the repeated hour are not confused. The Second Officer usually distributes the gained hour among the night watches to improve rest.
Saat ileri alındığında, ileri atlanan sa: When the clocks are advanced, the skipped hour is not actually "lived"; for example, if ship's time is put forward from 02:00 to 03:00, the period 02:00–03:00 is lost for that day. The Second Officer arranges the watch schedule and the rest periods accordingly; the advanced hour must not be applied in a way that shortens the watch concerned by one hour or squeezes a crew member's rest period.
Saat-bazlı joblar running hours counter': Hour-based jobs are linked to the running hours counter; for example, the main engine fuel injector overhaul is triggered at 8,000 running hours. Calendar-based jobs are linked to dates (e.g. annual liferaft service). The Chief Engineer checks that running hours are entered correctly; a counter error shifts the whole chain.
Saatlik/vardiya bazlı parametreler engin: Hourly/per-watch parameters are entered in the engine room logbook and the electronic recording system: main engine load/rpm, exhaust temperatures, cooling values, generator loads, tank levels, bunkers/daily consumption and any events. Records must be legible, true and made on time; false/backdated entries are a serious disciplinary offense.
Sabit basınçta gazın ısıtılması veya soğ: Heating or cooling a gas at constant pressure is an isobaric process. In this process volume and temperature change together. Charles's law applies.
Sabit donanımın muayenesi; kaynak bölgel: Inspection of the fixed fittings covers checks for cracks, corrosion and deformation at the welds, greasing of the roller bearings and smoothing of sharpened surfaces. The SWL markings must be legible.
Sabit hacimde W = 0 olduğundan, birinci: At constant volume W = 0, so the first law becomes Q = ΔU. All the heat supplied to the system becomes internal energy.
Sabit hacimde iş yapılamaz (W = 0) çünkü: No work can be done at constant volume (W = 0), because work = P·ΔV and ΔV = 0. All the heat supplied becomes a change in internal energy: Q = ΔU = m·cv·ΔT.
Sabit hatveli pervaneli gemilerde motor: On ships with a fixed pitch propeller the engine is stopped, then turned in the astern direction with starting air and run astern.
Sabit kerteriz / azalan mesafe (constant: A constant bearing with decreasing range (CBDR) is the classic indicator of risk of collision. If, while watching a ship, the AB notices that the bearing is not changing, they must report it; the OOW confirms this information with a radar plot and decides on the maneuver.
Sabit saat-bazlı bakım her zaman optimum: Fixed hour-based maintenance is not always optimal; needlessly replacing a bearing in good condition creates both cost and a risk of failure (assembly errors). A modern PMS uses condition monitoring data (vibration, oil analysis, thermography, performance trends) as a job trigger. The Chief Engineer decides, with class and manufacturer approval, which equipment is suitable for CBM.
Sabit söndürme sonrası en az 24 saat mak: After a fixed system release, the engine room is kept closed for at least 24 hours. The atmosphere is tested before entry. The damage is assessed and a root cause analysis is carried out.
Sabit taşlama tezgahında (bench grinder): On a bench grinder, the gap between the tool rest and the wheel is kept at ≤3 mm; otherwise the workpiece can jam in the gap. Work is done on the front face of the wheel, not on its side; a workpiece that overheats is cooled. A face shield and goggles are mandatory.
Saf bakır: Yüksek elektrik ve ısıl iletk: Pure copper: high electrical and thermal conductivity. Electric cables, heat exchanger tubes.
Safe Working Load (SWL), onaylı yük diya: The Safe Working Load (SWL) is the upper limit permitted for the boom angle/radius and working arrangement in the approved load diagram; the weights of the hook block, spreader and loose gear are taken into account.
Safety Committee ve near-miss yönetimi,: The Safety Committee and near-miss management only work when they are kept up continuously. By making sure that meetings are regular, minutes are true and actions get closed, the Third Officer keeps the safety culture alive; a committee that becomes a "formality" loses its value.

The Safety Committee and near-miss management are the pulse of the ship's safety culture. The open reporting, serious root-cause analysis and closed actions that the Third Officer keeps alive turn today's small warnings into tomorrow's prevented accidents.
Safety Management System (SMS), geminin: The Safety Management System (SMS) is the set of procedures established to conduct all of the ship's operations safely and in compliance with regulations. The cadet learns that the SMS is not "a binder sitting on a shelf" but the framework of daily work, and understands that every procedure was born from the lesson of an accident.
Safety Officer ayrıca salın throw-over e: The Safety Officer also checks that there is a clear working area from which the raft can be thrown over, that the lashings can be released freely and that the hydrostatic release unit (HRU) is connected correctly. Painted lashings or a cradle seized with rust prevent the raft from floating free in a real emergency — a common and deadly defect.
Safety Officer rolü, gemideki emniyet kü: The Safety Officer role is the pulse of the safety culture on board. Here the Chief Officer does not just keep records; the Chief Officer is the person who makes hazards visible, encourages reporting and closes the gaps in the system. A strong safety culture saves more lives than the best single piece of "equipment".
Safety Officer veya atanan gözlemci, mus: The Safety Officer or an appointed observer measures the muster time, how well equipment is donned and how the reporting chain works. Typical target: the whole crew mustered and the head count completed within the set time (usually a few minutes, depending on the ship).
Safety Officer'ın LSA yönetimindeki başa: The Safety Officer's success in LSA management remains invisible as long as no abandon ship situation occurs; but in a real abandonment, the lives of the crew depend on exactly this disciplined, recorded and date-tracked routine. Saying "the equipment is in place" is only the beginning; being able to say "it works, it is accessible, it is valid and it is documented" means the task is complete.
Safety Officer'ın acil durum rolü, emniy: The Safety Officer's emergency role is a natural extension of managing the safety equipment: being the person who uses that equipment and leads the team in a crisis. Clear awareness of roles, priority on team safety and realistic drills ensure that this critical duty saves lives in a real emergency.
Safety Officer'ın altın kuralı LSA bölüm: The Safety Officer's golden rule is the same as for LSA: what is not done is not recorded, and what is not recorded is considered not done. However, "filling in" records without holding a real drill (paper drill) is both an ISM violation and a deception that can be fatal in a real emergency. The record must reflect reality.
Safety Officer, alarm testini emergency: The Safety Officer also verifies the alarm test via the emergency switchboard; it is checked that the alarm is fed from the battery when the main power is cut. The test is recorded with the date and result.
Safety Officer, aylık olarak tüm tarihli: Every month, the Safety Officer updates all dated items (pyrotechnics, EPIRB/SART batteries, HRUs, liferaft service, immersion suit seam test, SCBA hydro-test, lifejacket lights) in a single expiry table. For upcoming dates (e.g. 3 months in advance), a resupply/service request is raised, so that no item suddenly becomes invalid.
Safety Officer, bu servislerin geçerlili: The Safety Officer tracks the validity dates of these services and plans them to fit the survey window. The service report (certificate) is kept on board; PSC and class surveyors ask for these certificates. For free-fall lifeboats, a free-fall launch or the simulated launching alternative (MSC.1/Circ.1206) is carried out at intervals of not more than 6 months.
Safety Officer, debrief'te ortaya çıkan: The Safety Officer turns equipment defects found in the debrief into work orders, procedural gaps into training/familiarization, and individual skill gaps into targeted coaching. The scenario of the next drill can target the weakest point of this drill.
Safety Officer, denetim öncesi müretteba: Before an inspection, the Safety Officer holds short rehearsals with the crew; new joiners in particular are reminded of their muster station, lifejacket donning and their own emergency duties. This prevents the picture of "good records but unprepared people".
Safety Officer, denetleyici değil kolayl: The Safety Officer is a facilitator, not an inspector. The role is to make hazards visible, encourage reporting, follow up actions and make safety performance measurable. The basic aim is to build a "just culture" instead of a blame culture; otherwise reporting stops and risks are hidden.
Safety Officer, emniyet ekipmanını yönet: Because the Safety Officer is the person who manages the safety equipment, they are a natural on-scene leader in an emergency. According to the station bill, they take on roles such as leading the fire team and coordinating life-saving. This is a role that "directs the response", not one that "keeps records".
Safety Officer, geminin SMS'i ve SOLAS g: Based on the ship's SMS and SOLAS requirements, the Safety Officer sets up a test matrix: which equipment, at what interval, by whom and in which record. Weekly tests are usually done together on a set day (e.g. every Monday); monthly tests are completed before the end of the month. The matrix is approved by the Master and followed up on the bridge.
Safety Officer, geminin SOLAS Record of: The Safety Officer compares the LSA list in the ship's SOLAS Record of Equipment (Form E/C) item by item with the physical inventory. There must be no difference between the quantity stated in the document (e.g. lifeboats of 100% + 100% capacity, 25% additional liferafts, one immersion suit per person) and the actual number on board.
Safety Officer, geminin fire control pla: The Safety Officer must know the ship's fire control plan by heart (under SOLAS II-2/15.2.4, it is kept on the bridge, at the entrances to the engine room and the bottle room + in an enclosure outside) and must know the location of every fire station, fixed system, detection zone, fire damper and ventilation stop. The FFE inventory is verified by comparing it with the Record of Equipment (Form E).
Safety Officer, general alarm sisteminin: The Safety Officer periodically tests that the general alarm system can be heard at a sufficient decibel level at all points (cabins, corridors, engine room, open deck). In high-noise areas such as the engine room, a visual (flashing) alarm must be provided in addition to the audible alarm.
Safety Officer, her tüpün dolu (tartı/ma: The Safety Officer checks that each extinguisher is full (weighing/pressure gauge), sealed (safety pin + tamper seal), accessible and of the correct class, and that its expiry/service date is valid. The extinguisher bracket must be sound, and the content pressure must be in the green band.
Safety Officer, near-miss raporlamasını: The Safety Officer encourages near-miss reporting and never punishes the person who reports. On the contrary, low reporting does not mean "everything is fine"; it means "problems are being hidden". The aim is the combination of high near-miss reporting and few actual accidents.
Safety Officer, periyodik olarak en uzak: The Safety Officer periodically verifies that the fire main pressure is sufficient by taking jets simultaneously from the two most remote hydrants. The emergency fire pump is isolated and tested separately. These tests are recorded in the logbook with the pressure value and date.
Safety Officer, personel değişiminde mus: The Safety Officer updates the muster list immediately at a crew change; the duty of a person who leaves must not remain unassigned. Every new crew member learns their muster station, the location of their lifejacket and their escape route through familiarization before being assigned shipboard duties; on-board training in the ship's life-saving and firefighting appliances is given within 2 weeks at the latest.
Safety Officer, tüm pyrotechnics'in expi: The Safety Officer keeps an expiry list of all pyrotechnics and obtains new stock before they expire. Expired pyrotechnics are not thrown away carelessly; they are disposed of properly (port facility or authorized disposal). These items are stored in easily accessible watertight boxes, protected from moisture.
Safety Officer, yolcu gemilerinde yolcul: On passenger ships, the Safety Officer also coordinates the muster procedure for passengers (on voyages where passengers are scheduled to be on board for more than 24 hours, a muster of newly embarked passengers prior to or immediately upon departure). On cargo ships, the focus is crew familiarization; the checklist is signed and kept as the familiarization record.
Safety Officer; filika içi inventory'i (: The Safety Officer checks the lifeboat inventory (sea anchor, paddles, hatchet, first-aid kit, rations, water, fishing kit, signaling mirror, whistle, bailer) against the MSC/Circ.1047 list. Missing or expired items (e.g. water tablets, rations) are listed and a resupply request is raised.
Safety Officer; her EEBD'nin mühürünün (: The Safety Officer checks that the seal of each EEBD is intact, the pressure gauge is in the green band, the expiry date is valid and the device is visible/accessible on the escape route. An EEBD with a broken seal is regarded as tested and is sent for servicing.
Safety Officer; light battery expiry'ler: The Safety Officer checks the expiry of the light batteries, the expiry of the smoke signals, the condition of the lines and that the bracket holding the lifebuoy can be released freely. MOB lifebuoys must be releasable from the bridge wing with a single action; the bracket must not be seized with rust.
Safety committee, Kaptan başkanlığında,: The safety committee, chaired by the Master, meets regularly (usually monthly) with representatives of all departments (officers, engine, deck ratings, catering). The Chief Officer prepares the agenda: status of previous actions, near-misses/accidents during the period, drill results, PSC/vetting findings and suggestions from the crew.
Safety contour (emniyet konturu), gemini: The safety contour is the safe depth limit for the ship's draft; the ECDIS highlights this contour and gives an alarm if it is crossed. The safety depth and the shallow and deep contour settings determine the colour coding. The guard zone / look-ahead warns in advance if there is a safety contour or a dangerous object ahead.
Safety contour, safety depth ve alarm ay: Correct configuration of the safety contour, safety depth and alarm settings is critical for safe navigation. The ECDIS software version and the ENC Presentation Library must also be up to date; an old version may display some new symbols incorrectly.
Safety depth, spot sounding'lerin vurgul: The safety depth is the threshold at which spot soundings are highlighted; it is not an alarm limit on its own. If there is no contour equal to the user value, the next deeper contour available in the ENC is selected as the safety contour; it is used as the boundary between safe and unsafe water and feeds the crossing/approach warning logic.
Safety familiarization, gemiye yeni katı: Safety familiarization is an investment made in the first few hours after a person joins the ship, but its effect lasts throughout the voyage. A well-conducted familiarization turns a person who "does not know the ship" into someone who "knows what to do" in a real emergency. Signing the record is the start; the job is done when the new crew member can don their lifejacket, walk to their station and recognize the alarm.
Safety housekeeping, emniyetin en somut: Safety housekeeping is safety in its most concrete, everyday form: keeping the front of the equipment clear, the routes free and the doors in the right position. The Third Officer's constant rounds and "fix it immediately" discipline ensure that, in a real emergency, every second and every item of equipment can save lives.
Safety housekeeping, sadece denetim önce: Safety housekeeping is not a clean-up done before an inspection but a daily habit. The Third Officer spreads awareness of "putting things back in their place" and "not blocking the way" throughout the team. Lasting safety is the sum of these small, correct daily actions.
Safety observation (BBS — Behaviour Base: Safety observation (BBS — Behavior-Based Safety) cards record safe and unsafe behavior as it happens. The Safety Officer collects the cards, carries out trend analysis (e.g. repeated PPE deficiencies, slip risk in the same area) and plans targeted interventions.
Safety settings şirket UKC politikası ve: The safety settings are derived from the company UKC policy and the Master-approved passage plan. Squat, heel/list, wave response/density allowance, the required UKC and the height of tide are added to the static draft with a clear sign convention; the single draft field in the ECDIS does not do this calculation on its own.
Safety valve (emniyet supabı), kazan bas: The safety valve limits the boiler pressure; it opens at excessive pressure and releases steam. The cadet learns the set pressure of the safety valve and the requirement for periodic testing. The pressure gauge, water level controller and flame failure device are also part of boiler safety.
Sagging (orta çökme) ve hogging (orta ka: Sagging and hogging create cyclic stresses in the hull and lead to fatigue cracks in the long term. The limits must be observed in port just as at sea; partly loaded intermediate conditions in particular may be overlooked.
Sahada bir sapma görülürse (ekipman arız: If a deviation is seen on deck (equipment failure, inadequate lashing, unexpected water ingress, stevedore error), the Bosun informs the Chief Officer immediately. The Bosun is the eyes and ears on deck; if the reporting chain breaks, the safety of the operation is weakened.
Sailing Directions (Pilot Books), List o: Publications such as Sailing Directions (Pilot Books), List of Lights and List of Radio Signals are updated through the "Updates to Admiralty Sailing Directions / Lists" sections of the weekly NtM. These updates are entered on the relevant pages of the publication or kept as an attached sheet (supplement).
Saldırı durumunda mürettebatın korunaklı: In the event of an attack, the crew are planned to withdraw to a protected area (the citadel); the citadel is kept ready with communications, water and food. UKMTO/MSCHOA and the naval units concerned are informed; the SSAS (Ship Security Alert System) is activated when necessary. The safety of the crew always comes before the ship and the cargo.
Salgın döneminde veya izolasyon alanı te: During an outbreak or when cleaning an isolation area, the steward uses suitable PPE (gloves, mask) and also protects their own health. Contaminated waste is collected separately. The steward's health is important for continuity of service.
Salinometer ile tuzluluk izlenir; eşik a: Salinity is monitored with the salinometer; if the limit is exceeded, the dump valve operates. Production is stopped in port and coastal waters because of contamination.
Salinometer ile tuzluluk izlenir; kıyı/l: Salinity is monitored with the salinometer; production is stopped near the coast and in port because of contamination. The water is disinfected.
Salinometer ile tuzluluk izlenir; limand: Salinity is monitored with the salinometer; production is stopped in port and near the coast because of contamination. The water is disinfected.
Salinometre (tuzluluk ölçer) üretilen su: The salinometer checks the quality of the water produced continuously. If the salinity rises above 10 ppm, the water is automatically returned to the sea.
Sample 4 şişeye paylaştırılır: gemide sa: The sample is divided into 4 bottles: one retained on board as the ship's sample, one sent to a laboratory such as FOBAS/VPS, a supplier copy and the MARPOL sample (kept on board for at least 12 months for PSC). Until the lab report arrives (CCAI, density, viscosity, water content, sulfur, vanadium, aluminum + silicon, sediment; ignition risk if CCAI > 870), the fuel is not used; if it is urgently needed, its use at risk despite the quality doubt is recorded.
Santrifüj (dinamik) pompalar, çark (impe: Centrifugal (dynamic) pumps give the liquid velocity with an impeller and convert it into pressure; they are ideal for high flow, low to medium pressure and low viscosity (seawater, ballast, fire). Positive displacement (PD) pumps move a fixed volume per revolution; they suit high viscosity and high pressure (fuel, oil, hydraulics).
Santrifüj kargo pompaları: ham petrol ve: Centrifugal cargo pumps: work at 1500–6000 m³/h on crude oil and product tankers; they are in the pump room and driven by steam or electric motors.
Santrifüj kargo pompası, tank seviyesi d: As the tank level falls, a centrifugal cargo pump cavitates because of insufficient suction (low NPSH); with volatile cargoes, gas can also collect in the pump (gas binding/vapour lock) and cut off the flow. The rate is then reduced, stripping mode is used or the pump is primed again.
Santrifüj kuvvet, ağır partikülleri dışa: Centrifugal force throws the heavy particles outwards. The disc stack increases the separating surface. The bowl rotates at 6000–9000 rpm.
Santrifüj pompa kendiliğinden emiş yapam: A centrifugal pump cannot prime itself; it needs priming (filling with water) or a self-priming device. Pumps connected in parallel increase the flow; connected in series they increase the head. Standby pumps can cut in automatically.
Santrifüj pompa overhaul'unda; coupling: In a centrifugal pump overhaul, the coupling is removed, the casing is opened and the impeller, wear ring, mechanical seal and bearings are checked. The cadet learns the function of each part: the impeller creates the flow, the wear ring limits internal leakage and the mechanical seal prevents leakage along the shaft.
Santrifüj pompalarda (deniz suyu, balast: Maintenance of centrifugal pumps (sea water, ballast, fire, general service) covers checking impeller wear, wear ring clearance, shaft condition, bearings and the gland packing/mechanical seal. When the wear ring clearance increases, pump efficiency falls and recirculation increases; the clearance is compared with the manufacturer's limit.
Santrifüj pompanın debisi (Q) arttıkça b: As the flow (Q) of a centrifugal pump increases, its head (H) falls (the H-Q curve). The operating point is where the pump curve crosses the system resistance curve. Throttling a valve increases the system resistance and reduces the flow; if the pump runs against a closed valve (shut-off), it heats up.
