Excessive icing is a cause of capsizing in fishing vessels and small ships.
Soğuk hava deposunda (chiller, hedef 0-4: In the cold room (chiller, target 0-4°C), a strict vertical hierarchy is applied to prevent cross-contamination: cooked/ready-to-eat products on the top shelf, raw fish in the middle, raw meat and poultry on the bottom shelf (the greatest drip risk lowest). No raw product is placed where it can drip onto a ready-to-eat product below it. Vegetables/fruit are kept in a separate compartment.
Soğuk iklimlerde yakıt ısıtma, yaşam mah: In cold climates fuel heating, accommodation heating and fresh water production benefit from cogeneration.
Soğuk sularda dalış elbisesi (immersion: In cold water, the immersion suit extends survival time by delaying hypothermia; SOLAS requires an immersion suit for every crew member under certain conditions. The AB must be able to don the suit quickly (usually with a target of 1-2 minutes) and check that the zipper and face seal are watertight. Donning time is measured during drills.
Soğuk sularda düşen kişide hipotermi dak: In cold water, hypothermia sets in within minutes for a person who has fallen in; fast rescue is vital. The AB knows by heart what to do if someone falls overboard and confirms the location of the MOB equipment before starting work. Overside work at night requires additional lighting and stricter precautions.
Soğuk zincir kaybı gıda kaynaklı salgın: A break in the cold chain increases the risk of food-borne outbreaks (norovirus and others).
Soğuk zincir, ürün gemiye teslim edildiğ: The cold chain means keeping a product cold without interruption from the moment it is delivered to the ship until the moment it is consumed. During provisioning, the cook measures the delivery temperature of chilled/frozen products and rejects any product showing signs of thawing (softening, water, signs of refreezing). Products received are placed in the appropriate store without delay; they are not left standing in the heat on the quay.
Soğutma COP'u, evaporatörde alınan ısını: The refrigeration COP is the ratio of the heat absorbed in the evaporator to the work done by the compressor. The heat pump COP is the ratio of the heat rejected in the condenser to the compressor work.
Soğutma COP'u, evaporatördeki ısı alımın: The refrigeration COP is the ratio of the heat absorbed in the evaporator to the work input of the compressor.
Soğutma kompresörleri ve refrigerant sis: The refrigeration compressors and the refrigerant system are maintained; store room temperatures are monitored continuously and kept on alarm. The hygiene and defrost programme is applied.
Soğutma kompresörü motoru, sistemin en y: The refrigeration compressor motor is the largest electrical load in the system. The ETO monitors the motor current (balance of the three phases), voltage and operating temperature; unbalanced current indicates a phase problem or a mechanical problem. In hermetic/semi-hermetic compressors the motor is cooled by the refrigerant gas, so a low charge can overheat the motor.
Soğutma ortamı: Tatlı su veya deniz suyu: Cooling medium: fresh water or seawater.
Soğutma serpantini yüzey sıcaklığı çiy n: When the surface temperature of the cooling coil is brought below the dew point, the moisture in the air condenses. This method is called cooling dehumidification.
Soğutma sistemi genleşme tankı (expansio: The level of the cooling system expansion tank is monitored; a continuous drop means a leak in the cooling circuit. Sight glasses — particularly those on the oil return lines — are used to check the oil flow and its color; foamy or cloudy oil indicates water contamination.
Soğutma sistemine eklenen makyaj suyu (m: Make-up water added to the cooling system must be low in chloride (usually distilled/evaporator water); otherwise every addition brings in chloride/hardness. The Second Engineer monitors the make-up water source and the expansion tank level.
Soğutma sistemleri, yüksek/düşük sıcaklı: Refrigeration systems are fitted with high/low temperature, pressure and compressor failure alarms; these alarms are relayed to the bridge/control room. The ETO verifies (by testing) that the alarm circuits and sensors work correctly, that the alarm setpoints are appropriate and that the alarm actually gets through. A silenced or bypassed alarm can lead to loss of cargo/food.
Soğutma sonrası oluşan kondens otomatik: The condensate formed after cooling is drained by an automatic drain valve.
Soğutma suyu analizi ve dozajlama, İkinc: Cooling water analysis and dosing is a discipline through which the Second Engineer protects the internal health of the engine "out of sight". Correct water chemistry, early leak detection and trend monitoring prevent liner/cover corrosion and secure a long service life for the main engine and the generators.
Soğutma suyu kanalları özellikle egzoz v: The cooling water passages are concentrated especially around the exhaust valve. Insufficient cooling leads to thermal cracks.
Soğutma suyu, yağlama yağı ve yaşam alan: It is used for measuring the temperatures of cooling water, lubricating oil and the accommodation.
Soğutma ve iklimlendirme bakımı, gıda gü: Refrigeration and air conditioning maintenance has a wide impact, from food safety to cargo value and crew comfort. The ETO's success with these systems is measured by reliable compressor operation, alarms that genuinely protect, refrigerant leaks managed with legal discipline and energy that is not wasted. Thanks to the ETO's careful maintenance, these unseen but continuously running cycles quietly keep the ship cool.
Soğutma ve klima sistemleri \"görünmez\": Refrigeration and air-conditioning systems go unnoticed while they work "invisibly"; when they fail, food, comfort or cargo is suddenly at risk. The Third/Fourth Engineer's regular, recorded checks ensure the reliability of these silent systems.
Soğutma çevrimi: kompresör soğutucu gazı: The refrigeration cycle: the compressor compresses the refrigerant gas (hot, high pressure), the condenser (seawater- or air-cooled) rejects the heat and liquefies the gas, the expansion valve lowers the pressure, and the evaporator (inside the store) draws heat from the store as the refrigerant evaporates at low pressure. Modern systems use environmentally friendly (low-GWP) refrigerants.
Soğutma çevriminde performans metriği CO: In the refrigeration cycle the performance metric is defined as COP_refrigeration = QL/Wnet. In a heat pump the aim is heating, and COP_heat pump = QH/Wnet.
Cooling unit: a chiller or a DX system. It uses chilled water or the refrigerant directly.
Soğutucu (0-4°C) ve dondurucunun (-18°C: Keeping the chiller (0-4°C) and the freezer (-18°C and below) running continuously at their target temperatures is the basis of food safety. The cook regularly checks the door seal (airtightness), visible dirt on the condenser/evaporator, the defrost condition and the temperature indicator. Dust/grease build-up on the condenser grille reduces cooling and strains the compressor; it is cleaned at user level.
Soğutucu akışkanlar (refrigerant) çevre: Refrigerants are subject to environmental regulations. The Montreal Protocol has phased out ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs/HCFCs, while the F-gas Regulation and the Kigali Amendment are reducing HFCs with a high global warming potential. As a legal requirement, the ETO keeps track of the refrigerant types on board, the leak records and that charging is carried out by licensed persons.
Soğutulmuş havanın yoğunluğu artar → sil: The density of the cooled air increases → more air enters the cylinder → more fuel can be burned → engine power increases.
Spade (asma) dümen: Alt tarafta yatak yo: Spade rudder: there is no bearing at the bottom; the stock carries its weight. High manoeuvrability.
Special Area'larda (Akdeniz, Baltık, Kar: In Special Areas (Mediterranean, Baltic, Black Sea, Red Sea, Gulfs area, North Sea, Antarctic, etc.) the discharge rules are much stricter; generally only comminuted food waste is permitted, and only under certain conditions. In polar waters (Polar Code) the rules are stricter still. The Chief Officer applies the correct rule for the area the ship is in; discharge in the wrong area is a serious violation.
Special Area'larda ve liman bölgelerinde: In Special Areas and port areas, sewage discharge is subject to strict restrictions; most ports require the use of a holding tank and delivery ashore. Greywater is also regulated separately in some regions (e.g. Alaska, polar waters).
Special survey'de surveyor, belirli sili: At a special survey, the surveyor may ask for certain cylinders, pistons, bearings and exhaust valves to be opened up and examined. The Chief Engineer plans the opening-up work, takes the measurements (liner wear, ring gap, bearing clearance) and compares them with the class acceptance criteria.
Speed log; doppler (su/zemin referanslı): A speed log may be of the Doppler (water/ground referenced), electromagnetic (EM) or pitometer type. A Doppler log gives dual-axis ground/water speed; an EM log measures speed through the water. Each type is affected by current, shallow water, fouling and transducer alignment.
Spektrometrik analiz (ASTM D5185/D6595),: Spectrometric analysis (ASTM D5185/D6595) measures metals at ppm level. Fe indicates ring/liner/crank wear; copper (Cu), bearings/cooler tubes; chromium (Cr), rings/valves; aluminum (Al), pistons/bearings; lead-tin (Pb/Sn), wear of bearing surfaces.
Spill sonrası temizlik atığı (oily waste: Cleanup waste from a spill (oily waste, contaminated absorbent) is stored separately as hazardous waste and delivered to a suitable reception facility; it is never thrown into the sea. The event is reported to the company in a near-miss/accident report and a root cause analysis is carried out.
Split drum vinçlerde tambur iki bölmelid: On split drum winches the drum has two sections: the working (tension) section and the storage section. Only one layer of rope carries tension in the working section; this prevents the brake holding capacity from falling with the rope diameter and the number of layers. On an undivided drum, the brake holding capacity decreases as the rope is wound in layers on top of each other.
Spring line: Gemiden rıhtıma boylamasına: Spring line: a line leading from the ship to the quay in a fore-and-aft direction. The fore spring (leading aft from forward) prevents the ship from moving ahead, and the aft spring (leading forward from aft) prevents it from moving astern.
Sprinkler başlığındaki cam ampul belirli: The glass bulb in a sprinkler head bursts at a set temperature (generally 68 °C) and releases the water.
Sprinkler bölgeleri (sections) köprü/yan: The sprinkler sections are monitored separately on the bridge or fire control panel; which section has been triggered is seen immediately. Flow switches and pressure sensors help to locate the fire.
Sprinkler sistemi sürekli basınçlı su il: The sprinkler system is filled with water under continuous pressure (wet pipe). Each sprinkler head has a glass bulb that breaks with heat or a fusible link; only the heads in the area of the fire open and spray water, and the pressure drop triggers the pump and the alarm. In this way water is applied only where it is needed.
Squat, geminin hareket halinde sular alt: Squat is the ship sinking deeper and changing trim when underway, because of the drop in pressure it creates beneath it. Squat increases in proportion to the square of speed and becomes significant particularly in shallow water and in narrow channels (blockage factor). The cadet learns the empirical squat formulae (e.g. the Barrass formula) and their relationship with the block coefficient (Cb).
Squat, hızın karesiyle yaklaşık orantılı: Squat increases approximately with the square of the speed; therefore halving the speed reduces squat to about one quarter. Squat is much more severe in narrow channels with a high blockage factor. The Second Officer sets the planned speed in critical UKC areas accordingly.
Stabilite sorunları (sludge oluşumu), uy: Stability problems (sludge formation), a risk of incompatibility and unexpected combustion behaviour may be seen. A compatibility test before bunkering is recommended.
Stabilite ve trim kontrolü, Birinci Zabi: Stability and trim control is the Chief Officer's least forgiving responsibility: errors do not appear instantly but build up step by step, and usually become visible only at the worst moment. Written verification, cross-checks and regulatory knowledge at every stage are the ship's only real line of defense.
Stabilite ve yük hesabına eğitim katılım: Taking part in stability and cargo calculations for training is the critical area in which the deck cadet begins to understand the physics of the ship. Seeing the concepts of GM, trim, free surface and strength in practice prepares the cadet to become an officer who will make safe loading decisions in the future.
Stacking cone: container'ları üst üste h: Stacking cone: a passive fitting that aligns containers on top of each other.
Cadet training may be completed on more than one ship. Although the ship record pages are completed separately for each ship, the evidence of competence accumulates in a single book. When changing ships, the cadet should plan to close on the new ship a gap left on the previous one; for example, if the tanker fuel system was not learned on the previous ship, priority is given to this opportunity on the new ship.
Stajyer \"5S\" benzeri bir düzen disipli: The cadet learns a "5S"-type housekeeping discipline: put back what you use, segregate waste, leave the area clean. Good maintenance work shows itself when, on completion, the area is cleaner than before the work started.
Stajyer ORB'yi imzalama yetkisine sahip: The cadet is not authorized to sign the ORB; this authority rests with the responsible engineer. However, the cadet learns the recording logic and internalizes the legal weight of this book, which one day will bear the cadet's own signature. Honesty in the ORB is part of the honor of the engineering profession.
Stajyer ayrıca \"neden bu işten önce tan: The cadet also learns the answer to the question "why was the tank made gas-free before this job?" In the past, many tankers and other ships have exploded, with loss of life, as a result of hot work carried out with inadequate preparation. Every step of the procedure is the lesson of a death.
Stajyer ayrıca grup LOTO mantığını öğren: The cadet also learns the logic of group LOTO: if more than one person is working on the same equipment, everyone fits their own lock and removes it when their work is finished. The equipment cannot be energized until the last lock is removed. This ensures that nobody is "forgotten" and left in danger.
Stajyer ayrıca katıldığı her bakımı TRB': The cadet also enters every maintenance job taken part in under the "maintenance and repair" competence area of the TRB and has it signed by the training engineer. In this way, the practical skills acquired become part of the official record.
Stajyer ayrıca periyodik stok sayımının: The cadet also learns why periodic stocktaking is carried out: the physical stock and the system record must agree. A discrepancy shows either that the records have not been updated or that a part has been used without being recorded. Disciplined recording is the only way to a reliable inventory.
Stajyer ayrıca yasal ve fiziksel kısıtla: The cadet also helps to assess legal and physical constraints: TSS (Traffic Separation Schemes), ECA (Emission Control Areas), VTS reporting lines, military/fishing areas, depth restrictions and compulsory pilotage in canals/straits. This information is compiled in the appraisal stage and incorporated into the route in the planning stage.
Stajyer eğitimi, görevleri yapma fırsatı: Cadet training cannot happen without giving the cadet the opportunity to carry out tasks. Following the principle of supervised responsibility, the Second Officer gives the cadet progressively greater tasks: first taking fixes and keeping the logbook, then radar plotting, ECDIS route monitoring and, in suitable conditions, supervised watchkeeping practice. Each task is assessed according to the level achieved, and feedback is given.
Stajyer her tatbikattan sonra kendine so: After every drill, the cadet should ask: "Did I know my duty? Did I use the equipment correctly? What could I have done faster/more safely?" This self-assessment and the post-drill debrief determine performance in a real emergency.
Stajyer her transferde \"kaynaktan hedef: In every transfer, the cadet learns to build the complete line-up "from source to destination" mentally: which valve is open, which pump is running, which tank is filling. This discipline is the basic skill that will prevent wrong-transfer errors later, as an independent engineer.
Stajyer için acil sistem testleri çok de: For the cadet, emergency system tests are very valuable learning opportunities: scenarios not seen in normal operation (loss of power, automatic cut-in) are observed under controlled conditions. The cadet enters every test in the TRB and discusses the observations with the training engineer.
Stajyer için en katı kural budur: hiçbir: This is the strictest rule for the cadet: under no circumstances is an enclosed space entered without a permit, without testing and without supervision. Thoughts such as "I'll just take a quick look" or "I'm only going to get my tool" are fatal. Most enclosed space fatalities are people who went in "just for a moment".
Stajyer köprüüstüne çıktığında ilk yapma: When the cadet comes onto the bridge, the first thing to do is to tell the OOW why they are there and make clear whether they are present as an "extra lookout" or for "training". When navigating in darkness, the cadet follows the red lighting rules and "lookout" discipline so as not to impair the OOW's night vision. Following the taking-over and handing-over (handover) process from start to finish is the basis for the cadet learning the watchkeeping culture.
Stajyer, \"monte ettik bitti\" değil \"t: The cadet learns the discipline not of "we assembled it, job done" but of "we tested it, verified it and recorded it". A small leak noticed on first start can be corrected without dismantling the equipment again; an error that is missed later turns into a major failure.
Stajyer, \"stop work authority\" (işi du: The cadet learns the concept of "stop work authority": every person on board can stop a job they consider unsafe and cannot be penalized for doing so. The cadet too must not hesitate to speak up on noticing a hazard; this is not weakness but professionalism.
Stajyer, \"vessels in sight of one anoth: The cadet understands that the rules for "vessels in sight of one another" (Part B Section II) and for "restricted visibility" (Rule 19) are different. In restricted visibility there is no stand-on/give-way distinction; every ship proceeds at a safe speed and takes action to avoid collision based on radar plotting. The cadet also learns the rules for narrow channels (Rule 9) and traffic separation schemes (Rule 10) and the priorities of vessels restricted in their ability to maneuver/not under command (Rule 18).
Stajyer, \"yaklaşık\" değil \"ölçülen\": The cadet learns to work with "measured" rather than "approximate" values. In using the micrometer, feeler gauge and dial gauge, the cadet gains awareness of correct reading, parallax error, temperature effects and calibration. Precise measurement is the basic language of engineering.
Stajyer, A, B ve D tipi mesajların (seyi: The cadet learns that message types A, B and D (navigational warnings, meteorological warnings, SAR) can never be disabled on the receiver; these messages are safety-critical. Reviewing incoming messages and reflecting the relevant ones in the plan or on the chart (for example, a temporary obstruction, a wreck or a drill area) is one of the routines the cadet supports.
Stajyer, AIS hedef bilgisinin radar hede: The cadet observes how AIS target information is associated with the radar target (AIS-radar association) and how the OOW cross-checks these two sources. The benefits and risks of communicating by VHF with a ship whose maneuvering intentions are unclear (the VHF-assisted collision trap) are also discussed at this stage.
Stajyer, ARPA'nın bir karar verici değil: The cadet must understand that ARPA is not a decision-maker but a decision-support tool. ARPA can lose track of a target (target swap), may not fully acquire small craft and may give delayed data on targets maneuvering in narrow waters. ARPA data is therefore always cross-checked by visual observation and conventional radar plotting.
Stajyer, Birinci Zabit gözetiminde loadi: Under the Chief Officer's supervision, the cadet works through simple scenarios on the loading computer/stability software: entering tank/hold loads and reading the GM/trim/draft and strength output. The cadet learns to read values such as displacement, TPC and MCT from the hydrostatic tables; understanding "what the software calculates" is critical.
Stajyer, COLREG'in en çok uygulanan kura: The cadet observes the most frequently applied COLREG rules in real encounters and learns that in a head-on situation (Rule 14) both ships must alter course to starboard, and which ship is the "stand-on" ship (not the one that gives way, but the one that keeps her course) and which is the "give-way" ship in crossing (Rule 15) and overtaking (Rule 13) situations. The cadet sees in practice why the principle that action must be early, readily apparent and sufficient (Rule 8) matters: small and late maneuvers may not be noticed by the other ship.
Stajyer, ECDIS üzerinde overscale (harit: The cadet understands the meaning of the overscale (zooming in on a chart beyond its own scale) and underscale warnings in ECDIS. Information displayed when overscaled can be misleading; the ENC of the appropriate scale (closest to the compilation scale) must therefore always be used. This awareness is an important part of checking the plan.
Stajyer, ECDIS'in tek başına yeterli olm: The cadet internalizes that ECDIS alone is not sufficient and that the position must be verified from independent sources (visual bearings, radar ranges, a second GNSS). Timely application of ECDIS updates (ENC updates) and checking the accuracy of the sensor inputs (GPS, gyro, log) are also among the daily routines the cadet must observe.
Stajyer, ENC (Electronic Navigational Ch: The cadet learns the difference between ENCs (Electronic Navigational Charts) and raster charts, the importance of scale selection (overscale/underscale warnings) and how to use the "chart 1" symbol library. Together with the OOW, the cadet follows how the route planning, route check and route monitoring modes work on ECDIS.
Stajyer, IALA buoyage sistemindeki A ve: The cadet understands the basic difference between IALA buoyage Regions A and B (the red/green sides of lateral marks are reversed). Memorizing the meanings and light characteristics of lateral, cardinal, isolated danger, safe water and special marks is a basic competence for both planning and watchkeeping.
Stajyer, INT/Admiralty harita sembolleri: The cadet learns to use "Chart 5011 — Symbols and Abbreviations Used on Admiralty Charts", which explains INT/Admiralty chart symbols. Depth figures, the low-water line (drying heights, underlined figures), wrecks (wreck symbols and the dangerous/non-dangerous distinction), rocks, buoys (IALA buoyage Regions A/B), light characteristics and danger symbols are learned from this publication.
Stajyer, OEM çizimlerini bakım işiyle bi: The cadet learns to use OEM drawings together with the maintenance job: which part is dismantled in which order, which gasket goes where, which clearance is measured. These drawings also contain spare part codes; these codes are critical for ordering the correct part in the PMS.
Stajyer, ORB formatını okumayı ve her ka: The cadet learns to read the ORB format and what each type of entry means: why and how a bilge transfer is recorded, where sludge was sent, how separator sludge was managed. The ORB is one of the documents most frequently examined in PSC inspections; entries must be consistent with the actual tank levels and with machinery operation.
Stajyer, STCW A-III/1 yeterlilik kazanma: The cadet is a trainee engineer working towards STCW A-III/1 competence; however, legal responsibility for the watch always rests with the EOOW on duty. Under no circumstances may the cadet independently start/stop machinery, switch valves, close breakers or reset alarms. Before every action, the cadet states the intention to the EOOW, obtains approval and carries out the action under supervision.
Stajyer, TRB'sini Sea Service süresiyle: The cadet should progress the TRB in parallel with the Sea Service period. If the evidence of competence is incomplete when the period runs out, even additional sea service will not secure the right to sit the examination. For this reason, the TRB gap analysis (see the TRB management section) is carried out together with sea service planning.
Stajyer, TRB'yi sınav dosyasının çekirde: The cadet should see the TRB as the core of the examination file. In the Administration's review, the answer to "how many months did you spend at sea?" is in the Sea Service record, and the answer to "what did you learn and what is your evidence?" is in the TRB. The two complement each other.
Stajyer, VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) ve S: The cadet learns that the VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) and S-VDR continuously record bridge audio, the radar/ECDIS display, helm/engine orders and sensor data. After an incident, the VDR data must be preserved (save/preserve button). Consistency between the manual logbook and the electronic records is key to the legal protection of the ship and crew.
Stajyer, acil sistem testlerine gözlemci: The cadet attends emergency system tests as an observer; the cadet does not start the system or intervene independently, but carefully follows the test procedure, the system's response and the success criteria. With each test, the cadet reinforces the answer to the question "when, why and how does this system cut in?"
Stajyer, acil sistemlerin bakımına gözet: By taking part in the maintenance of emergency systems under supervision, the cadet both gets to know the system and grasps the question "why is this maintenance critical": a poorly maintained emergency system runs the risk of not working in a real emergency, which is even more dangerous than not having the system at all (a false sense of safety). An emergency system kept ready is the ship's insurance.
Stajyer, alınan ve işlenen seyir uyarıla: The cadet observes that navigational warnings received and acted on are recorded. Relevant warnings are noted in the passage plan and plotted on the appropriate chart, and expired warnings are filed. This discipline keeps planning synchronized with the real-time flow of information.
Stajyer, ana makinenin temel parametrele: The cadet learns the main engine's key parameters and their normal ranges: the exhaust gas temperature of each cylinder (cylinder exhaust deviation), scavenge air pressure, turbocharger RPM, jacket cooling water inlet/outlet, piston cooling oil outlet, LO inlet pressure/temp and fuel oil viscosity/temp. These values are interrelated; the trend is interpreted, not a single value.
Stajyer, açık deniz geçişleri için \"gre: For ocean passages, the cadet learns the difference between "great circle" and "rhumb line" tracks; over long distances the great circle is shorter, but it requires a course alteration on each segment. Ocean Passages for the World and climatological routeing charts give information on seasonal winds, currents, ice limits and tropical storm areas; the cadet learns to read them.
Stajyer, bağlama düzeninin (mooring patt: The cadet learns how the mooring pattern is planned: head/stern lines, springs and breast lines have different functions. A well-balanced mooring prevents the ship from ranging along the berth and from moving under the effect of waves/current/wind. Equal tension in all mooring lines (load sharing) is important for load distribution.
Stajyer, bağlama istasyonundan gözlem ya: When observing from the mooring station, the cadet sees line handling, winch operation and the snap-back hazard at close quarters. The cadet understands the importance of communication between the bridge and the station. The rules on safe positioning and PPE apply here too.
Stajyer, başvuru öncesi idarenin güncel: Before applying, the cadet should obtain the Administration's current list of requirements and check every item. Requirements may be updated over time (such as the STCW Manila amendments); relying on old information leads to an incomplete application. Early planning prevents last-minute gaps.
Stajyer, belge sürecini \"sınav zamanı h: The cadet should regard the document process not as "a job to be dealt with at examination time" but as "a natural part of every period at sea". When each period is closed out properly, applying for the examination is simply a matter of bringing together documents that are already prepared.
Stajyer, bir P&ID'yi okuyup sahada doğru: By reading a P&ID and verifying it on site (finding on site the valve seen on the drawing), the cadet brings the two worlds together. This skill is the basis of valve alignment, fault isolation and operation planning.
Stajyer, bir bakım işi için doğru parçay: The cadet learns to find the correct part for a maintenance job in the PMS, to match the part code with the drawing/manual and to deduct the part used from the inventory. Although this discipline may look like "shelf keeping", it is the basis of the ship's operational continuity: an incorrect record leads to a part not being found at a critical moment.
Stajyer, bir permit formunun nasıl doldu: The cadet learns how a permit form is completed, which questions are asked and which approvals are required. The cadet understands that a permit is not just a piece of paper; each line represents a concrete precaution. The line "Has the atmosphere been tested?" is the guarantee of a life.
Stajyer, blackout recovery tatbikatını v: The cadet treats a blackout recovery drill, or observing a real one, as a major learning opportunity: prioritization of the power system, paralleling of generators, the role of starting air and team communication are displayed intensively within a few minutes. The cadet follows each step, notes questions and discusses them with the training engineer.
Stajyer, blackout recovery'de emergency: The cadet learns the role of the emergency air compressor in blackout recovery: there must be enough starting air to start the main engine. Keeping the air bottle pressure at a set level and keeping the emergency compressor in working order are prerequisites for recovery after a blackout. The test verifies the compressor's ability to build up pressure.
Stajyer, blackout recovery'yi gözlemleye: By observing blackout recovery, the cadet learns the prioritization of the power system: first the emergency switchboard, then the main generators, then heavy loads. A blackout during maneuvering or in confined waters creates a risk of collision/grounding, so the speed of recovery is critical.
Stajyer, boya ve solventlerin tehlikeli: The cadet learns that paints and solvents are hazardous substances, that they are stored in accordance with the MSDS/SDS information and that they are not used in an enclosed space without ventilation. The cadet understands that used paint, solvents and rags are managed as special waste under MARPOL Annex V.
Stajyer, bu belgelerin tutarlı olmasına: The cadet must make sure that these documents are consistent: the sign-on/sign-off dates in the seafarer's book, the SEA periods and the periods in the Sea Service certificate must match. Inconsistencies are questioned in an Administration/inspection review and undermine the validity of the documents.
Stajyer, bu tank zincirinin neden bu sır: The cadet learns why this tank chain is arranged in this order: the settling time allows water/sediment to separate, the separator removes the remaining impurities and the service tank holds the final clean reserve. If the settling tank water drain is not done regularly, water reaches the engine and combustion/injection problems arise.
Stajyer, charted depth'in chart datum'a: The cadet understands that charted depth is given relative to chart datum (usually LAT — Lowest Astronomical Tide) and that the height of tide at the time must be added to obtain the actual depth of water. The height of tide is found from the Tide Tables and, for intermediate times, by the "rule of twelfths" or algebraic interpolation. The cadet learns to do this calculation in practice.
Stajyer, cylinder oil feed rate'in (g/kW: The cadet learns why the cylinder oil feed rate (g/kWh) is adjusted according to fuel sulfur: insufficient lubrication causes liner wear and scuffing, while excessive lubrication causes deposits and cost. Scrape-down oil analysis is one way of monitoring cylinder condition. This balance is fundamental to engine life.
Stajyer, demirleme için gereken zincir m: The cadet learns that the amount of cable needed for anchoring is determined by the depth of water, the type of seabed, wind and current; a typical starting rule is to pay out 4-6 times the depth of water in cable, but this varies with conditions. Monitoring the anchor's holding and detecting dragging is done through coordination between the bridge and the forward station.
Stajyer, ekipmanların hidrolik/elektrik/: The cadet learns the hydraulic/electric/pneumatic power sources of the equipment and its emergency stop points. Noticing and reporting signs such as unusual noise, leaks or overheating in a piece of equipment becomes a habit.
Stajyer, elektrik işlerinin yetkili elek: The cadet learns that electrical work is done under the supervision of authorized electrical personnel (ETO/Electro-Technical Officer or an authorized engineer) and that high-voltage (HV) systems require special procedures. The cadet does not intervene in electrical systems independently.
Stajyer, emergency steering tatbikatını: The cadet observes the emergency steering drill: how control is transferred from the bridge to the steering gear room, how local control is carried out, how communication is maintained. SOLAS requires emergency steering drills to be held regularly; when a real steering failure occurs, the team must already have rehearsed.
Stajyer, emniyet prosedürlerine gözetiml: The cadet takes part in safety procedures under supervision: applies LOTO, reads the PTW form, observes atmosphere testing. However, under no circumstances does the cadet independently remove an isolation, enter an enclosed space without a permit or start hot work. Every safety-critical operation is carried out with the approval and under the supervision of an authorized person.
Stajyer, farklı gemilerdeki Sea Service: The cadet must make sure that the dates of the Sea Service certificates from different ships do not overlap; service on two different ships on the same date cannot be shown. In addition, Sea Service dates must be consistent with the seafarer's book entries and the TRB task dates. This three-way consistency is the basis of the reliability of the document file.
Stajyer, gece köprüüstü vardiyalarında d: During night bridge watches, the cadet learns to determine the type, size and aspect (angle of approach) of other ships by reading their lights (Part C): sidelights (red port, green starboard), forward/aft masthead lights, towing/pushing lights, and the special lights of fishing vessels, pilot vessels and vessels restricted in their ability to maneuver. Day shapes (ball, cone, cylinder, diamond) and sound signals in restricted visibility and maneuvering signals are also learned in practice.
Stajyer, gemi değişikliklerinde (yeni ge: When changing ships (transferring to a new ship), the cadet must not forget to complete familiarization again. Each ship's layout, equipment and procedures are different; familiarization from the previous ship is not automatically carried over to the new one.
Stajyer, gemi tipine göre yük operasyonl: The cadet observes cargo operations according to ship type: on dry cargo/bulk carriers, hatch covers and the use of cranes/grabs; on container ships, lashing/twistlocks; on tankers, the manifold, cargo hoses/arms and ISGOTT procedures. Each cargo type has its own risks and safety rules; the cadet first grasps the logic of the operation by observing.
Stajyer, gemi vinçlerinin (derrick/crane: The cadet learns the SWL (Safe Working Load) limits of the ship's derricks/cranes and the periodic inspection and certification of slings, shackles and lifting accessories. No lifting appliance is loaded above its SWL and no one stands under a suspended load. Hand signals and communication between the signalman (banksman/signaller) and the crane operator are standardized.
Stajyer, gemide bulunan ölçüm cihazlarıy: The cadet observes how measurements are taken with the instruments on board (viscometer, density meter / hydrometer) and learns how these values are reflected in operating settings. Measurement is not an abstract laboratory task; it is a practical tool directly serving the clean and safe operation of the engine.
Stajyer, gemideki kaçış yollarını, alter: The cadet learns the escape routes, alternative exits and muster points on board. The cadet becomes familiar with finding the way in darkness/smoke (low-location lighting, escape route signs). Knowing the right escape route in a fire saves lives.
Stajyer, gemiyi bir sistemler bütünü ola: The cadet learns the ship as a set of systems: the purpose of each system, its operating logic, its controls and its behavior in an emergency. This learning is based on understanding, not memorization; knowing "why" a system works the way it does makes it possible to make the right decision in a breakdown or an emergency.
Stajyer, giriş izni, sürekli haberleşme,: The cadet learns about the entry permit, continuous communication, rescue equipment (resuscitator, EEBD, winch/tripod) and the role of the attendant. One of the most dangerous scenarios is that a second person, entering without precautions to rescue a colleague who has collapsed inside, also dies; the rescue plan is therefore prepared in advance.
Stajyer, gözetimli bir bakım işinde kend: In a supervised maintenance job, the cadet learns to fit their own lock and learns the importance of zero energy verification. The attitude "we fitted the lock but did not test it" is dangerous; the proof of real isolation is attempting to start and seeing that the equipment does not run (try-to-start).
Stajyer, gözetimli olarak iş emri okumay: Under supervision, the cadet learns to read a work order and to find the relevant procedure and required parts in the PMS. When taking part in a maintenance job, the cadet opens the relevant work order, follows the procedure and observes how the close-out record is made at the end of the job. This is where drawing-reading and PMS skills come together with maintenance.
Stajyer, gözlemlediği manevraları ve öğr: The cadet records the maneuvers observed and the data learned in the TRB and reviews them with the training officer. This record both reinforces learning and provides evidence of competence.
Stajyer, güverte ekipmanlarını sistemati: The cadet learns the deck equipment systematically: mooring winches/anchor windlasses, winches/cranes, hatch cover hydraulics, the deck connections of the steering gear, watertight doors, freeing ports and the deck drainage system. Learning each item's working principle, check points and signs of failure is the basis for troubleshooting later as an officer.
Stajyer, güverte işlerinin hava ve deniz: The cadet learns that deck work depends on the weather and sea state: in heavy weather, overside work and work at height are stopped, and when there is a risk of seas being shipped on deck, personnel do not go out on the open deck. Closing hatch covers and ventilators before heavy weather (battening down) is critical for the ship's watertight integrity. The cadet observes how the work plan changes in line with the weather report and the Master's instructions.
Stajyer, güverte operasyonlarına bağımsı: The cadet takes part in deck operations not as an independent crew member but under supervision, for support and training. Before every job, the officer in charge or the Bosun gives a job briefing (toolbox talk); in this briefing the cadet learns their role, the stop points and the emergency exit. The cadet never carries out an order they do not understand; when in doubt, they ask.
Stajyer, halat verilirken eldeki gerginl: The cadet learns to control the tension on the line in hand while a line is being sent ashore, and to distinguish between the commands "make fast" and "let go". Throughout the operation, it is ensured that no one on deck stands between the bitts and the fairlead or under a line. Adequate lighting and visibility are provided for night operations.
Stajyer, hava tahmini kaynaklarını (NAVT: The cadet learns to follow weather forecast sources (NAVTEX weather bulletins, weather routing service, GMDSS MSI) and to reflect seasonal hazards (tropical cyclone season, ice limits, fog areas) in the plan. Currents and tides determine the timing of transits, especially in narrow passages and port approaches; calculating the "tidal window" is a critical skill the cadet must learn.
Stajyer, her gemiden ayrılırken eksiksiz: The cadet should regard obtaining a complete Sea Service Certificate on leaving each ship as their own responsibility. If this certificate is forgotten or obtained incomplete in the rush of signing off, it can be very difficult to obtain later; the ship may have gone to another port, or the Master may have changed. The attitude "I'll get it later" is a serious risk.
Stajyer, her gemiden döndüğünde belgeler: On returning from each ship, the cadet immediately adds the documents to their personal file and updates the service record sheet. Documents are kept in chronological order together with their digital backups. This discipline allows the file to be prepared within minutes when applying for the examination.
Stajyer, her imza turunu bir geri bildir: The cadet should turn every signing round into a feedback opportunity: "In which competence am I weak, what should I focus on next month?" These questions turn the TRB from a passive record into an active development tool and strengthen the mentoring relationship with the trainer.
Stajyer, her vardiya veya bakım işi sonr: After each watch or maintenance job, the cadet takes a few minutes to record the task: which system, which operation, observations, tools used, safety points observed. This discipline both feeds the TRB and serves as the cadet's own learning journal.
Stajyer, her vardiyadan önce Kaptan'ın S: Before each watch, the cadet must read the Master's Standing Orders and the Night Order Book. These documents contain critical instructions such as the minimum passing distance (CPA), when the Master is to be called and under what conditions the engine is to be put on standby. The cadet confirms having read these orders by signing them and observes how the OOW makes decisions within the framework of these orders.
Stajyer, hot work sırasında genellikle f: During hot work, the cadet is usually present as fire watch support or as an observer. The cadet learns how critical the fire watch is: a small spark can start a fire even minutes later. The cadet must know the location, type and use of the extinguisher.
Stajyer, iki belgenin tarihlerinin tutar: The cadet must make sure that the dates in the two documents are consistent: the task dates in the TRB must match the periods on board documented in the Sea Service record. Inconsistent dates are questioned during review and undermine the validity of the documents.
Stajyer, iş emri kapanış kaydının kalite: The cadet learns the importance of the quality of the work order close-out record: writing "done" is not enough; measured values, replaced parts and observations must be recorded. A good close-out record tells the next engineer the real condition of the equipment.
Stajyer, kaldırma kayıtlarının (Register: The cadet observes that lifting records (Register of Lifting Appliances) and test certificates are kept and that equipment is tracked with color-coded inspection marks. A damaged sling or shackle is taken out of service immediately and tagged out.
Stajyer, katıldığı her tatbikatı ve öğre: The cadet records every drill attended and every skill learned in the TRB and has it approved by the training officer. This record both reinforces learning and provides evidence of competence.
Stajyer, kayıtların gerçek zamanlı, okun: The cadet learns that entries must be made in real time, legibly and in permanent ink, and that corrections are made by striking through (never by erasing or scribbling out). False or subsequently altered entries have serious disciplinary and legal consequences. This discipline is the foundation of the cadet's credibility as a seafarer.
Stajyer, kağıt ve elektronik harita düze: The cadet learns that paper and electronic chart correction records (Chart Correction Log — NP133A or its electronic equivalent) are kept meticulously. This record is the official proof of the NtM up to which each chart is corrected and is frequently checked during inspections.
Stajyer, kendi katıldığı işlerin permit': The cadet should read the permit for the jobs they take part in and ask themselves "what is the risk in this job and how are we protected?" This habit forms the basis of the risk awareness of the responsible engineer who will sign permits in the future.
Stajyer, kişisel koruyucu donanımı (PPE): The cadet wears full personal protective equipment (PPE): safety helmet, steel-toecap safety boots, gloves, safety glasses and, where necessary, a lifejacket/safety harness. For overside work and work at height, a safety harness and a lifeline are mandatory. Behavior that could distract attention during the task is avoided; a moment's inattention during a deck operation can cause serious injury.
Stajyer, kıyı seyrinde radar ile rota iz: The cadet learns how the parallel indexing technique for monitoring the track by radar in coastal navigation, and clearing bearings/clearing ranges, are prepared in the planning stage. These auxiliary lines make it possible to notice quickly when the ship deviates from the planned track and form the basis of the monitoring stage.
Stajyer, makine dairesini fiziksel olara: By walking around the engine room, the cadet memorizes where each piece of equipment is: main engine, generator flat, boiler, purifier room, pump platform, compressors, switchboard room, steering gear room, separators and tank locations. In an emergency, reaching the right equipment quickly may be vital.
Stajyer, near-miss raporlamanın değerini: The cadet learns the value of near-miss reporting (every near-miss reported is an accident prevented) and the structure of the Safety Committee. The cadet also becomes familiar with environmental protection procedures under MARPOL, such as garbage, oil and emissions management. The cadet internalizes that protecting the sea is a duty.
Stajyer, planlama sırasında karşılaştığı: The cadet must ask the Second Officer without hesitation about any uncertainty met during planning (for example, how an NtM is to be applied to the chart, or the turning radius at a waypoint). A single wrongly applied correction or an overlooked danger can turn into a real navigational risk; the discipline of "if I am not sure, I ask" is therefore vital.
Stajyer, planın yalnızca bir kağıt çalış: The cadet learns that the plan is not merely paperwork but a "shared mental model" held by the ship's whole bridge team. The plan is the constant reference during the monitoring stage; if actual conditions invalidate the plan (weather, traffic, breakdown), the plan is revised in a controlled manner and the revision is recorded.
Stajyer, pozisyon belirlemenin (fixing): The cadet practices several methods of position fixing: the visual three-bearing fix, radar range + bearing, transits (leading lines) and dead reckoning (DR) / estimated position (EP) calculation. The cadet learns that the size of the "cocked hat" triangle formed by three bearings shows the quality of the fix; a small triangle means a good fix, while a large triangle means a source of error (gyro error, wrong identification of an object).
Stajyer, prosedürleri \"bürokrasi\" deği: The cadet should see procedures not as "bureaucracy" but as "survival tools". The thought "I will cut corners this time" is the first link in the accident chain. Experienced engineers know that following the procedure even in the most routine job is the mark of professionalism.
Stajyer, radarın temel kontrollerini OOW: Under the OOW's supervision, the cadet learns the basic radar controls: gain, sea clutter (STC), rain clutter (FTC), tuning, range scale selection and use of the EBL/VRM (Electronic Bearing Line / Variable Range Marker). The cadet sees in practice that a wrongly adjusted radar can suppress real targets or create interference. The cadet grasps the discipline of changing range: long ranges to watch the overall traffic picture and short ranges to watch close-in dangers.
Stajyer, separatör operasyonunu gözetiml: The cadet follows separator operation under supervision: feed temperature (the optimum temperature for oil/fuel improves separation), throughput, water outlet (water seal) and periodic desludging (sludge discharge). The correct temperature and throughput determine the separation efficiency; excessive throughput impairs cleaning.
Stajyer, separatörün \"normal\" çalışma: The cadet must learn the separator's "normal" running sound, vibration and appearance so as to be able to notice what is abnormal. Separator overhaul (bowl cleaning, gasket replacement) is a regular PMS job; by taking part in this maintenance, the cadet learns the internal construction. The sludge removed is managed subject to entry in the ORB.
Stajyer, seyir planının \"berth to berth: The cadet understands that the passage plan must be made "berth to berth"; planning covers not only the open sea but also the pilotage area, the anchorage, the maneuvering area and the berth. The plan is prepared allowing for the ship's draft, maneuvering characteristics, the weather forecast and ECDIS/paper chart coverage.
Stajyer, squat'ın geminin baş veya kıç t: The cadet learns that squat may be greater at the bow or at the stern (usually by the head in full-form ships with a high Cb), and that the point of minimum UKC at the shallowest point must therefore be allowed for. The most practical way to reduce squat is to reduce speed; this is a basic safety measure in shallow water transits.
Stajyer, tank/sintine/cofferdam gibi kap: The cadet learns the importance of the enclosed space entry permit and atmosphere testing (O2, LEL, H2S, CO) for enclosed spaces such as tanks, bilges and cofferdams. Unauthorized enclosed space entry is one of the deadliest types of accident at sea. Under no circumstances does the cadet enter an enclosed space without a permit and without supervision.
Stajyer, temel denizci bağlarını (bowlin: The cadet learns to make the basic seaman's knots (bowline, clove hitch, reef knot, figure-of-eight) and splices. The cadet practices how lines are made fast on bitts and cleats and led through fairleads, and how they are slacked and heaved under control at the windlass/winch warping ends (slack/heave). The cadet learns that a damaged rope (cut, crushed, internally rotten) must be taken out of service.
Stajyer, test kayıtlarının nasıl tutuldu: The cadet learns how test records are kept and enters every test/drill attended in the TRB. This supports both regulatory discipline and the TRB evidence of competence. A record is the only way to go beyond saying "the system exists" and to say "the system has been tested and works".
Stajyer, testte pompanın ne kadar sürede: In the test, the cadet observes how long the pump takes to supply pressure and observes the remote start mechanism. On most ships, the pump can be started remotely from outside the engine room; this makes it possible to respond to a fire without entering the engine room. The cadet learns where this remote start point is.
Stajyer, testte özellikle \"süre\" boyut: In the test, the cadet pays particular attention to the "time" dimension: how quickly was the generator ready to take load? Did the auto-start detect the loss of power correctly? Is the fuel tank sufficient (it is usually kept at a capacity for running for a set period)? These observations are indicators of the system's reliability in a real emergency.
Stajyer, tüm belgelerini (sea service, T: The cadet keeps all documents (sea service, TRB, training certificates, medical certificate, passport/seaman's book) in an orderly file and monitors their validity dates. This order is useful at every stage of a career and makes it possible to produce a document needed at short notice immediately.
Stajyer, waypoint'lerin güvenli yerlere: The cadet learns that waypoints must be placed in safe positions: turns are planned clear of dangers, in sufficient depth of water and to suit the ship's turning radius (turning circle / wheel-over point). The wheel-over point is the point at which the rudder must be put over and comes before the waypoint itself; it is calculated allowing for the ship's turning diameter.
Stajyer, yakıt sıcaklık ve viskozite kon: The cadet learns the direct relationship between fuel temperature/viscosity control and engine performance: fuel that is too cold/viscous atomizes poorly, and fuel that is too hot can cause problems in the injection pumps. This balance is the basis of clean and efficient combustion in the engine.
Stajyer, yük planının (cargo/stowage pla: The cadet observes how the cargo plan (cargo/stowage plan) is put into effect, the relationship between the loading sequence and stability and strength, and how the deck team communicates with the bridge/cargo control room. The cadet learns that changes in draft, list and trim are monitored continuously during loading/discharging.
Stajyer, çizim okumayı sistem tanıma ile: The cadet learns to read drawings in parallel with learning the systems: tracing on site a line seen on the drawing, and finding on the drawing a valve seen on site. This drawing-to-site matching (drawing-to-deck verification) is the basis of true engineering understanding. Memorized equipment knowledge, combined with the ability to read drawings, becomes mastery of the system.
Stajyer, çizim üzerinde planladığı izola: The cadet verifies on site the isolation planned on the drawing: the valve number on the drawing must match the label on site, the valve must actually close and LOTO must be applied. This sequence of "from drawing to plan, from plan to site, from site to verification" is the basis of safe maintenance.
Stajyer, çözme sonrası halatların temiz: The cadet learns that after unmooring, lines are recovered neatly, dried and properly stowed (coiling/faking). Maintenance to prevent wet and dirty lines from rotting is part of seamanship discipline.
Stajyer, öğrendiği her cihaz ve prosedür: The cadet should also keep personal notes on every item of equipment and every procedure learned: the make/model of the equipment, its particular settings, ship-specific procedures and problems encountered. This personal "bridge familiarisation" notebook becomes invaluable when joining the next ship and when preparing for the certificate examination.
Stajyer; ECDIS, radar/ARPA, AIS, GMDSS,: The cadet becomes familiar with bridge equipment such as ECDIS, radar/ARPA, AIS, GMDSS, the gyro/magnetic compass and the echo sounder. The capabilities and limitations of each are learned, and the cadet understands that the equipment must be used together, with cross-checking. This foundation is the key to safe watchkeeping in the future.
Stajyer; FO settling/service tank, DO ta: The cadet learns to read the levels of the FO settling/service tanks, DO tank, LO sump, fresh water tanks, cooling water expansion tank and bilge holding tank both remotely (remote level gauge) and manually (sounding pipe + tape). Manual sounding is vital when the automatic level gauge fails or when verification is needed.
Stajyer; GM (metasantr yüksekliği — başl: The cadet learns the concepts of GM (metacentric height — the measure of initial stability), trim (difference between forward and aft drafts) and list (transverse inclination). A low GM makes a "tender" ship and a high GM a "stiff" ship; both carry risks. The optimum range provides safety, comfort and cargo safety.
Stajyer; ISPS kapsamında güvenlik seviye: The cadet learns about security levels, access control, restricted areas and visitor management under ISPS. The cadet understands that security is a field distinct from, but complementary to, safety, and becomes familiar with the basics of dealing with unauthorized boarding, stowaways and threats.
Stajyer; LO inlet pressure/temperature,: The cadet learns to monitor LO inlet pressure/temperature, sump level, filter differential pressure and cooler inlet/outlet temperatures. Falling LO pressure (pump/filter/leak) is a critical alarm and triggers slow-down/shut-down; for this reason, the LO system is under constant monitoring.
Stajyer; ballast (stabilite/trim), bilge: The cadet learns the ballast (stability/trim), bilge (bilge pumping), fire main (fire water), steering gear and anchoring systems. The purpose and control of each, and its role in safety, are understood. For example, the cadet learns why it is vital to keep the fire main pressurized at all times.
Stajyer; belgeyi her sözleşme/gemi değiş: At every change of contract/ship, the cadet requests the certificate correctly, keeps it safe and documents the period in full. Discharge book/seaman's book entries also form part of this record. Correct and continuous documents ensure that no problems arise later when applying for the examination.
Stajyer; can yeleğini doğru ve hızlı giy: The cadet learns to put on a lifejacket correctly and quickly, to escape from a smoke-filled space with an EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) and to use a fire extinguisher correctly (PASS: Pull-Aim-Squeeze-Sweep). These skills are reinforced by repetition in drills.
Stajyer; demir (anchor), zincir (chain c: The cadet learns parts such as the anchor, chain cable, shackles, shackle marks, windlass, chain stopper (devil's claw/bow stopper), hawse pipe and chain locker, and the "shackle" as a unit of length (approximately 27.5 m / 15 fathoms). The length of cable is expressed as a number of shackles and is followed by paint/wire markings.
Stajyer; doğal lif halatlar, sentetik ha: The cadet learns the properties of natural fiber ropes, synthetic ropes (polypropylene, polyester, nylon, HMPE) and steel wire ropes. Each material has different stretch, floating and breaking behavior; for example, because of its high elongation, nylon snaps back dangerously when it parts, whereas HMPE has low elongation and high strength. The cadet understands how ropes are protected from sunlight, chafing, chemicals and crushing, and the need for regular inspection.
Stajyer; gemi tipine göre (bulk, tanker,: The cadet learns the basic principles of cargo operations by ship type (bulk, tanker, container, ro-ro), their effect on stability/strength and the safety precautions. Awareness of dangerous goods (IMDG/IMSBC) begins in this period. Understanding how cargo affects the ship is fundamental to becoming an officer.
Stajyer; gyro pusula ile manyetik pusula: The cadet learns the difference between the gyro compass and the magnetic compass, the concepts of gyro error and compass error (deviation + variation), and how compass error is found by azimuth/transit. Reading the speed log (speed), the echo sounder (depth of water) and the rate of turn indicator is also part of bridge awareness.
Stajyer; güverte ekipmanlarının yağlanma: The cadet learns routine maintenance such as greasing deck equipment, tightening nuts and bolts, renewing gaskets and checking drains/freeing ports. These jobs are usually defined in the Planned Maintenance System (PMS); the cadet understands that every maintenance job has a reason and an interval. The tightness of hatch covers, doors (watertight doors) and ventilator openings is critical for the ship's watertight integrity.
Stajyer; harita düzeltmelerini yapar, NA: The cadet makes chart corrections, processes NAVTEX/NtM records, drafts distance and course calculations and prepares UKC tables. However, all of this work is checked by the Second Officer and the final plan is approved by the Master. The cadet never forgets that everything they do in the planning process is the work "of a student under training, not of an independent professional".
Stajyer; mooring winch (bağlama vinci),: The cadet learns the function of equipment such as the mooring winch, the anchor windlass, the vertical warping drum, warping drums, stoppers (mooring line/chain stoppers) and roller fairleads. How many turns of the line are to be taken on the drum, rendering (controlled slipping) and use of the brake are critical skills. The cadet observes the lubrication of the equipment, brake testing and the concept of rendered brake capacity.
Stajyer; pilot boarding (kılavuz biniş),: The cadet observes each phase of the pilot boarding, approach, swing, berthing, line ashore and tug operations. The cadet notes the purpose of each phase and the team's duties in the TRB. Speed, angle and the use of tugs during the transition between phases are watched closely.
Stajyer; pilot card (geminin manevra öze: The cadet learns the contents of the pilot card (summary of the ship's maneuvering information), the maneuvering booklet and the wheelhouse poster. The cadet understands what data such as the turning circle, stopping distance and crash stop mean. These data show the "physical limits" of maneuvering.
Stajyerin en değerli öğrenme aracı, kend: The cadet's most valuable learning tool is recognizing their own plotting errors. Wrong identification of an object, parallax error, ignoring gyro error and a wrong time stamp are the most common errors. The OOW reviews the cadet's fixes and gives feedback; the cadet notes this feedback in the Training Record Book.
Stajyerin en güçlü emniyet aracı \"speak: The cadet's strongest safety tool is the right to "speak up". On seeing an unsafe situation — whatever the difference in seniority — the cadet must know to stop and report. In many accidents, a junior crew member's failure to voice a hazard they had noticed has ended in disaster.
Standart LOTO adımları: hazırlık ve bild: Standard LOTO steps: preparation and notification, stopping the equipment, isolating all energy sources, fitting locks and tags, releasing stored energy (pressure relief, capacitor discharge) and verification of zero energy (try-out: attempt to start, see that it does not run). Each worker fits their own lock; another person's lock may not be removed.
Standart bağlama paterni; head line, bre: A standard mooring pattern includes head lines, breast lines and spring lines (forward and aft). The springs restrain longitudinal movement, the breast lines restrain transverse movement and the head/stern lines provide general holding. In coordination with the bridge and the pilot, the Bosun knows which line is to be sent first; usually a spring or a breast line is sent first.
Standart bir Engine Cadet TRB; kişisel b: A standard Engine Cadet TRB consists of personal details, ship record pages (vessel record / particulars), familiarization checklists, task records, supervisor assessment pages and summary approval sections. On joining each ship, the ship's details (type, tonnage, main engine, class) are entered on the relevant page.
Standart denizcilik terminolojisi yerine: The main root cause was the use of local or habitual expressions instead of standard maritime terminology, the read-back/confirmation loop being skipped, and the common set of orders not being made clear before the manoeuvre.
Standart mooring düzeninde her halatın g: In a standard mooring arrangement, each line has a different function. The head line and stern line bring the ship in to the berth and limit movement fore and aft; breast lines lead at right angles to the berth and stop the ship's side from moving off; spring lines hold the ship against longitudinal (fore-and-aft) movement. A typical ship sends out lines distributed forward and aft in a 3+2+1 or similar combination.
Standart olmayan veya yüksek enerjili he: A written risk assessment (JSA/JHA) is made for every non-standard or high-energy job: hazard–exposure–existing barriers–additional measures. The Second Engineer adapts the generic risk assessment to the specifics of the job; a "copy-paste" risk assessment masks the real hazards. At the toolbox talk the whole team signs the risk assessment, and everyone is reminded of their right to ask questions and to say "stop" (stop-work authority).
Standartlaştırma; bir kişinin değil, eki: Standardization must become a shared habit of the whole team, not of one person. The Bosun ensures that everyone knows "where things go", so that order is kept even when a deckhand is on leave or being relieved.
Standby (attendant / gözcü), girişin dış: The standby (attendant) is the person who stays outside the entrance, maintains continuous communication with the person inside, monitors the atmosphere and the time, and raises the alarm in an emergency. It is a big mistake to think of this duty as "passive waiting"; the standby has the most active safety role in the operation. The AB must not leave the standby post, go off to another job or let their attention wander.
Standby AB ile giren kişi arasında sürek: Continuous, pre-agreed communication is established between the standby AB and the entrant: radio (intrinsically safe/non-sparking type), lifeline signals or voice confirmation. Communication is confirmed at set intervals (e.g., every 1-2 minutes); no response from the person inside is a sign of an emergency. In an explosive atmosphere, the radio must be suitably (Ex) certified.
Standby AB, içeri girmeye uygun ek perso: The standby AB does not attempt a rescue alone without additional personnel fit to enter and without SCBA; their duty is to raise the alarm and direct the rescue team. If the rescue equipment is missing or not ready, the entry is not started; this is part of the permit conditions.
Standby pompaların (yağ, soğutma suyu, y: The automatic start function of the standby pumps (lube oil, cooling water, fuel) (auto start on low pressure) is tested. It is verified that automatic generator start (blackout/load-dependent) and the auto synchronization system are ready, because during an unmanned period it is the automation that will respond to a pump or generator failure.
Standby öncesi makine ısıtılır, yakıt (g: Before standby the engine is warmed up, the fuel is changed over (to MGO if necessary), the air receivers are full and the speed limits are set. The telegraph test and bridge–engine room communication are verified.
Standing orders, kaptanın gemi süresince: The standing orders set out in writing the behaviour the Master expects from the officers of the watch throughout his or her time on board. All officers sign them. Typical content: the criteria for calling the Master, the rules for using the autopilot, when to call the helmsman, the conditions for posting an additional lookout, discipline in writing the log book, alarm management and the GMDSS test schedule.
Start denemesi limiti (genellikle 3 ardı: The start attempt limit (usually 3 consecutive attempts) and the waiting time between attempts are set on the panel. The ETO checks these setpoints and the starting air pressure (if fitted); if draining and moisture control in the compressed air system are neglected, the starting valves can stick.
Start hava kompresörleri, ana makine sta: The starting air compressors supply compressed air for starting the main engine. The Second Engineer manages valve maintenance, intercooler/aftercooler cleaning, the automatic drains and checks of the safety devices (relief valve, fusible plug). Excessive temperature and oil carry-over can create a risk of explosion in the air receivers.
Start-air receiver toplam kapasitesi, re: The total capacity of the starting air receivers is assessed against the criterion of at least 12 consecutive starts without recharging by the compressors for a reversible main engine, and at least 6 starts for a non-reversible arrangement, together with the approved piping and isolation arrangement.
Starting air hattında alev tutucu (flame: There is a flame arrester in the starting air line. A leaking starting valve can let hot combustion gases into the air line and cause an explosion.
Starting air kompresörleri ve servis hav: The delivery pressure, temperature and oil level of the starting air compressors and the service air compressor are monitored; main air receiver pressure (typically 25-30 bar) is critical for the main engine's ability to start. If the automatic drain does not work, the receivers are drained manually (accumulated water reduces the number of starts available).
Starting air yüksek basınçtır (~30 bar): Starting air is at high pressure (about 30 bar) and is stored in the air receivers; control/instrument air is at a lower pressure (about 7 bar) but must be very clean and dry; working air is for general use (cleaning, pneumatic hand tools). Starting air is usually also fed to the control and service air systems through pressure reduction.
Statement of Facts, port operasyonunun k: The Statement of Facts is the chronological record of the port operation: ship's arrival, NOR tendering and acceptance, anchoring/berthing times, start and finish of operations, gang changes, draft survey, weather delays, equipment breakdowns and all stoppages. Demurrage/laytime is calculated directly from the SoF; every event must therefore be recorded in real time and correctly.
Statik biriktiren kargolarda ölçüm/örnek: With static accumulator cargoes, the specified waiting (settling) times are observed before gauging or sampling; bonding is checked before metal equipment is lowered into a tank.
Statik form yetmez; koşullar saha boyunc: A static form is not enough; conditions change on site as the work proceeds. Dynamic risk assessment includes the performing party's "STOP WORK" authority: when a hazard is noticed, anyone can stop the job without fear of punishment. This culture is directly linked to near-miss reporting.
Stator sargılarına uygulanan üç fazlı ge: The three-phase voltage applied to the stator windings creates a rotating magnetic field. This field induces currents in the rotor conductors and the resulting force turns the rotor. The rotor always turns more slowly than the rotating field; this difference is called slip.
Stator sargılarına üç fazlı AC uygulandı: When three-phase AC is applied to the stator windings, a rotating magnetic field is produced. This field induces an EMF in the rotor conductors and produces a current. The current-carrying rotor conductors experience a force in the magnetic field and the rotor turns.
Stator sargısında indüklenen EMK etkin (: The effective (RMS) value of the EMF induced in the stator winding depends on the winding factor, frequency, magnetic flux and number of turns.
Steam trap (kondens kapanı): kondensi ay: Steam trap: separates the condensate and prevents steam from escaping.
Steering gear, gemide \"asla arıza verme: Steering gear is one of the foremost systems on board that "must never fail". The Third/Fourth Engineer's disciplined daily checks, serious conduct of the SOLAS tests and clean hydraulic oil keep this critical system running quietly but reliably.
Steering konsolundaki rate-of-turn göste: The rate-of-turn indicator on the steering console shows the ship's rate of turn (°/min); especially on large ships, the helmsman also monitors the turn with this instrument to prevent over-swinging. The rudder angle indicator confirms the rudder angle; agreement between the ordered angle and the angle on the indicator is monitored continuously.
Step-up/step-down transformer, HV switch: Maintenance of step-up/step-down transformers, HV switchgear and GIS includes insulation resistance, connection temperature (thermography), SF6 gas pressure (GIS) and protection relay tests. This work is generally done under vendor-approved procedures and training. The ETO monitors the maintenance records and the protection settings.
Stern line: Kıç taraftan rıhtıma geriye: Stern line: a line leading aft from the stern to the quay.
Stern ramp: kıç tarafta açılan, en yaygı: Stern ramp: the most common loading ramp, opening at the stern; the quarter ramp variant opens out to one side at a set angle.
Stern tube aft seal'den denize yağ sızın: Oil leakage from the stern tube aft seal to sea is marine pollution under MARPOL Annex I. If a leak is detected, the relevant records (for example the ORB and a leak report) must be kept and, where required, the authorities must be notified.
Stern tube bearing yağ sıcaklığı (geneld: Stern tube bearing oil temperature (generally <60 °C), the condition of the forward/aft seals and the oil consumption (check for water ingress) are monitored daily. If stern tube oil is found in the bilge tank, there is a seal leak; if necessary, drydocking is planned.
Stern tube iki temel tipte olabilir: oil: There are two basic types of stern tube: oil-lubricated (white metal bearing, lubricated by oil — the most common) and water-lubricated (usually a composite/synthetic bearing, lubricated by seawater). A water-lubricated system eliminates the risk of oil pollution, but bearing life and weardown management are different.
Stern tube içinde aft bearing (pervaneye: Inside the stern tube are the aft bearing (closest to the propeller, the most heavily loaded bearing) and the forward bearing; at the ends, the aft seal (sea side) and fore seal (engine room side) prevent water ingress and oil leakage.
Stern tube seal (örn. lip seal/Simplex),: The stern tube seal (e.g. lip seal/Simplex type) prevents seawater from entering and oil from escaping around the shaft. The spaces between the multiple lip rings are fed with oil. Seal wear causes oil leakage (pollution of the sea) or water ingress (bearing damage).
Stern tube yağ kaçağı görünür deniz kirl: An oil leak from the stern tube causes visible pollution of the sea and must be reported.
Stern tube yağı periyodik olarak analiz: Stern tube oil is analyzed periodically: water content (seawater ingress), white metal (Sn/Pb — aft bearing wear), Fe (shaft/liner), viscosity (contamination) and cleanliness (ISO 4406 particle count). These parameters show the condition of the bearing and seals without opening up.
Stern tube yağı sürekli olarak izlenir;: The stern tube oil is monitored continuously; water contamination leads to bearing damage. Seawater is kept out by the pressure difference from the header tank.
Stern tube: Pervane şaftının gemi gövdes: Stern tube: provides bearing support and sealing where the propeller shaft leaves the hull.
Stevedore kaynaklı hasar (hatch cover, k: Damage caused by stevedores (hatch covers, railings, paint, equipment) is common. The Bosun identifies the damage at once, photographs it and reports it to the Chief Officer; if necessary, a stevedore damage report and a Letter of Protest are issued. Damage not documented in time later becomes the responsibility of the ship/company.
Stok hareketleri, sayım sonuçları ve har: Stock movements, count results and expenditure are sent to the Master/company in a periodic report. This report provides data for budget tracking, evidence for inspections and input for planning future voyages. Regular, accurate records are the foundation of professional provisions management.
Stok kontrolü, kritik yedek parçaların m: Stock control ensures that the minimum stock level of critical spare parts is maintained. When a part is used, it is deducted from the inventory; when the level falls below the minimum, a reorder is triggered. Critical spares (for safety and the main engine) are always kept in stock; class may require them to be carried.
Stok minimuma yaklaşan kalemler için kam: For items whose stock is approaching the minimum, the steward prepares a requisition and passes it to the responsible officer (usually the Chief Officer/Master). The requisition contains the item, current stock, quantity required and urgency. Accurate forecasting prevents both shortages and unnecessary overstocking.
Stok takibi basit bir envanter listesiyl: Stock is tracked with a simple inventory list: product name, quantity on hand, rate of consumption and reorder point. By monitoring consumption, the steward forecasts how much is needed for a typical voyage and passes the resupply request to the person responsible for provisions (usually the chief cook or the Chief Officer).
Stok takibi, kâğıt envanter defteri veya: Stock is tracked with a paper inventory book or the ship's software (catering/inventory module). Every receipt is entered as an addition and every use as a withdrawal, so the quantity on hand (running balance) is always known. A regular physical count (usually monthly) reconciles the records with reality and reveals discrepancies (waste, errors).
Stok yönetimi minimum/maksimum seviye ve: Stock is managed with minimum/maximum levels and a reorder point. The ETO updates the levels by monitoring the consumption trend; the stock level of a component that fails frequently is increased. The PMS software is used to deduct used parts automatically and to trigger orders.
Stopper (chain stopper, carpenter stoppe: The stopper (chain stopper, carpenter stopper or rope stopper) holds the load while the line is transferred from the winch to the bollard. Incorrect stopper technique (e.g. a chain stopper on a synthetic line) creates a life-threatening hazard. The Chief Officer checks that the correct stopper is used on the correct line. On "self-tailing" winches, the minimum number of turns of the line on the drum must be maintained.
Storage tank ısıtması, transfer öncesi p: Storage tank heating is to obtain a pumpable viscosity before transfer. Overheating (condensation/flashpoint risk) and local overheating inside the tank (water ingress through a coil leak) are avoided.
Storage tanktan settling tanka, oradan s: Fuel transfer from storage tank to settling tank and from there to service tank is done in a planned and supervised manner. The Second Engineer verifies the transfer pump, heating and valve line-up; a valve wrongly left open can overflow a tank or unintentionally mix two different grades (commingling). During transfer the level is monitored; when it is complete, the valves are closed and the status is written in the log.
Store'un bir diğer kritik boyutu emniyet: Another critical aspect of the store is safety. Paints and solvents are flammable, some chemicals give off harmful vapors, and heavy gear (metal shackles, steel wire reels) can shift with the ship's motion and cause injury. The store is therefore not just a "storeroom" but also a controlled hazardous area.
Stored energy (akümülatör basıncı, sıkış: Stored energy (accumulator pressure, a compressed spring, hot fluid) is the hidden cause of many accidents. Work does not start until the isolation has been verified (try-out: attempt to operate).
