Yağcı, her transfer ve bertaraf işlemini: The Oiler reports every transfer and disposal operation to the engineer so that it is entered in Oil Record Book Part I with the correct codes; tank levels, transferred quantities and operation times are recorded. ORB inconsistencies are among the most frequent PSC findings and lead to detention of the ship.
Yağcı, kaldırma sırasında geri çekilme a: During the lift, the Oiler keeps a clear area to withdraw to, wears gloves and keeps their hands away from pinch points. If the ship is rolling, the load can swing freely; in bad weather/when rolling, heavy lifts are postponed or carried out with extra safety measures.
Yağcı, kapalı alanda çalışırken zaman sı: When working in an enclosed space, the Oiler knows the time limit, the escape route and the communication signals. When the gas alarm sounds or if they feel unwell, the Oiler gets out immediately, without hesitation. The enclosed space entry and rescue drills held at least every two months under SOLAS III/19 keep these skills alive.
Yağcı, kayıtları bizzat tutmasa da opera: Although the Oiler does not keep the records personally, they observe the operational data (start/finish times, quantity received, tank levels, alarm events) accurately and pass them to the engineer; these data are entered in the ORB. An ORB that is incorrect or filled in afterwards in bulk is regarded as falsification.
Yağcı, kendi muster station'ını, görev r: The Oiler knows by heart their own muster station, their role, the equipment they are to carry (e.g. nozzle, hose, SCBA) and their alternative duty (if the person originally assigned is absent). The muster list is posted on the board, but real readiness means being able to carry out one's duty without looking at the paper.
Yağcı, kullandığı ekipmanın sertifikasın: The Oiler verifies that the certificate of the equipment being used is current (date on the tag/in the register). Equipment that is out of date is not used, even if it looks sound; this is a finding both for safety and in class/PSC inspections.
Yağcı, kullandığı ve kontrol ettiği ekip: The Oiler records the condition of the equipment used and checked and the lifting operations carried out; the maintenance records must be available for the PMS and for class inspections. The decision to take equipment out of service is made without hesitation.
Yağcı, muster list'te boundary cooling g: If the Oiler is assigned to boundary cooling in the muster list, they cool the decks/bulkheads adjacent to the fire compartment with a hose; water evaporating shows that the surface is still overheated and cooling must continue. Excessive use of water is avoided so that accumulated water (free surface) does not impair stability and so that drainage remains open.
Yağcı, numune şişelerinin temiz olmasına: The Oiler helps ensure that the sample bottles are clean, correctly labeled and sealed. The sample is evidence of the fuel quality (ISO 8217 compliance, sulfur content); in an off-spec fuel claim, this sample is decisive.
Yağcı, operating water basıncını, debisi: The Oiler monitors the pressure, flow and cleanliness of the operating water and checks the operating water filter/strainer. A fault in the operating water system (low pressure, clogged nozzle) translates directly into desludge failure.
Yağcı, purifier'ın desludging (çamur atm: The Oiler monitors the purifier's desludging (sludge discharge) timing, the feed temperature (~98°C for HFO), the gravity disc (dam ring) selection and the operating water system. Detailed separator maintenance is a separate task; here the Oiler provides operational support and daily monitoring.
Yağcı, sapanı boylu boyunca elle (eldive: The Oiler checks the sling along its full length by hand (wearing gloves) and by eye; broken wires prick, and kinks can be felt by hand. If an oily rag is run along the full length of the sling, broken wires snag on the rag — a practical way of checking. The eye and the pressed ferrule area are the most critical inspection points.
Yağcı, scupper tıkaçlarının (deck scuppe: The Oiler verifies that the scupper plugs (deck scupper plugs) are fitted; these plugs prevent a possible deck spill from going into the sea. Drip trays are placed around the manifold, and absorbent material and shovels/rags are made ready. The no-smoking/no-naked-flame rule for bunkering is applied and the "B flag" (Bravo) is hoisted.
Yağcı, separatör start ve her desludge s: The Oiler watches that the water seal has been established at separator start-up and after every desludge (clean water coming from the water outlet, no fuel escaping). Water at the fuel outlet or fuel at the water outlet indicates a seal/gravity disc problem and is reported.
Yağcı, separatör çalışırken muhafazaları: While the separator is running, the Oiler does not remove guards, does not approach the rotating part and wears gloves against hot surfaces. If leaking fuel meets a hot surface, there is a fire risk; for this reason, cleanliness of the separator room and leak checks are critical.
Yağcı, sirkülasyon yağının renk, koku ve: The Oiler observes the color, smell and appearance of the circulating oil. Darkening or thickening, a burnt smell or foam are signs of water/contamination. Periodic oil samples (LO sampling) are taken and sent for laboratory analysis; viscosity, water content, TBN (Total Base Number) and metal content are evaluated.
Yağcı, toolbox meeting'te aktif rol alır: The Oiler takes an active part in the toolbox meeting and, drawing on experience, raises hazards that may have been overlooked (e.g. a hot surface on an adjacent line, difficulty of escape from a confined space). A good briefing turns the risk assessment on paper into real safety.
Yağcı, turunu rastgele değil sabit bir g: The oiler makes rounds along a fixed route, not at random, so that no equipment is missed. The general approach is systematic, from top to bottom and from forward to aft: first the upper platforms (purifier room, air compressors, boiler), then the middle platform (generators, upper part of the main engine), and finally the tank top level (lower part of the main engine, bilges, pumps, shaft bearings).
Yağcı, yakıt buharı kokusu veya gaz alar: In the event of a smell of fuel vapor or a gas alarm, the Oiler reports immediately. Gas accumulation in pump rooms and enclosed transfer areas is dangerous; entry into these spaces requires a gas test and ventilation.
Yağcı/Fitter, PTW kapsamındaki bir işe i: The Oiler/Fitter does not start a job covered by the PTW before the permit has been signed. The permit is usually issued by the responsible engineer; the person doing the work reads, understands and applies the precautions in the permit. When the job is finished, the permit is closed (sign-off); a permit is not left open without the area having been made safe.
Yağcı/Fitter, sıcak çalışma yapacağı ala: The Oiler/Fitter prepares the area where the hot work is to be done: removes combustible materials, cleans up oil/fuel leaks, checks adjacent compartments (sparks can pass through openings), sets up a fire blanket/curtain and keeps an extinguisher and a hose at hand. In a confined/enclosed space, ventilation is essential, as welding gases can accumulate.
Yağlama sisteminde full-flow filtre tüm: In the lubricating oil system, the full-flow filter filters the entire oil flow, while the bypass (partial-flow) filter keeps the oil clean by continuously passing a small portion of it through a fine filter. Auto-backwash filters discharge the dirt they have caught to the sludge side during backflushing; if the backflush frequency is increasing, oil contamination has increased.
Yağlama yağı (LO) basıncının düşmesi, ya: A drop in lubricating oil (LO) pressure means that the bearings run dry and are destroyed within minutes; this is why, on most engines, LO low pressure is linked first to an alarm and then to an automatic shutdown. The test is done by simulating the pressure switch/transmitter input or by reducing the pressure in a controlled way; it is verified that the alarm and trip setpoints trigger correctly.
Yağlama yağı analiz programı, Baş Mühend: The lubricating oil analysis program is the most powerful predictive tool that lets the Chief Engineer "see inside" the machinery without opening it up. Disciplined sampling, correct interpretation of parameters and trend tracking catch internal wear early, prevent unnecessary oil changes and optimize both equipment life and cost-effectiveness. Like a tribology specialist, the modern Chief Engineer reads the story the oil tells.
Yağlama yağı basıncı (LO pressure), maki: Lubricating oil pressure (LO pressure) is the lifeblood of the engine; low oil pressure causes bearing damage within seconds. The inlet oil pressures of the main engine and the generators are verified on every round. Fuel supply pressure (FO supply/booster pressure) affects injection quality and is monitored together with the viscosity control unit (viscotherm).
Yağlama yağı sürekli by-pass filtrasyon: Lubricating oil is continuously subjected to bypass filtration and centrifugal treatment. Oil taken from the main oil tank is cleaned by passing it through the purifier/clarifier and returns to the tank.
Yağlamalı tipte header tank seviyesi ve: On oil-lubricated stern tubes, the header tank level and the bearing temperature are monitored; a falling level points to a leak at the outboard seal. The use of an EAL (environmentally acceptable lubricant) is mandatory in some areas.
Yağlı atık, sludge, kullanılmış filtre v: Oily waste, sludge, used filters and garbage are segregated under MARPOL Annex I/V. The Second Engineer makes sure that engine room waste is taken to the proper collection points and that the delivery records are kept.
Yağlı atığın denize karışması veya yanlı: Oily waste entering the sea or being wrongly segregated means serious pollution and penalties. The cadet also learns that solvents/chemicals used for cleaning must be used in accordance with the MSDS and require proper waste management.
Yağlı operasyonlarda (yakıt ikmali, maki: During operations involving oil (bunkering, engine work), scupper plugs are fitted so that any spill does not go overboard (MARPOL). When the operation is over and any spill has been cleaned up, the plugs are removed; a plug forgotten in place causes the next rain or sea water to accumulate. The AB manages this cycle carefully.
Yağın alkalinitesi (BN), yakıttaki kükür: The alkalinity of the oil (BN) is chosen to neutralise the acid formed from the sulphur in the fuel. Using a high-BN oil after changing over to low-sulphur fuel can cause calcium deposits and piston ring and liner problems.
Yaş tip gömlek: Dış yüzey doğrudan soğut: Wet liner: the outer surface is in direct contact with the cooling water. Dry liner: it sits inside the block.
Yaşam mahalli genelde pozitif basınçta t: The accommodation is generally kept at positive pressure, so that air flows outwards through doors and openings and engine room smoke and smells and (on tankers) cargo vapour cannot get in. Sufficient fresh air changes prevent the build-up of CO₂ and smells.
Yaşam mahalli yangın kapıları kapalı (ve: Fire doors in the accommodation are kept closed (or self-closing); wedging them open allows fire and smoke to spread. The steward applies this rule while working and corrects/reports a wedged door. This common violation has fatal consequences in a real fire.
Yaşam mahalli yangınları çoğu zaman küçü: Accommodation fires often start from a small moment of carelessness — an unextinguished cigarette, an overloaded socket, an unauthorized heater — and grow rapidly. Because the steward sees these areas constantly, the steward can spot risks early. Fire safety is a natural part of the steward's daily work.
Yaşam mahalli çöpü ayrıştırılır ve MARPO: Garbage from the accommodation is separated and managed in accordance with MARPOL Annex V; food waste, plastics and other garbage are handled differently. The steward ensures that garbage is collected hygienically and delivered to the correct disposal point (incinerator/shore reception). Accumulated garbage creates both a hygiene and a pest risk.
Yaşam mahallindeki yangın kapıları (fire: Fire doors in the accommodation are kept closed; wedging them open allows fire/smoke to spread. Escape routes must be kept clear and unobstructed at all times. The steward follows these rules while working and corrects/reports violations (wedged doors, blocked routes).
Yaşam mahallinden çıkan çöp; gıda atığı: Garbage from the accommodation is separated into food waste, plastics, paper/cardboard, glass, metal and domestic waste. The steward separates this waste in accordance with the ship's approved Garbage Management Plan and the color/label-coded bin system. MARPOL Annex V strictly prohibits, in particular, the discharge of plastics into the sea; all plastics are retained on board and delivered to the port reception facility.
Yaşam mahallinin denetim standardına uyg: Keeping the accommodation up to inspection standard is a job done every day, not only on the day of a visit. By keeping the environment consistently tidy, the steward ensures that the ship is ready even for an unannounced inspection. Living conditions under the MLC are also part of this order.
Yaşam mahallinin hava kalitesi konfor ve: Air quality in the accommodation is fundamental to comfort and health. Ventilation grilles (HVAC grilles) collect dust; a clogged grille both restricts airflow and spreads dust and allergens back into the room. The steward cleans these grilles periodically and reports excessive dust/mold to the engine crew (filter replacement is usually the engine department's responsibility).
Yaşlanmış UPS bataryası, şebeke kesilinc: An aged UPS battery cannot provide the expected autonomy when the mains supply fails, and the critical load (ECDIS, IAS) drops out immediately. In addition, a wrong bypass sequence can cause loss of the load during maintenance. The ETO manages these risks through periodic capacity testing and correct bypass discipline.
Yedek parça siparişi, tedarik süresini (: Spare part orders allow for the lead time and the ship's itinerary; on long voyages, deliveries must be timed to coincide with port calls. The ETO marks critical orders as priority, checks parts on receipt (correct part, damage, certificate) and stores them under suitable conditions.
Yedek parça temini gereken aksiyonlar iç: For actions that require spare parts, the ordering process is started; if a temporary repair is needed, class approval is obtained and a permanent solution is planned.
Yedek parça ve kalibrasyon yönetimi, kri: Spare parts and calibration management is a discipline built up on quiet days, not in a crisis: when the right part is ready at the right moment, a breakdown is resolved within hours, whereas missing stock stretches the same breakdown over days. The ETO's success in this area is measured by short unplanned downtime, clean spares/calibration records at inspections and the reliability of every measurement.
Yedek parça ve malzeme yönetimi, geminin: Spare parts and materials management is an art of balance that requires protecting the ship's operational reliability and its cost-effectiveness at the same time. The Chief Engineer neither wastes capital by tying it up in excessive stock nor risks off-hire by leaving a critical part short. Systematic criticality analysis, a disciplined inventory and correctly timed supply are the technical basis of this balance.
Yedek parça veritabanının doğruluğu (mas: The accuracy of the spare parts database (master data quality) is the foundation of the whole system: wrong part numbers, missing maker information or duplicate records cause errors in both ordering and stock. The Chief Engineer and the engine team are responsible for entering the maker's spare list completely in the PMS when new equipment comes on board.
Yedek parçalar, deniz hareketine karşı e: Spare parts are stowed secured against the ship's motion (lashing/racks) and protected from moisture; heavy parts are kept on the lower shelves. The location of critical spares must be labeled and consistent with the stock records, so that no time is lost in an emergency breakdown.
Yedek parçaların OEM orijinali veya onay: It is important that spare parts are OEM originals or approved equivalents; the wrong part leads to early failure. The cadet learns to lay out dismantled parts in order (labeling them according to the assembly sequence); this eliminates the risk of errors and missing parts during reassembly.
Yedek/alternatif düzenlemeler (manuel pl: Backup/alternative arrangements (manual plotting, magnetic compass, a second position source) are kept ready. Navigation with defective equipment is carried out with additional measures that reduce the risk (reduced speed, an extra lookout).
Yedekler, makine deposu (engine store) i: Spares are labeled in the engine store with a systematic bin/rack number. Each part must match its record in the PMS (part number, manufacturer, location). A wrong location record means the part cannot be found during an emergency breakdown and leads to unnecessary duplicate orders.
Yedekli ECDIS gereksinimi için iki bağım: To meet the backup ECDIS requirement, two independent workstations must operate with separate power supplies and sensors. The ETO tests the takeover scenario: it is verified that when the main ECDIS fails, the backup takes over without problems.
Yellow/Red durumda dalış çanı geri alma: In Yellow or Red status, recovery of the diving bell and the emergency rescue plan are started in accordance with the ASOG.
Yellow/Red durumda transfer durdurulur;: In Yellow or Red status, the transfer is stopped; ESD/ERS and the disconnection sequence are carried out according to the approved terminal procedure.
Yelpaze gibi yalpalama (roll), baş-kıç v: Rolling, pitching and heaving create inertia forces on the cargo; the most critical transverse force comes from rolling. The lashing gear must withstand these forces and prevent the cargo from shifting or tipping. The force grows with acceleration × mass.
Yemek servisi, kamarotluğun mürettebatla: Meal service is the part of the steward's job in most direct contact with the crew. A hot, hygienic, varied and carefully served meal is the most valuable service there is: it eases the fatigue of long voyages, holds the team together and keeps up the ship's morale. Temperature control and hygiene discipline are the non-negotiable safety foundation of this service.
Yeni MEG4 yaklaşımı, sabit \"snap-back z: The new MEG4 approach stresses that fixed "snap-back zone" markings can be misleading, because the line changes direction around the fairlead. Instead of relying blindly on static markings, the Bosun develops the crew's awareness of the hazard as a dynamic one.
Yeni binen her ekip üyesi, görevine başl: Every newly joined crew member goes through familiarization under the ISM Code before starting duties. The Chief Engineer, or a Second Engineer designated for the task, shows the emergency escape routes, fire stations, EEBD/SCBA locations, emergency stops and quick-closing valves, and the bilge and ballast system.
Yeni gelen her personel, görevine başlam: Every new joiner is familiarized with the ship before starting duties: escape routes, alarm signals, muster station, PPE locations and the use of personal life-saving equipment. The Safety Officer keeps a record of this process; incomplete familiarization can be a ground for PSC detention.
Yeni gelen mühendis/tayfa; makine daires: Newly joined engineers/ratings are briefed on their first day on the engine room layout, emergency exits, locations of safety equipment (EEBD, fire extinguishers, emergency stops), alarm signals and basic procedures. The Second Engineer carries out this familiarization and completes the checklist.
Yeni halat tesliminde sertifika (test ce: When a new rope is delivered, its test certificate is checked and filed. Rope reels are kept in the store in a dry area, out of sunlight, away from heat sources and out of contact with chemicals; UV and contact with solvents quickly reduce the strength of synthetic rope.
Yeni katılan tayfa; gemiyi, ekipmanı ve: Newly joined deckhands do not yet fully know the ship, the equipment and the risks. This is why new personnel stand out in accident statistics. The Bosun knows that giving them the right start protects both their lives and the safety of the whole team.
Yeni mürettebata kendi kamarasından ve ç: New crew members are shown the primary and alternative escape routes from their cabin and work area to the muster station by actually walking them. The photoluminescent escape signs, the emergency lighting, the EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) locations and the engine room escape trunk are pointed out.
Yeni mürettebata önce hayat kurtaran tem: A new crew member is first shown the life-saving basics: where their own lifejacket is (cabin + spare at the muster station), how to don it (practical demonstration), where the immersion suit is and how to don it, their muster station, their abandon ship duty and which survival craft they will board. This information is reinforced by the station card.
Yeni nesil gemilerde sürekli sensör veri: On new-generation ships, continuous sensor data (temperature, pressure, vibration, load) is sent to cloud-based analytics platforms; through anomaly detection, failures are predicted before they happen. This moves the PMS from calendar-based to condition-based/predictive maintenance. The Chief Engineer owns the accuracy of this data, the alarm thresholds and the response on site; however rich the data, the final technical decision belongs to the engineer.
Yeni personel, deneyimli bir AB ile eşle: New personnel are paired with an experienced AB (buddy system) and work under supervision during the first weeks. The Chief Officer holds a review within the first 2 weeks to assess the person's adaptation, language/communication skills and abilities. In multinational crews, a common working language (usually English) and a clear command structure are critical for safety.
Yeni personel; muster station, can kurta: On their first day on board, new personnel are briefed on the muster station, the locations of life-saving and fire-fighting equipment, escape routes, alarm signals and basic safety rules (familiarization). The Bosun gives the practical familiarization on the deck side and completes the checklist.
Yeni personele en yakın fire alarm call: New crew members are shown the nearest fire alarm call points (manual push buttons), the locations and types of portable extinguishers, and the locations of the fire hydrants and hoses. It must be clear how they raise the alarm on discovering a fire (call point, telephone, radio) and to whom they report.
Yeni personele fire door (yangın bölmesi: New crew members are taught the difference between a fire door (fire division) and a watertight door (watertight subdivision), the conditions in which they are kept closed and the emergency closing mechanism. They are shown that power-operated watertight doors can be closed remotely from the bridge and that local controls are also provided.
Yeni personele kim kime rapor verir, aci: New crew members are told clearly who reports to whom, whom to notify in an emergency and what to do when they see a hazardous situation. Typical chain: seaman → bosun/officer → relevant supervisor → Master. The right to report directly to the bridge (OOW) in an emergency is always stressed.
Yeni referans önce monitor konumunda göz: A new reference is first observed in the monitor position; if its residual, variance and trend are consistent, it is enabled in a controlled way. If a reference deviates, rather than deselecting it at once, common sensors, targets, geometry and environmental causes are compared.
Yeni retrofit kararlarında (pre-swirl, p: In new retrofit decisions (pre-swirl ducts, propeller boss cap fins and so on), the EEDI/EEXI/CII should be assessed together, not only the return on investment.
Yeni sistemin devreye alınması, ekibin o: Commissioning a new system does not mean that the team knows it. If the operator stations and HMI have changed, familiarisation training and a familiarisation record are needed for the DPOs; the engine side also needs to learn the new fault diagnosis flows.
Yeni yük öncesi ambar; önceki yük artıkl: Before a new cargo, the hold is cleaned of residues of the previous cargo, rust, water, oil and bad odors. The cleaning standard depends on the cargo: grain/food cargoes require "grain clean" or "hospital clean", whereas scrap metal can be loaded to a lower standard. The AB learns the required cleanliness level from the Bosun and sweeps, washes and dries accordingly.
Yer değiştirme (displacement), hız (velo: Displacement, velocity and acceleration are the measures of vibration. At low frequencies displacement is the dominant indicator, at high frequencies acceleration.
Yer giderleri (floor drains) ve evye süz: Floor drains and sink strainers are cleared regularly; a blocked drain causes odors and standing water (slipping hazard) and attracts pests. Pouring grease down the drain causes blockages; grease is collected separately.
Yetersiz arıtmayla deşarj çevre ihlali v: Discharge with insufficient treatment is an environmental violation and a public health risk.
Yetersiz aydınlatma, gece güverte çalışm: Inadequate lighting increases the risk of accidents during night work and when moving about the deck. The AB reports defective deck lighting, uses a portable lamp for night work and takes visual obstructions (steam, smoke) into account. High-visibility PPE helps the wearer to be noticed by others and increases safety in maneuvering areas.
Yetersiz aydınlatma, gece operasyonların: Inadequate lighting increases the risk of accidents during night operations and in passageways. The Bosun routinely checks that deck lights, passageway lighting and emergency lighting are working, and reports defective lights. Lighting of the mooring deck, access ways and store entrances has priority.
Yetersiz aydınlatma; hatalı okuma, kaza: Poor lighting means misreadings, accidents and incomplete maintenance. The Second Engineer ensures that light fittings that are not working are replaced immediately, especially the lamps at the maneuvering console, in the boiler room and along the walkways.
Yetersiz ballast kapasitesi hızlı yüklem: Insufficient ballast pump capacity can lead to SF/BM limits being exceeded during fast loading.
Yetersiz dezenfeksiyon gastrointestinal: Insufficient disinfection creates a risk of gastrointestinal outbreaks and Legionella; water quality is monitored continuously.
Yetersiz manning (eksik personel) yorgun: Insufficient manning is a structural cause of fatigue; if the Master finds that the manning is not enough for the operation, he or she reports it to the DPA (under-manning is a safety and MLC issue). Intensive port rotations, frequent PSC/vetting inspections, drills and emergencies put pressure on rest hours; the Master plans according to this reality and, if necessary, takes the decision to slow down operations under the overriding authority.
Yetersiz reception facility durumunda (ö: Where reception facilities are inadequate (particularly in some ports), this can be reported under MEPC.1/Circ.834. If waste cannot be delivered, the Chief Officer manages the storage capacity and plans for the next suitable port.
Yetersiz stabilite alabora; aşırı stabil: Insufficient stability means capsizing; excessive stability (stiff) means violent rolling and high lashing loads; an incorrect distribution with respect to strength means hull damage. The cadet learns that stability is not "an abstract calculation" but the basis of the ship's survival. Many marine casualties have been caused by stability/cargo errors.
Yetersiz starting air manevrada ana maki: Insufficient starting air means a risk of being unable to start the main engine during manoeuvring.
Yetersiz uyku, bölünmüş dinlenme, ağır i: The main factors are insufficient sleep, broken rest, heavy workload, intensive port operations, noise and vibration, disruption of the circadian rhythm (night watches, frequent time zone changes) and stress. On ships with small crews, the intensity of port calls and manoeuvring rapidly increases fatigue.
Yetersiz ventilasyon CO birikimi ve yakı: Insufficient ventilation creates a risk of CO build-up and of an explosion from fuel vapour; the system is kept in continuous working order.
Yokohama fender'lar ve mooring pattern,: Yokohama fenders and the mooring pattern keep the two ships at a safe distance. The approach manoeuvre is made slowly and under control. A leak test is carried out after the hoses are connected.
Yolcu alanları, kaymaz yüzey ve korkuluk: Passenger areas are maintained with attention to non-slip surfaces and the safety of railings; wet floors are marked. Paint and corrosion maintenance is carried out regularly.
Yolcu gemilerinde muster organizasyonu,: On passenger ships, the muster organization also covers directing the passengers: a muster drill is held at the start of the voyage, the passenger lifejacket donning points are marked and marshalling personnel are assigned. The Safety Officer checks that the passenger counting system and the plan for passengers with special needs are ready.
Yolcu gemilerinde stabilite kriterleri e: On passenger ships the stability criteria are stricter because of the additional crowding and turning moments.
Yolcu gemilerinde tahliye süresi (SOLAS): On passenger ships the evacuation time criteria (SOLAS) must be verified through drills.
Yolcu gemisi yangınında erken algılama v: In a passenger ship fire, early detection and subdivision prevent mass casualties.
Yolcu gemisinde LSA eksikliği toplu can: On a passenger ship, a shortfall in LSA means a risk of mass loss of life; maintenance allows no compromise.
On a passenger ship water quality is monitored closely because of the risk of a waterborne outbreak (e.g. Legionella).
Yolcu gemisinde yangının yayılması paniğ: On a passenger ship, the spread of a fire can lead to panic and mass casualties; subdivision and a fast response are essential.
Yolcu/bagaj X-ray ve metal detektör ile: Passengers and luggage are screened by X-ray and metal detectors; unauthorised entry is prevented at access control points. Measures are increased according to the security level.
Yolcular acil durumda ilk kez öğrenmemel: Passengers should not be learning this for the first time in an emergency; the briefing must be early and easy to understand.
Yolcular alarm sonrası muster station'a: After the alarm, passengers are directed to their muster stations, where the lifejacket and the procedure are demonstrated. Attendance is verified by counting and marking. If possible, this is done before departure.
Yolcular boarding pass ve ISPS güvenlik: Passengers pass through boarding pass checks and ISPS security screening and are entered in the manifest. Boarding and disembarking flows are organised with gangway safety and crowd management in mind.
Yorgunluk (fatigue) lookout etkinliğini: Fatigue is the number one factor that reduces lookout effectiveness. Late at night and on long watches, the risk of micro-sleep increases. The AB must report fatigue or the risk of dozing off to the OOW and use strategies to stay alert, such as standing, moving around or stepping out into the fresh air.
Yorgunluk (fatigue), denizcilik kazaları: Fatigue is the most common human factor behind marine accidents. The Chief Officer plans so that real rest is achieved, not so that rest hours add up on paper; "adjusting the records" (manipulating records) is both an MLC violation and a serious safety risk.
Yorgunluk etkileri: yavaş reaksiyon, dik: Effects of fatigue: slow reactions, lack of attention, wrong decisions, micro-sleeps. It is similar to the effect of alcohol: being awake for 17 hours ≈ a blood alcohol level of 0.05%.
Yorgunluk yönetimi (rest hours) ve net v: Fatigue is managed (rest hours) and a clear handover of the watch is made; when in doubt, the Master is called.
Yorgunluk yönetimi de operasyon güvenliğ: Fatigue management is also part of operational safety. During long port operations, MLC rest hours are observed; a tired crew increases the risk of accidents in lashing and hatch operations.
Yorgunluk yönetimi, kaptanın hem yasal y: Fatigue management is both the Master's legal obligation and one of the most effective tools for preventing accidents. Honest records, realistic workload planning and an open culture minimise the invisible risk that a tired crew can cause.
Yorgunluk, deniz kazalarının önde gelen: Fatigue is one of the leading human factors in marine accidents, and nutrition is an important part of this equation. Regular mealtimes, hot food planned to suit watch changes and a "night lunch" available 24 hours a day support the watchkeeper whose sleep-wake cycle is disrupted. Instead of the false energy of caffeine, sugar and heavy, greasy food, the cook designs meals that give sustained energy.
Yorgunluk, denizcilik kazalarının en yay: Fatigue is the most common human-factor root cause of maritime accidents (identified in the Exxon Valdez, the Cosco Busan and countless groundings and collisions). MSC.1/Circ.1598 (Guidelines on Fatigue) deals with factors such as sleep debt, circadian rhythm, monotony and workload. The Master's most critical responsibility is to close the gap between rest hours "looking compliant on paper" and the seafarer "actually being rested".
Yorgunluk, denizdeki kazaların başlıca i: Fatigue is the main human factor in accidents at sea. A rating who has worked long hours during a port/maneuvering period is not given risky work the following morning. By making sure the team actually rests, the Bosun both complies with the regulations and prevents accidents.
Yorgunluk, dikkat ve refleksi düşürerek: Fatigue increases the risk of accidents by reducing attention and reflexes. STCW A-VIII/1 and MLC 2006 make minimum hours of rest mandatory (at least 10 hours in any 24 hours, at least 77 hours in any 7 days). When fatigued, the Oiler does not start critical/high-risk work and reports the situation to the engineer.
Yorgunluk; dikkat dağınıklığı, gecikmiş: Fatigue shows up as distraction, delayed reactions, more errors and impaired decision-making, and it can be fatal in the engine room. The Second Engineer gives priority to rest after busy port stays and consecutive maneuvers, does not give critical jobs to fatigued personnel and spreads the workload evenly across the team. A workload piled onto one person is both a violation and an accident risk.
Yorgunluk; tepki süresini uzatır, dikkat: Fatigue lengthens reaction time, distracts attention, impairs judgement and leads to dangerous states such as "microsleep". Fatigue plays a direct or indirect part in most accidents on the bridge and in the engine room. The Master sees fatigue not as a "weakness" but as a serious operational risk that must be managed.
Yoğun trafik, kısıtlı görüş, dar sular v: In heavy traffic, restricted visibility, narrow waters and at night, the officer has an additional lookout posted. The lookout's only job is to look out; the lookout must not be given the helm or any other task, otherwise the lookout duty is compromised. The lookout is expected to report every target seen to the officer (e.g. "two points on the starboard bow, light in sight").
Yoğun trafikte stajyer, OOW'nin tüm hede: In heavy traffic, the cadet observes how the OOW manages the simultaneous assessment of all targets. Priority is given to the target with the smallest CPA/TCPA and the fastest approach. The cadet learns not to fixate on a single target (target fixation) and lose the "big picture"; the whole horizon and all radar ranges must be scanned periodically.
